# Decisions — ruling register

Every ruling of SCaaS has one entry here: its id, the old ids it replaces (aliases), its status, whether it is an
owner ruling, and **why** it holds. The rule itself is defined once, in the doc named by `normative`, at an anchor
`<a id="ID">`; other docs link that anchor and never restate it. Entries whose `normative` is `decisions.md` are
system-wide positions defined here. Precedence between sources is [ARCH-POS-01](#ARCH-POS-01); the doc map is
[README.md](README.md).

Each entry is a `###` heading `<ID> — <title>`, a meta line `- old: … · status: … · owner: yes|no · date: … ·
normative: <file#ID> · superseded-by: …`, then **Rule.** (only where useful as a summary, or for self-defining
entries), **Why.**, **Cost if wrong.** and **Source.** Superseded entries keep one sentence of what they said.

- **Ids** are `<AREA>-<TOPIC>-<NN>`: `ARCH-POS` (system-wide), `NODE-*` ([node/](node/README.md)), `CTR-*`
  ([contracts/](contracts/README.md)), `NET-*` ([networks/](networks/README.md)), `CLI-*` ([clients/](clients/app.md)),
  `INT-ERP` / `INT-ODOO` ([integration.md](integration.md)). `01`–`79` are current or open, `80`–`99` superseded,
  withdrawn or unused. Ids are never renumbered ([ARCH-POS-07](#ARCH-POS-07)).
- **`open`** = an owner question whose stated default is already applied in the normative text.
- **`old:`** lists the ids used before the 2026-10-07 reorganization (`R91`, `RS5-9`, `CR-PD-2`, `SCaaS:N4`, …);
  `CR-PD-1(c)` names one clause of a split ruling. The generated [alias index](#alias-index) at the end maps every old
  id to its new id(s); from a shell: `python3 scripts/docs_check.py resolve R91`.
- **Source** lines point into `history/` (frozen designs) and `research/` (background); both are read-only.

## 1. Architecture and register policy

These entries define themselves (`normative: decisions.md`): they are system-wide positions, and
[architecture.md](architecture.md) and [README.md](README.md) only explain them.

<a id="ARCH-POS-01"></a>
### ARCH-POS-01 — Source precedence: owner rulings first
- old: owner:2026-10-06:precedence · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-01 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** When two sources disagree, the higher one wins: (1) owner rulings, i.e. entries of this register with
`owner: yes`; (2) the component docs under `node/`, `contracts/`, `networks/`, `clients/` and `integration.md`, each
for its own subject; (3) code, but only for pinned byte formats (typehashes, KAT and conformance vectors); (4)
`history/`; (5) `research/`, which is background only. [architecture.md](architecture.md)
and [README.md](README.md) are not normative. A difference between code and an owner ruling is a bug in the code, not
in the ruling.
**Why.** The earlier system specification ranked itself above the component specs while restating them, and the
copies drifted; the specs disagreed with each other in several places. One register of rulings plus one normative home
per rule removes the second copy. Owner rulings override code that has not caught up, so a ruling is never "undone" by
an implementation shortcut.
**Cost if wrong.** A reader who trusts the overview instead of the component doc applies a stale rule; the checker
keeps ids out of the overview so there is nothing to trust there.
**Source.** [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) line 33; [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) §4 K14.

<a id="ARCH-POS-02"></a>
### ARCH-POS-02 — Family taxonomy
- old: owner:2026-10-06:families · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-02 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** SCaaS supports six families; a family is a group of chains that share one contract code base and one node
adapter: `evm` (EVM chains, including Hedera), `cosmos` (CosmWasm), `soroban` (Stellar and Pi Network), `move` (Aptos
and Sui), `ton` and `solana`. A chain is keyed `chain_key = family:network`. This replaces the earlier list of
"Six ecosystems" (EVM, Hedera, GRAM, Sui, Soroban, Cosmos).
**Why.** Hedera runs EVM contracts and shares the EVM code base and signer, so it is not a family of its own; Aptos and
Sui share the Move language but not their object models, so they are one family with two adapters; Aptos and Solana
were added by the owner. A taxonomy by code base matches how contracts, adapters, tests and the availability matrices
are organized ([networks/README.md](networks/README.md)).
**Cost if wrong.** Counting by ecosystem duplicates the EVM rules for Hedera and hides that one Move fix must be made
twice.
**Source.** [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) line 92; [history/blockchain.md](history/blockchain.md) line 17.

<a id="ARCH-POS-03"></a>
### ARCH-POS-03 — `scaas` names everywhere
- old: owner:2026-10-06:naming · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-03 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every product name is a `scaas` name: the node `scaas-node`, the envelope `scaas-intent/1.2`, the pay-lane
label `scaas.pay.lane`, environment variables `SCAAS_*`, metrics `scaas_*`, HTTP headers `X-Scaas-*`, EIP-712 domain
names `"SCaaS …"`, tags `scaas.*`, `SCAAS-ZETHER-*`, `scaas/zether/…`. Clients read the domain a deployed contract
reports (`eip712Domain()`) instead of assuming a string.
**Why.** SCaaS is a standalone product; the first implementation carried the brand of its first client in node,
envelope, lane and environment names, which tied every operator and every other client to that brand. The rename has
landed in code.
**Cost if wrong.** A domain string assumed by a client breaks signatures against any deployment that kept an older
name; reading `eip712Domain()` avoids it.
**Source.** [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) lines 93, 102.

<a id="ARCH-POS-04"></a>
### ARCH-POS-04 — Market-neutral protocol and docs
- old: owner:2026-10-06:market-neutral · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** SCaaS names no country's law, currency or regulator in its protocol, contracts or docs. Data protection is
specified as technical controls (no personal data on chain, off-chain linkage, minimized node state, crypto-shredding,
disclosure) that a deployment maps to its own regime (GDPR-class: lawful basis, minimization, erasure, retention,
cross-border transfer, processor agreements).
**Why.** SCaaS is sold worldwide. A rule written for one market either does not apply elsewhere or reads as a
compliance claim the product cannot make for every deployment.
**Cost if wrong.** A deployment in a market with stricter rules must add controls on its side; the generic controls
are designed to be the strict superset.
**Source.** [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) lines 94, 1959.

<a id="ARCH-POS-05"></a>
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): "no personal data on chain" becomes a recommendation for payment metadata (owner O5): a business identifier in clear is not recommended and never refused, wallets warn ([ARCH-POS-17](#ARCH-POS-17)); the technical controls stay.
### ARCH-POS-05 — The node is independent of any ERP
- old: R87, owner:2026-10-06:node-independent · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-05 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `scaas-node` never connects to an ERP. Every ERP, portal or application is one client among others: it
pushes jobs to the node's job API and reads the node's feeds. The node's control plane is its own store and admin API;
every node is "standalone". This supersedes the earlier design in which the node claimed jobs from an ERP database and
the ERP stayed the control plane.
**Why.** One product serves many ERPs; a node that depends on one ERP's database, models and RPC is a component of
that ERP, not a service. Keeping the journal, configuration and feeds in the node's own store also keeps
journal-before-broadcast local, without an ERP round trip.
**Cost if wrong.** The ERP learns job and chain state by polling the feeds instead of being called; the client's sync
schedule bounds the delay.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-node-independence-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-node-independence-design.md) line 109; [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) line 37.

Change (2026-11-08, owner, status: decided, PLANNED for node round P4): "the node never calls a client" gains one exception, the optional doorbell of [NODE-IDX-09](node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-09): a signed ping per API key with no job or event data, after which the client reads the feeds. Data webhooks and callbacks stay refused; the feeds stay the only source of truth.

<a id="ARCH-POS-06"></a>
### ARCH-POS-06 — Three use cases from the first wave
- old: UD:§1:use-cases, UD:§15:D12, canon:D12 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-06 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** SCaaS serves three use cases, all configurable from the first deployment: loyalty and rewards, B2B
settlement between a brand and its distributors or suppliers, and end-user payments. The technical focus is
meta-transactions, confidential amounts (Zether) and stablecoins.
**Why.** The owner chose full configuration over a staged launch. The three cases share one token, meta-transaction
and settlement core; what differs is configuration (fee mode, sponsorship, custody, confidentiality).
**Cost if wrong.** Enabling B2B from the start makes organizational custody of signing and decryption keys a launch
requirement rather than a later option.
**Source.** [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) lines 38, 862.

<a id="ARCH-POS-07"></a>
### ARCH-POS-07 — Register policy: open entries, defaults, superseded owner rulings
- old: reorg:Q2, reorg:Q10, reorg:Q13, reorg:Q14 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Ids are `<AREA>-<TOPIC>-<NN>`; `01`–`79` are current or open, `80`–`99` superseded, withdrawn or unused.
Ids are never renumbered or reused; a clarification keeps its id, a reversal creates a new id and the old one becomes
`superseded`. Status `open` means an owner question whose stated default is already applied in the normative text.
Interpretations awaiting confirmation keep their stated defaults as `open` entries. Requirements of the original
requirements note that no design ever ruled on are recorded as `open` entries, `PLANNED` where a seam exists. Earlier
owner decisions that a later ruling replaced are recorded as `superseded` owner rulings, not re-opened; unruled items
of the earlier decision log are `open` entries.
**Why.** Nothing the owner asked for or decided may disappear silently, and nothing may be decided silently either: an
`open` entry makes the default visible and keeps it reversible.
**Cost if wrong.** An `open` default that the owner later reverses needs a new id and a doc change; the alias index
keeps the old reference resolvable.
**Source.** [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) §3.1, §8 (Q2, Q10, Q13, Q14).

<a id="ARCH-POS-08"></a>
### ARCH-POS-08 — Market-specific research stays private
- old: reorg:Q9 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The research note on one market's law and the large raw tool-output file stay in `research/` while the
repository is private and are removed before any public release. Neither ever enters the current docs.
**Why.** The market-neutral rule ([ARCH-POS-04](#ARCH-POS-04)) keeps market law out of the product; the files remain
useful background for the owner meanwhile.
**Source.** [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) §8 Q9.

<a id="ARCH-POS-09"></a>
### ARCH-POS-09 — Work plans stay in history and the TODO list
- old: reorg:Q11 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Implementation work items (their scope, gates and dependencies) stay in the frozen design specs under
`history/` and are tracked in the repository TODO list; there is no roadmap document under `docs/`, and the current
docs carry no work-item ids.
**Why.** Work plans change weekly; normative docs that cite them go stale with every plan change.
**Source.** [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) §4 K22, §8 Q11.

<a id="ARCH-POS-10"></a>
### ARCH-POS-10 — Client data platforms are out of scope
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-10 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** SCaaS delivers finalized facts and operating data: the event feed, the job feed, metrics, usage reports and
disclosure openings. What a client builds on top of them is the client's platform and out of scope: landing tables in a
data warehouse, projections into operational, vector, knowledge-graph, semantic-metric or OLAP stores, AI tool
gateways, and an enterprise-wide multi-plane target architecture.
**Why.** Those layers depend on the client's data model and tooling; SCaaS stays a service whose interface is the
contracts plus the node's feeds ([node/indexer-feeds.md](node/indexer-feeds.md), [node/ops.md](node/ops.md)).
**Cost if wrong.** A client that wants these projections builds them from `/v1/events` and `/v1/jobs`; nothing in the
feeds prevents it.
**Source.** [history/blockchain.md](history/blockchain.md) lines 38–48, 56–74; [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) §2.5.

<a id="ARCH-POS-11"></a>
### ARCH-POS-11 — Documentation language and structure
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The docs are English throughout and self-contained. Rulings carry new component ids with the old ids as
aliases in this register. The old system specification is frozen as `history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md` for reference;
[README.md](README.md) is the entry page and product introduction (non-normative). Line-budget overruns of the Zether, PQ
Zether, network pages and the node overview are accepted, and so is the overrun of this register (owner
2026-10-07).
**Why.** One language and one id scheme for a product used worldwide; the old ids stay resolvable for code comments
(`python3 scripts/docs_check.py resolve <id>`).
**Source.** [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) §8 (owner answers 2026-10-07).

<a id="ARCH-POS-12"></a>
### ARCH-POS-12 — One Rust toolchain for the repository
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-05 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-12 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every Rust crate builds with one Rust toolchain, today 1.97.1, named once: the `rust-toolchain.toml` at the
repository root (targets `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm32v1-none`); no crate has its own toolchain file and no script
names a toolchain. A local run overrides it with the standard `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`; CI sets one workflow variable
`RUST_TOOLCHAIN` (default 1.97.1, a manual run may choose another), which every job installs and exports as
`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`. Every package that declares a `rust-version` declares 1.97.1. Solana's `cargo build-sbf` keeps the
platform-tools rustc it brings. A version above 1.97.1 needs a NEAR wasm build check first. The MSRV-aware resolver no
longer holds alloy at 1.6, so its requirement does: `alloy = "~1.6"` (scaas-node, the only crate that declares alloy).
**Why.** The owner asked to raise the version, keep one, and make it one shared variable with 1.97.1 as its default
(2026-11-05). 1.97.1 is the floor of the Solana host tests (Agave 4.3 crates) and within the rustc cap that cargo-near
0.22 sets from near-sdk's minimum protocol version; a newer version would split NEAR off.
**Cost if wrong.** A crate that needs a newer compiler waits until NEAR's cap moves, or the repository moves together.
**Source.** Owner rulings 2026-11-05 (toolchain; alloy held at `~1.6`).

<a id="ARCH-POS-13"></a>
### ARCH-POS-13 — Never a decryption oracle
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-13 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** No part of SCaaS ever acts as a decryption oracle, for PQZ or Zether: no wallet, client library, binding, CLI,
service, node, MPC quorum or auditor tool decrypts, opens or test-decrypts a ciphertext chosen by anyone other than the
key holder and lets that party learn anything about the result: the plaintext, success or failure, an error code,
timing, or a later action that depends on it. A decryption result reaches only the key holder, or a viewer the key
holder names. Where a ciphertext arrives from outside (an RPC or indexer response, a disclosure bundle, a peer message),
nothing about its decryption is returned or signalled to that source. No exception, no opt-in.
**Why.** PQZ encryption is IND-CPA, not CCA: a decryption oracle recovers the secret `s` with 8·K crafted queries (288 at
`n2304-kmax4096`; research note on PQZ threshold decryption, §12.1). MPC does not
help: inside a quorum the oracle hands one member the whole key (§12.5, open). Zether's ElGamal has no such key
recovery, but one rule for every scheme keeps every decrypt path the same. Owner (2026-11-06): never use an oracle.
It applies to every key holder, not only an MPC quorum: a single-holder wallet, the operator of option (A), and the
auditor key of a token are all exposed the same way.
The check that a ciphertext is real chain state lives in the layer that reads the chain (the wallet layer and the
app), from a source the holder trusts; the signing library (`ua-rs`) holds no light client or state verifier, takes
only named chain locations with the words that layer supplies, and offers no bare-ciphertext decrypt in release builds
(owner 2026-11-06).
**Cost if wrong.** A reachable decrypt path is a key-recovery attack on every account behind it. PQZ MPC quorums for
account keys are not built while the in-quorum oracle is open; `msig` holders use option (A), the operator, meanwhile.
**Source.** Owner ruling 2026-11-06; [research/pqz-threshold-decrypt-prove.md](research/pqz-threshold-decrypt-prove.md) §12.1, §12.5; the code audit of decrypt entry points (2026-11-06, done; the fix spec and the library rules are on branch `ua-rs-sign`).

<a id="ARCH-POS-15"></a>
### ARCH-POS-15 — Every RPC consumer takes a list of nodes
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-08 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-15 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner 2026-11-08: anything that reads or writes a chain through an RPC (the node, scaas-wallet, the app, the client
libraries' reading layers, the reference readers, CLIs and operator tools) accepts a **list** of RPC endpoints, one or more. An
endpoint is **named** (by the operator or holder), a **default** (in the release's own reviewed list, from public RPC information;
trusted like a named one) or **discovered** (found at run time); all three are allowed everywhere (owner 2026-11-08). **Reads that
feed a decryption** (PQZ, Zether; ARCH-POS-13): named and default endpoints may serve alone, a discovered one only under the
agreement option with at least three nodes, so one unknown node can never put a ciphertext of its choice into a decryption. **Reads:** by default **failover** in the order
given: one read is answered completely by one node, never mixing answers of different nodes, and the next node starts over when
one fails or is inconsistent; with the **agreement option** a **strict majority** of the named nodes (⌊n/2⌋ + 1) must return the
same complete answer at the same block (by hash), agreement counted per node over the whole read, else the read is refused.
**Writes:** the same signed bytes go to one or more of the named nodes (never re-signed per node); the node keeps its own lane
rules (journal before broadcast, one transaction per nonce). Built first in the reference readers `pqz-read` and
`zether-read-balance` (`--rpc` repeated, `--rpc-agree`, branch `ua-rs-sign`); the node's indexer already takes `rpc_urls`
with a quorum; every other consumer follows in its own round.
**Why.** One node can lie, lag or fail; a list gives availability by failover and, with the majority option, a read that one
dishonest or broken node cannot change.
**Cost if wrong.** A single-endpoint consumer either stops when its node is down or trusts whatever that node answers.
**Source.** owner 2026-11-08 (chat): several `--rpc`, an agreement option, "chỉ cần quá bán", and "ví, hoặc bất cứ thứ gì cần đọc/ghi rpc đều cần cho phép mảng nhiều rpc như vậy".

**Why.** Owner 2026-11-02: an AI audit is better than a human one; a label tied to a round and a commit cannot claim more than was reviewed.
**Cost if wrong.** A label on code its round did not cover would overstate; the commit in the label and the "changed after its round" rule prevent it.

<a id="ARCH-POS-16"></a>
<a id="ARCH-POS-17"></a>
### ARCH-POS-17 — Business identifiers in clear on chain: not recommended, never refused; wallets warn
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-05 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-17 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A business document number, tax id or party name in clear on chain (a non-empty `PayMeta.payNo`, a schema 1 or 2 body) is **not recommended and never refused** by the contracts; a payer may put it in the payment metadata ([CTR-MTX-26](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-26)). Wallets warn before signing such a payment, once per payee per session, show the decoded fields beside the typed data and recommend schema 4 (encrypted). Three separate privacy properties hold: an unpublished random-salted preimage resists document-number guessing (only until it is paid through a pay entry, which publishes it); a clear `payNo` or body is publicly searchable forever; repeated `entryRef` values are linkable whatever the salt. The transaction carries `from` and `to` in clear.
**Status.** BUILT: the contracts refuse no metadata (T37 `3740b85e`); `clientkeys` `payMetaWarning` (`clients/clientkeys/test/paymeta.test.js`). The other signers' warnings follow their own rounds.
**Why.** Owner O5: invoice numbers on chain are a warning, not a ban; a ban the contract cannot enforce on free bytes would only push the data elsewhere.
**Cost if wrong.** A payer publishes personal or business data forever without being told; or a protocol ban blocks a legitimate reconciliation need.
**Source.** `superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-pay-meta-tax.md` §3.3, §9, §12 PT-7 (owner O5, 2026-11-05; controller call C4). The spec proposed the id ARCH-POS-13, taken by the decryption-oracle rule; this entry takes the next free id.

### ARCH-POS-16 — No temporary or machine path in a committed file
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: decisions.md#ARCH-POS-16 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner 2026-11-10: no committed file (scripts, gate runners, CI, run logs and evidence, notes, docs, plans, test strings) carries a temporary path such as one under the system temp directory, or another path of one machine. Scripts make their temp directory at run time (`mktemp -d` with a trap, Python `tempfile`, CI `$RUNNER_TEMP`) or use a git-ignored path in the tree; logs and notes write `<tmp>/name`. `*/legacy/*` and `docs/history/*` are left as they are. A CI step in the `docs` job (`git grep` for the temp prefix outside those two) refuses a new one. Built on `ua-mtx-merge` 2026-11-10 (`098a5de1`, `e9bbfd57`, `2da8f841`, `5a23e1a7`).
**Why.** The repository is public; such paths are one machine's noise, and the summary-only rule for gate logs already asks for no absolute paths.
**Cost if wrong.** None in behaviour: only where a script writes its scratch files changes.
**Source.** owner 2026-11-10 (chat): "không đưa cả đường dẫn tạm tmp lên".

## 2. Node — General

### NODE-GEN-01 — Node holds no subject funds or keys
- old: SCaaS:N1, UD:§23.2 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: node/README.md#NODE-GEN-01 · superseded-by: —

**Owner ruling (2026-10-07).** Lane keys hold gas only and never hold a role on any contract, dev deployments included; role-holding targets go through a Safe (NODE-JOB-19).
**Why.** Funds and subject keys stay with subjects and contracts; a compromised node can only stop working or lie on its feed. A relayer signs only the outer transaction, with its `authKey`; it never needs a subject's confidential key `x`: it cannot decrypt the amount, build the proof or change any field (all are in the signed digest), and that blindness is the property, not a limitation. A server holds `x` only when the company itself sends from its own confidential treasury, which is custody, not relay; the key oracle that serves it is small (under 300 lines; the enclave image under 5,000 lines including the crypto backend), so it stays out of the node process, which parses strangers' bytes.
**Source.** [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) line 880; [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 2055.
Change (2026-11-06, group 3f, controller call C7 in the owner-approved spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-attested-verify.md`; NODE-JOB-22): **applied.** The node holds no PQZ verifier key either: it carries or fetches verdicts and never signs one; signing is the PQZ verifier (off-chain), a separately operated process with its own key custody ([ops.md](node/ops.md#pqz-verifier)). Status: BUILT (T47 `75ddccc4`…`062133b6`, T48 `06e11d23`, `5d4a2780`).

### NODE-JOB-20 — Meta-tx `data` read through the implementation's selector allowlist
- old: typed-signing:TS-D21 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-20 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The token gateway runs a transfer, a payment or a self-call of the token's own allowlisted functions (owner: "functions of the token itself", "a fixed per-implementation selector allowlist"); a fixed op list in the node would refuse every new operation and need a node release each time. Reading the published `mtxSelectors()` table per immutable implementation keeps intake, pricing (fee class, amount argument), display and the canonical-encoding check exact, and keeps role functions out of the token path.
**Cost if wrong.** The node relays self-calls whose fee basis it misreads, or refuses valid wraps/burns; a non-canonical dynamic encoding would give one intent two mesh identities.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §2 A1–A3, §3 MG-1, MG-2, MG-5, MG-6.
Change (2026-10-08): the table covers every SCaaS contract on `MetaTxBase`, not only tokens; `metatx` jobs name their struct (`call` | `transfer`); a `MetaTransfer` counts as selector `transfer`/`pay` in the breaker. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-7, GC-8.

Under "Node — Submit lanes":
Change (2026-10-08): non-EVM `signed_op` jobs carry `op_kind` `call`/`transfer`; the node relays only the `mtx_` entries it lists per contract (`SELECTOR_NOT_ALLOWED` otherwise) and breaks per `(from, function)`. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-2, §5.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner rule 2026-10-31 (explicit named JSON), controller calls, owner may override; status: documented; built in typed-signing N1; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the job API is explicit JSON per operation (`docs/node/job-api.md` §5.3): `op` with `entry`, `contract`, `token`, `envelope`, `args`, `signature` / `auth`; the node builds calldata and the typed digest from one parse; hex is refused on every kind (`HEX_DATA_REFUSED`). **Consumers follow** (scaas defines the interface): `op` on every EVM job, `op` instead of `calldata` on the venue's `settle` / `cancel` / `invalidate` jobs, `auth` as the `UASig` object, `contract` on Zether and PQZ `MetaTransfer` jobs, relay fees by job only with a named `call`. **`POST /v1/op` keeps the old door**: a registered token's `mtx*` entries only, nothing the old door refused (the factory, the registry, a DEX, a wallet, a relay fee are jobs of a namespace with the grant), and no `ua*` entry (it goes as a `ua_metatx` job). The node computes the typed digest locally (no `mtxDigest` read) and holds it as the in-flight key, together with `keccak(to ‖ data)` for a derived-UA or contract signer. Soroban job shapes are not documented here: they moved to `ua8-soroban`.
Change (2026-11-09, owner Q1 B, group 3i): the table is fixed for every kind but `service`, whose rows are the configured services' declared entries; the node still builds every call from named fields, by the declared EIP-712 type, under bounds ([NODE-JOB-25](node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-25)). Status: BUILT (T79 `711f4f35`).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R43; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED: `scaas-node/src/gateway.rs`, `submit.rs` and `mesh/accept.rs` with their tests): `OP_KIND_MISMATCH` means an entry that the per-kind call table does not list for the job's kind (names no longer carry the form); an address `MetaTransfer` names no token or mandate wallet entry.

### NODE-JOB-21 — The node's queue claims by kind: a stopped kind never hides another
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-21 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The node's own queue claims by kind, so a stopped kind never hides another, and each namespace has a `call` quota.
**Why.** A stopped kind stays queued, and on an oldest-first read its backlog hides every other kind. The node is open and any consumer can run it, so the guarantee is the node's (owner correction 2026-11-02).
**Cost if wrong.** A free `call` backlog stops payments on a lane with budget left.
**Source.** owner correction 2026-11-02, ua8-soroban B9a review.

### NODE-JOB-22 — PQZ jobs carry a named pqz_verdict; the node rebuilds the PqzVerdict, relays verdicts and never signs one
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-22 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every PQZ proof-carrying named entry (the six signed `UAEnvelope` forms and their six direct inner calls) takes `args.pqz_verdict: {pqzVerifierEpoch, validUntil, auth}`, exactly these fields, `auth` a `UASig`; the node builds `PqzVerdict{token, chainId, proofSystemId, statementHash, proofHash, pqzVerifierEpoch, validUntil}` itself from the target token, the chain, `proofSystemId()`, the statement the token's own view builds for the job's named arguments and binding, and the job's proof, and appends `PqzSignedVerdict` last; a hex or packed verdict is `HEX_ARGS_REFUSED`, the struct itself `BAD_PAYLOAD`. A `PRECOMPILE` token gets the empty verdict and a job naming one is `PQZ_VERDICT_NOT_EXPECTED`. An `OFFCHAIN` job without a usable verdict is fetched from the operator's `[pqz_verifier] endpoints` in order; none answers ⇒ `PQZ_VERDICT_MISSING`, zero sends. Liftable verifier errors are `PQZ_VERDICT_REFUSED: <error>`, back in the queue, never `dead` while a transaction may land; the job's deadline is the sooner of the envelope's and the verdict's `validUntil`. The indexer keeps a per-token health signal; the opt-in `refuse_shield_when_unserved` refuses shields into an `OFFCHAIN` token nobody serves (`PQZ_VERIFIER_UNREACHABLE`), the same rule for every consumer. The node holds no verifier key and signs nothing. **UNAUDITED.**

**Status.** BUILT (T47 `75ddccc4`, `fd2dfb2f`, `e50251b4`, `b3b31560`, `062133b6`): `args.pqz_verdict`, the rebuild, the fetch, the refusals, the router rows, the indexer's health signal and `refuse_shield_when_unserved`; tests `pqz_verdict_subobject_builds_struct`, `pqz_verdict_hex_refused`, `offchain_job_without_pqz_verdict_fetches_or_refuses`, `precompile_job_with_pqz_verdict_refused`, `pqz_verdict_epoch_mismatch_refetch_once`, `pqz_verdict_mismatch_not_dead`, `shield_refused_when_unserved_and_enabled`, `router_pqz_verifier_rows`, `indexer_joins_proof_offchain_with_position`, `offchain_job_not_refused_without_precompile`, e2e `pqz_offchain_transfer_on_anvil`, `pqz_revoked_verifier_on_anvil` (local anvil). The token view (`GET /v1/tokens/{chain}` per-token row): SPECIFIED.

**Why.** C7 (Codex #8): an in-node signer changes key custody; the verifier role is the token's (O2), the node is open and keyless, a lane key holds gas only. C8 (Fable P2-7): shields keep landing in a pool whose verifier is gone. CTR-PQZ-15 applied: no new job kind (Fable P2-9 (i)).

**Cost if wrong.** A node that signs becomes the trust root of every token it serves; a node that sends without a verdict pays for certain reverts.

**Source.** Spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-attested-verify.md` §11.1 (approved by the owner 2026-11-06 with its controller calls C7, C8), §10 rows 6, 10; contract rules CTR-PQZ-27, CTR-PQZ-29.

Change (owner 2026-11-11, group 3t, [CTR-PQZ-36](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36); status: BUILT on `ua-mtx-3t`, UNAUDITED): a proof-carrying PQZ job names `args.pqz_fee`, the fee word its proof was built over (a `uint64` decimal string), required on an `OFFCHAIN` token and optional on a `PRECOMPILE` one (controller call, Fable P3-4); the node compares it with word 256 of the statement the token's view builds, at intake and before every send, and refuses a difference `PQZ_FEE_MISMATCH`, zero sends, back in the queue and never `dead` while the op may land; a simulation's `AuthRejected` after an indexed `VerifierFeeSet` of the token maps to the same.

### NODE-JOB-23 — A PQZ job names the key version it debits; stale, reused, unknown, pending and rotated versions are refused by name
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-23 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `keyVersion` is a named field (a `uint64` decimal string) of every PQZ debit, rollover and prepare; the registry rows take the version (`setPqzKey(ua, version, …)`, `storePqzPop(ua, version, pqzPop)`); the rollover is one row per kind (`UARollOver` on Zether, `UAPqzRollOver` on PQZ). Refusals: `PQZ_KEY_STALE`, `PQZ_KEY_REUSED` (`dead`), `PQZ_KEY_VERSION_UNKNOWN` (queued), `PQZ_KEY_ROTATION_PENDING` at intake (`dead`, nothing simulated), `PQZ_KEY_ROTATED` (queued, never `dead`) only after a `UAPqzKeyCurrent` of a party in the last 10,000 blocks, with the simulation error. Indexer rows `UAPqzKeyAdded` (feed `pqz_pending`), `UAPqzPopStored`, `UAPqzKeyCurrent` (feed `pqz_current`), and `Credited` / `Debited` / `PqzRolledOver` with `key_version`. Keepers run per `(ua, version)`. **UNAUDITED.**

**Status.** BUILT (T55, `scaas-node/src/{abi,guard,submit,typed,indexer}.rs`, `tests/e2e.rs`); the keeper per `(ua, version)` SPECIFIED (the node has no keeper yet).

**Why.** Owner rulings O1–O7 and R1–R6 of 2026-11-06 make PQZ state per `(ua, version)` (CTR-UA-42, CTR-PQZ-31); a job that does not name the version it debits cannot be checked before simulation, and a rotation must never leave a job silently `dead` while it may still land.

**Cost if wrong.** A debit on a stale or pending version reverts after the lane paid for it, or a rotating UA's in-flight credits are reported dead and lost to the sender's view.

**Source.** Owner 2026-11-06 (O1–O7, R1–R6); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-key-versions.md` §7, §12; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md` T55.

### NODE-JOB-24 — A PQZ debit above the lane's cap on a token storing proofs in its log is held, never reported dead early
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: node/submit-lanes.md#NODE-JOB-24 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A PQZ debit whose simulation is over the lane's cap (`max_gas_per_tx`, the chain's block gas limit, or the 2^24 per-transaction limit) on a token whose `proofStore()` answers LOG is requeued with `PROOF_STORE_OVER_LANE_CAP: <reason>` and reported `dead` only at its `validUntil`; under NONE, or on a release without `proofStore()`, it is the plain refusal as before; a transport error on the probe requeues. Every PQZ debit job names `ownTag` (`bytes32` hex) in `args`; the shape before 3h is refused at intake `BAD_PAYLOAD: args.args.ownTag: missing`. **UNAUDITED.**

**Status.** BUILT (T63 `39fa296c`, `a6040f9a`; the legacy copy `f01ff0ec`; node mutants N1–N3 killed).

**Why.** Fable P2 on the proof-path spec: the issuer's switch to LOG can push a large debit over the lane's cap; the issuer may switch back (CTR-GOV-22), so the job may still land and must not be reported dead.

**Cost if wrong.** A debit that could land after the issuer sets NONE is reported dead, and its sender re-proves or gives up.

**Source.** Spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-proof-path.md` §12 (owner approved 2026-11-07); Fable review P2; contract rules CTR-PQZ-34, CTR-PQZ-35.

### NODE-JOB-25 — The contract kind service: a third-party service pull, its entries from operator config, equal to the contract's
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-09 · normative: node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-25 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** One generic node kind `service` (owner Q1 B): its rows come from operator config (`[[chains.services]] address, entries = [{entry, op_type}]`, EVM only, 1–32 entries, `op_type` at most 1,024 bytes and at most 16 fields of `address`, `bool`, `bytesN`, `uintN`, `bytes`, `string`, no array, no nested struct; `intN` refused at startup), checked at startup against the contract's `servicePullEntries()` and `eip712Domain()` in both directions (`SERVICE_ENTRIES_MISMATCH` stops the lane). An address has one kind, both ways. The job is a `ua_metatx` named entry `{entry, contract: "service", token: <S>, args: {op, pullToken, t, auth}}`, every value a named field; the node builds `<entry>(<Op>, UAMetaTransfer, UASig)` itself, checks the spec's §3.3 steps 1–4 (`SERVICE_PULL_SHAPE`), reads the pulled token from the contract (`SERVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH`, `TOKEN_NOT_SERVED`), and with a fee in the pulled token on the pull's lane requires the fee's nonce to be the pull's + 1. No service is named in node code; the gateway is unchanged. **UNAUDITED.**

**Status.** BUILT (T79 `711f4f35`: `scaas-node/src/service.rs`, the guard's service rule, config; tests `service::tests`, `guard::tests::service_pull_through_the_guard`, `service_config_one_kind_per_address`, `submit::tests`; 8 node mutants killed). The `chain_contract` kind `service` of the store: SPECIFIED (the node reads `[[chains.services]]`).

**Why.** Owner 2026-11-09, Q1 B: a node is open, so a service pull must be relayable for any service without a node release, and the node still builds every call from named fields by a declared EIP-712 type under bounds.

**Cost if wrong.** A config row that differs from the contract would let the lane sign calls the service does not declare, or a second kind on one address would let one row's rule cover another's call.

**Source.** Owner 2026-11-09 (Q1–Q5 as recommended); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-service-pull.md` §8, §13; contract rule CTR-MTX-32.

- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: node/submit-lanes.md#NODE-LANE-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** 16 is the default per-sender pending limit of common execution clients (`txpool.accountslots`); chains differ, so the depth is configuration.
**Cost if wrong.** Too high: transactions beyond the pool limit are dropped and must be replaced; too low: lane throughput is capped below what the chain allows.

**Cost if wrong.** Relayer gas drained by one subject repeating one failing call, or a subject's payments throttled for an unrelated wrap failure.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §3 MG-6; §12 M11.

- old: R93 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-04 · superseded-by: —

### NODE-IDX-05 — Event feed items equal ingest arguments
- old: R94 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Feed items carry exactly what the ingest needs, so clients do not re-read the chain.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-node-independence-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-node-independence-design.md) line 116.

### NODE-IDX-06 — Repeated entryRef: node flags, client checks
- old: NI:I6 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-06 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner: both — the client system must know about an overpayment so that the business can later decide to refund the payer. The node already indexes every `PaymentSettled`, so one uniqueness check per `(chain_key, token, entryRef)` serves every client; the client keeps its own check because a node only knows the history it has indexed. The field name `repeat_of` is chosen here.
**Cost if wrong.** Without the flag each client re-implements duplicate detection and some miss overpayments; without the client check a new or restored node would hide a repeat whose first payment it never indexed.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-node-independence-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-node-independence-design.md) line 1615.

### NODE-IDX-07 — Second independent event source
- old: reorg:Q7 · status: open · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A compromised node can lie on its feed; a second independent source would detect it.
**Cost if wrong.** Planned.
**Source.** [history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md](history/plans/2026-10-07-docs-reorg.md) line 1221.

### NODE-IDX-08 — The node keeps and serves the bytes of an `msig`'s member signatures
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-03 · normative: node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner 2026-11-03: on EVM an `msig` keeps hashes of its `pop` and of each member signature (CTR-UA-33 A, CTR-UA-37); the bytes are only in `UAMemberSig`. The node indexes those events, keeps their bytes as long as the record lives, and serves them per `(ua)` and `(ua, index)`, with the `pop` rebuilt in `index` order, each checked against `memberSigHashOf` / `popOf` before it is served. SPECIFIED, not built.
**Why.** History expiry drops logs; without a keeper a copy of an `msig` record has no bytes to send.
**Cost if wrong.** A copy needs another archive of the logs, or the members sign again.
**Source.** owner 2026-11-03, relayed by the coordinator; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-msig-nested.md` N15.

### NODE-IDX-09 — Doorbell: a signed, content-free ping per API key
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-08 · normative: node/indexer-feeds.md#NODE-IDX-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner 2026-11-08: an API key may register one `https` URL; when a feed of its namespace gains items the node sends a ping `{namespace, feed, head_seq, at}` signed by HMAC with that key, carrying no job or event data; the client then reads `/v1/jobs` and `/v1/events` from its cursor. The feeds stay the only source of truth. Outbound guard fails closed: `https` only, no loopback, link-local, private or multicast address after DNS, no redirects, short timeouts, a per-namespace rate limit, its own worker. PLANNED (node round P4).
**Why.** Clients get low latency without a polling worker, while a lost ping loses nothing and a ping leaks nothing; the guard keeps a client's URL from reaching the operator's internal network (SSRF).
**Cost if wrong.** Planned. Without the guard, a tenant could make the node call internal services; with data in the ping, a wrong URL would leak job state.
**Source.** owner 2026-11-08 (chat), Change on ARCH-POS-05.

### NODE-GW-07 — Every SCaaS contract bound to the chain's chain_uid
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: node/gateway.md#NODE-GW-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `chain_uid` is the salt of every SCaaS domain; a contract cannot read its own genesis hash after block 256, so a wrong constructor value can only be caught off chain. **Cost if wrong.** Correct signatures fail on a mis-deployed contract, or — if the value equals another chain's — signatures replay across chains.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §3 MG-4, MG-6; §13 L-12(b).

**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-tender-sponsorship-shredding.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-tender-sponsorship-shredding.md) line 199.

### NODE-DEX-15 — mtxSettle over role-free TradeOrders; the venue arranges taker and makers
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: node/dex-venue.md#NODE-DEX-15 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner rulings: SCaaS legs are token-verified orders with no maker allowance; an order carries no role (the node or submitter decides taker and makers at settlement), keeps `relayer` as the matching party, adds `dex` as the only place funds go, signs one `fee` rate, and every order in a settlement fills at least its signed `minFill` (owner 2026-10-29, CTR-DEX-14; the 2026-10-08 ruling was `max(minFill, 50 %)`). The book keeps price-time; per-role pricing is venue intake policy, not an on-chain setting.
**Cost if wrong.** The venue builds settlements the contracts refuse (minimum fill, fee bound), charges a role rate the signer never accepted, or misses that a one-settlement FOK may span several makers.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §2 A7, A10, A12–A15; §3 MG-8.1–MG-8.4.
Change (2026-10-08): outside legs are funded by an allowance to the DEX's `DexPuller`; intake reads `allowance(from, puller)`. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §3 DS-4.
Change (2026-10-30): the minimum fill is **built** (DEX round, branch `dex-round`, tasks T11 and T12 fix): `min_fill` is the signed `minFill` (no half-order floor, CTR-DEX-14), a maker leg whose base amount is below the market's `min_base_amount` is skipped unless it closes the order on chain, large signed `minFill` orders sit in a separate `min_fill` depth bucket outside best bid / ask and the ticker, and a stale line "partial fills below half an order are impossible" is removed from the rule's Why paragraph. What stays **SPECIFIED**: the rule "no settlement worth less than its gas" — a controller call (plan decision, owner may override): it needs plan pricing, so it is built with the `OrderRouter` (TODO step 6) and the venue today applies only the per-leg `min_base_amount` rule. Cost if wrong: until step 6 a settlement can be smaller than its gas; the submitter pays that gas and the maker still gets its price.


### NODE-DEX-16 — The venue serves only DEXes on the chain profile's DEX list
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: node/dex-venue.md#NODE-DEX-16 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The token requires only that `dex` is a contract; a contract made to look like a DEX can report any fill and take the signed amount. The owner accepted that residual risk (2026-10-08) and placed the defence off chain: the node never routes, settles, replicates or lists an order for an unlisted DEX.
**Cost if wrong.** The node lends its relay and its book to a phishing contract.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §4 (phishing `dex`), §3 MG-6; §8 Q5; §13 N-H1.

Under "Networks — common model":

### NODE-DEX-17 — `OrderRouter`: exchange-only intake, book first, AMM routes, fees by role
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: node/dex-venue.md#NODE-DEX-17 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The node runs its own algorithm over the same orders (owner): book matching first, then coincidences of wants and AMM routes (quoted by `eth_call`, at most 3 hops, cycles), resting orders filled through AMMs when a route reaches their limit; a floor below the quote by a buffer costs the signer nothing because the surplus comes back; exchange-only orders (no listed market, or a cycle) never rest in the book. Off unless the chain enables it.
**Cost if wrong.** Without a book-first rule the venue pays pool fees for liquidity it already holds; without the intake split a cycle order would rest in a book that can never match it.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §2 S3, §3 DS-7.
Change (2026-10-30): **rewritten** (SPECIFIED; the planner is built in TODO step 6, `OrderRouter` EVM, in parallel with non-EVM 1 × N) as one atomic plan per matching event of an order, in four matching modes: (1) book, `mtxSettle`; (2) outside liquidity, `mtxExchange` / `mtxExchangeVia`; (3) hybrid, `mtxHybrid` / `mtxHybridVia` (makers at their own price, the rest through a route, one call); (4) CoW / ring, `mtxExchange` plans among exchange-only orders with the net imbalance routed outside. Rows recorded in full: **Planner order per tick** — options: research note order (CoW / ring first) or the book first of this rule (owner 2026-10-08); choice: the book first for listed-market orders (mode 1, else mode 3 in one plan), CoW / ring among exchange-only orders, then mode 2 for what is left; a listed-market order's outside remainder is netted with exchange-only counterparts only inside one `mtxExchange` plan; never `mtxSettle` and then an AMM transaction for the same incoming order (IOC closes at its single pull, FOK cannot span two calls); cost if wrong: a CoW counterpart that could have improved a listed-market taker is used one tick later; who: owner (this rule, 2026-10-08; research note §8.1) plus the controller's merge rule. **CoW / ring clearing price** — options: per-leg floors chosen freely or one uniform price; choice: the AMM marginal price when a pool exists, else the midpoint of the two limits, applied by the planner through the floors, never below a signed limit, the contract unchanged (CTR-DEX-21); who: owner 2026-10-29 (research note §8.2). **What the round builds in the node** — options: the whole `OrderRouter` or the minimum the contracts need; choice: the minimum — `min_fill`, the `min_fill` depth bucket, the ABI and call-table rows (16 → 19, only a listed DEX) and KAT pins of `mtxHybrid`, `mtxHybridVia`, `mtxExchangeBatch`, and this rewrite in docs; the planner, quoter, routes, jobs and `GET /v1/dex/exchanges/{ref}` wait for step 6 as ordered; cost if wrong: none, the contracts are usable by tests and the reference executor without the planner; who: TODO order (owner 2026-10-29) plus the controller. Commits: node T11, T12, T12 fix, docs T16.
Change (2026-11-03, owner; status: documented, the planner itself still SPECIFIED): **renamed TradeEngine → `OrderRouter`.** The node's planner that executes an order across the book, outside AMM liquidity and hybrid is named `OrderRouter`, always written in full, never "the router" (the Soroban relay-fee router and `RelayFeeRouter` are other things). Why: it routes one order to the best liquidity — the book (mode 1), AMMs (modes 2 and 4) or both in one hybrid call (mode 3); the matching engine (`node/dex-venue.md` §2 "Matching") keeps its name, is a separate part that is built, and the `OrderRouter` calls it for the book. What changes: the current docs (`node/dex-venue.md` §4 heading, contents and text, `contracts/dex.md`, `contracts/settlement.md`, `README.md`, this register) and the unbuilt config keys `trade_engine.enabled` / `.tick` / `.executor`, now `order_router.*`; the new anchor `order-router` sits beside the old anchor ids `trade-engine`, `4-tradeengine` and `NODE-DEX-17`, which still resolve. What keeps the old word: `docs/history/`, `docs/research/`, `docs/superpowers/plans/` and `docs/superpowers/specs/` (dated records), `TODO.md` and `COMPLETED.md`. No code or code comment names it (the planner is not built). Cost if wrong: none, a name only.


### NODE-DEX-18 — The node keeps no surplus: income is the relayer share of the signed fee
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: node/dex-venue.md#NODE-DEX-18 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner: the surplus is the signer's and the node's income is only the relayer share. The contract pays all output that reaches the DEX to the signers; what it cannot see is output routed elsewhere, so the node never sets a swap recipient outside the DEX and publishes quote and result per plan (`/v1/dex/exchanges/{ref}`).
**Cost if wrong.** A node that keeps part of the route output turns its quote into a hidden fee on top of the signed one.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §2 S4, S6, §3 DS-7.

DEX with the liquidity mark read as a retry with more gas.

### NODE-MESH-20 — Node is a capability matrix, not modes
- old: UD:§21.4 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-31 · normative: node/README.md#NODE-MESH-20 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Capabilities combine freely; fixed modes would need a second implementation. The earlier "Mode 1 / mode 2" split suggested a global enum, while there are three independent axes (ingest, pool, submit) and submit varies per `(chain, contract)`: a node may submit on one chain and only forward for another. The gateway shape is the old "mode 1". The research shapes "private pool" and "private relayer" (a private-mempool pair) showed that the mesh needs a pull mode next to gossip, with an explicit peer allowlist instead of discovery; the bus pull with pinned peers is that mode (the research table had called the mesh module "ingest + pool" and assumed gossip). Two queues shared the name "pool": the mesh-facing intent queue and the submit job queue, which exists even when nothing is pooled; the research note named "relay-pool" described the second. The store is now the mesh-facing queue.
**Source.** [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 1394.

## 12. Node — Gossip

### NODE-GSP-01 — Gossip required alongside the pull bus
- old: R112, UD:§6 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-01 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The pull bus covers admitted partners; gossip reaches the open network. Both are needed. The open network uses libp2p gossipsub v1.1 instead of a home-grown protocol: it is the stack the ERC-4337 shared mempool mandates (`eth-infinitism/bundler-spec/p2p-specs/p2p-interface.md`), and its peer scoring is the network-layer anti-spam primitive; intents are validated before they are forwarded, so spam costs real money.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 73; [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 224.

### NODE-GSP-02 — Selectable carriers; admitted peers PQ only
- old: R113 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-02 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** QUIC is the default; TCP covers networks that block UDP. Admitted peers carry private data, so PQ only.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 74.

### NODE-GSP-03 — PQ key exchange via aws-lc-rs, classical identity
- old: R114 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Harvest-now-decrypt-later threatens key exchange today; identity forgery needs a live quantum attacker. One crypto library keeps the build small.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 75.

### NODE-GSP-04 — Wire names and topics use scaas and chain_key
- old: R115 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Product-neutral names and chain keys make topics unambiguous across networks.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 76.

### NODE-GSP-05 — One Ed25519 node key for all identities
- old: R116 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One key and separate signing contexts make rotation one action and keep signatures non-interchangeable.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 77.

### NODE-GSP-06 — Gossip wire is bus JSON, content message-id
- old: R117 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-06 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Reusing the bus JSON keeps one codec; a content-addressed message id makes duplicates collapse.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 78.

### NODE-GSP-07 — Gossip validation pipeline and Reject rule
- old: R118, UD:§22.3 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Rejects cost the sender score; only faults decidable from the bytes may reject, so honest peers are never punished. Checking the meta nonce with `eth_call` at receipt is exact but does not run at gossip speed: a node receiving 500 intents a second would make 500 RPC calls a second just to filter garbage. The freshness check is therefore one batched read, off the event loop and failing open for forwarding.
**Cost if wrong.** Over-rejecting eclipses a node by itself.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 79; [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 1767.

### NODE-GSP-08 — Peer scoring and limits
- old: R119 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-08 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Fixed, published scoring numbers make peer behaviour predictable and testable.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 80.

### NODE-GSP-09 — Own Kademlia DHT with dial filter
- old: R120 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An own DHT namespace and dial filter stop the node from being used to scan private networks.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-mesh-gossip-amendment.md) line 81.

- old: R121 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: node/gossip.md#NODE-GSP-10 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Exclusivity reduces duplicate submissions; automatic trust requires a chain-credited track record.
