## 16. Contracts — General

### CTR-GEN-01 — Separate blockchain CI; forge libs pinned by tag
- old: R52 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/README.md#CTR-GEN-01 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Contracts break in ways the node tests do not see; pinning the forge libraries by tag makes a CI run reproducible because `lib/` is not committed.
**Cost if wrong.** An unpinned dependency changes bytecode between two runs and a deployed address no longer matches its audited source.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md:525`
Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — **forge libraries pinned by commit and source checksum, one place for CI and local builds** (the second code review, on-chain part (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-sol`; triage W-A…W-S in `pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, row W-N; report `V2-claude-ua-account-wallet.md` V2-6). Before: CI installed OpenZeppelin `fda6b85f` and forge-std tag `v1.16.2` from env variables, while local builds (every SCaaS testnet deployment) used whatever `lib/` held — an untracked symlink, the README said "v5.2+", this entry's normative text "v5.2.0" — and the local forge-std was master `88c8a288` (2026-08-28), not `v1.16.2`. Now `scripts/evm_libs.sh` holds each pin (repository, commit, source directory, sha256 over the `sha256sum` lines of its `*.sol` files sorted by path): `install` runs `forge install --no-git` at the commits (both CI jobs), `check` compares any `lib/` (a checkout, a symlink, a CI install) with the pins (CI after the install; locally before a build that is deployed). OpenZeppelin stays `fda6b85f` (no bytecode changes); CI's forge-std moves from `v1.16.2` to `88c8a288`, the tree every local test ran with (tests and scripts only). Why not a git submodule: the repo installs `lib/` without submodule bookkeeping (CI), the main checkout's `lib/openzeppelin-contracts` is a symlink a submodule would collide with, and a submodule pins a commit but checks no local tree; the checksum covers a symlinked or copied checkout too. Vendoring the sources (allowed: source, not binaries) gives the same guarantee for ~ 400 files in the tree; not needed. Verified: a fresh `install` into an empty tree and the local `lib/` give the pinned digests. Same row: `IUARegistry` declares `chainKeyHash()` (the spec's interface had it; `UARegistry` exposes it as a public immutable). Status: **done** (`a94c9ffd`).
Change (2026-11-03, owner): **CI tests every on-chain family, one job each, `contract-<family>`** — `contract-evm` (was `contracts`), `contract-soroban`, `contract-solana`, `contract-near` (was `near`), `contract-algorand` (was `algorand`), `contract-aptos`, `contract-sui`, `contract-cosmos`, `contract-ton`. Each runs `smartcontracts/scripts/test.sh <family>` (unit and in-process tests; localnet e2e stays local; `contract-algorand` runs test.sh's steps without its localnet pytest), with the toolchain versions used locally, installed from the official release artifacts by exact version and checked against their sha256. `contract-evm` runs the whole forge suite at each of the four PQZ sets (`script/pqz/at-set.sh <set> test`, a matrix), because forge at the default set is not enough for PQZ; `--isolate`, the size gate and the `scaas-testnet` build run once. A group runs whatever the paths through a pull-request label or a manual run: `ci-full-contracts`, `ci-full-node`, `ci-full-clients`, `ci-full-pqz`, `ci-full` (`.github/ci_changes.py`). Why: soroban, solana, aptos, sui, cosmos and ton had no CI job, and PQZ ran in CI at one set only. Cost if wrong: CI minutes. Status: **done**.

### CTR-GEN-02 — Value-holding programs immutable from deploy
- old: CR-R3-11, UD:§20.2, owner:2026-10-07:immutable · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/README.md#CTR-GEN-02 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Users can verify once what a program does and rely on it forever; an upgrade key is an admin key over every balance. Rejected alternatives: UUPS/ERC-1822 proxies "for all contracts", `ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable` + an admin `Pausable` on every function, and "delegate to share code, support many versions": versions are new implementations behind immutable clones, and a registry must never be upgradeable.
**Cost if wrong.** A bug is permanent for that deployment; the remedy is a new deployment plus voluntary migration, so audits and the deploy gate must precede real funds.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md:714`, `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:1140`, `history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md:40`. Owner wording for the Aptos, Sui and Solana programs: "Bất biến ngay khi deploy" (immutable as soon as deployed).

### CTR-GEN-03 — Contracts in their own tree per family
- old: UD:§1:smartcontracts-tree · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/README.md#CTR-GEN-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Each family has its own toolchain; one tree per family keeps builds and audits separable.
**Cost if wrong.** Mixed trees force every family build to know every other toolchain.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:46`

### CTR-GEN-04 — Issuer choices are not protocol decisions
- old: UD:§20.5 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/README.md#CTR-GEN-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** SCaaS ships a protocol, not a token catalogue; names, symbols, rates and roles belong to the issuer who answers for them.
**Cost if wrong.** If SCaaS made issuer choices it would carry issuer liability and become a gatekeeper.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:1272`

### CTR-GEN-05 — salt = chain_uid in every SCaaS EIP-712 domain and chain-bound digest
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/README.md#CTR-GEN-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Chain ids collide (the private chain's earlier id was a public testnet's), so every domain carries the genesis hash as `salt` through one helper, with one source per contract (an implementation immutable for clones, a constructor argument elsewhere) checked against the RPC by the deploy gate and the node. The owner ruled that a fork of a chain we run is a new chain (new chain id and `chain_key`); a PoA chain re-created from the same genesis is refused by a unique `extraData` nonce.
**Cost if wrong.** A signature for one chain verifies on another that shares its chain id; a second salt source lets a clone declare another chain.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 (fixed constraints), §3 MG-4, §10 OQ3, §12 (H9, M4).
Change (2026-11-07, chain-neutral releases, CTR-TOK-29): the `chain_uid` of a factory-made contract (every token kind, `SCaaSDex`, a generic class such as `PqChat`) is no longer an immutable of its implementation: the factory appends it in the instance's `ChainEnv` to the clone's code, read on every use with no cache; the implementation reads an all-zero env and signs nothing (`ChainUidZero`). `OpenFactory`'s own is set once by `configureChain`. Contracts outside the factory keep their constructor immutable. Status: BUILT (T71 `b61ac38d`, T72 `612981b9`).

### CTR-GEN-06 — CREATE2 deployer with a fixed salt for every contract
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/README.md#CTR-GEN-06 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner moved every deployment (implementations, factories, registries, DEX) to a deterministic CREATE2 deployer: addresses follow from init code, so contracts with a `chain_uid` constructor argument (and their clones and accounts) differ per chain, and others share one address everywhere; safety rests on the salted digests, not on addresses.
**Cost if wrong.** CREATE addresses depend on deployer nonces and drift between chains and redeploys.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A11, §3 MG-4.

### CTR-GOV-01 — GovernanceBase on every token kind and the DEX
- old: governance:D1 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-01 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** One layer, `GovernanceBase` (owner, features, roles, lock, delay), in its own ERC-7201 namespace, inheritable by any contract, on every token kind and on `SCaaSDex`. `scaas.token` splits: `scaas.token` keeps identity (`creator`, `version`, `kind`, `decimals`, `initialized`, `name`, `symbol`), `scaas.governance` takes `features`, `lockedFeatures`, `owner`, `pendingOwner`, the holders and the delay state. `AdminLib` becomes `GovernanceLib`; `IGovernance` replaces `ITokenAdmin` with every name kept. On the DEX `admin` becomes `owner`, the market setters (`setMarket`, `setExchangeTarget`, `setListedOnly`) run under bit `LISTING` and `setFeeSplit` under bit `FEE_ROUTING`. The namespace roots join the layout pins. It is not in `MetaTxBase` or `UAMetaTxBase`, which are authentication and relay.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance`: `GovernanceBase`, `GovernanceLib` (external, DELEGATECALL), `GovernanceUse`, `IGovernance` and the namespace `scaas.governance` on the six token kinds and `SCaaSDex`, the DEX's `admin` now `owner` with bits 11 `LISTING` and 12 `FEE_ROUTING`, the guard on its four powers and `supportsInterface` (plan T3 `7825361b`, on the D1 prototype); roots pinned in `test/v2/layout/namespaces.json`. `AdminLib`, `ITokenAdmin` and the prototype's `requireRole` are kept in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/governance/`. Summary and picture: [contracts/README.md](contracts/README.md#governance); the design: `superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-governance.md`.
**Why.** Today the same five words mean different things at each address: the DEX has an `admin` with no transfer and no renounce, a token has an `owner`. One base reads the same way at every address, and a third-party application can inherit it.
**Cost if wrong.** One new env version per domain, DEX runtime grows, clients rename `admin` to `owner` on the DEX. Every token created after it has another address than a prediction made before it, a non-event while every chain is test-only.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §1, §2, §6.
**Change (owner 2026-11-04, governance:D1, identity by UA).** Every governance identity is a UA id (`bytes32`), the same on every family: `owner`, `pendingOwner`, every holder in `roles` / `grants` / `epoch` / `pending`, every grantor in a `Grant`, every proposer in a `PendingGrant`, and every event and view that names one. Old rule: those were EVM `address`es. A native account is its native id (on EVM `bytes32(uint256(uint160(addr)))`); a derived UA is its registered id. The governed contract maps its caller with `_govSubject()`: the native id of `msg.sender`, or, when `msg.sender` is the chain's `GOV_ROUTER` immutable, the UA the router authenticated for that call (0 outside a live call: refused). No signature is verified in the governed contract and the relay rule (G19) stands. Payout destinations (`rescueTo`, the DEX `treasury`) stay native addresses. `UA_POOL`, `SHIELD_POOL` and 0 stay refused as owner and holder. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` by plan task T10b (`ac29de05`; `_govSubject()`, `GOV_ROUTER` from `Env.govRouter`, test `GovIdentity.t.sol`). Why: one identity on every chain; a PQ or `msig` issuer holds a power under its own id, with no per-issuer contract. Cost if wrong: the governed contracts' storage, ABI and events were widened for nothing; about 0.2–0.5 KB per contract (estimate). Source: owner 2026-11-04 (use UA, one identity on every chain; the three points of `superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-governance-ua-identity.md` §7 accepted).

Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3r; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3r`, UNAUDITED): `owner` becomes `admin` in every name of the layer (views, entries, events, errors, the storage fields in the same slots, the config field), which reverses the 2026-11-02 rename of the DEX's `admin` to `owner` for every contract. Source: owner 2026-11-10; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md` §4; CTR-GOV-23.

### CTR-GOV-02 — The Grant record in the contract, subject to measuring
- old: governance:D2 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-02 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A limit on a power lives in the contract that owns the power, in `GovernanceBase`: `use(bit, holder, scalar) → scope`, `setGrant`, `grantOf`. Two levels: the owner grants, a holder with a `delegable` grant may grant a narrower leaf, a leaf cannot delegate. An edit carries `spent` and never refreshes a budget. `renounceOwnership` reverts while a bit that is not locked has holders. **Subject to measuring** the bytes first (owner): the default until the measurement is read is the rule as stated.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance`, the whole record on every kind and the DEX: `setGrant` refusals (plan T5 `7d0c6a86`), leaves, revoke, `barred`, `Counts` and the renounce rule on live roots (T6 `ead16677`), `cancelGrant` and the two calls (T7 `c2525e28`). Measured before the build: as designed it did not fit `WrappedPqzToken` (65,520 B); owner 2026-11-02: reduce the size rather than cut the record; owner 2026-11-03: the whole record is built and size is decided later (CTR-GOV-19). `WrappedPqzToken` is 72,160 B now, the one contract above 65,536 B (`size-baseline.json` `_above64KiB`).
**Why.** The owner's examples (a loan approval in a band, a subtree, a group) and the mint allowance need a limit bound to the number the contract acts on; a separate holder clone cannot carry them, and a holder that reports its own limit is believed for nothing.
**Cost if wrong.** Bytes on every kind, and two disclosure shapes on one chain if one kind goes flat-only. CTR-TOK-22's "revoke every role, then renounce" turns from advice into a revert for unlocked bits.
**Change (owner 2026-11-03).** `renounceOwnership` reverts while a bit that is not locked has a live root: a dead leaf does not count. Reviews of the spec, 2026-11-03.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §1.3, §6, §7; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A3, A10, A19.

### CTR-GOV-03 — A plain transfer stays +0: one regulated implementation per kind, never per feature
- old: governance:D3 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-03 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A plain transfer's gas does not rise, in the sense of CTR-GOV-11: no new read. A regulated instance is known on the hot path by its implementation, not by a storage read: one regulated implementation per kind, never one per feature. Ids 8 `NORMAL_REGULATED` and 9 `WRAPPED_REGULATED` are real enum members, off until built with flags 5–8 ([CTR-GOV-16](#ctr-gov-16--regulated-kinds-are-real-enum-members-before-the-factory-freezes)). The confidential kinds will have regulated versions too (owner 2026-11-02): "one regulated implementation per kind" covers them, under [CTR-GOV-17](#ctr-gov-17--regulated-confidential-kinds-the-rules).
**Status.** The plain half BUILT on branch `governance`: no kind carries a hook, `NORMAL` and `WRAPPED` refuse flags 5–9 with `FeatureNotBuilt`, the four confidential kinds with `FeatureInvalidForKind` (plan T3 `7825361b`, GD-19), "+0" pinned on every kind (CTR-GOV-11). The regulated implementations are SPECIFIED, not built. CTR-AS-17's placement ("on the ordinary kinds") follows it: its Change (governance spec §12.1) is applied (owner 2026-11-04). The refusal of flags 5–9 at creation is the current built state, not a permanent rule.
**Why.** `_update` and `_uaMove` read no governance slot today; a `features` read there would charge every holder of every plain token for a control their token does not have. Two implementations meet the rule by construction.
**Cost if wrong.** More catalogue rows and more artifacts in the size gate and the audit. The alternatives were immutable-args clones (every clone address formula changes, factory bytecode before the freeze) or accepting the read (the rule breaks on the entry that matters most).
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §2.5, §6; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A17; owner statement 2026-11-02 on the confidential kinds.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the regulated half. Each of the kinds 8–13 is one regulated implementation, its base kind's source with the hooks overridden ([CTR-AS-17](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-17), asset-suite §2.1): T27 `23a86992`, T28 `3a0c99fb` (8, 9), T30 `da66a98b` (10, 11), T31 `65caf46f` (12, 13), the releases T33 `63aa8696`. The plain kinds 0–5 refuse 5–10, 21 and 22 with `FeatureInvalidForKind` (regulated-kinds spec Q3, T25 `23eb0f37`; `FeatureNotBuilt` stays declared), and "+0" is pinned in slots and gas on every plain row (T26 `f55f43c0`, `test/governance/PlusZero.t.sol`, `test/vectors/plus_zero_gas.json`).

### CTR-GOV-04 — Two-call grantDelay and holderCount
- old: governance:D4 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `grantDelay` is set at creation (`TokenConfig`, `DexConfig`), immutable, 0 allowed. The **owner calls `grantRole` twice**: propose, then confirm in `[eta, eta + grantDelay]`; nobody else executes, the confirmer must be the proposer, outside the window the pending is dead, so an owner of 0 and a new owner cannot confirm. Views `pendingGrant(bit, account)`, `lastProposedAt()`, `holderCount(bit)`; `holderCount` counts INIT grants once and never a pending. `acceptOwnership` is **not** delayed. Wizard default 2 days, dev chains 0.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` with its Change (plan T7 `c2525e28`): two calls within `[eta, eta + grantDelay]`, confirmer = proposer, `termsHash` on `setGrant`, `cancelGrant`, the ownership generation, `grantDelay` in `TokenConfig` and `DexConfig`, bound 30 days (`GrantDelayTooLong`), views `pendingGrant`, `lastProposedAt`, `holderCount`; test `GovDelay.t.sol`. No wizard exists in this repository: "wizard default 2 days" binds a later wizard (GD-9).
**Why.** An executable pending grant survives a renounce or a transfer and makes "owner 0 means nothing above can change" false; a window and an owner-only confirm remove both. A delay on `acceptOwnership` gives a stalemate with a shared key, not recovery.
**Cost if wrong.** `grantRole` tests double; a config field through init on every kind.
**Change (owner 2026-11-02).** `setGrant` that creates a holder or widens any term takes the same two calls, and the pending binds a `termsHash` the confirm must match; a pure narrowing runs at once. `grantDelay = 0` means one call. `grantDelay ≤ 30 days`. Attack B-01, B-27.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §3 A1, A2, A20, §6; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A1, A2, A6.

### CTR-GOV-05 — A wrapped kind refuses a SCaaS leg with FORCE or MODERATE
- old: governance:D5 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-05 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `_addLeg` of every wrapped kind refuses a leg that is a SCaaS token (`factory.isToken`) whose `features()` carries bit 6 `FORCE` or bit 21 `MODERATE`; features only lose bits, so a check at init holds. The wizard refuses a `MODERATE` token as a tender, vesting or offer deposit asset. Outside legs cannot be checked: a wrapped unit's value is as good as each leg's issuer, and the disclosure says so.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` with its Change (plan T8 `233b874b`): `_addLeg` of every wrapped kind reads `isRegisteredToken` and refuses a leg with bit 6 or 21 (`UnderlyingInvalid`); test `GovLeg.t.sol`. The wizard rule binds a later wizard.
**Why.** A leg's issuer who can move the wrapper's balance empties a wrapper that shows no power of its own. Under wrapped PQZ or Zether that is value gone behind intact ciphertexts, with no record and no proof.
**Cost if wrong.** A few bytes in `WrappedLib`, one read per leg at init; a legitimate regulated leg cannot be wrapped.
**Change (owner 2026-11-02).** The check reads `isRegisteredToken`, not `isToken`. An unregistered leg is an outside leg, disclosed as one. Attack B-15.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §3 A4, §6; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A4, A5.
Change (2026-11-11, controller call under the owner's leave of 2026-11-10, quoted in [CTR-GOV-24](#ctr-gov-24--kyc-bit-28-allowlist-and-denylist-lists-held-in-the-token-enabled-at-once)'s Source; group 3s, after Fable's review; status: BUILT (ua-mtx-3s)): the reason "features only lose bits, so a check at init holds" no longer holds for every bit (8, 9 and 28 may be added later); it still holds for 6 `FORCE` and 21 `MODERATE`, which are never enabled after creation, so the check at `_addLeg` stands. A leg's 5, 7, 8, 9 and 28 are disclosed from its live `features()` and `lockedFeatures()`.

### CTR-GOV-06 — Rescue to an immutable rescueTo
- old: governance:D6 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-06 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Bit 17 `RESCUABLE`, a capability: `rescue(asset)` by anyone, to `rescueTo`, immutable, set at creation, on the kinds that fit. A foreign asset: every leg's balance is unchanged across the call. A leg asset: that leg's `balanceOf ≥ reserve` after. On the DEX only if CTR-DEX-20 does not already pay strays out, else on `DexPuller` alone. `WrappedPqzToken` last.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` (plan T10 `dc9bfde0`): `RESCUABLE` and `rescueTo` on the six token kinds (`IRescuable`, `nonReentrant`, the per-asset check), `DexPuller.rescue(token)`; test `GovRescue.t.sol`. CTR-DEX-20 was read at `main` on 2026-11-02: the sweep rule stands, so the DEX takes no `rescue` entry and `DexPuller` is the case left. Review fixes (2026-11-04, T19): a leg's rescue also requires every other leg's balance unchanged (`RescueTouchedLeg`: two legs over one ledger), and `SCaaSDex.initialize` refuses a pool, the DEX or the puller as `rescueTo` (`RescueConfigInvalid`); spec §6.2.
**Why.** A stray on a wrapper is stuck forever today; a destination the admin can rewrite is a power with a holder again.
**Cost if wrong.** Bytes on each kind that takes it; a kind without it keeps strays stuck, as today.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §3 A15, A16, §6; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A15, A16.

### CTR-GOV-07 — set_admin and renounce_admin outside the EVM
- old: governance:D7 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `set_admin` (two-step) and `renounce_admin` on the Soroban token and DEX before their freeze. NEAR takes the same two entries in its UA round. Algorand takes the same two entries in its UA round. Sui's `AdminCap` gets `store` or a two-step transfer before `make_immutable`.
**Status.** Decided as recommended, not built: Part D7 of the governance plan, on its own branch after `ua8-soroban` merges; the other families in their own rounds. SPECIFIED (governance spec §6.3).
**Why.** Without it every Soroban token is write-once forever, and a fixed supply there is "initial mint, then renounce", which needs the entry.
**Cost if wrong.** Small per family; a family frozen first cannot add it later without a new deployment.
**Change (owner 2026-11-02).** TON, Solana, Cosmos and Aptos take the same entries in their rounds. Semantics, every family: a two-step with acceptance; a renounce clears the pending; the admin is an option; a renounce is one-way. Sui takes the two-step and a burn, not `store`. Attack B-23, B-24.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §4, §6.

### CTR-GOV-08 — MODERATE: later, with flags 5-8
- old: governance:D8 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Bit 21 `MODERATE` (bit 9 until CTR-GOV-18): a holder moves units out of an account with no record. One direct entry `moderatedTransfer(bytes32 from, bytes32 to, uint256 amount, bytes32 ref)` on `_uaMove`, no `mtx` or `ua` twin; it refuses 0, `pad(UA_POOL)`, `pad(SHIELD_POOL)`, `pad(this)`, an unregistered or non-SIGNING derived `to`, and a native `from` with code; it passes `FREEZE` and `ALLOWLIST`; its scope is any or a registry. Bit 9 joins the CTR-AS-02 disclosure and `termsHash`; CTR-TOK-10, the contracts README §3 and architecture.md are amended.
**Status.** Decided as recommended, later: built with the regulated implementations. Only the bit number is taken (21, `GovernanceBits.MODERATE`), 0 B; SPECIFIED.
**Why.** A moderator without the refusals reaches tender deposits, vesting clones, wrapper reserves and pools; refusing a `from` with code leaves Safe-held balances out of reach, the lesser hole.
**Cost if wrong.** Three normative sentences rewritten; bytes on the plain kinds later.
**Change (owner 2026-11-03).** `forceTransfer` moves on an unhooked body with its own refusals of both pools and `this`: a hook would stop it on the frozen account it exists for. `moderatedTransfer` stays on the hooked path: "passes `FREEZE` and `ALLOWLIST`" above means it is subject to them, so a frozen `from` is refused, a paused token refuses it and the receiver check applies (`permission-model.md` F11). A review read the word as a bypass and the controller relayed that; corrected the same day.
**Change (owner 2026-11-05).** The entry moves to bit 22. Old: bit 21 `MODERATE` carries `moderatedTransfer`, a contract-only holder moving units with no record. New: the transfer power, its entry and its refusals move unchanged to bit 22 `OPERATOR_TRANSFER` as `operatorTransfer` ([CTR-GOV-20](#ctr-gov-20--operator_transfer-bit-22-any-holder-the-regulated-kinds)), any holder; bit 21 keeps its name and its contract-only rule (CTR-AS-03, RK-1) and is re-scoped by the owner to "other hierarchical moderation", meaning TBD, no body built. Why: the loyalty / point-of-sale case needs the transfer power for any holder within a daily cap, which is not what a moderation bit means. Cost if wrong: bit 21's meaning stays open until the owner states it. Status: SPECIFIED (`superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-regulated-kinds.md` §3.4).
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §3, §6; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A4.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; owner 2026-11-05; status: the bit BUILT, its body SPECIFIED): bit 21 `MODERATE` is in the masks of the kinds 8–13 and contract-only (an `msig` UA counts, [CTR-AS-20](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-20); T24 `295e073b`, T25 `23eb0f37`); the owner re-scoped it to "other hierarchical moderation", meaning to be stated, so no body is built. The transfer power this entry drafted is bit 22 `OPERATOR_TRANSFER`, any holder ([CTR-GOV-20](#ctr-gov-20--operator_transfer-bit-22-any-holder-the-regulated-kinds), BUILT T32 `e46cdb71`).

### CTR-GOV-09 — Delayed relaxing and RECORD: later, with the asset suite
- old: governance:D9 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A mask `_delayedRelaxBits()`: `revokeRole` and `disableFeature` on `FREEZE`, `FORCE`, `PAUSE` take `grantDelay`. Bit 10 `RECORD` is the compliance right, distinct from `FORCE`; one holder is refused both.
**Status.** Decided as recommended, later: built with the asset suite and the regulated implementations; SPECIFIED. `_delayedRelaxBits()` is not in the code; bit 10 `RECORD` is a number only, and `init` refuses `roles.compliance ≠ 0` with `RoleWithoutFeature(10)` (plan T3). The Change of 2026-11-03 on expired roots is BUILT for the renounce rule (`Counts.roots`, plan T6 `ead16677`). It rewrites CTR-AS-03's "losing a role relaxes at once". The mask costs 0 B until the asset suite sets it.
**Why.** Revoking the last issuer ends every freeze at once, so one owner key releases what a threshold guards; and one holder must not both write an order and execute it.
**Cost if wrong.** A delay on a relaxation also delays a correct release.
**Change (owner 2026-11-02).** The mask covers `renounceRole`, a `setGrant` to a past `validUntil`, and a parent's revoke killing a leaf. Attack B-28.
**Change (owner 2026-11-03).** The relaxing rule counts live roots, not listed holders. An edit that makes a protected power end before `now + grantDelay` takes the delay, not only an expiry already past.
**Change (owner 2026-11-03).** an expired root counts as live until it is revoked, for the relaxing rule and for the renounce rule of CTR-GOV-02. `Counts.roots` is a stored number, and the chain sees an expiry only by a walk.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §3 A9, escalation F6, §6; `research/governance/permission-model-attack.md` A9.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `_delayedRelaxBits()` is 5, 6, 7 on the kinds 8–13 (0 elsewhere), with the relaxation state machine of [CTR-AS-21](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-21) / [CTR-AS-22](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-22) (T24 `295e073b`, `test/governance/GovRelax.t.sol`); bit 10 `RECORD` has its body (T28 `3a0c99fb`, `test/as/Record.t.sol`); the emergency runbook of the regulated-kinds spec §3.6 is in the operator note ([ops.md](node/ops.md#operator-notes)).
Change (2026-11-11, Fable review D P2-2 and A-4; controller call under the owner's leave; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-fix-contracts`, UNAUDITED): **every path that relaxes** now includes the narrowing words that empty a role: on a bit of `_delayedRelaxBits()` with a `grantDelay`, a `setGrant` (admin or grantor path) that lowers the holder's `max` or sets a new or lower `maxUses` is a cut, proposed and confirmed like a `validUntil` cut (`GovernanceLib._cuts`; a `WHOLE` holder has neither bound, a non-holder nothing to lose). Why: `setGrant(5, issuer, {maxUses: 1})` or `setGrant(6, issuer, {max: 0})` applied at once as a "narrowing" and emptied the role, while `revokeRole` of the same holder waited `grantDelay`. Scope as the controller stated it: `max` and `maxUses`; `total` and `perWindow` (scalar bit 6) are not cuts in this change. Cost if wrong: the owner's instant stop of a compromised issuer by `setGrant` is gone; its stop is `revokeRole` after `grantDelay`, as the runbook says. Test: `test_relaxSetGrantMaxUsesAndMaxAreCuts`.

### CTR-GOV-10 — Bit bands: 0-127 one meaning, 128-255 per application, none refused
- old: governance:bands · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-10 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** (The bands below are amended by the Change of 2026-11-04: 0–127 SCaaS's, 128–255 per application, none refused.) Bits 0–63 are SCaaS's: one global table, each bit allocated once, never renumbered, the same meaning on every SCaaS contract, and a contract without the power leaves the bit off. Bits 64–127 are per application contract, declared with a label. Bits 128 and above are refused today; the word stays `uint256` so the ABI does not move when they open. The owner's three examples must run on the model: a loan approval bounded on a named argument of the application's function, adding or removing members only in one's own subtree, circulation only within a group.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` with its Changes: `GovernanceBits` holds bits 0–21 as governance spec §1.2 allocates them, `bitLabel(bit)` names an application's bits, the bands of 2026-11-04 (`33fc080d`), and `smartcontracts/vectors/governance/governance_bits.json` carries every bit's name, type and sentences, bit 5 two (plan T14 `7887a712`), read by `clientkeys` and every `ua-*`. The owner's three examples run on the model (`GovExamples.t.sol`).
**Why.** A wallet names a bit without reading the contract, and the top band gives exhaustion an answer other than renumbering.
**Cost if wrong.** A second meaning for a bit on one contract would break every wallet's reading of that bit.
**Change (owner 2026-11-03).** bit 5 has one sentence per class of kind. Public kinds: the account in any role, the envelope `from` of a meta-tx op included. Confidential kinds: the account as a proof's sender.
**Change (owner 2026-11-04, governance:bands).** The bands move and none is refused. Old rule: bits 0–63 SCaaS's, 64–127 per application, 128 and above refused (`FeatureReserved`). New rule: bits 0–127 belong to SCaaS, one global table with the same meaning on every SCaaS contract; bits 128–255 belong to the customer, per application, labelled by `bitLabel`, the contract's own choice; no band is refused, and a contract's `_validBits()` is the only check, so a kind refuses a bit it does not implement with `FeatureInvalidForKind` in either band. Code, branch `governance`: `GovernanceLib.init` and `_check` lose the two refusals (`features >> 128`, `bit >= 128`); `FeatureReserved` has no reachable case left and its declaration stays in `IGovernance`; `GovernanceBits`, `GovernanceBase.bitLabel` and `IGovernance` NatSpec name the new bands. Tests: the application mocks (`BranchApp`, `DelayApp`, `LoanBook`, `FamilyTree`, `GroupLedger`) move from bits 64 and 65 to 128 and 129; `test_refusals` reads `NoSuchRole(128)` on a token where it read `FeatureReserved(128)`; new `test_bitsAbove127AreApplicationBits` (bits 128 and 255 on an application, bit 200 refused by a token's own mask) and `test_bits64To127AreScaasBits`. The word stays `uint256`, so no ABI moves.
**Source.** `research/governance/permission-model.md` §1.4, opening decisions A, B, C.
Change (2026-11-07, group 3h, CTR-GOV-22): bit 24 `PQZ_PROOF` is allocated: a power of the PQZ kinds 4, 5, 12, 13, any holder, in `ISSUER_BITS`; `governance_bits.json` row 24 with its sentence. Status: BUILT (T61 `6fb7a845`, `d4ae676d`).
Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3s, [CTR-GOV-24](#ctr-gov-24--kyc-bit-28-allowlist-and-denylist-lists-held-in-the-token-enabled-at-once); status: BUILT (ua-mtx-3s)): bit 28 `KYC` is allocated (a capability of the regulated kinds 8–13: the registry check); bits 8 and 9 become powers (the list holders); `governance_bits.json` rows 8, 9 and 28; bits 29–127 free.

### CTR-GOV-11 — "+0" on a plain transfer means no new read
- old: governance:plus0 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The "+0" of [CTR-GOV-03](#ctr-gov-03--a-plain-transfer-stays-0-one-regulated-implementation-per-kind-never-per-feature) means: a plain `transfer` and `mtxTransfer` add no storage read, on every kind, pinned by a test on every kind.
**Note on the other reading.** A gas figure exactly equal to the previous one was considered and rejected. It cannot be met: every added selector reshapes the dispatcher, so the figure moves though no read was added (measured 0 to +23, and +110 on `WrappedPqzToken` with D2, `research/governance/prototype/RESULTS.md`). "No new read" is the more reasonable rule: a read is what every holder of every plain token would pay for a control their token lacks, it holds across releases, and it does not forbid adding an entry. Gas figures stay in the pins, with old and new in the commit.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` (plan T1 `a678a770`): `PlusZero.t.sol` pins `transfer`, `mtxTransfer`, `transferToUA` and `uaExecuteTransfer` on every kind (GD-16); the selector audit `test/vectors/selector_audit.json` classifies every non-view entry of the governed contracts (plan T13 `d8f2e492`). The Change to CTR-AS-17 (governance spec §12.1, applied 2026-11-04) is worded to this rule.
**Why.** Read literally, CTR-GOV-01 already breaks CTR-GOV-03.
**Cost if wrong.** Small dispatcher drift stays allowed; the gas pins show it.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02; `research/governance/permission-model-v2-attack.md` §4.

### CTR-GOV-12 — Hybrid underlying: wrap and issuer mint on one token, the reserve can run out
- old: governance:hybrid · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-12 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A wrapped token may also be minted by its issuer, under a cap. **Redemption runs until the reserve is empty:** any unit redeems at the rate while the reserve lasts, first come, with no pro-rata share and no queue. When it is empty the units stay valid and redemption of the underlying stops; a holder's way out is then off chain. A `RATE_ADJUSTABLE` hybrid's rate may fall with no `addReserve`, which also leaves the reserve short: the issuer runs that rate, and depositors accept it (owner 2026-11-03); the disclosure states it. The owner's example: a government issues a CBDC on a public chain; a foreign user deposits USDC and receives e-VND at the rate, up to a cap; the user must understand and accept that others can drain the USDC reserve, in which case the user still holds e-VND and can change it at a bank.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` on every `WRAPPED*` kind (plan T9 `20620a1e`): `maxSupply` in `TokenConfig` (0 = no hybrid), `MINTABLE` on a hybrid, one cap on every path, `executeRate` without the supply comparison on a hybrid; test `GovHybrid.t.sol`. The disclosure sentences are bit 1's hybrid row of `governance_bits.json` (plan T14). A hybrid token claims no full backing.
**Why.** The redeemable reserve serves a holder who wants out; the unit itself stays money off chain.
**Cost if wrong.** A holder who reads the token as fully backed loses the exit. The risk must be shown by the token's disclosure, not left to a document.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02; `research/governance/permission-model-gaps.md` §3.8.

### CTR-GOV-13 — MODERATE only on public balances
- old: governance:moderate-public · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-13 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `MODERATE` moves public balances only, on every kind; it never moves a shielded balance. [CTR-GOV-08](#ctr-gov-08--moderate-later-with-flags-5-8) stands otherwise.
**Status.** Decided, not built: `MODERATE` has no body (CTR-GOV-08); SPECIFIED. It binds the regulated confidential kinds (CTR-GOV-17).
**Why.** A shielded balance cannot be moved without its owner's proof.
**Cost if wrong.** A regulator of a confidential kind has no moderator's reach over shielded value.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; status: BUILT for bit 22, UNAUDITED): `operatorTransfer` (bit 22, [CTR-GOV-20](#ctr-gov-20--operator_transfer-bit-22-any-holder-the-regulated-kinds)) moves public balances only, on every regulated kind, the confidential ones included (T32 `e46cdb71`; `test/as/OperatorTransfer.t.sol`, `confidential/ZetherOperator.t.sol`, `PqzOperator.t.sol`); bit 21 has no body (CTR-GOV-08's Change).

### CTR-GOV-14 — Bits 13 and 14 stay unallocated; a party fixed at creation holds no bit; no tender rescue
- old: governance:bits-13-14 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-14 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `DISQUALIFY` and `REVOKE_GRANT` are not contract-wide bits: those rights stay with the parties fixed at creation. Bits 13 and 14 are left unused and never reused. A party fixed at creation is not a holder of a bit, so a contract with only such parties does not take `GovernanceBase`. The tender keeps CTR-TND-08: no owner, pause, upgrade or sweep, no rescue.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` as far as it is code: bits 13 and 14 are absent from `GovernanceBits` and marked unused in `governance_bits.json` (plan T14); no contract whose parties are fixed at creation takes `GovernanceBase` (the tender, vesting, distribution and offer contracts are not built on EVM yet). It narrows v2's "every SCaaS contract that has rights".
**Why.** `DISQUALIFY` can send a bidder's deposit to `slashSink` and `REVOKE_GRANT` covers three different per-clone rights, so neither is reduce-only or one meaning.
**Cost if wrong.** A later contract wanting these as bits takes new numbers.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02; `research/governance/permission-model-gaps.md` §4.

### CTR-GOV-15 — No operator delay on a governance holder
- old: governance:operator-delay · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-15 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A holder's operator changes in two calls and with no delay: `proposeOperator(next)` by the operator, `acceptOperator()` signed by `next`; `proposeOperator(0)` cancels and the pending is readable. The disclosure says once: `grantDelay` delays an address, never who controls it.
**Status.** Overtaken by the Change of 2026-11-04 below: no holder contract and no operator exist. The note's proposed `operatorDelay` is dropped: the owner first kept it, then followed the attack's reading; the disclosure's sentence stays, for a contract holder (`governance_bits.json`, plan T14).
**Why.** It would not close what it claimed (attack B-22): a token cannot compare it with `grantDelay`, an owner holder moves control by `transferOwnership` at once, a contract holder rotates by its own rules, a quorum hands keys over off chain, and a compromised operator keeps its power through the delay. It would also slow an emergency rotation and need the salt, window and cancel of B-20 and B-21.
**Cost if wrong.** Nobody sees an honest change of operator in advance.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02; `research/governance/permission-model-gaps.md` §1.6; `research/governance/permission-model-v2-attack.md` B-20 to B-22.
**Change (owner 2026-11-04, governance:operator-delay, router).** The per-operator `GovernanceHolder` and its rotation (`proposeOperator`, `acceptOperator`, `generation`) are replaced by one `GovernanceRouter` per chain: the closed table of typed `mtx<Op>` / `ua<Op>` entries, fee mode `NONE`, verifies through `UARegistry.requireAuthorized`, writes the transient `(subject, target)`, calls the target, clears it. Changing who controls a power is the governed contract's own rule: the owner grants or revokes the new UA (two calls when widening), and ownership moves by `transferOwnership(bytes32)` and `acceptOwnership` signed by the new UA. No operator delay exists, as before. Status: decided; built on branch `governance` by plan task T11 (`GovernanceRouterBase`, `GovernanceRouter`: 19 ops, 38 typed entries, the generic path refused; deployed by CREATE2 by `DeployBase` and by `script/pqz/e2e.py` before the releases, every release's `Env.govRouter`; `e2e.py`'s is on its own registry, a second router the node lists too, T19); the `clientkeys` rows and `typed_ops.json` by T12 (`6d4f5b04`), the node rows (`gov_router`, `governance_routers`) by T15 (`efa7f54f`), the selector audit by T13 (`d8f2e492`: `mtxSelectors()` of the router empty). Why: with identity by UA (CTR-GOV-01 Change, same day) a holder clone per UA adds a deployment and a rotation that would move powers away from the UA they were granted to. Cost if wrong: an issuer that wanted to swap keys behind a fixed address now re-grants. Source: owner 2026-11-04, `superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-governance-ua-identity.md` §3.
**Change (owner 2026-11-04, router per registry).** One `GovernanceRouter` per chain and per UA registry. Old rule: one per chain. A router authenticates against its own registry (`UARegistry.requireAuthorized`), so a stack with its own registry has its own router: the PQZ e2e stack (`script/pqz/e2e.py`, its registry carrying `pqz-mlwe`) deploys one by CREATE2 with `DeployBase`'s salt, JSON `governance_router` in `deployments/scaas-testnet-pqz.json` (NET-EVM-13; was `7622-pqz.json`), and the node's `governance_routers` lists both on the SCaaS testnet. Why: reuse is not possible, the deploy JSON's registry lacks the `pqz-mlwe` kind and the ML-DSA verifiers; a router on another registry would refuse the PQZ stack's UAs. Cost if wrong: one more router address per such stack, listed by the operator. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` by plan task T19 (`73b3abbd`). Source: owner 2026-11-04.
Change (2026-11-06 to 2026-11-07, groups 3f, 3h and the factory's S3): the router's closed table gains `mtxPqzSetVerifier`, `mtxPqzCancelVerifier`, `mtxPqzRevokeVerifier` over `UAPqzSetVerifier` / `UAPqzCancelVerifier` / `UAPqzRevokeVerifier` (`target` a PQZ token, which reads the router's subject as `_govSubject()` and requires the owner; CTR-PQZ-28, T45 `2cce490d`), `mtxSetProofStore` over `UASetProofStore` (CTR-GOV-22, T61 `6fb7a845`), and the factory's three creations `mtxCreateToken`, `mtxCreateDex`, `mtxCreateInstance` (`target` the chain's `OpenFactory`, the creation's named parameters, `initHash = keccak256(initArgs or initCall)` signed; the factory reads `subject()` once at entry and refuses 0, `RouterSubjectZero`; CTR-TOK-29, T76 `e8ca069b`); all fee mode `NONE`, relayable at fee 0. The router's code and CREATE2 address move. No node row for the creations until relaying them is decided (anyone submits them). Status: BUILT.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R14; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED: `src/governance/`, `test/governance/GovRouter.t.sol`): the router's pairs merge to one `mtx<Op>(UAEnvelope e, …, UASig auth)` per operation, no `ua*` entry left. The spec counted 19 ops; the router today has **38** `mtx*` entries (9 in `GovernanceRouterBase`, 29 in `GovernanceRouter`; `git grep -c 'function mtx'`), the later rounds' operations included (tax, PQZ verifier, proof store, wrap limits, market, factory). G19 holds on the governed contracts.

Change (owner 2026-11-11, group 3t, [CTR-PQZ-36](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36); status: BUILT on `ua-mtx-3t`, UNAUDITED): the router's closed table gains `mtxSetVerifierFee(UAEnvelope e, address target, uint64 next, UASig auth)` over `UASetVerifierFee` (`target` a PQZ token, which reads the router's subject as `_govSubject()` and requires the admin), fee mode `NONE`, relayable at fee 0.

### CTR-GOV-16 — Regulated kinds are real enum members before the factory freezes
- old: governance:enum-ids · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-16 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The factory's kind enum gets real members before it freezes: placeholders 6 and 7 (a Solidity enum has no gaps), 8 `NORMAL_REGULATED`, 9 `WRAPPED_REGULATED`, and four ids for the regulated confidential kinds: one each for `NORMAL_ZETHER`, `WRAPPED_ZETHER`, `NORMAL_PQZ`, `WRAPPED_PQZ`. Every one is off until its implementation is published. It amends CTR-GOV-03's "reserved in the enum comment".
**Status.** BUILT on branch `governance` (plan T4 `60406d42`): `TokenKind` members 0–13, `RETIRED_6` and `RETIRED_7` refused by `deployTokenImplementation`, 8–13 (`NORMAL_REGULATED`, `WRAPPED_REGULATED`, `NORMAL_ZETHER_REGULATED`, `WRAPPED_ZETHER_REGULATED`, `NORMAL_PQZ_REGULATED`, `WRAPPED_PQZ_REGULATED`) off until an implementation is published; `test_regulatedKindPublishesOnTheSameFactory`. The four confidential ids reserve a number only; their rules are CTR-GOV-17.

After a freeze a regulated kind could only come from a second factory, whose token is an outside leg to [CTR-GOV-05](#ctr-gov-05--a-wrapped-kind-refuses-a-scaas-leg-with-force-or-moderate) and `KIND_OUTSIDE` to the DEX (attack B-03).
**Cost if wrong.** A few unused enum values.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02; `research/governance/permission-model-v2-attack.md` B-03.

### CTR-GOV-17 — Regulated confidential kinds: the rules
- old: governance:regulated-confidential · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-17 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** On a regulated `NORMAL_ZETHER`, `WRAPPED_ZETHER`, `NORMAL_PQZ` or `WRAPPED_PQZ`:
- **FREEZE** of an account blocks its shield, wrap-shield, unshield and transfer, whatever the destination, and locks its public balance. A frozen account still receives shielded credits: it may be a decoy, and a refusal would break the ring and name it. It cannot take the credit out, but it may roll a credit over into its own balance, since that moves nothing out. A frozen `beneficiaryUA` is refused: that name is public, not a decoy. The check reads the proof's sender, so a frozen account may submit another account's proof as envelope `from`, against CTR-AS-05's rule on these kinds.
- **PAUSE** means what it means on the public kinds (CTR-AS-06): unwrap is never paused. It stops shielded and public transfers, shield, unshield and unshield-unwrap (owner 2026-11-03); direct unwrap of public units, holder burn and `FORCE` stay open, and roll-over too, since it moves nothing out (controller reading, owner may override). Freeze and pause durations are CTR-AS-05's and CTR-AS-06's.
- **A denylist, not an allowlist,** when `DENYLIST` is on: a denied account cannot receive into a public balance. `ALLOWLIST` is invalid on these four kinds: decoys hide the real receiver. The check sits on the public balance, so a multi-recipient transfer with decoys is not checked, and each leg's `decoyFee` stays unchecked: a denied or frozen account named as a leg still receives it, since a refusal would reveal the decoy. That fee is bounded only by `minDecoyFee ≤ d < 2^64` and one leg is enough, so a sender can reach a denied account's public balance by it: accepted by the owner, 2026-11-03. The disclosure states this exception.
- **FORCE** acts on public balances only, as `MODERATE` does (CTR-GOV-13): a shielded balance never moves without its owner's proof.
- **Who sees what is not on chain.** An auditor decides what to share, off chain; no on-chain viewing right exists.
**Status.** Rules decided, not designed in detail, not built; SPECIFIED (governance spec §4.3). Whether a regulated form fits is **not known**: `WrappedPqzToken` is 72,160 B already, on the SCaaS testnet's higher ceiling only (CTR-GOV-19). The denylist is the receiver check of [CTR-GOV-18](#ctr-gov-18--receiver-check-two-feature-bits-allowlist-and-denylist-off-by-default).
**Why.** Regulation needs to stop an account and the token and to reach public value, without weakening what a shielded balance promises: only its owner's proof moves it.
**Cost if wrong.** A regulator cannot seize shielded value on chain: it must wait for an unshield, which FREEZE blocks.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the regulated confidential kinds 10–13 (T30 `da66a98b` Zether, T31 `65caf46f` PQZ; four PQZ sets): the hooks at the confidential sites before the proof, a confidential balance frozen but never seized, bit 8 outside their mask, the PQZ refresh open ([CTR-AS-30](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-30)); Zether and PQZ kept apart. The size question is answered: after the T66b module split every regulated release's core and module is under 32 KiB runtime (`size-baseline.json`), none above 64 KiB.
Change (2026-11-11, controller call under the owner's leave of 2026-11-10, quoted in [CTR-GOV-24](#ctr-gov-24--kyc-bit-28-allowlist-and-denylist-lists-held-in-the-token-enabled-at-once)'s Source; group 3s, after Fable's review; status: BUILT (ua-mtx-3s)): on kinds 10–13 bit 9 `DENYLIST` is the token's deny list: besides a public receiver it stops the proof's sender, the shield and `shieldIn` payers and the beneficiary (every site `F` or `R` reads), still never a shielded receiver, a ring member, a leg or its `decoyFee`; the registry's deny mask moves under bit 28 `KYC` (`requiredFlags` 0 on these kinds); `ALLOWLIST` stays invalid here.

### CTR-GOV-18 — Receiver check: two feature bits, ALLOWLIST and DENYLIST, off by default
- old: governance:denied-flags · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-18 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The receiver check has two feature bits on the same `ComplianceRegistry`, both off by default, so by default nobody is stopped. `ALLOWLIST` keeps bit 8 and reads `requiredFlags`; `DENYLIST` takes bit 9, beside it, and reads `deniedFlags`; `MODERATE` moves to bit 21:
`R(a) = (!ALLOWLIST || (flags(a) & requiredFlags) == requiredFlags) && (!DENYLIST || (flags(a) & deniedFlags) == 0)`.
Both on means: known, and not denied. `ELIGIBLE_CONTRACT` satisfies `requiredFlags` (CTR-AS-16), never `deniedFlags`. Each bit is disabled and locked on its own. Features only lose bits after creation, so a token created with a bit off never gets it: the issuer chooses at creation.
**Status.** Decided, not built; SPECIFIED (governance spec §4.4, asset-suite CTR-AS-07). Bits 8 and 9 exist, refused on every kind of this release (`FeatureNotBuilt` on `NORMAL` and `WRAPPED`, `FeatureInvalidForKind` on the confidential kinds; plan T3), so no token carries a receiver check yet. It changes CTR-AS-07 and CTR-AS-17's `ALLOWLIST ⇔ registry ≠ 0 && requiredFlags ≠ 0` row. A token with both off adds no read (CTR-GOV-11). An earlier draft of this entry had one bit with two flag sets and a denylist by default.
**Why.** One bit, one meaning: a wallet reads the two controls directly. Money for general use, such as a CBDC or a stablecoin, turns on `DENYLIST`; a security needing known holders turns on `ALLOWLIST`. `FREEZE` stops a sender and expires; a denied account cannot receive; a sanctioned account takes both.
**Cost if wrong.** A token created with both off can never stop anyone. A denylist acts after the fact.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-02.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `ALLOWLIST` (bit 8, kinds 8, 9) and `DENYLIST` (bit 9, kinds 8–13) with `ComplianceRegistry` keyed by `bytes32`, the bounded call and the codehash pin ([CTR-AS-28](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-28); T29 `7411a468`; `test/as/Receiver.t.sol`, `Registry.t.sol`, `RegistryFailure.t.sol`).
Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3s, [CTR-GOV-24](#ctr-gov-24--kyc-bit-28-allowlist-and-denylist-lists-held-in-the-token-enabled-at-once); status: BUILT (ua-mtx-3s)): the registry check moves to bit 28 `KYC`, unchanged in meaning (`requiredFlags` and `deniedFlags` both under it, `requiredFlags` 0 on 10–13, receivers only); bits 8 `ALLOWLIST` and 9 `DENYLIST` keep their numbers and become lists held in the token, checked on both parties. Old: "Features only lose bits after creation, so a token created with a bit off never gets it". New: that holds for every bit but 8, 9 and 28, which the admin may switch on after creation (`enableFeature`, at once) unless locked off; 8 and 9 are never switched off once on; `KYC` is disabled as before, delayed, and may be enabled again.

### CTR-GOV-19 — Build first on the SCaaS testnet at a higher code size ceiling; reduce later
- old: governance:pqz-size · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-03 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-19 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `NormalPqzToken`, `WrappedPqzToken` and their regulated forms run only where the PQZ precompile exists, so only on a chain whose configuration is under its operator's control. On such a chain the code size limit (`maxCodeSize`) is raised for them. **Every kind, `WrappedZetherToken` included, first runs on the SCaaS testnet at that higher limit:** size does not block the governance build. How to reduce size, and what `WrappedZetherToken` needs before a public chain, is decided later.
**Status.** BUILT; the SCaaS testnet reset executed 2026-11-04 (below). The controller proposed `maxCodeSize` `0x20000` on the SCaaS testnet, owner may override; 22776 stays the owner's. Probed on throwaway nodes (`pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-11-03-code-size-probe.txt`): T0 (`687afdb3`), arm A, EIP-7954 holds the limit at 65,536 B whatever `maxCodeSize` says; arm C, without EIP-7954 and with `maxCodeSize` `0x20000`, larger code deploys. T0b (`dc14ebbe`): 131,072 B deploys and 131,073 B does not; the init code limit is 262,144 B, twice `maxCodeSize`. **Owner 2026-11-03: the SCaaS testnet leaves EIP-7954 out**, every other Amsterdam EIP stays: NET-EVM-06's Change. The size gate's ceiling is 131,072 B runtime and 262,144 B init, and the contracts above 65,536 B are the pinned list `_above64KiB` of `size-baseline.json`, today `WrappedPqzToken` (72,160 B) alone (T2 `7edcad34`). The deploy declares the chain's limit, `CHAIN_CODE_LIMIT` (default 65,536 B), and refuses a larger release by name before sending (GD-4); every kind has a deploy path and every release fits a 200 M block, the gate admitting up to 119,753 B there (T16 `52ef7d22`, `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-03-governance-deploy-gas.txt`). The reset ran on 2026-11-04 (SCaaS testnet reset 1, the owner's go of 2026-11-04): image `2.2.0-pqz7`, genesis unchanged `0xf1f491ab…3164`, 65,537 B and 119,800 B deploy at a 200 M block, every kind deployed (`WrappedPqzToken` 72,160 B among them), PQZ and Zether e2e and a governance smoke through the `GovernanceRouter` passed; `pqz-core/nethermind/chain/RUNBOOK.md` "Code size 128 KiB on the SCaaS testnet: reset 1", `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-04-testnet-reset1-7622.txt`. A kind above 64 KiB is not deployable on a public chain until the owner decides: the size gate names which.
**Why.** The precompile already needs a chain of that kind, and code size on it is the operator's setting, unlike on a public chain.
**Cost if wrong.** Above 65,536 B every jump widens, about 4.7 KB at once (inferred), and deploy gas grows with the runtime. A customer chain has one more setting to change.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-03, two statements; `research/governance/prototype/RESULTS.md`; measured options on branch `token-core`.

Change (2026-11-07, owner, status: decided, to be built in plan task T66b part 4 of branch `ua-mtx-merge`; research `research/evm-library-organisation.md`): every deployed contract, PQZ kinds included where possible ("if not possible, that is still OK"), fits one transaction of 60 M on T10's formula, about 35.3 KB runtime for a token released through the factory and 35.7 KB for a library. The owner allows **lever L in its forward form** (reverses the 2026-11-05 deprecation for this form only): every body but the ERC-20 core moves into DELEGATECALL body modules compiled on the token's own bases, the token keeps every typed entry point and the one `nonReentrant` (variant A of 2026-10-21 kept); the release cost of 1 + 3–5 transactions per kind per chain is accepted; the `UARegistryLib` ↔ `UARegistry` pair is rebalanced first (R4's 60 M); the extra calldata copies of proof-carrying PQZ operations (+0.2 % to +4.8 % gas) are accepted. Lever D stays deprecated.
Change (owner 2026-11-07, as specified 2026-11-09 in the T66b spec §2; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, T66b `816f226d`): **the size window closes.** With the body modules ([CTR-TOK-30](#ctr-tok-30--body-modules-every-body-but-the-erc-20-core-runs-in-a-delegatecall-module-of-its-kind)) no contract is above 65,536 B: `_above64KiB` and its check leave `size-baseline.json` and `scripts/size_gate.py`, and the eight `.init` rows go (every init code is under EIP-3860). The gate's stop line is the 60 M line per form, an error above it, with the 57 M line a notice: release 35,386 / 33,594 B, body module 35,570 / 33,780 B, library 35,694 / 33,903 B, plain contract 35,286 / 33,516 B (the registry's fit); each row's form is derived (a library by its head, a module by `script/KindModules.sol` and the DEX's D, a release by its kind's module file and the DEX) and pinned in `_forms`. The ceiling of 131,072 B runtime and 262,144 B init stays above everything. Rows old -> new at `816f226d`: the token releases 34,757–74,449 -> 13,734–27,713 B, `SCaaSDex` 34,929 -> 32,991 B; the largest per form: release `SCaaSDex` 32,991 B, module `NormalPqzRegulatedTokenQ` 32,423 B, library `UARegistryCoreLib` 33,685 B, plain `OpenFactory` 29,225 B (0 errors, 0 notices). Deploy gas at T66b 4.4, each contract its own CREATE2 transaction, `(regular + state) × 1.05`: all 93 deployed contracts (12 releases, 55 body modules, the DEX and D, the registry trio, 15 libraries, the factory, the routers, `ComplianceRegistry`, the wallets) ask at most 60 M with regular × 1.05 < 2^24; the largest `UARegistryCoreLib` 56.64 M, `SCaaSDex` 55.70 M, the module `NormalPqzRegulatedTokenQ` 54.76 M, the largest release `WrappedPqzRegulatedToken` 47.02 M plus the factory frame of 0.31 M.

### CTR-GOV-20 — OPERATOR_TRANSFER: bit 22, any holder, the regulated kinds
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-05 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-20 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Bit 22 `OPERATOR_TRANSFER` (power, scalar): a holder moves units out of an account to another with no record. One direct entry `operatorTransfer(bytes32 from, bytes32 to, uint256 amount, bytes32 ref)`, relayed through the `GovernanceRouter` as `mtxOperatorTransfer` (no `mtx` twin on the token); the CTR-GOV-08 refusals unchanged (0, `pad(UA_POOL)`, `pad(SHIELD_POOL)`, `pad(this)`, an unregistered or non-SIGNING derived `to`, a native `from` with code); public balances only (CTR-GOV-13). **Any holder**: an EOA, a single-key UA, an `msig` or a contract, never contract-only. The bit grants the power; each holder's own grant is `WHOLE` (one or two operators) or `LIMITED` (`perWindow` over a 1-day `window`, `total`, `maxUses`, `validUntil`, `delegable` leaves). On the regulated kinds 8–13 only (owner correction, 2026-11-05): a plain kind refuses bit 22 as it refuses 5–9 (`FeatureInvalidForKind`), so the plain kinds take no byte and CTR-GOV-03's "+0" is untouched.
**Status.** SPECIFIED. The constant `GovernanceBits.OPERATOR_TRANSFER` and the holder rule BUILT (ua-mtx-merge T24, `test/governance/GovRelax.t.sol`: an EOA and a single-key UA held `WHOLE` and `LIMITED`, refused past a daily cap; `GovRegulatedBits`: the plain kinds refuse bit 22); the entry and the router op BUILT in ua-mtx-merge T32 (`e46cdb71`; `governance_bits.json` and the vector rows in T34). **Change (owner 2026-11-06):** the router's signed struct names the moved account `account`, not `from`: `UAOperatorTransfer(bytes32 from, address target, bytes32 account, bytes32 to, uint256 amount, bytes32 ref, …)`, since the envelope's `from` is the signer and EIP-712 cannot hold two fields of one name; the direct entry keeps `operatorTransfer(bytes32 from, bytes32 to, uint256 amount, bytes32 ref)`.
**Why.** Loyalty: each sales clerk (an EOA at the point of sale) moves a buyer's points or gives the store's points within a daily limit; a store manager grants the clerks. The transfer power of the draft's `moderatedTransfer` was contract-only on bit 21, which a clerk's key is not.
**Cost if wrong.** A single key moves balances within its grant: bounded by the grant terms and the owner's revoke; a `WHOLE` holder is unbounded by design. A loyalty program on a plain kind must use a regulated kind for it.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-05 (relayed by the controller); `superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-regulated-kinds.md` §3.4; `research/governance/bit-table.md` row 22.
Change (2026-11-11, Fable review A-2; controller call under the owner's leave; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-fix-contracts`, UNAUDITED): the "native `from` with code" refusal of `operatorTransfer` reads `SigCheck.isContract`, as the rest of the tree does: an EIP-7702 designator account is an EOA ([CTR-UA-24](#ctr-ua-24--eip-7702-eoas-are-native-classify-by-code)) and stays within the operator's reach. Before, one 7702 authorization put any EOA holder out of it while it kept transacting by signature. Test: `test/as/OperatorTransfer.t.sol` `test_designatorFromIsAnEoa`.

### CTR-GOV-21 — TAX: bit 23, the regulated kinds, any holder, granted with the issuer seat, not delay-relaxed
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-21 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Bit 23 `TAX` (power, not scalar, no scope) is valid on the regulated kinds 8–13 only (a plain kind refuses it, `FeatureInvalidForKind(23)`). Any holder: an EOA, a single-key UA, an `msig` or a contract; it is in `_roleBits()` of 8–13 and in `ISSUER_BITS` (so `init` grants it to `roles.issuer` when set; an issuer holding only bit 23 is accepted), never in `_contractOnlyBits()`, `REGULATED_ROLES` or `_delayedRelaxBits()`. Its powers are `setTaxRate` and `setTaxRecipient` ([CTR-AS-19](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-19)), relayed as `mtxSetTaxRate` / `mtxSetTaxRecipient` through the router. A token that wants a contract for 5–7 and an EOA for 23 is created with the contract issuer and then `grantRole(23, eoa)`.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, T39 `0d054f65`; UNAUDITED. Tests `test/as/Tax.t.sol` (`test_taxBit_*`).
**Why.** Owner O9: the tax collector may be a single key; Q5: with a single-key holder allowed, the owner's revoke of a compromised holder must be immediate, so bit 23 is not delay-relaxed; alerts and an immediate set-back cover the authority's concern.
**Cost if wrong.** A stolen single key redirects tax revenue at once (bounded by the owner's immediate revoke and the alerts); a delayed revoke would leave it redirecting for up to 30 days.
**Source.** `superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-pay-meta-tax.md` §6.1, §12 PT-6 (owner O9, O16 on Q5, 2026-11-06).

### CTR-GOV-22 — PQZ_PROOF: bit 24, the PQZ kinds, any holder, effect from the next debit, disabling freezes the value
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-22 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Bit 24 `PQZ_PROOF` is a power of the PQZ kinds 4, 5, 12, 13, held by any holder (an EOA, a single-key UA, an `msig`, a contract), in `ISSUER_BITS`, never contract-only and never delay-relaxed (`RegulatedBase._delayedRelaxBits` stays 5, 6, 7); a plain PQZ kind's `roles.issuer` takes bit 24 alone. `setProofStore(uint8 next)` is `use(24)`: `ProofStoreInvalid(next)` for 2 and above, a no-op on the current value, else `ProofStoreSet(previous, next)`, applied from the next debit ([pq-zero-knowledge.md CTR-PQZ-35](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-35)). `disableFeature(24)` freezes `proofStore` at its value. Relayed through the `GovernanceRouter`: `mtxSetProofStore` over `UASetProofStore`, fee mode `NONE`; the token's own allow-list is unchanged (a direct entry). `governance_bits.json` row 24 carries its name and sentence.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`: T61 `6fb7a845`, `d4ae676d` (tests `test/governance/GovProofBit.t.sol`); UNAUDITED. The freeze question of the proof-path spec §5, answered by T60's matrix: LOG changes no 2^24 verdict (PQZH LOG costs 0 regular under the EIP-7976 floor), so disabling bit 24 takes no debit away on 2^24; one 64 M node-limit row differs (`n2560-kmax16384` PQZL op 7 M = 8, no auditor, direct).
**Why.** O4, O10: the proof storage mode is the holder's operational choice, not a protocol constant, and a token that gives it up must keep one fixed mode.
**Cost if wrong.** A holder that switches to LOG raises every debit's cost (PQZL +380 k to +874 k regular); one that switches to NONE leaves rebuilding a past statement to the transaction's calldata.
**Source.** Owner rulings O4, O10 (proof-path spec, approved 2026-11-07); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-proof-path.md` §5, §12; plan T61.

### CTR-GOV-23 — One admin per contract, a UA, named admin on every contract
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-23 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every SCaaS contract with an administrator has exactly one, a UA id (`bytes32`), named `admin`. (1) The 12 token kinds and `SCaaSDex` (`GovernanceBase`, `GovernanceLib`): `admin()`, `pendingAdmin()`, `transferAdmin(bytes32)`, `acceptAdmin()`, `renounceAdmin()`, `AdminTransferStarted` / `AdminTransferred(previousAdmin, newAdmin)`, `NotAdmin(bytes32)`, `NotPendingAdmin(bytes32)`, `AdminAccountPool`, `AdminHasHolders`, the storage fields `admin`, `pendingAdmin`, `adminGeneration` in the same slots, the config field `admin`, the selector-audit class `ADMIN`; the two-step transfer, the renounce, every bit, delay and rule unchanged; the router's `UATransferAdmin(…,bytes32 newAdmin,…)`, `UAAcceptAdmin`, `UARenounceAdmin`. The PqChat topic record's creator is its `admin` (`PqTopic.admin`, `topicsByAdmin`, `PqTopicNotAdmin`; topic ids unchanged, the typehash moves). Not renamed: the PqChat instance's `owner()` (`bytes32`), the `owner` of `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount` (the holder of the assets). (2) `OpenFactory`'s registrar becomes its admin: `OpenFactory(bytes32 admin)` with a native first admin (`AdminNotNative`), `configureChain` its direct call, then a two-step transfer and a renounce as in `GovernanceBase`, both only on a configured chain (owner, Q1); a renounce also ends deprecation, with every other admin op. (3) `ComplianceRegistry(bytes32 admin, address govRouter)`: a two-step transfer and no renounce (owner, Q2), a regulated token checking its registry's router (CTR-AS-07); the parties it enables to write compliance rows are its **KYC providers** (owner 2026-11-10; the spec's draft said attesters), UA ids too (owner, Q5): `setKycProvider(bytes32 provider, bool enabled)`, `kycProviderId(bytes32)`, `kycProviderEnabled(uint32)`, `KycProviderSet`, `NotKycProvider`, the row field `providerId`, the row op `setCompliance` by its subject with `ComplianceSet` and `complianceOf`, the router's `UASetKycProvider` and `UASetCompliance`; every row rule kept, the registry's own `admin` and `AdminWrittenSlot` unchanged. (4) An admin or a KYC provider acts directly as its native id (an EIP-7702 designator refused) or through the chain's `GovernanceRouter`, which names it by `subject()`; every admin op has a typed `mtx<Op>`, fee mode `NONE`, relayable at fee 0. **Release deploys: approve, then an open deploy** (owner, final ruling on the review's P1-2): the admin, any UA kind through the same pattern, approves one release by hash (`approveTokenRelease`, `approveDexRelease`, `approveRelease`: the release id, `envVersion`, `initcodeHash`, `implArgsHash`, `chainUid`, the factory, `adminGeneration`, `until`; relayable, fee 0 too; `revokeApproval` for an unused one; an approval dies at an admin change or at `until`); `deployTokenImplementation`, `deployDexImplementation`, `deployImplementation` keep their names and ABI, are open to anyone, carry no signature and go straight to the factory, which accepts one only against a matching live approval and consumes it. The approval key binds every caller-supplied field a deploy stores (for a class release `initSelector` and `interfaceId` too), and the deploy rebuilds it from its own arguments and the hashes of its bytes; a live approval is `LIVE`, of the current `adminGeneration` and not past `until`, which is at most 30 days ahead. A deploy's result does not depend on the sender's gas: every probe in the deploy path fails closed or is absent. No approval is needed only when the admin is a native id and that same account sends the deploy (`msg.sender == admin`: one transaction, as today); a native EOA admin whose deploy another account sends, and a derived admin always, approve first; the shortcut checks `msg.sender` only, never a signature. Release management is not a node job: neither the approvals nor the deploys are node rows (`NOT_ROWS`, "release management is not a node job (owner 2026-11-10)"; owner, Q3 as updated); every other admin op is a node row. A deploy verifies no signature, so its gas is today's plus the approval lookup, within NET-EVM-11's 60 M. Derived admins may be used on every chain at once, with no audit gate (owner, on the review's P2-5). `FactoryInfo` loses `ownerUA` (owner, Q4); the names as proposed (owner, Q6). The 3f verifier UA (CTR-PQZ-27 to CTR-PQZ-30) is unchanged but for the word.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3r` (T1-T15, UNAUDITED; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md`); the stacked final gate (every forge directory, the size gate, the four PQZ sets, the node e2e, every client, the local matrix run) runs at the 3t tip before the merge into `ua-mtx-merge`. Fable review 2026-11-10: approve with fixes, no P0, every finding applied to the spec; the release deploys (approve, then an open deploy: the owner's final ruling after two drafts), P2-5 and the relay pair ruled by the owner the same day.
**Why.** Owner 2026-11-10: an admin may be any UA, an `msig` or a PQ-signing UA included, which is more secure and more flexible; a recorded owner goes stale; one word for the same power on every contract and every chain (the non-EVM families already say admin, CTR-GOV-07).
**Cost if wrong.** Every governance selector, event and error and four typehashes move (test-only chains: no alias); a derived admin depends on the router; a renounced factory can never deprecate a release again.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-10 (three rulings in chat, the answers to the spec's Q1–Q6, the directory, the release deploys, P2-5, the relay pair and the KYC provider name the same day); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md` §1, §4, §5, §10, §13; Fable review 2026-11-10.

<a id="CTR-GOV-24"></a>
### CTR-GOV-24 — KYC bit 28; ALLOWLIST and DENYLIST lists held in the token; enabled at once
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: decisions.md#CTR-GOV-24 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** On the regulated kinds 8–13; the plain kinds keep "+0". (1) **Bit 28 `KYC`**, a capability of kinds 8–13, takes over the receiver check that bits 8 and 9 make today, unchanged in meaning: the pinned `complianceRegistry` (code hash `COMPLIANCE_REGISTRY_CODEHASH`, its router checked, CTR-AS-07), `requiredFlags` and `deniedFlags` through the bounded `hasFlags`, receivers only; `KYC ⇒ complianceRegistry ≠ 0`, `complianceRegistry ≠ 0 ⇔ (requiredFlags | deniedFlags) ≠ 0`, `requiredFlags == 0` on 10–13. (2) **Bits 8 `ALLOWLIST` (kinds 8, 9) and 9 `DENYLIST` (8–13) become lists held in the token:** `listFlags[account]` (`ALLOWED`, `DENIED`, one slot, `scaas.regulated` +7). Under `ALLOWLIST` every party a hook checks must be `ALLOWED`, under `DENYLIST` none may be `DENIED`: the senders, payers and meta-tx `from` that `F` reads and the receivers, fee recipients and beneficiaries that `R` reads; never a forced transfer's subject or the unwrap recipient; contracts (the DEX and its puller, escrow, clones, wrappers) are listed like anyone else; on 10–13 no shielded receiver or leg is read (I9). The three bits are independent. (3) **Ops:** `setAllowed(bytes32[] accounts, bool on)` and `setDenied(bytes32[] accounts, bool on)`, 1 to 256 accounts (`ListBatchInvalid`), at once both ways, one `AllowedSet` / `DeniedSet` per account, the view `listFlagsOf`; relayed as `mtxSetAllowed` / `mtxSetDenied` through the `GovernanceRouter`, fee mode `NONE`, relayable at fee 0. (4) **Who:** a holder of bit 8 edits the allow list, a holder of bit 9 the deny list; any holder, never contract-only; the issuer seat holds each list bit set at creation; the admin grants others under `grantRole` / `grantDelay`, also while the bit is off and not locked off, so a list is written before it is switched on; `revokeRole` acts at once (8 and 9 stay out of `_delayedRelaxBits()`); the admin has no direct list op. (5) **Governance of the three bits:** `enableFeature(bit)` (the admin, `governed`, relayed as `mtxEnableFeature` at fee 0) takes `KYC`, `ALLOWLIST` and `DENYLIST` only (`FeatureNotEnableable(bit)` for any other) and acts at once (`FeatureEnabled(bit, by)`). `ALLOWLIST` and `DENYLIST` are a reverse ratchet: once on, never off (`disableFeature` refuses `FeatureNotDisableable(bit)`); relief is editing the list. `KYC` is the escape from a dead or compromised registry: enabled at once (`ComplianceRegistryNotSet()` without a registry; the registry and its masks may be set at creation while `KYC` is off) and disabled as today (`disableFeature`, in the regulated delayed set, now 5, 6, 7 and 28: two calls with `grantDelay`, at once when it is 0), then enabled again. `lockedFeatures` locks a bit's creation state, on or off (`FeatureLocked` both ways; a lock off is allowed for 8, 9 and 28 only). Every other bit is unchanged: one-way off, never enabled. The lists persist while a bit is off. `termsHash` is required while one of 8, 9, 28 can still be enabled (CTR-AS-02). The controller's calls after the review are listed under Source.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3s` (group 3s T0–T11, spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-token-lists.md`; UNAUDITED); the list mechanics are [CTR-AS-31](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-31). Defaults the owner may override (spec §16): a denied or unlisted holder cannot burn or unwrap; `termsHash` while a bit can still be enabled; list holders are any holder. Fable review 2026-11-11 (at `28c6b5d8`): approve with changes, no P0, 2 P1, 5 P2, 8 P3; re-check 2026-11-11 (at `9ed9c880`): approve with changes, one P2 and six P3; every call decided by the controller under the owner's leave of 2026-11-10 (do it automatically, no need to ask again; quoted under Source), applied in the spec (§17).
**Why.** Owner: a compliance registry per token is an extra deploy step, while a list held in the token is fast and easy to check; the registry stays for the flags its KYC providers keep. The lists usually start off and are switched on during operation, so they are enabled after creation and never switched off again; `KYC` keeps an off switch as the escape from a dead or compromised registry.
**Cost if wrong.** An admin's `enableFeature(ALLOWLIST)` over an empty list stops every public transfer at once, and the bit can never be cleared (only listing relieves it); a compromised list holder stops any account at once with no end date until it is revoked; holders get no notice of an enable beyond the event.
**Source.** Parts (2)'s two-sidedness and contract listing, (3), (4) and the scope are the controller's brief of 2026-11-10, approved by the owner as a design without words of his own: controller calls. Owner 2026-11-10, in chat, relayed by the controller, in order. The ruling: "OK, coi như thêm bit KYC, sử dụng ComplianceRegistry. Còn ALLOWLIST / DENYLIST tương đương WHITELIST/BLACKLIST." (add a KYC bit that uses the ComplianceRegistry; ALLOWLIST / DENYLIST mean a whitelist / blacklist), with the reason above. The governance of the three bits: first "as every other feature bit" (set at creation, lockable, one-way `disableFeature`); then "3 bit bật tắt được." (the three bits can be switched on and off) and "Và có tác dụng ngay lập tức" (and at once), both withdrawn by "Thôi, như những bit khác đi. còn có lockFeatures mà nhỉ?" (no, like the other bits; there is lockFeatures after all); then "Như vậy không đúng với bit DENYLIST lắm, vì khởi đầu có thể tắt, rồi sau đó bật. Thôi, thêm enableFeature cho bit nayf." (that does not fit DENYLIST, which may start off and be switched on later; add enableFeature for this bit); then the final rule: "Thường, 3 bit này là tắt, trong quá trình vận hành thì bật. Nhưng ở đây lại cấm bật về sau?" (usually these three bits are off and are switched on during operation; yet here switching on later is forbidden?), "Có lẽ theo chiều ngược lại, không cho gọi disableFeature trên các bit này. Tức khi bật lên rồi thì không tắt. Ngược với các bit khác, tắt rồi thì không bật." (rather the reverse: no disableFeature on these bits; once on, never off; the opposite of the other bits, which once off are never on), and, on KYC keeping its escape: "OK, KYC sẽ như thế."
