(OK, KYC stays like that). **Controller calls under the owner's leave** ("tự động làm, không cần hỏi nữa", do it automatically, no need to ask again; owner 2026-11-10 23:48), made 2026-11-11 on Fable's review and re-check (spec §17): an enable of 8 or 9 is refused while that bit has no holder root, checked at the enable only (`ListHolderMissing(bit)`); the issuer seat holds each list bit for which the "enableable" predicate holds at creation, set or not; with `ALLOWLIST` set at creation and an initial supply, init lists `initialHolder` before the mint; one predicate, "enableable" (valid, not set, not locked off, the admin not 0, and for 28 a registry set), decides where `termsHash` is required and what every wallet warns of; the node acts on a list row only while its bit is on, and a deny or an allow-off of the venue, its puller or a market contract halts that leg's markets; documented consequences, no code: a renounce with a list on leaves the list final, a list may be on with no writer, a token may be born with an allow list nobody can write, a denied or unlisted party's units held by another contract cannot be released to it, and a payout to several recipients reverts as a whole when one is blocked; a new rule of `contracts/asset-suite.md`, written at the build, will hold the list mechanics and link here, this entry the bit allocation and the governance of the three bits. Spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-token-lists.md` §1, §5.

## 17. Contracts — Meta-transactions

### CTR-MTX-01 — Payment is a MetaTransfer with entryRef ≠ 0
- old: R2(op) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-01 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A payment is one signed typed `MetaTransfer` with its reference (`mtxExecuteTransfer`, `mtxPay`), not a self-call, so `PaymentSettled` keeps its fee fields and wallets show recipient, amount and reference field by field; until 2026-10-08 it was the `pay(bytes32)` shape of the single struct.
**Cost if wrong.** A separate payment entry point would duplicate the pipeline and its audit surface; making payment a self-call would lose the fee in `PaymentSettled`.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md:664`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-1, MG-5.
Change (2026-10-08): a payment is a `MetaTransfer` with `entryRef ≠ 0`, run through `mtxExecuteTransfer`, `mtxPay` or `mtxPayReceiverFee`; `PaymentSettled` unchanged. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-4.
Change (2026-11-09, group 3i, CTR-MTX-32): the tender's deposit and every service pull are this shape (a `UAMetaTransfer` with `entryRef ≠ 0` is a payment: there the operation's EIP-712 digest in the service's domain). Status: BUILT for the token side and the reference service (T77 `b9b130bb`).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R20; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): a relayed payment is a `UAMetaTransfer` with `entryRef ≠ 0`, run through `mtxExecuteTransfer` or built by `mtxPay` and `mtxPayReceiverFee`; it emits `UAPaymentSettled`.

### CTR-MTX-02 — Clone domain: implementation name, version 1, clone verifyingContract, salt chain_uid
- old: R5 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-02 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Clones share the implementation name and the one version `"1"`; each clone is its own `verifyingContract` and the domain carries `salt = chain_uid` from the implementation's immutable, so a signature never replays on another token or another chain with the same chain id.
**Cost if wrong.** A shared domain would let a signature move between clones; without the salt it would move between chains that share a chain id.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md:674`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-4.
Change (2026-10-08): every SCaaS contract on `MetaTxBase` signs in `("SCaaS <Contract>", "1", chainId, contract, chain_uid)`; both structs of a contract share its domain. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-1.

### CTR-MTX-03 — Random entryRef; pay lane derived from it
- old: R9(lane) · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A random `entryRef` cannot be guessed or front-run, and deriving the pay lane from it lets the contract enforce pay-once without a request registry.
**Cost if wrong.** Sequential references leak volumes and allow pre-emptive lane exhaustion.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md:692`
Change (2026-10-27): **review C5-9, no gas run (controller ruling, owner may override)**: the metatx.md §8 Amsterdam figures (lane first write about 98 k, `mtxPay` 181,810, CTR-MTX-27 estimate about +200-230 k) are the existing `AMS_*` constants of `MetaTxGasV2.t.sol`, not a new measurement; a fresh gas run needs the owner to stop other heavy sessions. The pre-Amsterdam table stays, marked as such. Cost until a re-measure: the CTR-MTX-27 estimate is an estimate. Status: **done** as documentation (review2 T8).
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O3, O11 (T37 `3740b85e`): a pay entry's `entryRef` is always the `PayMeta` commitment `metaPayId(meta)` (its salt random), never a bare random value; the lane is a client convention and one `entryRef` takes several payments ([CTR-MTX-31](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-31)); "each request payable at most once" and "issue one request per instalment" are withdrawn.

### CTR-MTX-04 — Pay-once holds under lane horizon H
- old: CR-PD-4(issuer) · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Pay-once is a protocol rule only within the lane horizon; stating the horizon makes the guarantee checkable instead of implied.
**Cost if wrong.** Clients that assume unconditional pay-once could double-pay after the horizon.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md:901`
Change (2026-10-27): **review C0-12 (controller proposal, owner may override)**: `cancelNonce(batch)` advances a lane by one, so it invalidates the one intent signed for the current nonce, not every pending intent: with E5 and E6 signed ahead one cancel kills E5 and makes E6 executable at once (every executed intent is still signed and bounded by `validUntil`). metatx.md is corrected (k pending intents need k cancels). The code option, `cancelNonceTo(batch, newNonce)` with a UA twin (it would also close V3-02), is not built: it adds an entry point to every token and the review rates the harm as bounded. Status: **done** (review2 T8, branch `review2-fix`; documentation only).
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O3, controller call C3 (T37 `3740b85e`): invoice pay-once leaves the protocol; what stays is the nonce lifetime: one signature runs at most once, and on the families that prune lane state the horizon `H` and its obligations stay, keyed on every lane, until each family's round gives a complete replay answer.

### CTR-MTX-05 — Receiver-pays via payee co-signed ReceiverFee
- old: R192 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-05 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — the UA twin `uaPayReceiverFee(UAMetaTransfer t, payerAuth, fee, feeRecipient, rfValidUntil, payeeAuth)`: payer and payee are ids; the payee co-signs the same `ReceiverFee` over the payer's UA digest, a derived payee through `requireAuthorized` under purpose `receiver-fee`; event `UAReceiverFeePaid`. SPECIFIED (UA-5a). The address-path function is BUILT (P1b/P1c), not planned. Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.8.

**Why.** Receiver-pays needs the payee to consent to the fee; a co-signed `ReceiverFee` keeps both parties bound to the same numbers.
**Cost if wrong.** Without the payee signature a relayer could charge the payee arbitrarily.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-tender-sponsorship-shredding.md:172`
Change (2026-10-08): `paymentDigest` is the digest of the payer's `MetaTransfer`; `mtxPayReceiverFee` takes `MetaTransfer t`. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-5.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call, owner may override, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): `ReceiverFee(MetaTransfer payment,uint256 fee,address feeRecipient,uint256 validUntil)` nests the payer's whole struct (`UAReceiverFee` nests `UAMetaTransfer`), so the payee's wallet shows the payment's fields; before C6 the field was `bytes32 paymentDigest`. The views are `receiverFeeDigest(MetaTransfer, …)` / `uaReceiverFeeDigest(UAMetaTransfer, …)`; the event keeps the payment digest as `paymentDigest`; `uaPayReceiverFee` takes `UASig` for payer and payee.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R21; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `UAReceiverFee(UAMetaTransfer payment, uint256 fee, address feeRecipient, uint256 validUntil)` is the token's only receiver-fee struct (`mtxPayReceiverFee`); `ReceiverFee` is no longer in `src`.

### CTR-MTX-06 — Receiver-pays shape; every tier of the one base
- old: R193(shape) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-06 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Receiver-pays keeps its fixed shape (fee `NONE` on the payer, restricted relayer, pay lane with nonce 0, payee-signed absolute fee); with the v1 line deleted it is available on every tier of the one base, still not in `mtxBatch`.
**Cost if wrong.** A looser shape would let a submitter attach the co-signature to another intent.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-tender-sponsorship-shredding.md:181`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-9.
Change (2026-10-08): the payer shape is a `MetaTransfer` with `entryRef ≠ 0`, fee `NONE`, relayer bound, `payLane`/0; not in `mtxBatchTransfer`. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-5.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the shape rules are unchanged; only what the payee signs moved (CTR-MTX-05). The node's in-flight key for a receiver fee is the outer `ReceiverFee` digest, and the job compares the payment's `MetaTransfer` digest, which is what the chain emits (N1).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R21; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the payer shape is a `UAMetaTransfer` with the same constraints, nested in `UAReceiverFee` ([CTR-MTX-05](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-05)'s Change).
Change (owner ruling O3 2026-11-05, pay-meta-tax spec §2.5; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, T37 `3740b85e`, UNAUDITED): the payer shape loses `batch = payLane(entryRef)` and `nonce = 0`; it keeps `entryRef ≠ 0` (now `entryRef == metaPayId(meta)`, the `PayMeta` last), fee `NONE` with `fee == 0`, the relayer bound, `feeRecipient ≠ 0`, `0 < fee ≤ value`, `feeRecipient ≠ payee`, the token and the pools refused. The co-signature stays single-use: `UAReceiverFee` nests the whole `UAMetaTransfer`, lane and nonce included. Tests: `test/ua/UAReceiverFee.t.sol` `test_uaPayReceiverFee_shapeErrors`, `test/metatx/PayLanes.t.sol` `test_receiverFee_freeLane`, `test_receiverFee_coSignDeadAfterNonceUsed`.

### CTR-MTX-07 — One meta-tx tree: MetaTxBase, ERC20MetaTx, MetaTokenBase
- old: R131, typed-signing:TS-D18 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner folded every meta-transaction base into one, `ERC20MetaTx` (the built `MetaTxCore` renamed): the v1 `ERC20MetaTx`/`MetaToken`/`HederaMetaToken`, factory v1 and `ZetherMetaTx` go, and the struct, typehash and one domain version serve every token. Nothing is deployed, so no version coexists.
**Cost if wrong.** Two or three bases keep two security models and three pipelines in sync by hand.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:72`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A4, A8, §3 MG-9.
Change (2026-10-08): `ERC20MetaTx is MetaTxBase`: the token base adds the fee in this token, the typed `MetaTransfer` path, `payLane`, receiver-pays, trade and the UA path on the generic base (CTR-MTX-22); `PqzMetaTx` disappears too (CTR-PQZ-21). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-2.
Change (2026-10-08): the tree is `MetaTxBase` → `ERC20MetaTx` → `MetaTokenBase`; trade and pay sit in `MetaTokenBase`, not `ERC20MetaTx`; the kinds, Hedera and the Zether kinds sit on it. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §2 (T10), §3.
Change (2026-10-28, controller calls 2026-10-27, owner approved the split and the plan 2026-10-27, owner may override each ruling; status: current; commits: metatx-split T1 c9ec6fb0..2ceda92d, T2 76dc5be2, T3 04a2ede6, T4 b36c9dac, T5 840f0642, T6 c213e24a, T8 69fce983 + 004890a2): the relayed pipeline of every token moves into the linked library `MtxPipelineLib` (variant A of the spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-design.md`); `MetaTxBase` keeps the same code inlined for the wallets that link nothing. Rulings recorded in full: (1) the parity replay (`MetaTxParity`, 1,822 cases) compares gas only under `PARITY_GAS=1`, the pre-split self-check; after the split gas differs by design and is measured in T5 / T8 (cost if wrong: a gas regression is caught by T5 / T8 instead of the replay). (2) The global constraint is "DELEGATECALL only to a library the code names", not "only in MtxPipelineLib": `test_libraryOpcodes` allows 0xf4 once in `MtxPipelineLib` (to `HederaLib`) and once in `WrappedLib` (to `AdminLib`, pre-existing, a linked library pinned in the closure); same trust anchor (Env.libs code hash). (3) The stale natspec in `TradeLib.sol:11` stays in code (TradeLib is unchanged by the spec and a comment edit moves its code hash); the documents carry the correct text (cost if wrong: one misleading comment until a later TradeLib change). (4) About +550 gas per relayed call is permanent for the wallets on `MetaTxBase` (`_envelopeOf` pads and hashes the envelope). (5) Measured cost on the token path: +7.4 k to +7.6 k per relayed call (`unwrap` +8.9 k, cancel 0), size-independent within 2,405 gas of the 8,000 bound for the largest PQZL / PQZH envelopes (`smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-overhead-final.txt`, `...-overhead.txt`); the pre-split overhead JSON is regenerated from `2ceda92d` with `MTX_OV_PRESPLIT=1` (recipe in contracts/metatx.md §8). (6) Process: the clientkeys / scaas-node tests against the regenerated DEX KAT ran in T17 / T18 and the T20 gates (the worktree had no node_modules at T4); every brief states the worktree path and requires `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to equal it before a heavy command (a T8 `cd` into the main checkout gave a false green gate, re-run in T8 fix 1); review packages are built with `git diff BASE..HEAD` by hand. Observation, not ruled: today's code refuses an EIP-7702-delegate-only signature on the address path (`err_e7702_viaDelegate_addrPathRefuses`) and accepts it on the UA path (`ok_e7702_viaDelegate`); the parity fixture pins both as they are; intent not yet checked against CTR-MTX-25 / accounts.md (TODO.md, "metatx split — final review"). (Ruled by owner ruling 2026-10-28: accepted on both paths, see the EIP-7702 owner-ruling Change below.)

### CTR-MTX-08 — Fee never goes to the payee
- old: R132 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-08 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A fee that goes to the payee lets a payee inflate its own receipts; the check applies to the transfer and payment shapes and `payWithFee`, and a self-call has no payee.
**Cost if wrong.** Payees could disguise discounts or extract hidden charges through the fee field.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:78`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-5.
Change (2026-10-08): the payee check applies to every `MetaTransfer` (payee = `t.to`) and to `payWithFee`; a `MetaTransaction` has no payee. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-4.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O11 (T37 `3740b85e`): `payWithFee` and `payWithFeeToUA` take `PayMeta` last; their `entryRef` is always its commitment, never any value (0 included).

### CTR-MTX-09 — Named meta-tx functions are thin entry points
- old: R138, typed-signing:TS-D16 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Named functions (`mtxTransfer`, `mtxTransferWithFee`, `mtxExecuteWithFee`, `mtxPay`, `mtxBatch`) are readable in wallets and explorers but only route into the one pipeline; the unwrap pseudo-op and its named functions are gone because `mtxExecute` runs the real `unwrap`.
**Cost if wrong.** Logic in the named functions would drift from the generic path.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:119`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-3.
Change (2026-10-08): the named functions keep their signatures and build the struct of their kind — `mtxTransfer`, `mtxTransferWithFee`, `mtxPay` a `MetaTransfer`, `mtxExecuteWithFee`, `mtxBatch` a `MetaTransaction`; nothing is merged (owner); `mtxExecuteTransfer` and `mtxBatchTransfer` are added (CTR-MTX-23, CTR-MTX-24). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G4, §3 GC-5.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner option B 2026-10-31 and controller calls, owner may override; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2–C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): every operation gets a named entry beside the flat named functions above (TS-D16, CTR-MTX-28): `mtx` / `ua` + struct name, an overload with an `Envelope` first where the operation function already has that name; the wrap-by-signature entries are `mtxWrapOrder` / `uaWrapOrder`. **`mtxExecuteWithFee` is removed** (typed-signing C2; controller call, owner may override): it duplicated `mtxExecute`; it is kept in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/typed-signing/`. The flat functions of `MetaTransfer` (`mtxTransfer`, `mtxTransferWithFee`, `mtxPay`, `mtxPayMeta`) and the batches stay. The gasless unwrap is now also the named `mtxUnwrap`; `mtxExecute` with the real `unwrap` calldata still runs it. Text: `contracts/metatx.md` CTR-MTX-09, -21.
Change (owner 2026-11-04, `ua*` / `mtx*` merge; status: SPECIFIED, not built): "nothing is merged" is reversed by [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) (spec row R1): `mtxTransfer`, `mtxTransferWithFee`, `mtxPay`, `mtxPayMeta`, `mtxBatch`, `mtxBatchTransfer` take the form of today's `ua*` twin (`bytes32` ids, `UASig`) and build `UAMetaTransfer` / `UAMetaTransaction`; one form per operation. The Rule text and `contracts/metatx.md` are rewritten by the build.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O2 (T37 `3740b85e`): `mtxPay(UAMetaTransfer t, UASig auth, PayMeta meta)` takes the struct (the flat form had too few argument slots); `mtxPayMeta` is in `legacy/ua-mtx-merge/`.

### CTR-MTX-10 — mtxPay payId is entryRef, lane on chain
- old: R139 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-10 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `payId` is the payment reference and the lane is derived on chain, so a client cannot mislabel the lane; `cancelNonce` replaces `cancelMetaNonce` in the per-path caveat.
**Cost if wrong.** Client-chosen lanes would break pay-once.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:124`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-3.
Change (2026-10-08): a payment on a client-chosen lane uses `mtxExecuteTransfer` (owner G6); the generic `pay` shape is gone. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G6, §3 GC-5.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O3 (T37 `3740b85e`): the token derives no lane from `payId`; `payLane` stays a pure view, a client convention ("a client convention, not enforced"); reconcilers add the amounts of one key ([CTR-MTX-31](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-31)).

### CTR-MTX-11 — One intent, one digest; no second typehash for the same struct; batches atomic
- old: R140, typed-signing:TS-D15 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-11 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One typehash per struct keeps every signer and verifier on one digest rule; different structs in the token's domain (`UAMetaTransaction`, `TradeOrder`, `CancelOrder`, `InvalidateNonces`) are not a second hash of `MetaTransaction`. `mtxBatch` is atomic with a fresh ticket per item.
**Cost if wrong.** A second hash of the same struct invites cross-path replay; a non-atomic batch leaves half-paid states.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:131`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §7 (CTR-MTX-11 row).
Change (2026-10-08): one intent, one digest across two structs: transfer and payment only as `MetaTransfer`, calls only as `MetaTransaction`; batches never mix structs; `UAMetaTransfer` joins the different-struct list. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G5, §3 GC-1, GC-5.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner 2026-10-31, TS-D15; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): **the generic batch is kept, not dropped.** The plan first dropped it; the owner ruling of 2026-10-31 on the plan keeps `mtxExecute`, `mtxBatch`, `uaExecute`, `uaBatch`, and the defaults of open questions 1-8 stand: no typed mixed batch (EIP-712 arrays are homogeneous), `mtxBatchTransfer` / `uaBatchTransfer` stay, a homogeneous `mtx<Op>Batch` only on a named use case (none built). A named entry and the generic call of one operation share the `(from, batch)` lane, so one signature runs once. PQZ selectors stay unbatchable (CTR-PQZ-21).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R22; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): on tokens a transfer or payment is signed only as a `UAMetaTransfer` and a call only as a `UAMetaTransaction`, plus `MetaTransaction` for `executeMetaTransaction` (R3); `SmartKeyAccount` unchanged; the mandate wallets as tokens.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O6, O7(2) (T40 `bc6592b1`): "one type per intent means one wallet display" gains a second payment type signed by the payer, `UAPayWithTax` on the regulated kinds ([CTR-AS-18](contracts/asset-suite.md#CTR-AS-18)), with `UARelayFee` (TS-D19) as precedent.

### CTR-MTX-12 — Gasless unwrap is mtxExecute(unwrap) with minOut
- old: R148(contract) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-12 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A gasless unwrap lets holders exit without native gas; it is now `mtxExecute` with the wrapper's real `unwrap` calldata (fee class `AMOUNT`, fee after the call), and `minOut` still protects against rate moves between signing and execution.
**Cost if wrong.** Without `minOut` a relayer could time execution against the holder; a pseudo-op duplicates the direct function's checks.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:172`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-2, §7.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R23; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `mtxUnwrap(UAEnvelope, uint256 wrapped, address recipient, uint256 minOut, UASig)` and `mtxUnwrapLeg(UAEnvelope, address underlying, …, UASig)` take today's `uaUnwrap` form, for native and derived ids.

### CTR-MTX-13 — Public fee modes NONE, PERCENT, FIXED; 1 % cap on amount bases
- old: UD:§3.1, UD:§11:fee-denominator · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-13 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Three fee modes cover the business cases with a 1 % cap (10 000 ppm of a 1e6 denominator) on transfer, payment and `AMOUNT` selectors; the owner narrowed the cap so that calls moving no amount pay an absolute, uncapped `FIXED` fee (CTR-MTX-20).
**Cost if wrong.** More modes multiply audit cases; an uncapped percentage would let a signer be overcharged by a misreading; a cap on a zero basis would make wrap and cancel fee-less forever.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:107`, `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:450`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-5, §10 OQ4.
Change (2026-10-08): fees exist only where `_chargeFee` is overridden (every token); any other SCaaS contract accepts `NONE` only and the sponsor pays native gas (owner G2). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G2, §3 GC-2.

### CTR-MTX-14 — EIP-712 typed data, not personal_sign
- old: UD:§4 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-14 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** EIP-712 typed data is what wallets display; `personal_sign` of a hash shows the user nothing they can check. The first committed code hashed with `toEthSignedMessageHash()` (`personal_sign`) while the design sketch signed with `wallet._signTypedData(domain, types, data)` (EIP-712); the design was right and the code was changed.
**Cost if wrong.** Users would sign blind hashes, the precondition for drain attacks.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:206`
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R6; status: holds; the real-wallet display test (Q5, T20) is owner-assisted and not recorded yet): still typed data, every field named, no blind hash; for an EOA the fields the spec's §6 lists go from `address` to `bytes32` (a 32-byte word with 12 leading zero bytes) on token paths; an unbound `relayer` / `feeRecipient` is signed as 0 and shown as unbound.

### CTR-MTX-15 — Two structs, one nonce space; no forwarder; drop feeToken, innerGasLimit; keep mode
- old: UD:§24, UD:§24.1 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-15 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Meta-tx logic lives in the token, so there is no trusted forwarder; `feeToken` and `innerGasLimit` were dropped and `mode` kept, split into two nibbles: the low nibble holds flags (`RESTRICT_RELAYER` 0x01, `RESTRICT_FEE_RECIPIENT` 0x02), the high nibble an enum of the fee mode (`NONE` 0x00, `PERCENT` 0x10, `FIXED` 0x20); `if (mode & MODE_FEE_PERCENT)` is a bug, because `MODE_FEE_FIXED = 0x20` lacks bit 0x10 but a future 0x30 would have it; validation checks unknown flag bits and enum values above 2. `data` is an allowlisted call of the contract itself — the owner's explicit `to`/`value`/`data` never meant a fixed op list; since 2026-10-08 a transfer or payment is a typed `MetaTransfer` beside it, because a token transfer is a special case of a meta-transaction, not its definition (owner). Rejected: the early `IEIP1776` sketch (`tokenContract`, `batchNonce`, `expiry`, `meta_nonce(from, batchId)`).
**Cost if wrong.** A forwarder becomes a shared trust root for every token; an op list makes `wrap`, `burn`, `addReserve` and `fund` impossible to relay.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:2504`, `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:2534`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §1, §3 MG-1.
Change (2026-10-08): two structs share one lane space: the generic `MetaTransaction{from, data, batch, nonce, validUntil, mode, relayer, fee, feeRecipient}` for a call of any SCaaS contract and the token-only typed `MetaTransfer{from, to, value, entryRef, …}` that wallets display field by field; `data` is always a self-call; `transfer`/`pay` are never allowlisted; new typehashes and KATs (`metatx_kat.json`, `metatransfer_kat.json`). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G1, G10, §3 GC-1.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner option B 2026-10-31; status: documented; built in typed-signing C1–C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): a third family of structs, one per named entry (74 rows in `typed_ops.json`), joins `MetaTransaction` and `MetaTransfer`; all consume the same `(from, batch)` lane `mtxNonce`. `MetaTransaction`, its typehash, `mtxDigest` / `uaDigest` and the generic builders are unchanged (owner 2026-10-31). The node no longer reads `mtxDigest`: it computes the typed digest of the op locally and uses it as its in-flight key (N1); the views stay. The generic `MetaTransaction` path and its allowlist were **not** replaced (the brief of this task said so; the owner rulings of 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-01 keep them).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R2; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): on tokens the signed structs are `UAMetaTransaction` and `UAMetaTransfer`, in one nonce space as before; `MetaTransaction` stays on tokens only for `executeMetaTransaction` ([CTR-MTX-17](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-17)) and on `SmartKeyAccount`; the mandate wallets take `UAMetaTransaction`. `MetaTransfer` has no EVM entry and is no longer in `src` (R46).

### CTR-MTX-16 — No generic forwarder; the token calls only itself; all or nothing
- old: UD:§24.2, UD:§24.3 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-16 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** No generic forwarder means each token owns its replay protection; legacy tokens are wrapped instead of trusted. The prototype's flaw was a call **out** with the signer's calldata, not executing calldata: the token now runs allowlisted functions of itself only. The owner accepted the new invariant: transfer and payment check everything before the fee; a self-call runs first and pays after, and any failure reverts everything with the inner revert data, so the user never pays for an operation that did not happen.
**Cost if wrong.** A generic forwarder would let one bug affect every legacy token at once; charging before a self-call could not let a wrap pay from minted units.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:2570`, `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:2586`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §1, §2 A1, §3 MG-1, §10 OQ2.
Change (2026-10-08): the logic lives in every SCaaS contract (`MetaTxBase`), not only tokens; `mtxExecute` calls one of the contract's own allowlisted functions, a token's transfer and payment run through `mtxExecuteTransfer`. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-2, GC-3.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): a named entry runs one operation by the same ticket self-call, so "no call out, the signer in a transient slot, all or nothing" holds unchanged; there is still no forwarder.
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-01 with its Change, CTR-GOV-15 with its Change): a `GovernanceRouter` calls out, by typed entries only, with named parameters the signer signed, each to a `target` it names; no generic forwarder exists, there as anywhere. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T11 `ea9f4e9d`).

### CTR-MTX-17 — mtxExecute runs the signer's calldata on the token itself
- old: typed-signing:TS-D14 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-17 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner asked for the explicit `to`/`value`/`data` envelope to execute any function of the token itself, so `wrap`, `burn`, `addReserve`, `cancelNonce` and Zether ops become gasless without a forwarder; `executeMetaTransaction` stays as the EIP-1776 alias returning `bool` for tender and outside tools. The pipeline is cheap-first, writes the nonce before the call, bubbles inner reverts and charges a self-call's fee after it.
**Cost if wrong.** A hand-written op dispatch must grow per function and diverges from the direct functions' checks; swallowing errors would charge users for nothing.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A1, A3, §3 MG-1.
Change (2026-10-08): `mtxExecute` serves every SCaaS contract and `data` is always a self-call: the shape table is gone; the signature check is the virtual `_requireValidSignature`; the fee is `_chargeFee` after the call and is refused outside `NONE` where not overridden. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-3.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commits: metatx-split T3 04a2ede6, T8 69fce983): the step table runs on `MtxPipelineLib.preCall`: step 3 (the fee checks: class, amount argument, `FeeExceedsCap`, mode) is checked before the call and the fee is moved at step 6, after the call, from the `Out` the library returned; the order of every revert is pinned by `test_preCall_orderAddressPath` / `test_preCall_orderUaPath`. The ERC-1271 call of a `SmartKeyAccount` signer now runs two frames below the token (token, library, wallet): the least relayer call gas is 446,904 (`runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-node-floor.txt`), and the node floor follows (CTR-MTX-27 Change, Task 17).
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-01, TS-D14; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): **named entries are added beside the kept generic path.** Kept: `mtxExecute`, `mtxBatch`, `uaExecute`, `uaBatch`, their structs, typehashes, `mtxDigest` / `uaDigest`, `mtxSelectors()`, `_mtxRule`, `_uaAllowed`, and `executeMetaTransaction`, which stays in `MetaTxBase` and `IMetaTx` (owner ruling 2026-11-01, replacing the plan's removal; selector `0x47aea5b5`, the EIP-1776 name only). Gone to `legacy/typed-signing/`: `mtxExecuteWithFee` and the flat `uaUnwrap(bytes32 from, …)` (owner 2026-11-01). Clients and the node build the named entry by default and use the generic path for a mixed batch or an operation with no named entry. The mechanism is the existing ticket self-call (`_selfCall`), so the operation bodies and `_msgSender()` are unchanged. Text: CTR-MTX-17, -28.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R3; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): holds, not reopened (owner 2026-11-01): on tokens `executeMetaTransaction(MetaTransaction, bytes)` stays beside the merged `mtxExecute(UAMetaTransaction, UASig)`, over the address pipeline with the address proof binding; it lives in the `MetaTxBase` core (MD-1); on `SmartKeyAccount` unchanged.

### CTR-MTX-18 — Transient sender and one-shot ticket
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-18 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The signer is stored in transient slots and `_msgSender()` trusts it only for `msg.sender == this` with a live ticket, so no calldata suffix can spoof a sender (the ERC-2771 + multicall class); the guard admits exactly one self-call and consumes the ticket, so guarded functions still run under `mtxExecute` while any re-entry reverts. Every direct `msg.sender` read is listed and a lint pins the ones that stay; `from ≠ this` and no transfers to `this` remove the exploit's fuel.
**Cost if wrong.** A same-slot guard blocks every guarded self-call; a trusted calldata sender lets an attacker spend tokens parked at the token's address.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-1, §3.1, §12 (H1, H2).

Change (2026-10-30, **owner ruling D2 (a)** — owner 2026-10-30, after the 2026-10-29 EIP-7702 hot-wallet drain: "an EOA must really sign — no delegation at all; an EOA must not run code"; status: current, decided (owner); commit: `no7702` `6bb05818`): **a direct caller that is an EIP-7702 designator is refused wherever the caller is authority**, with `SigCheck.CallerDelegated(caller)`: `MetaTxBase._msgSender()` calls `SigCheck.requireNotDelegated(msg.sender)` before `return msg.sender` (every token, `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount` entry that reads the direct caller: `transfer`, `approve` / `transferFrom` (now `CallerDelegated` before `CallerNotContract`), `payWithFee*`, `transferToUA`, `wrap` / `unwrap`, `mtxShield`, `cancelNonce`, owner and role functions); `SmartKeyAccount.initiateRecovery` reads the guardian through `_msgSender()`; `SCaaSDex._onlyAdmin` and the `OpenFactory` registrar check inline. The step-5 ticket branch is unchanged. Not guarded (audit optional, not in the ruling): the `OpenFactory` creator (it only creates new things; the new token's owner calls go through `_msgSender()`). Why: a sweeper delegate runs whenever anyone calls the account and then calls SCaaS as the account (audit A2); only a caller refusal closes it. Cost if wrong: **a 7702-delegated user cannot call SCaaS contracts directly while delegated**: it acts through relayed `mtx*` / `ua*` signed by its own key (the fee may be 0) or clears its delegation first. Gas: 313 per guarded read for a warm caller (`test_requireNotDelegated_gas`; a direct caller is always warm), ≈ 626 for `payWithFee` / `payWithFeeToUA` with a fee (two reads); a designator caller pays an `extcodecopy` and reverts. Lint pin (`MsgSenderLint`): `MetaTxBase` 7 → 8. Tests: `Sweeper7702.t.sol` (`test_sweeper_directCallsRefused`, `test_plainEoaAndContractCallersUnchanged`), `test_recovery_delegatedGuardianRefused`, `test_adminOnly_delegatedAdminRefused`, `test_delegatedRegistrarRefused`, `test_shield_delegatedCallerRefused`, Tier1 `test_allowance_7702DelegatedEoaRefused`. Source: the EIP-7702 audit of 2026-10-30 (`research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`) §4 M1–M6, §6.3.

Change (2026-10-30, **owner ruling D3** — guard only the relayer-binding check; status: current, decided (owner); commit: `no7702` `6bb05818`): under `MODE_RESTRICT_RELAYER` the pipeline (`MtxPipelineLib`) checks `relayer == msg.sender` first (`MetaTxUnauthorizedRelayer`), then `SigCheck.requireNotDelegated(msg.sender)` (`CallerDelegated`). Open roles stay open: any submitter of an open-mode envelope, the `mtxWrap` / `uaWrap` fee mint, the `RelayFeeRouter` open-mode payee, the DEX settle submitter and the DEX order `relayer` binding (`TradeLib`, `SCaaSDex`; same kind of check, not named in the ruling, the submitter cannot change the order). Why: the binding is the one "who may act" check among the relayer roles; elsewhere only the relayer's own fee is exposed. Cost if wrong: a delegated relayer cannot submit bound envelopes until it clears its delegation. Gas: a bound relayed call +352 per item (guard ≈ 313 plus ≈ 39 from the restructured `isValid` / pipeline; open-mode rows +39; a two-item batch +704). Lint pin: `MtxPipelineLib` 4 → 5. Test: `test_boundRelayerDelegatedRefused`. Source: the EIP-7702 audit of 2026-10-30 (`research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`) §4 M7–M8. Fix (no7702 review m1, 2026-10-30, controller ruling within D3; commit `5f2724fa`): the PQZ layer (`PqzLayer._toPool`) read `_msgSender()` on every op, so a designator submitter of a UA-authorised transfer / unshield / unshield-unwrap was refused; it now reads the caller only when `shieldIn ≠ 0` (the submitter's own units are pulled: authority, still refused). Test: PqzNormal `test_transfer_delegatedSubmitterOnlyRefusedOnAPull`.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R24; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `MsgSenderLint`'s pinned `msg.sender` read counts move with old → new in each task's commit, and its file list covers every merged body (MD-6).

### CTR-MTX-19 — Fixed selector allowlist per implementation
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-19 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner chose a fixed per-implementation allowlist, published by `mtxSelectors()` with fee classes; `approve`, `transferFrom`, `transfer`, `payWithFee`, every `mtx…` entry and every role function are never listed (the owner flipped the earlier default: role holders act through their own contract, whose caps and guards a signature check would skip). Every listed function is `nonReentrant`; dynamic Zether arguments are canonicalized by the node.
**Cost if wrong.** An open allowlist lets a signature reach role functions or `approve`; a second encoding of one intent splits its digest.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A2, §3 MG-2, §10 OQ1.
Change (2026-10-20, owner): every state-changing `mtx*` function is relayable, even with no fee: itself a meta-tx entry point or an allowlisted self-call with outer fee `NONE` / `FIXED` 0 (general rule in `contracts/metatx.md`, CTR-MTX-19). Status: BUILT for the confidential tokens (Zether roll-overs, PQZ `mtxRollOver` / `mtxPrepareAcc`), commit `b5e61c96`; the audit of the other contracts found no gap (every other `mtx*` write is an envelope entry point carrying its own signature).
Change (2026-10-08): `transfer` and `pay` are never allowlisted (they are `MetaTransfer`s); rows added for `PqzToken`, `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount` (fee `NONE` only on the latter two). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-1, GC-6, GC-10.
Change (2026-10-27): **review C0-18 (controller proposal (1), owner may override)**: the native-coin `mtxWrapShield` is the **one exception** to "every state-changing `mtx*` is relayable" (owner 2026-10-20, above). It is `payable` and takes the leg from `msg.value`; the relayed self-call carries no value, so a relayer cannot supply the signer's native coin (`NativeValueMismatch`). The holder wraps directly, then relays `mtxShield` (the two-step route accounts.md already records for a UA source). The ERC-20 leg is relayable on `mtxExecute`. The other option, a value-carrying relay path (a `payable` envelope, `msg.value` bound to the authorization, the relayer reimbursed from the signer's balance), was not taken: it adds a payable entry to every token. Written into metatx.md CTR-MTX-19, zether.md CTR-ZTH-34 and pq-zero-knowledge.md §7.11. Status: **done** (review2 T8, branch `review2-fix`; documentation only, no code change).
Change (2026-10-27): **review C0-3 follow-up (controller ruling, owner may override)**: the retired `mtxConfidentialTransferNoBundle` selector, called directly, reverts with empty data (the PQZ precedent, `PqzNormal.t.sol`): a named error would need a fallback stub, which is code-size work (owner: none before Glamsterdam). Through a relayer the allowlist answers `MtxSelectorNotAllowed`, the clear error. Status: **done** (review2 T5 `41b798d9`; recorded in review2 T8).
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2–C6, N1; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the allowlist and `mtxSelectors()` stay for the generic path, and the named entries are not in them. The confidential rows list the explicit signatures of the direct ops (CTR-MTX-29). Since N1 the node does not read the allowlist: its own entry table decides what it relays (NODE-JOB-20).
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner ruling CTR-GOV-01 and the relay rule of the governance spec, G19): a governance operation (`IGovernance` and the powers' own entries) is no allow-list row on a governed contract; a UA reaches it through the router, whose `mtxSelectors()` is empty. Status: BUILT on branch `governance`, pinned by `test/vectors/selector_audit.json` (T13 `d8f2e492`).

### CTR-MTX-20 — Fee classes per selector: AMOUNT(i) and ABSOLUTE
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-20 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A self-call carries no amount field, so the fee basis comes from the selector: `AMOUNT(i)` uses argument `i` with the 1 % cap, `ABSOLUTE` allows only an uncapped `FIXED` amount (or `NONE`), extending the confidential rule to public calls that move no amount; the wallet shows the exact fee.
**Cost if wrong.** A fee on a zero `value` is either always zero or uncheckable; a percentage of a hidden or absent amount is meaningless.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-5, §10 OQ4.
Change (2026-10-08): a `MetaTransaction` has no amount field, so the basis always comes from the selector; on contracts that charge no fee every class admits `NONE` only. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G2, §3 GC-2.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): a named entry carries the fee class of its operation (amount class on `mtxUnwrap` over `wrapped`, absolute on `mtxWrap`; `test_namedEntryFeeClass`); the node and wallets read the struct's fields, not `data`.

### CTR-MTX-21 — mtx names for every signature-authorized entry point
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-21 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Every external function whose authority comes from a subject's signature starts with `mtx` (tokens, `ZetherToken` rollover, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`, `SCaaSDex`), so readers and the node's call table tell signed paths from direct ones at a glance; `executeMetaTransaction` stays as the alias; EIP-712 type names and non-EVM op names are unchanged.
**Cost if wrong.** Mixed names hide which entry points need a signature and which only a caller.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A3, §3 MG-3.
Change (2026-10-08): entry table: every contract on `MetaTxBase` has `mtxExecute`/`mtxBatch`/`cancelNonce`; tokens add `mtxExecuteTransfer`, `mtxBatchTransfer`; `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount` named entries build a `MetaTransaction`. The non-EVM line is unchanged here. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G4, §3 GC-5, GC-6.
Change (2026-10-08): the non-EVM exception is gone — non-EVM families name signed entries `mtx` in their own case (NET-ALL-28). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §6 Q1.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R25; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the entry table is one `mtx*` form per operation on tokens and the router, with `mtxCancelNonce(UAEnvelope, uint256 lane, UASig)` there (Q2); the address forms only on `SmartKeyAccount`; the merged forms on the mandate wallets; `executeMetaTransaction` per R3.

### CTR-MTX-22 — MetaTxBase: the generic base of every SCaaS contract; fee NONE unless overridden
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-22 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — the generic UA path (`uaExecute`, `uaBatch`, `uaCancelNonce`, the UA allowlist, the cancel-used set, the registry immutable) moves from `ERC20MetaTx` into `MetaTxBase` with a virtual `_chargeUAFee` refusing every mode but `NONE`, so `MandateWallet` and any contract on the base take UA signers; balances, `_uaMove` and the typed UA path stay in `ERC20MetaTx`. SPECIFIED (UA-5c). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.12, UP-13, O7, Q8.

**Why.** SCaaS meta-transactions exist so that someone other than the subject pays for a call of any SCaaS contract, not only for moving tokens (owner: a family-tree contract whose edits a service company pays for in native gas). One generic base gives every contract the struct, digest, lanes, ticket, allowlist and `mtxExecute`; a contract that holds no charged balance cannot collect a fee, so `_chargeFee` refuses every mode but `NONE` unless a token overrides it, and the sponsor settles with the user off chain.
**Cost if wrong.** A token-only base forces every other contract to invent its own signed struct and nonce rules (as `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount` did); a fee field such a contract cannot collect would mislead signers.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §1, §2 G2, G3, §3 GC-2, GC-7.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner ruling 2026-11-01, status: documented; built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the UA path moves out of `MetaTxBase` into the new `UAMetaTxBase` (the registry reference, `_mtxCtx`, `uaExecute`, `uaBatch`, `uaCancelNonce`, `uaDigest`, `uaNonce`, `_uaAllowed`, the fee hook `_uaChargeFee` that refuses a fee other than zero by default); `MetaTxBase` holds no UA code, `SmartKeyAccount` and `MandateWallet` stay without a registry. `executeMetaTransaction` stays in `MetaTxBase`. `mtxCancelNonce` is on `MetaTxBase`, declared in `IMetaTx` (`type(IMetaTx).interfaceId` 0xf6695913 -> 0x2f1aa7fe). The earlier text (the UA path "moves down into `MetaTxBase`") is superseded.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R26; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `MetaTxBase` holds the core and `executeMetaTransaction` with its address pipeline (MD-1); `MetaTxAddressBase` / `IMetaTxAddress` hold the address `mtxNonce`, `mtxDigest`, `mtxExecute`, `mtxBatch` and `mtxCancelNonce(Envelope, uint256, bytes)`, inherited through `WalletExecute` by `SmartKeyAccount` only; `UAMetaTxBase` at `registry() == 0` follows [CTR-UA-19](contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-19)'s Change (a derived side reverts `UALedgerOff`, a call whose every side is native runs).

### CTR-MTX-23 — The typed path: MetaTransfer through mtxExecuteTransfer
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-23 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A token transfer is a special case of a meta-transaction (owner); keeping it as a typed struct (`to`, `value`, `entryRef`) lets outside wallets show "send value to to" instead of opaque `data` (owner G1 (b)), and `mtxExecuteTransfer` takes the struct as given so a payment can use a client-chosen lane (owner G6).
**Cost if wrong.** Without the typed struct a transfer would be hex in every outside wallet; without the struct entry a payment could use only `payLane`.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G1, G6, §3 GC-1, GC-4, GC-5.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R4; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the typed transfer path is `mtxExecuteTransfer(MetaTxLib.UAMetaTransfer t, IUARegistry.UASig auth)`, for native and derived ids; the steps stay, step 3 becomes the UA receiver rule (a derived `to` registered and SIGNING); a merged path emits the `UA…` events only (R18).

### CTR-MTX-24 — mtxBatchTransfer beside mtxBatch
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** With transfers in their own struct, `mtxBatch(MetaTransaction[])` can no longer carry the payments the node batches; a typed batch keeps that saving (owner G5 1a) under the same atomic rules, and a batch never mixes the two structs.
**Cost if wrong.** Payments could no longer be batched, or one batch function would have to decode two structs.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G5, §3 GC-5.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R4; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `mtxBatchTransfer(MetaTxLib.UAMetaTransfer[] ts, IUARegistry.UASig[] auths)`, the steps of [CTR-MTX-23](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-23) over `UAMetaTransfer`.

### CTR-MTX-25 — One SigCheck
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-25 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One internal `SigCheck` (ECDSA low-s, ERC-1271 with the gas-cap rule, the HIP-632 hook) serves `MetaTxBase`, `SCaaSDex`, `MandateWallet` and `SmartKeyAccount`; `SigLib`, which has no importer, is deleted. Today the check is written six times and the HIP-632 override four times.
**Cost if wrong.** Copies drift: a fix to the gas cap or the low-s rule lands in one contract and not in the others.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §1, §4.

Change (2026-10-30, **owner ruling D1** — owner 2026-10-30, after the 2026-10-29 EIP-7702 hot-wallet drain: "an EOA must really sign — no delegation at all; an EOA must not run code"; status: current, decided (owner); commits: `no7702` `5ddc577d`, sizes `684f5643`, node `dad611dc`): on the address path a 7702 designator account signs by its own key only, never ERC-1271 through the delegate. `SigCheck.isValid`: `!isContract(signer)` (no code, or code that is exactly `0xef0100 ‖ delegate`, 23 bytes) ⇒ ECDSA low-s only; other code ⇒ ERC-1271 only, caps and the EIP-150 floor unchanged. New helpers `isDesignator` (`extcodesize == 23`, then a 3-byte `extcodecopy` compared with `0xef0100`), `isContract` (as before), `requireNotDelegated` and `error CallerDelegated(address caller)` (defined once, in the library; it reaches the ABI of every token, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`, `SCaaSDex` and `OpenFactory`). Callers: `MetaTxBase` / `MtxPipelineLib` (`mtxExecute*`, the transfers, pay-meta, the UA ledger's native `from`), `SCaaSDex` orders / cancels / `mtxInvalidateNonces`, `mtxWrap` / `uaWrap`, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`; the node's DEX venue `valid_sig` mirrors it (`chain::is_contract`), and the node's gas guard gives a designator payer no ERC-1271 gas floor (`Chain::is_contract_at` replaces `has_code`). Supersedes the 2026-10-28 rule (CTR-MTX-27 change of that date). Why: a delegate's ERC-1271 lets whatever code the account is delegated to — a sweeper after one phishing signature — sign every relayable action as the account (audit A1); the base key is root at protocol level, so key-only adds no restriction a sweeper could not already bypass with the key. Cost if wrong: a 7702 wallet's session keys or passkeys cannot sign for SCaaS; its base key still can. Tests flipped: `SigCheck.t.sol` `test_isValid_7702_ctrUa24` (the delegate is never called: `expectCall` count 0), `UALedger` `test_7702_nativeFrom`, `UAReceiverFee` `test_uaPayReceiverFee_7702Payee`, parity rows `ok_e7702_viaDelegate*` → `err_e7702_viaDelegate*` (12 rows, `PARITY_WRITE=1`), node `a_7702_maker_signs_with_its_key_only`. Gas (parity fixture): designator base-key rows −260, a designator's bad signature −5,640 (the delegate is no longer called), ERC-1271 wallet signers +31 / −246. Source: the EIP-7702 audit of 2026-10-30 (`research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`) §3, §6.

### CTR-MTX-26 — Payment metadata by commitment: mtxPayMeta / uaPayMeta
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-26 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-26 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner asked for metadata on a payment id. `payId = keccak256("scaas.pay.meta" ‖ salt ‖ keccak256(meta))`
lets the existing signature over `entryRef` bind the metadata, so there is no new struct field, no second typehash
(CTR-MTX-11), and `payId` stays unlinkable (CTR-MTX-03). `mtxPayMeta` / `uaPayMeta` publish it in `PaymentMeta`; plain
`mtxPay` with the same id keeps it off chain. Every tier and every non-EVM family (owner 2026-10-26). A new typed
struct with a `meta` field (native wallet display) was rejected: a second struct path and more bytecode in every token.
**Cost if wrong.** Wallets show only the opaque `entryRef`, so a connector that skips the commitment check shows the
user metadata the signature does not bind.
**Source.** `research/mtx-relay-fees.md` §2, §5 (owner answers 2026-10-26: "OK, vậy phần mtxPayMeta như vậy đi").
Change (2026-10-27, controller call, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T7 fix 1): the `meta` body encodings are fixed and family-neutral (one rule for every chain kind) inside `meta = abi.encode(uint16 schema, bytes body)`: schema 1 the raw UTF-8 bytes; schema 2 `abi.encode(string creditorRef, string invoiceNo, uint64 dueDate)`, `dueDate` in Unix seconds; schema 3 `abi.encode(uint256 chainId, bytes32 target, bytes32 callHash)`, `target` as 32 bytes (an EVM address left-padded with zeros, other families their native 32-byte id), `callHash = keccak256(callData)` (research §3); schema 4's inner layout (KEM wrap ‖ AES-256-GCM) stays undefined, a later client item. The shared vectors `smartcontracts/vectors/metatx/paymeta.json` follow them; `long_body_4096` is a hash vector only. Source add: `superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-design.md` §6.1.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27/28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T15): TON only. (1) Pay-meta is the plain `OP_PAY` `SignedOp` with `params = salt:uint256 ^meta` (`meta` as snake bytes): the payer's jetton wallet requires `payRef == metaPayId(salt, meta)`, `lane == payLane(payRef)`, `nonce == 0` (else exit `E_PARAMS` 713; a malformed `params` is TVM's cell underflow 9), emits the external-out `PaymentMeta { master, payId, meta: ^Cell }` (opcode `0x9b1c0d04`) right after `MetaTransactionExecuted`, in the payer wallet's transaction, so it precedes the payee wallet's `PaymentSettled` in logical time, and pays as before; `params = null` is today's `OP_PAY` unchanged. `metaPayId` / `payLane` hash with Tact's `keccak256(Slice)` over the snake chain (each cell's data along its first ref, so the chunking does not matter); getters `get_meta_pay_id(salt, meta)`, `get_pay_lane(p)` on the wallet. (2) The once-set is the payer's own wallet lanes, so once per `(payer, payId)`: another payer's pre-burn of the same `payId` does not block the victim; a plain `OP_PAY` on the same `payRef` / lane shares it (exit `E_NONCE` 706). As every TON lane, the entry lives two `LANE_TTL` windows (30 days each), longer than any op may be valid. (3) Size: no contract cap; measured through a W5R1 lane in @ton/sandbox 0.45.0, 38,100 B (300 snake cells) settles and the 301st cell aborts the emulator whatever the TON attached; config param 43 bounds the lane's external message at 65,535 B and depth 512. The node's `max_pay_meta_bytes` cap (2,048 B) is far below, and `long_body_4096` (4,192 B) also settles on TON. Fees of the payer wallet's transaction at the node's 0.15 TON attach: plain pay 2,792,811 nanoton (27,687 gas); pay-meta 0 B 3,235,545 (32,573), 160 B 3,340,012 (32,760), 2,048 B 4,631,412 (35,527), 4,192 B 6,097,278 (38,663). (4) Adapter (`scaas-node` `ton.rs` `pay_params`): `op.kind` none = plain pay (refused if it carries `extra.params`), `"pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta` hex) checked before any getter, any other kind refused. A TON pay job names no master (the job source keeps the token list, review H1), so the pay-meta job, as every family's, has no token check of its own. (5) The wallet code changed, so every jetton wallet and master address changed: `ton-vectors.json` and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated (test-only chains, no migration).
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27/28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16): TON only, two T15 follow-ups. (1) The wallet refuses a pay-meta whose `meta` is not a plain snake (a cell with more than one ref anywhere along the first-ref chain) with `E_PARAMS` 713 (`common.tact` `requireSnake`): Tact's `keccak256(Slice)` follows only the first ref of each cell, so a second ref would be unsigned yet emitted in `PaymentMeta`. (2) `jetton.spec.ts` › meta size limit asserts only that the largest settling `meta` is ≥ 4,192 B; the binary search runs only with `TON_META_SIZE_SEARCH=1` (the measured 38,100 B = 300 snake cells in @ton/sandbox 0.45.0 stands, entry above). The wallet code changed again, so `ton-vectors.json` and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated (test-only chains).
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T19): client rules from the family builds. TON: a payee wallet bounce leaves `PaymentMeta` emitted without `PaymentSettled` and burns `(payer, payId)` for good, so `PaymentMeta` alone is never proof of payment and a payer signs again with a new salt (T15). Solana: the once-set is the payer's lane PDA, so it lasts until the lane is pruned after `valid_until`; the same `payId` can then be signed and settled again. Aptos (added in the final fix wave, final review M9): the once-set is the payer Account's lane, pruned permissionlessly 30 days after its `valid_until` (`meta::prune`, `PRUNE_DELAY_S`), so it lasts until the prune; the same `payId` can then be signed and settled again. TON (same): the once-set is the payer wallet's lane, which rotates out after one to two `LANE_TTL` (30 days each, `rotateLanes`), so it lasts until the rotation; the same `payId` can then be signed and settled again. On all three a signed payment never replays (`valid_until` bounds it); whether a permanent once-set is wanted instead is on the owner rulings list (final-review.md item 8). Soroban: the once-set is `(from, pay_ref)` (T10 fix 1). The network documents carry the per-family sections (networks/*.md "Pay-meta and relay fee"). Settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (final review owner rulings list item 8): once per (payer, payId) until the lane is pruned / rotated is accepted as family behaviour on Solana, Aptos and TON.
Change (2026-11-09, **owner rulings 2026-11-09**, plan T83; status: current; commit: ua-mtx-merge T83 `ba280ade`): **`payNo` as `bytes32`, `PayMeta.save`, and the on-chain pay records.** The rulings, each as recommended, superseding the `string` form of the pay-meta-tax spec's O15: (1) `PayMeta.payNo` is `bytes32` (was `string`, at most 256 bytes): `0` = none; the canonical form a UUIDv7 right-aligned (its 128 bits in the low 16 bytes, as `MetaTxLib.pad` places an address); any other 32-byte id accepted; the contract never parses it; `PayNoTooLong` and the clients' UTF-8 / control / bidi rules for `payNo` go; UUIDv7 recommended (owner 2026-11-09): unique without coordination, time-ordered, no business sequence numbers on chain. (2) The event is `PaymentMeta(bytes32 indexed payId, bytes32 indexed payNo, bool save, uint16 schema, bytes body)`. (3) The tag is `scaas.pay.meta.v3`: `metaPayId = keccak256(abi.encodePacked("scaas.pay.meta.v3", salt, keccak256(abi.encode(payNo, save, schema, body))))`, `PayMeta { bytes32 salt; bytes32 payNo; bool save; uint16 schema; bytes body; }`. (4) A readable document number stays off chain or in `body` (schema 2 or 4). (5) On-chain pay records (option 2): logs are not kept for ever (EIP-4444), so an ERP asks the chain by `payNo` alone with `eth_call`; per token, ERC-7201 `scaas.pay.records`: `mapping(bytes32 payNo => PayRecord[])`, `PayRecord { bytes32 to; uint192 amount; uint64 blockNumber; }` (two slots), written by every public pay entry whose `PayMeta.save` is set, after the transfer (`save` the payer's choice, option A, signed inside the commitment; `save` with `payNo == 0` a shape error; `save == false` costs what a pay cost); `amount` what the payee received, `≥ 2^192` reverts; keyed by `payNo` only (an ERP may roll its addresses); no sum on chain; views `paymentCount`, `paymentsOf`; anyone may append, the reader filters by `to`; confidential pays not recorded; no node API. (6) Cost accepted (about +300 k / +200 k); measured (forge, fresh lane, fee `NONE`): `save` off 202,814, first 534,203 (+331,389), later 436,300 (+233,486). (7) Every family follows in its own round. Controller calls in the build (owner may override): the overflow error is a named `PayRecordAmount(uint256)` in the token ABI; the node's `max_pay_meta_bytes` counts `body` only; the node JSON names `pay_no` (0x-hex) and `meta_save`. Status: BUILT on the EVM (T83 `ba280ade`, gate `5e5fbce2`; the pay-meta-tax build T37–T42 before it); the separate `mtxPayMeta` / `uaPayMeta` entries are gone on the EVM; the non-EVM families keep the v1 form until their round.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): pay-meta-tax PT-2 (owner O2, O11, O12; T37 `3740b85e`, the tag then `scaas.pay.meta.v2`, v3 since T83): `PayMeta` is the required last parameter of every pay entry (`mtxPay`, `mtxPayReceiverFee`, `payWithFee`, `payWithFeeToUA`, `mtxPayWithTax`, `payWithTax`, the mandate wallets' pays); a non-zero salt, schema 0 iff the body is empty; `entryRef == metaPayId(meta)`; `PaymentMeta` always emitted, before the payment's events; `mtxPayMeta` / `uaPayMeta` and the off-chain path are gone. O12: the generic `mtxExecuteTransfer` lands a payment without `PaymentMeta`, reconciled off chain ([CTR-MTX-31](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-31)). Schema 2 has no `invoiceNo` (O15).

### CTR-MTX-27 — RelayFeeRouter: token fee for a fee-less call
- old: typed-signing:TS-D19 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-26 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-27 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner wants a payer to pay, in an mtx token, for a fee-less call such as a PqChat message: the relayer
pays the gas, and the payer pays the relayer. Tender's deposit (CTR-TND-01) already binds a payment to an action
through `entryRef` and the relayer binding. A stateless router generalises it to any target, without token logic in
the target and without changing any token: `ref` commits to (chain, target, call bytes); the payment is bound to the
router as relayer; the router runs the call through an unprivileged executor, then the payment. Owner answers
(2026-10-26): the controller names it and places it in `src/metatx/` with a `DeployBase` CREATE2 deployment; open to
every relayer by default; public balances only; every token tier; non-EVM too (GRAM by escrow); PQ payers sign twice
(option (a), after first picking (c)); no budget mode for now. Rejected: a pay-and-call hook in every token (ERC-1363
style: a new outbound call and bytecode in each token); one combined PQ signature with a transient verified mark
(option (c), studied). CTR-MTX-16's "no generic forwarder" stands: the router grants no authority.
**Cost if wrong.** If the router called targets itself, a `callData` could execute another router-bound payment
through a token, with no call behind it.
**Source.** `research/mtx-relay-fees.md` §3, §5 (owner answers 2026-10-26; "Có, viết spec luôn đi").
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T9 fix 1): (1) the router refuses a target without code, `RelayTargetNoCode(target)`: a counterfactual target (a `SmartKeyAccountFactory` prediction, a CREATE2 clone) relayed before its deploy would succeed as an empty call, pay the fee and burn the lane (against CTR-MTX-13); CTR-MTX-27 gets a ninth conformance item for every family: the target must exist as code / an executable program / an instantiated contract at relay time. (2) `RelayFeePaid.payee` is `bytes32` (a padded address, or the UA id of a derived payee), like `payer`; the other families' events follow this form. (3) The router refuses `t.to == EXECUTOR` (UA: `pad(EXECUTOR)`), and clients never pay or approve the executor. Cost if wrong: a target deployed in the same transaction before the relay is still accepted; a relay cannot pre-pay a target's deploy. Source add: `superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-design.md` §7.1, §7.2.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T10 fix 1): Soroban only. (3) The token's `PayRef` set is keyed by `(from, pay_ref)` for `pay` and `pay_meta`, the per-payer lane of the EVM (`payLane(ref)` in the payer's nonce space), so nobody can pre-burn another payer's `ref` / `payId` with a 0-amount `pay(attacker, attacker, 0, ref, ..)`. (4) The Soroban `relay` takes a payer-signed `salt: BytesN<32>` that enters `ref` (Soroban's call bytes are not unique, the target's auth lives in auth entries): `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ network id ‖ xdr(target) ‖ keccak256(xdr((func, args))) ‖ salt)`, so the same payer can fee-pay two identical calls. (5) Before a relay-fee job the node checks the configured router, a registered token and `amount >= relay_fee.min_amount` (spec §9 names no key; `params.relay_fee = { router, min_amount }`, default 1); the indexer decoding of `PaymentMeta` / `RelayFeePaid` and the `max_pay_meta_bytes` config move to Task 17 for every family. (6) The relayer's `require_auth` is not satisfied by the transaction source alone: the node adds an explicit `SourceAccount` auth entry rooted at the `relay` call.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T11): Solana only. (1) `relay_fee`'s `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ Config.network ‖ target program ‖ keccak256(call) ‖ salt)` with `call = target ‖ u8 n ‖ (pubkey ‖ is_signer ‖ is_writable)×n ‖ data` (the account count added to the spec's preimage so the account list and the data cannot be re-split) and `salt = args.extra`, the payer-signed `MetaOp.extra` (no new argument: a Solana target's own authorisation lives outside its data, so two identical calls need distinct refs). (2) The pay-meta and relay-fee once-set is the payer's lane PDA `[b"lane", Account, lane]`, already per payer: nobody can pre-burn a payer's `payId` / `ref`. (3) New errors `PayMetaShape` (pay-meta `pay_ref` / lane / nonce mismatch), `RelayFeeShape`, `RelayTargetNoCode` (the target is not an executable program). (4) Open mode pays the lane's ATA directly, so `PaymentSettled.to` and `RelayFeePaid.payee` name the lane (no hop through the marker, which never holds tokens and never signs). (5) No executor: `scaas` invokes the target with plain `invoke` (no PDA signer seeds). Because `invoke` forwards the outer transaction's signer privileges, `relay_fee` refuses on chain (`RelayFeeShape`, before the CPI) any target account flagged signer, the lane or any co-signer, so the router grants no authority to whichever relayer submits it (CTR-MTX-16; T11 fix 1). The node refuses the same, and the lane as a target account, before simulating. Cost if wrong: a target that needs a signer (a rent payer) cannot be fee-relayed through the generic `relay_fee`.
Change (2026-10-27, owner 2026-10-27; status: current; commit: metatx-split T11 fix 2): owner 2026-10-27: Solana uses static relay_fee_<entry> wrappers (as Sui/Aptos); generic CPI relay_fee kept for external programs. Wrapped: `manage_signed`, `mandate_open`, `mandate_revoke_signed`, `mandate_close_signed`, `cancel_signed`, `invalidate_nonces_signed` (every fee-less signed entry of `scaas` but `open_passkey`, excluded as a scope choice: account creation is not among the entries Sui / Aptos wrap, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; `settle` is a trade with its own market fee and the pay entries are payments). Each runs the entry's body in-process, then the router payment (marker as relayer, open mode pays the lane), atomically. `ref` uses the Solana preimage with target = `scaas` and `call` = the entry's instruction as if sent alone (declared accounts with their flags, `discriminator ‖ Borsh(arguments)`, its `auth` included), salt `args.extra`. To nest beside any entry's accounts, `RelayPay` no longer reads instruction arguments (`subject` and `lane_pda` are derived, checked and the lane PDA created in the shared body); `manage_signed` persists its Account before returning so a wrapper's payment reads the new key set. The self-target refusal of the generic `relay_fee` stays. Settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 5): the generic CPI `relay_fee` for external programs is kept next to the static wrappers.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T11 fix 3): the wrapper ref hashes the router marker in the lane slot (lane-agnostic, as Sui/Aptos): `call`'s first account (the inner entry's `lane`, flags as declared) is the marker PDA `[b"relayfee"]`, so the payer signs before any lane is known, open mode stays open to every relayer, and a job moved to another lane still settles. Cost if wrong: none found; the lane is still the transaction's signer and the entry's rent payer.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T12): Cosmos only. (1) `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ chain id bytes ‖ target (canonical address bytes, 32 for a contract) ‖ keccak256(msg))`, `msg` the exact bytes the executor sends; no salt: the target sees the unprivileged `relayexec` and no funds, so nothing outside `msg` authorises the call, and the SCaaS fee-less signed entries carry their signature and nonce / once-ref inside `msg` (token `Relay` / `RelayPayMeta`, mandate `PayUnderMandate`, DEX `Settle`); the entries authorised by `info.sender` (mandate `Revoke` / `Withdraw`, DEX admin) fail through the router, so nothing is paid. (2) The router refuses a target without contract info (`relayfee: target is not an instantiated contract`), `op.to == executor`, and non-empty funds; the executor refuses funds and every caller but its router. (3) Re-entry into the router is refused by a stored flag set in `Relay` and cleared in the reply of its last message (CTR-MTX-27 conformance; CosmWasm allows re-entry). (4) The router computes its executor's address with `instantiate2_address(code checksum, router, "scaas.relayexec")` at instantiate (its one stored item besides the flag). (5) `relay_fee_paid` (`ref`, `target`, `token`, `payer`, `payee`, `amount`, bech32 `Addr`s) is the router's own event, so wasmd lists it before the sub-messages' events; it exists only when the whole transaction succeeded. (6) The token's lanes are already per payer (`NONCES[(from, lane)]`), so `RelayPayMeta` and the router payment are once per `(payer, payId / ref)` and an attacker's 0-amount pay of the same id uses its own lane. (7) Node: `op.kind = "pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta`) builds `relay_pay_meta`; `op.kind = "relay_fee"` (`op.contract` = `params.relay_fee.router`, `op.extra.target`, `op.extra.msg` hex) builds the router's `Relay` after the policy, ref, lane, nonce and relayer checks; a `params.relay_fee.router` that is set but is not a lowercase 32-byte contract address of the chain's prefix is a startup error.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T12 fix 1): Cosmos only. (1) The router and the executor have no admin: a migrated router is the bound relayer of every payment signed to it and could settle one without running the call (CTR-MTX-13). `Relay` queries the router's own `ContractInfo` and refuses while `admin` is set (`relayfee: the router has an admin`; a failed query fails closed); the executor is instantiated with `admin: None`; deploy tooling instantiates `relayfee` with `--no-admin`; clients check `ContractInfo.admin == None` before signing `relayer = router`. (2) The router as its own target is refused by the re-entry flag. (3) A `params.relay_fee.min_amount` that is not a non-negative integer is a node startup error, like an unparsable `router`. (4) `build-wasm.sh` links with `-C link-arg=--allow-undefined` (cosmwasm-std 3.0.10 declares its host imports without `wasm_import_module = "env"`, and newer rustc no longer passes the flag) and then fails unless every wasm import is a cosmwasm-std `env` host function (`cosmwasm-check` when installed, else a stdlib import-section parser).
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T13): Sui only. (1) `meta::relay_pay_meta` derives `pay_ref = meta_pay_id(salt, meta)`, `lane = pay_lane(pay_ref)`, `nonce = 0` on chain and runs `relay_pay`'s body (a private `settle` shared with `relay_pay` and `pay_routed`), emitting `PaymentMeta` before `PaymentSettled`; the once-set is the payer's own `Account.lanes`, so once per `(payer, payId)` and another payer's pay of the same id uses its own table. (2) `scaas::relayfee` has one static wrapper per fee-less signed entry (`relay_manage`, `relay_revoke_with_sig`, `relay_cancel`, `relay_invalidate_nonces`); each runs the entry, then `meta::pay_routed` (`public(package)`), which fixes `pay_ref = ref`, `lane = pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce = 0`, `relayer = marker` on chain, so a payment settles only for the call it was signed for; `dex::cancel`'s `false` aborts the relay (`ECallRefused`). (3) `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ network ‖ original package id ‖ keccak256(call) ‖ salt)`, `call` = BCS of the entry's name and every argument (objects as ids, the entry's `Auth` included), `salt` = the payment's payer-signed `extra`; no sender and no lane, so any relayer may submit. (4) Marker = the shared `RelayFee` object (created in `init`); plain `relay_pay` / `relay_pay_meta` refuse a payment bound to it (`EWrongRelayer`: no sender is an object); open mode pays `ctx.sender()`, the marker is never paid. (5) manage / cancel / invalidate pay from the account the entry names (Move allows one `&mut` per object in a PTB command); paying another coin or another payer's account for these needs a further wrapper variant (not built). (6) Upgrade authority: `relayfee` is a module of the `scaas` package, so it shares the token's `UpgradeCap` and cannot be upgraded separately; the router's trust equals the token's, so no code change. NET-SUI-15 (immutable package) is still SPECIFIED; as built the publisher keeps the `UpgradeCap`. (7) Node: `op.kind = "pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta`) builds `relay_pay_meta`; `op.kind = "relay_fee"` (`op.extra.call` = the call bytes, `op.extra.registry`, `op.extra.mandate_coin_type` for revoke) builds `relayfee::relay_<entry>` after the checks: payment relayer = `params.relay_fee.router` (the `RelayFee` id), registry registered and the paying account derived from it and the payer, `amount ≥ min_amount`, canonical call bytes of a wrapped entry naming the paying account, `pay_ref == ref`, `lane == pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce == 0`; an unparsable `router` or `min_amount` is a startup error. (8) Fix 1 (controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; commit: metatx-split T13 fix 1): `RelayFee` exists only if `relayfee` is in the package's first publish (Sui runs no `init` for a module added by an upgrade); for manage / cancel / invalidate the payer is the call's own account, so a sponsor needs `_from` variants (not built); the node refuses a plain pay / pay-meta whose `to` is the configured router marker, and a malformed `tokens[].address` is a startup error. Item (6) settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 9): the package is made immutable at deploy (`deploy.sh sui` destroys the `UpgradeCap`), so nobody can upgrade token or router.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T14): Aptos only.
