(1) `meta::relay_pay_meta` (`package entry`) derives `pay_ref = meta_pay_id(salt, meta)`, `lane = pay_lane(pay_ref)`, `nonce = 0` on chain and runs `relay_pay`'s body (a private `settle` shared with `relay_pay` and `pay_routed`), emitting `PaymentMeta` before `PaymentSettled`; the view `pay_meta_check` is its `pay_check` twin; the once-set is the payer's own `Account.lanes`, so once per `(payer, payId)`. (2) `scaas::relayfee` has one `package entry` wrapper per fee-less signed entry (`relay_manage_signed`, `relay_mandate_open`, `relay_revoke_signed`, `relay_cancel_signed`, `relay_invalidate_nonces_signed`); each runs the entry, then `meta::pay_routed` (`package`), which fixes `pay_ref = ref`, `lane = pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce = 0`, `relayer = marker` on chain; `dex::cancel_signed`'s body moved to `package fun dex::cancel(…): bool` and a `false` (order already closed) aborts the relay (`ECALL_REFUSED`). (3) `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ chain_id (1 byte) ‖ @scaas ‖ keccak256(call) ‖ salt)`: Aptos's `MetaOp` domain carries a `u8` chain id, not network bytes, so `chain` is that byte; `call` = BCS of the entry's name and every argument (signature included, lane signer excluded), `salt` = the payment's payer-signed `extra`; no sender, no lane. (4) Marker = `object::create_object_address(&@scaas, b"scaas.relayfee")`, a derived address no transaction can sign for: plain `relay_pay` / `relay_pay_meta` refuse a payment bound to it (`EWRONG_RELAYER`); open mode pays the lane; the marker is never paid; nothing is stored, so `relayfee` needs no `init_module`. (5) Any Account pays (no Sui-style one-account limit). (6) Upgrade authority: `relayfee` is a module of the `scaas` package, so the code object's owner can upgrade it only together with `meta`; the router's trust equals the token's, so no code change; NET-APT-20 (immutable) is still SPECIFIED, as built `upgrade_policy = "compatible"`. (7) Node: `op.kind = "pay_meta"` (`op.salt`, `op.meta`) builds `relay_pay_meta` (or calls `pay_meta_check` while the Account is not open); `op.kind = "relay_fee"` (`op.extra.call` = the call bytes, optional `op.ref`) builds `relayfee::relay_<entry>` after the checks: payment relayer = `params.relay_fee.router`, which must equal `relayfee::marker()` of the package (else a startup error), the asset a registered token, `amount ≥ min_amount`, canonical call bytes of a wrapped entry, `pay_ref == ref`, `lane == pay_lane(ref)`, `nonce == 0`; a plain pay / pay-meta to the marker is refused; a relay-fee job whose payer's Account is not open is refused (simulation cannot run it); a malformed `tokens[].address` or `min_amount` is a startup error. (8) Fix 1 (controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; commit: metatx-split T14 fix 1): the Aptos node refuses a plain pay / pay-meta to `relayfee::marker()` of the package whether or not a router is configured (the marker is derived, so it is always known); on Aptos and Sui an unknown `op.kind` is refused (only none = plain pay, `pay_meta`, `relay_fee`), so a typo never burns the `(payer, payId)` lane as a plain pay without publishing `meta`. Item (6) settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 9): `upgrade_policy = "immutable"`, so nobody can upgrade `relayfee` or `meta`.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-27/28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16): TON only (spec §7.2 TON row). (1) Escrow, not a call: `ScaasRelayFee` (`relayfee.tact`) takes `RelayCall { target, call, salt, payWallet, payOp, payAuth, payStateInit?, master, deadline }`, recomputes `ref = keccak256("scaas.relayfee" ‖ global id:int32 ‖ target wc:int8 ‖ target hash ‖ cellHash(call) ‖ salt)` (the representation hash covers every ref of `call`; `salt` is payer-chosen and signed through `payRef`; no sender or lane, any relayer may submit), checks the router-bound `OP_PAY` (`payRef == ref`, `lane == payLane(ref)`, `nonce == 0`, `relayer == to == router`, `amount > 0`, `payWallet == walletAddress(from, master)`; exit 741), escrows it under `(from, ref)` (742 while pending or while that payer wallet has a payment in flight) and sends the payer wallet the `SignedOp` with `params = null`. (2) Provable success: a one-shot `RelayExecutor` (per router, payer, salt; the target sees it, never the router) sends the call and right after it a bounceable `RelayProbe`; TON's in-order delivery per account pair makes the probe's bounce, with no call bounce before it, the proof the call ran → release to the relayer and `RelayFeePaid` (`0x9b1c0d05`); the call's bounce (also: a target with no account) → refund. The call carries at least config param 21's `gas_limit` priced by `getComputeFee` + 0.02 TON, so a failed call can always bounce (no silent failure). This replaces the brief's "release on the target's excess": an excess can be forged by any transfer to the target that names the router as response destination. (3) Timeout: `deadline` in `(now, now + 3,600 s]` (743); anyone's `RelayRefund { from, ref }` at or after it refunds a funded escrow or drops an unfunded one (745 before, 744 unknown). Release and refund delete the escrow first: exclusive; a late report pays nothing; the router holds no jetton after settlement (tested) and its TON moves by < 0.001 TON per relay. Refund wins whenever success is not provable (a target that accepts the probe). (4) Per payer: escrow keys and the payer's wallet lane are per `(payer, ref)`, so a copied `ref` paid first by an attacker is its own escrow and the victim's relay still settles (tested); the brief's "one pending call per target" is not built (the executor makes the outcome attributable without it). (5) Notifications other than the escrow's own (a plain transfer, a payment whose escrow timed out, a foreign wallet) are handed back to the notifying wallet's sender; R18: a `call` that is a `SignedOp` / `MandatePay` naming the router as relayer is refused (707), and so is the probe opcode. (6) No admin and no upgrade path: the router's and the executor's code are fixed at deploy. (7) Adapter (`ton.rs`): `op.kind = "relay_fee"` checked before any getter (router = `params.relay_fee.router`, startup error if unparsable; master in the chain's `tokens`; `amount >= min_amount`, default 1, non-integer = startup error; the binding to `(target, call, salt)`), then the payer wallet derivation, the signature simulation and `get_relay_value`; deadline = now + 600 s. `tx_status` follows the escrow (`get_escrow_state`): pending while open, mined once `RelayFeePaid` of the ref is seen, reverted when refunded; past `deadline` the lane sends `RelayRefund` (retried every 120 s). A plain pay to the router and a present but non-string `op.kind` are refused. Measured (sandbox): `get_relay_value` 306,666,673 nanoton; release 15 transactions, 16,684,899 nanoton fees; refund 15 transactions, 15,540,542.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner delegated "choose the best option"; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16 fix 1): TON only, supersedes items (2) and (5) of the T16 entry above. (1) Release only on a positive acknowledgment from a known SCaaS target. The review reproduced that a call whose action phase fails gets no bounce (only sends with mode +16 bounce on action failure), rolls its state back, and still let the probe bounce, so the T16 rule "probe bounce without a call bounce = success" released the fee for a call that did not happen. Now: the router serves only targets whose `RelayCall.targetInit` derives the target and whose code hash is the SCaaS jetton wallet's or the Mandate's (compiled into the router), and only their fee-less entries (wallet `set_key` / `revoke`, Mandate owner `revoke`); each sends `RelayAck { digest }` to its sender as its last message before the excess, and a failed action phase sends no message at all; the executor releases iff the ack (sender = target, digest = the call's MetaOp) arrives before the probe's bounce, refunds on a probe bounce without one or on the call's bounce, and the timeout refunds. The ack echoes the executed MetaOp's digest, not the executor's lt as the ruling sketched: the target cannot know the lt, and the digest binds the ack to this very call (the executor sends nothing else that acks). (2) The call's `SignedOp.responseDestination` must be the payer's executor (on chain, 741), so a payer-chosen target cannot keep the relayer's call TON (review important 1), and a copied `ref` cannot be relayed by another payer. The node also prices the exposure: a relay-fee job's fee × `params.relay_fee.min_ton_value[master]` (nanoton per base unit; no price feed exists) must reach the `get_relay_value` the lane sends, else the job is refused (spec §9). (3) Every TON amount is priced at run time: `getComputeFee` of fixed gas units (×2 the measured use), `getForwardFee` of each message's `computeDataSize`, `getStorageFee` for the router's rent; the call is sent with `SendPayFwdFeesSeparately` and carries `max(config param 21's gas_limit priced + its bounce, the served entry's own floor: the wallet's 0.05 TON, the Mandate's 0.1 TON)`; `get_relay_value(body)` and `get_refund_value` replace the fixed constants (review important 2). (4) Settlement transfers carry a `queryId` (a ring of the last 16); a bounce from the router's wallet restores the escrow as release-owed / refund-owed and any `RelayRefund` sends it again at any time; `RelayRefund` needs `get_refund_value` (714 below; review important 3). (5) The node identifies a closed escrow positively by the router's `RelayFeePaid` / new `RelayFeeRefunded { ref, payer, amount }` (`0x9b1c0d06`, also emitted with amount 0 when an unfunded entry is dropped) of this `(payer, ref)`; neither seen = pending, never "refunded" by absence (review important 4). (6) The router reserves its prior balance in every handler and keeps each escrow's rent from the relay, so it never pays for relays and never freezes (minor 3). (7) Recorded (minor 1): one payment of a payer wallet in flight at a time; a griefer can hold that slot for one round trip per spam (garbage auth bounces quickly): liveness only. (8) Recorded (minor 2): a served target always refuses the probe, so a swallowed probe (executor dust waiting for a timeout) does not happen with the served code set; the dust of a probe that bounces after a call bounce stays in the executor (≈ 0.001 TON). (9) Recorded (minor 4): success = the target's handling transaction was acknowledged; the messages it sends on (a revoke's cancel to the DEX) are not covered. Measured (sandbox, @ton/sandbox 0.45.0): `get_relay_value` 167,085,766 nanoton; release 16 transactions, 24,900,308 nanoton fees; refund 15 transactions, 23,524,374. The wallet and Mandate code changed (the ack), so `ton-vectors.json` and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated. (10) Recorded residual (final review M8, recorded in the metatx-split final fix wave): the settlement ring of (4) keeps the last `SETTLE_RING = 16` settlements (`relayfee.tact:106`, `settle`); more than 16 settlements between a settlement's send and its bounce evict the entry, the bounce is then ignored and the tokens stay in the router's jetton wallet with no admin to recover them. Rare: only an underfunded settlement bounces, and the bounce arrives in the next transaction (networks/ton.md). Scope settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 4): only the SCaaS jetton wallet's set_key / revoke and the Mandate owner revoke, open mode only, a 3,600 s timeout, no third-party targets.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T16 fix 2): TON only. (1) A signed revoke runs at most once (NET-TON-18, BUILT): the wallet accepted `next == nonce` or `next == nonce + 1` for a revoke and set `next + 1`, so a revoke that ran in its first form (the order never left: `next == nonce`) could be replayed by anyone in the second form, spending `nonce + 1` and sending a `CancelTag` (reproduced through the relay router, where the replay was also released). Every revoke now leaves its lane at `nonce + 2`; the fix is in the wallet, so the direct (non-relayed) path is fixed too; the Mandate's owner revoke checks its lane exactly (`used == nonce`) and had no such replay. (2) Node attribution: `RelayFeeRefunded` gains `relayer` (the escrow's), and the node counts only events of its own relay: `RelayFeePaid` with `payee` = its lane, `RelayFeeRefunded` with `relayer` = its lane, a release winning over a refund of the same `(payer, ref)` (paid at most once; a refund of ours next to it is an earlier attempt). So a third party's copied `RelayCall` after a release (refunded with amount 0 to its own relayer) and another relayer's release are never reported as ours; our own amount-0 refund (our payment refused or dropped) still closes our job, which ignoring all amount-0 events would have left pending forever. The router does not refuse a settled `(payer, ref)`: the payer wallet's lane does (the copy bounces at nonce 0). (3) TON that reaches the executor after its report (a revoke-cancel's excess, about 0.36 TON in the review's run) goes on to the relayer (`RelayExec.relayer`); a revoke-cancel's call carries `MIN_SIGNED_OP_TON + forwardTon` at least, so it is not under-funded. (4) The settlement ring keeps the escrow without its `call` (rent). (5) Wording: the ack goes just before the entry's own outgoing message (the excess, or a revoke's cancel transfer), not always before the excess. The wallet code changed, so `ton-vectors.json` (now with the event layouts) and the TON cases of `mesh-envelope-v1.2.json` were regenerated.
Change (2026-10-28, controller rulings 2026-10-27/28 widening Task 17, owner may override; status: current; commits: metatx-split T17a 9777679f, T17b 1683d2ac, T17c 3a98e74a, T17d 399e9e77, T17e ea3a0330, T17f d784f264): the node (`scaas-node`), every family. (A) `guard::ERC1271_FLOOR` = 21,000 + (400,000 · 64/63 + 5,000) · 64/63 + `ERC1271_PREFIX` = 467,904: the ERC-1271 call of a `SmartKeyAccount` signer now runs two frames below the token (token → `MtxPipelineLib` → wallet); `ERC1271_PREFIX` = 29,026 is forge's measured minimum relayer call gas of a `SmartKeyAccount`-signed `mtxExecute` (446,904, `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-node-floor.txt`, Task 8) minus the two-frame term (417,878); calldata gas still comes from the simulation (+20 %); pinned by `erc1271_floor_covers_forge_minimum` (reads the log). (B) One config key set for every family: `params.relay_fee = { router, min_amount (default 1), relay_bound_payee (default false), min_ton_value (TON), min_lamports_value (Solana) }` and `params.max_pay_meta_bytes` (default 2,048), read by `ChainCfg::relay_params` and checked in `Config::validate`; a set-but-invalid value (an unparsable router in the family's address form, a non-integer or negative amount, a non-integer cap, a non-boolean flag) is a startup error in every adapter (Soroban fell back to `min_amount` 1 and dropped an unparsable router; Solana clamped a negative amount). (C) One `op.kind` rule (`adapter::op_kind`): absent / null = the plain pay, `pay_meta` / `relay_fee` (Solana's wrappers ride `relay_fee` with `extra.entry`) = those, any other string or a present non-string (`7`, `true`, `{}`) is refused, and a kind-less job carrying `salt` / `meta` is refused; EVM and Hedera jobs: `kind` absent, `metatx` or `call`. (D) Never a plain pay or pay-meta to the router, marker or executor: EVM (router, executor = the router's first `CREATE`, `router.create(1)`), Soroban (router), Solana (the marker PDA and the program id), Cosmos (router and its `relayexec`, read once with `QueryMsg::Executor`); Sui, Aptos, TON as before. (E) A relay-fee job is relayed only when the fee reaches the node's lane (open mode, or a payee bound to the lane) and is at least `min_amount`; a fee bound to anyone else is refused unless `relay_bound_payee = true`, and then counts as sponsored (no `min_amount`); TON relays are always open (the escrow releases to the relaying lane). (F) The fee covers what the adapter can price: `amount >= min_amount` everywhere (the operator's price of the gas; no token price feed, no gas price or block limit assumed); Solana: when the payment's `LanePda` (56 B) does not exist yet and the fee is the node's, `amount × min_lamports_value[mint]` must reach its rent-exempt minimum (`getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption`), and a mint without a price gets no such job; TON: `min_ton_value` (T16). Not priced (recorded): a first-use recipient ATA or a lazily opened Account on Solana; Soroban / Sui / Aptos storage and rent are inside the simulated fee. (G) The indexer of every family decodes `PaymentMeta` and `RelayFeePaid` and joins them (`indexer::join_pay_events`): only the expected token's `PaymentSettled` proves a payment; a `PaymentMeta` gives its `meta` to the next `PaymentSettled` of the same token, transaction and payId (and `from` where the event names one); a `RelayFeePaid` from the configured router gives `relay_target` / `relay_payee` to its token's `PaymentSettled` with the same `(from, ref)`, amount and payee (or the router, open mode); never by id alone; neither is sent as a row of its own, because the client's `chain_event_ingest` (the ERP side) accepts only `PaymentSettled`, `MetaTransactionExecuted` and `Transfer` and reads new keys only as fields (`meta`, `relay_target`, `relay_payee`). TON: `PaymentMeta` has no `from`, so it takes the payer from the same transaction's authenticated `Executed` and waits (in memory, bounded by 10,000 masterchain blocks; a restart drops the wait, the payment then reaches the client without `meta`) for the later `PaymentSettled` of the same `(master, from, pay_ref)`; a meta cell with more than one ref is refused by the decoder; `RelayFeePaid` / `RelayFeeRefunded` stay with `tx_status` (the outcome scan of the last 128 router transactions, `Pending` when unseen): their release or refund lands after the escrow's `PaymentSettled` already reached the client, so the indexer cannot attach them. (H) The regenerated DEX KAT (Task 4) passes in `clients/clientkeys` (107 pass, 2 skipped) and `scaas-node` (337 lib tests, EVM e2e 4/4, the e2e harness on Amsterdam anvil as main 123e947f). The EVM node has no UA job path, so `uaPayMeta` / `uaRelay` are not served (a later item). Cost if wrong: a stricter node (refused kinds, refused bound payees) turns jobs away that a looser rule would have relayed; operators set `relay_bound_payee` / `min_lamports_value` to widen it. Settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28: the flat `params.relay_fee.min_amount` (default 1 base unit, per chain) is kept until before mainnet, then re-decided (item 7, TODO); the TON outcome window (`tx_status`, the last 128 router transactions; an older job stays Pending) is accepted (item 11).
Change (2026-10-28, controller calls 2026-10-28 on the owner's delegation "choose the best option"; status: current; commit: metatx-split T17 fix 1): supersedes items (A) and the TON wait of (G) above, and tightens (B). (A) The floor a contract signer's meta-tx gets is per job: `guard::erc1271_floor(len)` = 21,000 + 64 gas per calldata byte (the EIP-7976 floor rate) + `ERC1271_CALL_GAS` (446,904, forge's minimum relayer CALL gas, which counts no intrinsic and no calldata) + 10 % of it (512,594 at zero calldata); an anvil e2e sends a `SmartKeyAccount`-signed `mtxExecute` with exactly that gas and it settles. (G) TON: the `PaymentMeta` wait is looked up, never taken, so a range that fails after the join and is read again still carries `meta` (the `(master, from, payId)` triple happens once on chain); entries leave by expiry (10,000 masterchain blocks) or, past 4,096, oldest first with a warning; the wait is written atomically to `params.meta_journal` (default: `<store dir>/ton-meta-<chain>.json`) and loaded at start, so a restart keeps it. (B) A `params.relay_fee` key outside `router`, `min_amount`, `relay_bound_payee` and the family's own price key (`min_ton_value` on TON, `min_lamports_value` on Solana) is a startup error naming the key; Solana and Soroban refuse a malformed `tokens[].address` at start (as Sui, Aptos, TON); Solana refuses a `router` that is not its program id; Cosmos reads the router's executor lazily, once, on the first job that needs it (a relay-fee job, or a pay to a 32-byte contract address), and retries only such jobs until it answers, so a down router never stalls plain pays (T17 fix 2). The TON meta journal is written to a temporary file, synced, then renamed; over the cap, entries whose payment was already seen leave before still-waiting ones (T17 fix 2). Recorded, not built: the EVM node's UA path (`uaPayMeta`, `uaRelay`, the `UAPaymentSettled` join) is a new feature (TODO.md); TON `RelayFeePaid` / `RelayFeeRefunded` stay with `tx_status` (`Pending` when unseen), accepted. Cost if wrong: a contract signer's job pays for up to 10 % more gas limit than it uses.
Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split T19): rules and records from the family builds, in full. (1) Solana `cancel_signed` and `mandate_revoke_signed` are idempotent: a front-run of the signed entry still lets the wrapper run and the payer pays its signed fee once (superseded by owner ruling 2026-10-28, item 6 of the final review's owner rulings list: the wrappers refuse a no-op, `RelayCallNoOp`, see the owner-rulings Change below); a passkey x passkey wrapper transaction against the 4,096-byte v1 limit is untested and fails closed. (2) Aptos: a relay-fee job needs the payer's Account open first (no view runs the wrapped call, `simulate` hangs on a payment that opens the Account), the node refuses otherwise; a customer chain that reuses an Aptos chain id and publishes the package at the same address shares signatures with that chain (the `MetaOp` domain and `ref` carry a 1-byte `chain_id`): give a customer chain its own id or package address. (3) TON: a client does not queue an op at `n + 1` behind a revocable order at `n` (a signed revoke leaves its lane at `n + 2`); a racing other relayer's release makes our amount-0 refund path report "payer not charged" though the other relayer charged the payer (low, recorded). (4) Cosmos: a client checks `ContractInfo.admin == None` of the router before signing `relayer = router`. (5) Owed e2e on a real node, not in the tests: Soroban `relay_fee` simulate and submit (the `SourceAccount` auth entry), Cosmos gas of `Relay` on a wasmd localnet, Aptos two-passkey relay against the 9,200 exec-gas ceiling, Solana `gen_vectors.py --check` where the vector generator's checkout exists (TODO.md). (6) The EVM node serves address payers only: `uaPayMeta`, `RelayFeeRouter.uaRelay` and the `UAPaymentSettled` join are a new node feature (the `ua_metatx` job kind), not Task 17; cost if wrong: UA payers cannot use pay-meta or relay-fee through our EVM node until it is built (TODO.md). (7) NEAR and Algorand carry CTR-MTX-26 / -27 on their own branch from `metatx-split` (owner 2026-10-27; spec approved 2026-10-28): networks/README.md. Item (6) settled by owner ruling 2026-10-28 (item 10): the EVM node's UA path (`uaPayMeta`, `uaRelay`, the `UAPaymentSettled` join) is a TODO after the merge.
Change (2026-10-27, controller call 2026-10-27, owner may override; status: current, done; commits: metatx-split T10 fix 1 `351f67ea` (Soroban), T11–T16 (each family's adapter), T17 `9777679f`..`d784f264`; standalone line added in the final fix wave, final review M7): every family, one rule. The spec §9 node checks of a pay-meta or relay-fee job (configured router, registered token, `amount >= relay_fee.min_amount`, the binding of the payment to the call) go into each family's own adapter task (T10–T16), not into one node task; the indexer decoding of `PaymentMeta` / `RelayFeePaid` and the `max_pay_meta_bytes` config move to Task 17 for every family. Change (2026-10-28, controller call 2026-10-28 on final review I1, owner may override; status: current, its residuals superseded by the re-review Change below; commit: metatx-split final fix wave `deead173`): TON only, node. Before it sends a `RelayCall` the node checks the relayed call against its target with getters, as it checks the payment (`check_relayed_call` in `scaas-node/src/adapters/ton.rs`), and refuses the job with `RELAY_CALL_REFUSED`. Every other family simulates the whole relay; on TON a failing call bounced after the payment settled, the escrow refunded the payer and the relayer paid the bounce (about 0.025 TON in the sandbox, `runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-ton.txt:143`), repeatable at no cost to the submitter. Checks: the call's `contract`, network and `from` are the target, this chain and the target's owner (the first field of its StateInit data); it is valid past the relay's `deadline`; its `relayer` is none or the call's `responseDestination` (the router checks that this is the executor). Jetton wallet target: `simulate_signed` as for any signed op (lane nonce incl. a revoke at n + 1; the bound key or the StateInit key; the TON Connect signature), `valid_until <= now + LANE_TTL`, a set_key's `params` hashing to `extra` and never by passkey, a cancel's forward >= `CANCEL_TON`. Mandate target: an owner revoke only, TON Connect-signed, the Mandate not yet revoked, the signature verified against `get_state`'s `ownerPubkey`. The residuals first recorded here (a passkey's P-256 signature unchecked; no Mandate lane-nonce getter) were wrong to call owner-limited (any submitter owns a wallet, and a passkey call needs no key at all) and are closed by the re-review Change below. Not built (optional in the review): a per-payer failure budget and the payer's jetton balance check. Test: `ton_relay_fee_refuses_failing_call_before_send` (RED before the check: a wrongly signed call built). The meta journal also syncs its directory after the rename (final review M13).
Change (2026-10-28, controller calls 2026-10-28 on the fix-wave re-review F1 / F2 / m2–m4, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split final fix wave re-review fixes `6c31fbac`): TON only, node and Mandate. (F1) The node refuses a passkey-signed relayed call on the jetton wallet (`RELAY_CALL_REFUSED`, "a passkey-signed call is not relayed") until it can verify P-256: any submitter could otherwise relay a passkey revoke with a garbage signature at the relayer's cost. Passkey users on TON cannot use the relay-fee router meanwhile; they send revoke / set_key directly. Cost if wrong: passkey users lose the gasless revoke / set_key until P-256 lands in the node (`p256` dependency, owner's call). (F2a) A set_key with `extra != 0` must carry `params` that hash to `extra` and are laid out as the wallet parses a passkey record (exactly 520 bits and one ref, `jetton.tact` set_key); a malformed record bounced without spending the lane, repeatable. (F2b) The call's `responseDestination` must equal the router's `get_executor(payer, salt)`; a mismatch made the router throw 741 after the relayer paid its gas and forward fees. (F2c) The TON Mandate gains `get fun get_lane_nonce(lane)` (its owner lanes never rotate; a contract change, all chains test-only, no migration; the router address and `ton-vectors.json` `relay_fee` router / pay-op / RelayCall vectors moved with the Mandate code hash, regenerated); the node refuses a Mandate revoke whose nonce is not the lane's next. (m2) A revoke of an already revoked Mandate would run and change nothing: the node refuses it as a no-op, so the payer does not pay for nothing (owner rulings list item 6), not because it would fail. (m3) The call's validity floor is documented: `valid_until` later than the relay's deadline, now + 600 s (`RELAY_DEADLINE_S`). (m4) A target code that is neither the wallet's nor the Mandate's (`get_codes` on the router) is refused at once instead of retried as a transport error. (P1, second re-review, controller call 2026-10-28, owner may override; status: current; commit: metatx-split final fix wave second re-review `f0d4025e`) The payment leg is checked as the payer's wallet runs it: valid at most `LANE_TTL` ahead (`E_TTL`) and within the payer wallet's `get_wallet_data` balance (`E_BALANCE`), else the job is refused before anything is sent; a plain pay has the same two gaps at one hop's cost, left to the fee policy (owner rulings list item 7). Remaining exposure, recorded: a race in which the owner spends the lane, or moves its tokens away, between the check and the message's arrival still bounces at the relayer's cost, but costs the submitter a direct op or a paid relay each time; two relay-fee jobs of one payer wallet within one payment round trip make the router refuse the second (742) after the relayer paid its forward fee; every burst of such failures rides on one paid relay of the submitter, so the node does not hold the second job (an adapter-level per-payer-wallet hold is possible but not built, controller call); no per-payer failure budget is built (owner's call). Test: `ton_relay_fee_refuses_failing_payment_before_send`. (Q1, controller call 2026-10-28, then owner ruling 2026-10-28: risk acceptance reversed, fix kept; status: current; commits: metatx-split final fix wave third re-review `07d2f411`, removed by `2cac867a` under the owner's first answer, restored by its revert `0c90f031`) The payment gets the call's validity floor: it must stay valid more than 600 s (`RELAY_DEADLINE_S`), since the payer's wallet sees it two hops after the lane (`E_EXPIRED` would bounce at the relayer's cost, repeatable), and the lane transaction expires at `min(valid_until − 300 s, deadline)`, so a late lane transaction never delivers a nearly expired payment; a plain pay has the same window, left to the fee policy (owner rulings list item 7), no code. A balance equal to the amount pays (tested). Tests: `ton_relay_fee_refuses_failing_call_before_send` (every check has a case that fails without it, mutation-checked), jest `mandate.spec.ts` (`get_lane_nonce`).

Change (2026-10-28, owner ruling 2026-10-28 on the final review's owner rulings list item 1; status: **superseded 2026-10-30** by owner rulings D1 (signatures) and D2 (callers), CTR-MTX-25 / CTR-MTX-18 / CTR-UA-24 changes of 2026-10-30, built on `no7702` `5ddc577d` / `6bb05818`; commit: metatx-split owner rulings `84b0a469`): EIP-7702 delegate-only signatures are accepted on both paths. The address path (`SigCheck.isValid`: `MetaTxBase` / `MtxPipelineLib` `mtxExecute` and the transfers, `SCaaSDex` orders and cancels, `MandateWallet`, `SmartKeyAccount`) follows accounts.md CTR-UA-24, one rule with the UA path: empty code ⇒ ECDSA low-s by the address; code exactly the designator `0xef0100 ‖ address` ⇒ ECDSA by the address accepted, otherwise ERC-1271 on the address (it runs the delegate) under the 50 k cap (400 k for `SmartKeyAccount` clones); other code ⇒ ERC-1271. `SigCheck.isValid7702` is folded into `isValid`. The node's DEX venue mirrors it (`valid_sig`); the node's ERC-1271 gas floor already applies to a 7702 `from` (`has_code` is true for a designator). Unchanged: `MtxRule`, typehashes, domains, selectors, transient slots, storage layouts; a 7702 account is still not a contract for allowances (CTR-TOK-01). Sizes: no baseline entry moves (`runs/2026-10-28-metatx-split-7702-sizes.txt`). Tests: parity case `ok_e7702_viaDelegate_addr` (was `err_e7702_viaDelegate_addrPathRefuses`, fixture regenerated with `PARITY_WRITE=1`: only those six rows change outcome), `SigCheck.t.sol` `test_isValid_7702_ctrUa24` (RED before the change: the delegate's ERC-1271 refused) and `test_isValid_7702_badDelegates` (T-AUTH-3 negatives on the address path), node `a_7702_maker_signs_with_its_key_or_its_delegate`. Follow-up `12039013`: `SCaaSDex` grew 45 B, so the DEX KAT's clone address and DEX-domain digests moved (`dex_order_kat.json` regenerated, clientkeys and scaas-node re-gated green); `test_7702_nativeFrom` now expects the address-path delegate signature to pass.
Change (2026-10-30, controller call 2026-10-28 and owner ruling 2026-10-28 item 10 "the EVM node's UA path after the merge"; choices made by the node-ua-jobs build, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs `f0f8fd50`): the EVM node relays the `ua_metatx` job kind (job-api.md), with `uaPayMeta`, `RelayFeeRouter.uaRelay` and the `UAPaymentSettled` join. (1) Payload as job-api.md specifies, `{token, struct, m, auth}`; `m` keeps the address structs' wire field names with `from` / `to` as bytes32 ids; a `ua_metatx` job carrying `metatx`, `signature`, `entry` or `call` is refused, a `metatx` job never carries a UA body. (2) `uaPayMeta` is no new kind: a `ua_metatx` job with `struct = transfer` and `salt` / `meta`, the address pay-meta checks on ids before any simulation (`entryRef = metaPayId(salt, meta)`, `batch = payLane(entryRef)`, nonce 0, `max_pay_meta_bytes`), an off-chain meta relays the plain `uaExecuteTransfer`. (3) `uaRelay` is a `call` job with its own call-table row `RelayFeeRouter.uaRelay` (rule `RelayFee`), as `relay` is: the router's shape on ids (payee never `pad(executor)`, open mode `t.to = pad(router)`), `min_amount` and `relay_bound_payee` unchanged. (4) A `ua_metatx` job runs only on a registered token whose UA ledger is on (`registry() ≠ 0`, cached once true; else `FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED`): `uaExecute*` exists only on the token's UA ledger until UA-5c (c)(d) puts the generic UA pipeline into `MetaTxBase` / `MandateWallet`. (5) No pre-simulation UA allowlist check: tokens publish no UA selector table (`mtxSelectors()` is the address allowlist), so the selector, the fee class, the kind and the registration of `from` are answered by the simulation of the exact call; the gateway's record cache and local verify of cheap kinds (`UA_NOT_REGISTERED` at intake, gateway.md) are not built. (6) The relayer never loses on a relay fee (owner rule): after the simulation the fee × `params.relay_fee.min_wei_value[token]` (wei per base unit; EVM only; token-address keys, an integer or a decimal string, anything else a startup error) must reach the quote = the gas limit × the max fee per gas the lane signs with (the same fees then sign it), else `RELAY_FEE_REFUSED` and nothing is signed; as NEAR `min_yocto_value` and Algorand `min_microalgo_value`. Required for `uaRelay` (a UA's verify gas depends on its kind: secp256k1 ≈ 0.05 M cap, P-256 0.4 M, a Solidity PQ verify 1.4–5.95 M; a token without a price is refused for a UA payer); for the address `relay` only when its token has a price (owner ruling 2026-10-28 item 7 keeps the flat `min_amount` until before mainnet); a sponsored fee (bound elsewhere, `relay_bound_payee`) is not priced. (7) `ua_metatx` jobs, as `metatx` jobs, get no fee check (every state-changing mtx* is relayable with fee 0, owner 2026-10-20): the "never fails at the relayer's cost" check is the simulation of the exact call, whose estimate covers the kind's verify (the registry hands each verifier its cap only when it can: a starved verify reverts `UAVerifyGas`, never a verdict); a native-id UA with code gets the ERC-1271 floor as on the address path, a derived UA none. (8) The lane's subject is an id (`MetaRef.from: bytes32` + `ua`): the `consumed` check reads `uaNonce(from, batch)` (the one nonce map), the in-flight key is the token's `uaDigest` / `uaTransferDigest`, the classification reads `UAMetaTransactionExecuted`. (9) Indexer: `UAPaymentSettled` and `UAMetaTransactionExecuted` are sent as `PaymentSettled` and `MetaTransactionExecuted` rows with ids (a native id as its address, a derived UA as bytes32 hex), as NEAR and Algorand send their holders, so the client's ingest gains no event name; `PaymentMeta` and a UA payer's `RelayFeePaid` (`payer` = the UA id) join them by `(from, entry_ref)` (and amount and payee), unchanged. (10) Recorded ceilings: the quote is the first send's; a stuck transaction's replacement (`track`, fee bump up to `max_fee_cap_gwei`) can cost more than it; the e2e uses a secp256k1 UA (no Rust signer for a PQ kind here), the PQ verify gas enters only through the simulation. Not built (UA F5): the gateway route `/v1/ua-metatx`, the record cache, mesh `evm.ua_meta_tx`, `UATransfer` / `UA_POOL` pairing, `uaBatch*` / `uaCancelNonce` / `uaPayReceiverFee` jobs. Tests: `metatx::ua_*` (the clientkeys vectors `vectors/ua/metatx3.json`), `submit::ua_*`, `submit::min_wei_value_is_parsed_or_refused`, `indexer::ua_payments_are_payment_rows_and_join_their_meta_and_relay_fee`, e2e `ua_pay_meta_and_relay_fee_jobs_on_anvil` (QUOTE ≥ the lane's ETH cost for both jobs; `scaas-node/runs/2026-10-30-ua-jobs-*.txt`). Cost if wrong: a UA payer's relay fee priced by an operator floor that is too low loses the lane the difference (the operator sets `min_wei_value`); without the price no UA relay fee is served on that token.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review C1, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): the EVM indexer's rows for a derived UA. The client's ingest (the reference ERP connector's `chain_event_ingest`) takes only `0x` + 40 hex for `contract`, `from`, `to`, `fee_recipient` and `relayer` on an EVM chain and refuses the whole range otherwise; a bytes32 id in one row (any derived UA's `UAPaymentSettled` or `UAMetaTransactionExecuted`, e.g. a permissionless `payWithFeeToUA`) would stop the chain's indexer for good. Now a derived id's `from` / `to` is `UA_POOL` (`MetaTxLib.UA_POOL`, the holder ERC-20 observers see for every UA move) and the bytes32 id travels in `from_ua` / `to_ua` (`relay_payee_ua` for a derived bound payee); a native id stays its address. Joins compare the ids (`*_ua` when present), never `UA_POOL`. Supersedes item (9) of the Change above ("bytes32 hex as NEAR / Algorand"). The unit tests and the e2e's fake client run every row through the client's 40-hex rule. Client follow-up (TODO.md): the connector reads `from_ua` / `to_ua`. Checked (report only): the client has no `near` or `algorand` family (`lib/addresses.py` `canonical` raises "unknown network family"), so it refuses every row of those chains today, UA or not; their adapters send a UA holder as `0x` + 64 hex, which the client will have to accept when it adds the families. Cost if wrong: a derived UA's payments show `UA_POOL` in the client until it reads the id keys.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review I1, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): a priced relay-fee job's fee ceiling. The quote is the gas limit × the job's fee ceiling = `FEE_HEADROOM` (2, `guard::FEE_HEADROOM`) × the max fee per gas of its first send (+ the L1 fee, I3), stored per job (`Sent.ceiling`); `track` clamps every replacement of a live priced job at `min(max_fee_cap_gwei, ceiling)`, so at the ceiling it waits ("stuck at the fee cap") and expires; the gap-fill that then takes the nonce uses the operator's cap (21,000 gas, it runs no job). After a restart the first send's ceiling is not journaled, so a tracked priced job's ceiling is its tracked transaction's max fee and it is re-checked (fee × price ≥ gas × that fee) before it can be re-signed; not covered, an unknown fee, or an OP-stack chain ⇒ the nonce is only gap-filled. Not chosen: quoting at `max_fee_cap_gwei` (orders of magnitude too dear) or H = 1 (no replacement passes a mempool's +10 % rule). The generic lane runner signs once and never replaces; its build-time fees are frozen for `sign` (a runner that replaces must clamp at `fee_ceiling`). Tests: `submit::priced_relay_fee_replacements_stay_under_the_job_ceiling`, `submit::a_tracked_priced_relay_job_is_rechecked_after_a_restart`, the e2e's stuck uaRelay (5 sends, the last exactly at the ceiling). Cost if wrong: a job that cannot land under 2 × its first fee expires and the payer re-signs.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review I2, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): a per-subject in-flight hold. A balance drain fails a relayed payment after the inner call and the whole verify (up to ~6 M gas for a Solidity PQ kind), at the lane's cost; through our own node it was free (a fee-0 `ua_metatx` drain on another lane). Now the chain's shared in-flight set also counts, per `subject_key(token, id)`, the relay-fee jobs and the other jobs of a subject: a relay-fee job (`relay`: its address, padded; `uaRelay`: its id) is signed only when no job of that subject on that token is in flight, and no other job of the subject (a `ua_metatx` or `metatx` of it, or another relay-fee job) is signed while one is; a held job is requeued `SUBJECT_HELD` (retried). The hold travels with the digest guard (released when the job leaves the lane), is rebuilt for tracked jobs at a restart, and the generic lane runner takes it too (Hedera). Residual (recorded, priced by the kind's verify until NODE-LANE-15's grief score is built): another relayer's send, a direct transaction of the payer, a plain ERC-20 `transfer`, a DEX leg or `mtxWrap` lowering the balance. Test: `submit::a_relay_fee_job_holds_its_payer`.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review I3, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): the L1 data fee in the quote. On a chain whose config marks it OP-stack (`params.l1_fee = "op-stack"`; any other value a startup error; Base, Celo) the quote of a priced relay-fee job adds `FEE_HEADROOM` × `GasPriceOracle.getL1Fee(raw)` (predeploy `0x420000000000000000000000000000000000000F`) of the signed transaction the lane is about to send (signed, not sent: a refusal consumes no nonce); an oracle that reverts refuses the job (terminal), a transport error retries it. The generic lane runner refuses a priced job on an OP-stack chain (it does not sign before its check). Other rollup fee models (Arbitrum's L1 component in `gasUsed`, which `eth_estimateGas` covers) need no flag. Test: `submit::op_stack_l1_fee_is_in_the_quote`.
Change (2026-10-30, controller rulings for node-ua-jobs fix 1 on review minors, owner may override; status: current; commit: node-ua-jobs fix 1): (1) `min_wei_value` also takes `"<wei>/<10^k>"` (wei per 10^k base units, the denominator a power of ten) so an 18-decimal token below 1 wei per unit is priced exactly; covered iff `fee × wei >= quote × 10^k` in 256 bits; 0 refuses every priced job; docs say to round a price down. (2) `min_wei_value` without `router`, and one token under two spellings (case), are startup errors. (3) "Below the quote" is a retry (`queued`), not a kill; a missing price for a UA payer stays terminal. (4) The e2e's QUOTE check can fail: a stuck priced uaRelay is replaced while blocks are paused and every send's max fee must stay ≤ 2 × the first (unclamped, the fourth 25 % bump passes it); the unpriced `uaPayMeta` QUOTE line is gone. (5) A native-id UA job's classification reads both `UAMetaTransactionExecuted` and `MetaTransactionExecuted` (one nonce map; `chain::executed_events`). (6) The generic runner's frozen build-time fees are commented (I1). (7) The gate's fixed step logs are copied per feature to `scaas-node/runs/2026-10-30-ua-jobs-fix1-gate-*.txt` with the commit in their first line.

Change (2026-10-30, **owner ruling D4** — SCaaS never calls into a designator where it picks the callee; status: current, decided (owner); commit: `no7702` `955f5337`): (1) `RelayFeeRouter._shape`: `!SigCheck.isContract(target)` ⇒ `RelayTargetNoCode(target)` (was `target.code.length == 0`). This is also a **bug fix**: a designator pointing at a code-less address passed the old check and the call succeeded empty, so the payer paid for nothing (the very case `RelayTargetNoCode` exists for); one pointing at code ran the delegate as the executor's callee. (2) `WrappedLib.payOut`, `NATIVE` leg: a designator recipient is refused with `UnwrapRecipientInvalid(recipient)` (`unwrap` and the Zether / PQZ unshield-unwrap `payOutTo`); an ERC-20 leg may still pay a designator (a plain ERC-20 runs no recipient code; an outside token with ERC-777 / ERC-1363 hooks may, on a recipient the unwrapper chose). Left as they are (owner-chosen or solver-chosen, conservation-checked): `MandateWallet` / `SmartKeyAccount` `execute` targets and DEX `_interact` targets. Why: "an EOA must not run code" — a native-coin send runs the delegate with all forwarded gas. Cost if wrong: a 7702 user cannot receive native coin through `unwrap` while delegated (it unwraps to another address or clears its delegation). The router's bytecode changed (+74 B), so its CREATE2 address moves: redeploy (all chains are test-only). Tests: `test_relay_targetDesignatorRefused`, `test_native_unwrapToDesignatorRefused`. Source: the EIP-7702 audit of 2026-10-30 (`research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`) §4 T1–T4.

Change (2026-10-31, **controller ruling 2026-10-31 after the UA-Soroban T8 review** (critical finding, EVM executor parity, owner may override); the owner chose to split the fix out of UA-Soroban and merge it early (2026-10-31); status: current, built and merged into `main` 2026-10-31; branch `soroban-router-fix`, task "Soroban relay-fee router fix"): Soroban only. (1) The relay-fee router (`smartcontracts/soroban/contracts/relay-fee`) no longer calls the target as itself: Soroban grants a contract's authority to every contract it calls directly, so a target saw `router.require_auth()` satisfied and a target `token.transfer(router, attacker, n)` drained any balance on the router (repro: a victim's signed plain `pay` to the router as the target of an attacker's open-mode `relay`, then a second `relay` draining it), against CTR-MTX-13 and CTR-MTX-27. The new contract `contracts/relay-executor` runs the target: the router's `relay` calls `executor.exec(target, func, args)`, and `exec` accepts only its router (`router.require_auth()`). (2) The two are bound for life: the executor's constructor names the router; the router's constructor takes the executor and checks `executor.router() == self` (else `BadExecutor` = 3), so the router is no longer stateless (it stores the executor). (3) A payee equal to the router or the executor (`to`, or the relayer in open mode) is `BadPayee` = 2. (4) `smartcontracts/scripts/deploy.sh soroban <net> relay_fee` derives the router id from a salt (`SOROBAN_SALT` or random), deploys the executor naming it, then the router at that salt, checks the id, and passes `stellar contract id wasm` only the source / RPC / config options. (5) Node (item (D) of the node Change above, "never a plain pay or pay-meta to the router, marker or executor", extended to the Soroban executor): the Soroban adapter reads `router.executor()` once and refuses plain `pay` / `pay_meta` / `transfer` jobs and relay-fee jobs whose `to` / payee is the router or its executor. (6) On branch `ua-soroban` (merged with this fix, its side kept for the code) the same executor covers the UA payer form `ua_relay` (a victim's router-bound `ua_pay` would otherwise be submittable as the target); `RelayFeePaid` payer and payee are `Holder`; the node applies the payee rule to the UA pays too. Details: NET-SOR-21. (7) Router-fix review, carried to `ua-soroban` (controller 2026-10-31, owner may override; status: current): the node also refuses `approve` naming the router or the executor as spender (amount 0, a withdrawal, allowed), `transfer_from` naming either as spender or `to`, and (UA-Soroban final review B-I1, controller 2026-10-31, owner may override; status: current) a mandate `mtx_set_mandate` naming either as the delegate (argument 1: the executor as a native delegate lets anyone run `mtx_mandate_pay` through `relay`, the executor being the direct invoker that meets the delegate's `require_auth_for_args`; the router as delegate is refused by the same rule), and checks a `relay` / `ua_relay` job's relayed target call by the same rule (anything approved to the executor is spendable by anyone through `relay`); a router without `executor()` is a config error that fails the chain's Soroban jobs (`Revert`, job `dead`) instead of requeueing them forever. Tests: `node_refuses_approvals_to_router_or_executor`, `missing_executor_is_a_config_error`, `pays_router_covers_ua_pay` (the `mtx_set_mandate` delegate).
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller calls, owner may override, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): **`RelayFee` has a token path.** `RelayFee(address from,address target,bytes32 callDataHash,address payee,uint256 value,uint256 validUntil,address relayer)` (`UARelayFee` with ids) is executed by `mtxRelayFee` / `uaRelayFee` on the token: `relayer` is `msg.sender` (the router), lane `payLane(ref)`, nonce 0, `ref` = today's `relayRef`. The router is `relay(target, callData, token, from, payee, value, validUntil, sig)` / `uaRelay(…, UASig auth)` and keeps `_shape`'s refusal of the executor as payee and the target-has-code rule. A payment for another target, call or chain now fails at the signature after the call ran (the revert unwinds it), where `RelayFeeShape` fired first. Both ERC-165 ids moved.
Change (2026-11-09, owner 2026-11-09; status: current; commit: ua-mtx-merge T82): **renamed `MtxRelayFee` → `RelayFeeRouter` and `MtxRelayExecutor` → `RelayFeeExecutor`** (`src/metatx/MtxRelayFee.sol` → `src/metatx/RelayFeeRouter.sol`). Why: the old name named the payment, not the role, and read like the token's entry `mtxRelayFee`; the docs already called it the router and its executor holds it as `ROUTER`. A pure rename: the ABI is unchanged (`relay`, `relayRef`, `EXECUTOR`, `exec`, `ROUTER`), and so are the token entry `mtxRelayFee`, `UARelayFee`, `RelayFeePaid`, `relayRef`'s tag `scaas.relayfee`, the errors `RelayFeeShape`, `RelayTargetNoCode`, `NotRouter`, the node config `params.relay_fee.router` and the other families' module names (`relay-fee`, `relayfee`, `ScaasRelayFee`). What follows the name: `DeployBase._deployRelayFeeRouter` and its deploy JSON keys `relay_fee_router` / `relay_fee_executor` (were `mtx_relay_fee` / `mtx_relay_executor`; a reader of `deployments/<id>.json` takes the new keys), the node's `abi::IRelayFeeRouter` (was `IMtxRelayFee`), the test file `test/metatx/RelayFeeRouter.t.sol`. The metadata hash moves the CREATE2 addresses (deterministic deployer, default `DEPLOY_SALT`): the router `0x8B56809BBf5f6595351F648a499E194292B6100C` → `0x6e5ADaD0b26E45d76250564dC569D2C05a082762`, its executor (the router's CREATE at nonce 1) `0x5ecDB11E3C7679637EdD6E4f0A47D48Fd9d7c01E` → `0x5E65D1Aa4f88e54D59f8974148B08BeDF04408Df`; a `UARelayFee` signed for the router binds the new address. Routers already deployed on the SCaaS testnet keep their addresses and the name they were verified under.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): pay-meta-tax PT-3 (owner O4, O14; T38 `e273978e`): `UARelayFee` carries `batch` and `nonce` (a new typehash), the payment runs on the payer's lane `(from, batch)` at `nonce`; a relay fee is not pay-once, a signature is (paying twice for one call needs two signatures and a target that runs twice); router open mode unchanged on every kind, the regulated ones included (O14). Tests `test/metatx/RelayFeeRouter.t.sol` (`test_relayFee_staleNonce`, `test_relayFee_oldTypehashRefused`, `test_relayFee_dedicatedLane`, `test_relayFee_twoSignaturesReplayableTargetPaysTwice`, `test_relayFee_guardedTargetSecondReverts`).

### CTR-MTX-28 — A named entry per operation: the signed struct is `from` + the operation's explicit parameters + the envelope
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-28 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every operation that was allowlisted for `mtxExecute` has `mtx<Op>(Envelope e, <explicit params>, bytes sig)` and, where UA-allowed, `ua<Op>(UAEnvelope e, <params>, UASig auth)`, each with its own typehash, `<Op>(address from,<params>,batch,nonce,validUntil,mode,relayer,fee,feeRecipient)`; same lane as the generic path; the generic `mtxExecute` / `mtxBatch` / `uaExecute` / `uaBatch` and `executeMetaTransaction` stay (owner 2026-10-31, 2026-11-01).
**Why.** Owner option B, 2026-10-31: "a named entry point per operation, everything explicit", so a wallet shows the operation's own fields. Who: owner (the rule); controller calls (names, overloads, `uaExecute` / `uaBatch` / `uaShield` keeping `bytes auth`). Status: built in typed-signing C2-C6.
**Cost if wrong.** Selector and typehash churn per operation; the size ratchet (`WrappedPqzToken` 63,423 B).
**Source.** plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md` (TS-D14, TS-D16, TS-D18).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R5; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): one form per operation on tokens and the router: `mtx<Op>(MetaTxLib.UAEnvelope e, <explicit operation parameters, bytes32 ids>, IUARegistry.UASig auth)` over the struct `UA<Op>`; the five no-twin wrap entries stay on `Envelope`; `SmartKeyAccount` keeps `Envelope` + `AccountSig`; the mandate wallets take the merged form ([CTR-ACC-12](contracts/mandates.md#CTR-ACC-12)'s Change); the generic entries take `UASig` (R47, [CTR-MTX-29](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-29)'s Change).

### CTR-MTX-29 — Every parameter is explicit
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-29 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** "Every parameter is explicit, as in a REST / JSON / RPC API — no packed / opaque `bytes` that bundle several fields"; genuine cryptographic blobs stay `bytes` "but as their own named parameter"; the statement and digest bytes the verifiers hash stay byte-identical; what is stored is what the packed bytes were (never lose ciphertext).
**Why.** The owner's rule of 2026-10-31, applied to the contracts (Zether, PQZ, registry, `UASig`, `DexLeg`), the node (NODE-JOB-20) and every family (NET-ALL-84 row 20). Exceptions by ruling: packed `register` (owner 2026-10-31), `bytes auth` on `uaExecute` / `uaBatch` / `uaShield`, kind-specific signature encodings. Status: built.
**Cost if wrong.** Larger calldata for the typed forms (measured per op, `evm-size-levers.md`, the C4 overhead log).
**Source.** owner 2026-10-31; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md` (TS-D17, Appendix X).
Change (owner 2026-11-04, `ua*` / `mtx*` merge; status: SPECIFIED, not built): the exception "`uaExecute` / `uaBatch` / `uaShield` keep `bytes auth`" is reversed by [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) (spec row R47): the merged `mtxExecute`, `mtxBatch` and `mtxShield` take `UASig`. The Rule text and `contracts/metatx.md` are rewritten by the build.
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner Q7 (O16): `PayMeta.body` of schemas 2 and 3 holds several fields in `bytes` on chain, a commitment preimage never parsed (the class of the kind-specific signature encodings); named fields in node JSON and every client (T42 `9e3cf553`: the node builds the body from named fields, a hex body `HEX_ARGS_REFUSED`).

### CTR-MTX-30 — One signed entry per operation: the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-04 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The owner's answers of 2026-11-04 to the merge spec ([spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md) §10, Q1–Q7), all accepted as recommended.
- **Q1, the merge is A + B + C.** **A:** every `ua*` / `mtx*` pair of a SCaaS EVM token kind, `RelayFeeRouter`, the DEX's SCaaS legs and `GovernanceRouter` merges: the `ua<Op>` body takes the `mtx<Op>` name, with today's `ua<Op>` ABI (`MetaTxLib.UAEnvelope e`, the explicit operation parameters with `bytes32` ids, `IUARegistry.UASig auth`; the flat transfer group with `bytes32 from`) and the typed struct `UA<Op>` with `bytes32 from`; the old `mtx*` address bodies move to `legacy/ua-mtx-merge/`. **B:** an EOA signs the `UA<Op>` struct with its own key: its id is its address zero-padded, its signature travels in `auth.signature`, and it is checked by `_authorizeNative` (ECDSA low-s, ERC-1271 under the code-hash cap, HIP-632 on Hedera) with **no registry call**; on the generic entry a derived subject reads `_uaAllowed` only, a native one `_mtxRule`. **C:** a registry is needed only when a side is a derived UA: at `registry() == 0` a derived side reverts `UALedgerOff` by name, and a call whose every side is native runs, so `NORMAL` and `WRAPPED` without a registry keep a relayed path for an EOA. The wallets keep the address surface; `executeMetaTransaction` (owner 2026-11-01) and the five no-twin wrap entries stay as they are; direct entries do not change. The spec's follow-on rows (R2, R4, R5, R7, R20–R31, R33–R39, R42–R44) apply as written in its §5, and its controller decisions (§10) stand as controller calls, owner may override.
- **Q1, the reversals accepted with it** (old text → new text; why; cost):
  - **R1, CTR-MTX-09** (owner 2026-10-08). Old: "the named functions keep their signatures and build the struct of their kind — `mtxTransfer`, `mtxTransferWithFee`, `mtxPay` a `MetaTransfer` …; nothing is merged". New: "`mtxTransfer`, `mtxTransferWithFee`, `mtxPay`, `mtxPayMeta`, `mtxBatch`, `mtxBatchTransfer` take the form of today's `ua*` twin (the same flat explicit parameters with `bytes32` ids, `UASig`) and build `UAMetaTransfer` / `UAMetaTransaction`; one form per operation." Why: a pair is one feature written twice (owner 2026-11-03). Cost: every caller of the address forms moves (clients, node, vectors, tests); an EOA's relayed transfer costs about +0.9 to +1.0 K gas, calldata of a three-field `UASig` (spike, old base); a wallet shows `bytes32` for `from` and `to`.
  - **R9, CTR-UA-19** (owner: yes) and **CTR-DEX-25's C5b-2** (controller ruling confirmed by the owner 2026-10-13). Old: "the registry … 0 = the ledger is off: every `ua*` reverts `UALedgerOff`"; "the `ua*` trade functions revert `UALedgerOff` while the ledger is off, a padded native `from` included". New: the UA structs are the token's signed structs for every merged operation; at `registry() == 0` a derived side reverts `UALedgerOff`, and a call whose every side is native runs (C). Why: an EOA keeps a relayed path on a plain token without a registry. Cost: `supportsInterface(IUALedger)` stays false at 0, so `IUALedger` splits into the entries and the ledger views (new interface ids); the DEX asks for a ledger only for a derived seller (+134 B, spike); the tests whose meaning reverses are reviewed by hand.
  - **R12, CTR-DEX-25's rationale** (owner 2026-10-13). Old: "Widening `TradeOrder` for everyone was rejected: native wallets keep displaying an `address`, and existing vectors and node encoders stay." New: "A SCaaS token leg is a `UATradeOrder`, native or derived; `TradeOrder` and its vectors stay for outside legs"; CTR-DEX-26's shape 0 on a SCaaS token goes, and the token's `mtxTrade` is today's `uaTrade`. Why: it follows R1. Cost: EOA makers on SCaaS legs sign `bytes32 from` and `bytes32 destination`; the DEX KAT regenerates; about 30 DEX test files move to shape 1; the node's book gains `UATradeOrder` intake, the UA cancel and invalidate and a `UALegSettled` watcher (new node work); the public DEX API changes (operator note).
  - **R47, the `bytes auth` exception** (CTR-MTX-29, recorded 2026-11-01 in CTR-TOK-24's typed-signing C2 / C6 / C8 Changes, "owner table"). Old: "`uaExecute`, `uaBatch` and `uaShield` keep `bytes auth`". New: `mtxExecute(UAMetaTransaction, UASig)`, `mtxBatch(UAMetaTransaction[], UASig[])`, `mtxShield(…, UASig)`; `executeMetaTransaction` keeps its `bytes signature` (one cryptographic object). Why: explicit parameters (owner 2026-10-31): for a derived subject that `bytes` is a packed `UASig` (`abi.encode(keyData, sig)`); after the merge it is every EOA's generic entry too, and the spec's R17 (a native id's `UASig` with non-empty `keyData` or `members` is refused, `MetaTxBadSignature`) then holds on it. Cost: the generic path's `bytes` authorize branch and the `UAKinds.uaSig` bridge go; the `clientkeys` and `zether-prover` builders change; the PQZ set parameters measured on the relay path (`roll_max`, `debit_min_gas`) are re-measured on the merged `mtxExecute` (spec R41).
- **Q2, the signed cancel.** One entry, the ordered `mtxCancelNonce(MetaTxLib.UAEnvelope e, uint256 lane, IUARegistry.UASig auth)` over `UACancelNonce(bytes32 from,uint256 lane,uint256 batch,uint256 nonce,uint256 validUntil,uint32 mode,address relayer,uint256 fee,address feeRecipient)`, run through `MtxPipelineLib.preNamedUA` like every named operation: nonce-ordered on its lane `e.batch`, relayer-bound when the mode says so, fee 0 or more, for native and derived subjects, on tokens and the router. This departs from "the `ua*` body wins" for this one pair: the kept body is the ordered `mtx*` one, widened to `bytes32`. The unordered `uaCancelNonce`, `uaCancelDigest` and the old `UACancelNonce(bytes32 ua,uint256 batch,uint256 validUntil)` move to legacy; the `cancelUsed` slot stays (layout pinned). Why: today's `ua*` body cannot serve a native and binds no nonce, so a withheld cancel could kill a later operation on its lane, and the router would have no ordered cancel. Cost: a derived subject's cancel becomes nonce-ordered (clients move); one `typed_ops.json` row changes. Soroban's `ua_cancel_nonce` is its own family's answer.
- **Q3, size.** Target: `NormalToken`, `WrappedToken` and a stand-in of their regulated form fit the owner's 60 M and 70 M blocks, counted as deploy gas: the gas each deploy transaction asks under the EIP-8037 inclusion rule (total × 1.05). The Zether kinds are measured against the same thresholds and reported; whether they must fit is decided later (CTR-GOV-19). The levers are L (the `zether-lib` pattern on the base bodies: `ERC20MetaTx` and `UAMetaTxBase` bodies in a linked library) and D (read-only views behind a `fallback` to an immutable module pinned in `Env`, only with the spec's §8 invariant 7), chosen by the spec's §4 rule: the smallest set that meets the target; between two that meet it, the one with no hot-path gas cost (D before L), then the one with fewer new mechanisms. If no lever set fits, the merge lands with the best set and the 60 M target stays open with the measured gap per kind (recorded in TODO); an out-of-scope lever only by the owner's choice then. The final choice is made after the spec's §9 measurement.
- **Q4, the deploy gate.** On a public chain the gate is the measured gas of the release transaction (regular + state, by a fork or local simulation through `deployTokenImplementation`) × 1.05, against that chain's block limit, with regular × 1.05 < 2^24. The SCaaS testnet keeps the owner's formula `runtime × 1,530 + 2^24` ([NET-EVM-06](networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-06)).
- **Q5, wallet display.** Before reset 2, a test in real wallets: the regenerated `UAMetaTransfer`, one `UA<Op>` row of `typed_ops.json`, a `UATradeOrder` with a non-zero `destination` and a `UARelayFee` row, signed in two widely used browser wallets and one hardware wallet; what each shows is recorded in a text note in `docs/research/` (screenshots stay local).
- **Q6, mandate-wallet twins.** CTR-ACC-12 (UA-5c) is deferred: the wallets stay address-only, as the owner's 2026-11-03 words keep the wallets' address surface; UA-5c reopens it with merged entries as its proposal.
- **Q7, node doors.** Built in this round: the gateway's token doors (`POST /v1/op` takes the merged named entries with `auth` as `UASig`; `POST /v1/ua-metatx` is built for `UAMetaTransaction` / `UAMetaTransfer`; `POST /v1/metatx` refuses a token by name) and the mesh's `evm.ua_meta_tx` (the EVM and Hedera token body is the UA structs, its intent id the UA digest, its KAT cases regenerated; the wallets keep the address body). Why: gateway and mesh relaying of EVM token operations are BUILT today and reset 2 must not drop them; the node is open, so the guarantee stays in the node.

**Status.** SPECIFIED: nothing is built. The build, its own round between SCaaS testnet reset 1 and reset 2, rewrites the normative texts (`contracts/metatx.md`, `accounts.md`, `dex.md` and the rest of the spec's §7 Docs row) and moves this rule's home there; every figure is re-measured after the governance merge (spec §9), none is a pin. Changes pointing here: CTR-MTX-09, CTR-MTX-29, CTR-TOK-24, CTR-UA-19, CTR-DEX-25, CTR-ACC-12, CTR-UA-27.
**Why.** Owner 2026-11-03: for every pair keep the `ua*` implementation and give it the `mtx*` name, because the pair is one feature written twice; B and C keep a relayed path for an EOA with and without a registry.
**Cost if wrong.** Every caller of the address forms moves (clients, node, vectors, about 86 test files on the spike's base); an EOA's relayed transfer costs about +0.9 to +1.0 K gas; a wallet shows `bytes32` ids where it showed addresses (spec §6); new selectors, typehashes, interface ids and the router's CREATE2 address.
**Source.** owner 2026-11-04 (Q1 accepted, Q2–Q7 as recommended); [spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md) §2, §4, §5 (R1, R9, R12, R19, R40, R44, R45, R47), §10; spike `research/governance/prototype/merge-entries.md` (branch `token-merge`, not merged).
Change (owner 2026-11-04, after T1 of the build; status: SPECIFIED, not built): **Q6 changes.** Old: "CTR-ACC-12 (UA-5c) is deferred: the wallets stay address-only, as the owner's 2026-11-03 words keep the wallets' address surface; UA-5c reopens it with merged entries as its proposal." New: the mandate wallets `MandateWallet` and `HederaMandateWallet` are built now, in this round, in the merged form. **One entry per operation:** each wallet operation has exactly one signed entry, `mtx<Op>(MetaTxLib.UAEnvelope e, <the operation's explicit parameters with bytes32 ids>, IUARegistry.UASig auth)`, over its typed struct `UA<Op>` (`UASetMandate`, `UASetPayee`, `UARevokeMandate`, `UAPayUnderMandate`, `UADelegateRevoke`, `UAExecute`) in the wallet's existing domain, plus the generic `mtxExecute` / `mtxBatch` and the ordered `mtxCancelNonce` of Q2 on ids, at fee mode `NONE`; CTR-ACC-12's `uaExecute`, `uaPayUnderMandate`, `uaRevoke`, `uaExecuteAsOwner` beside the `mtx*` ones are not built. **Signers:** a native signer (an EOA, or ERC-1271 code) signs with its own key and needs no registry; a derived UA authenticates through `UARegistry.requireAuthorized`, so the registry is needed only when a side is derived (C). **Old bodies:** the wallets' address-form bodies move to `legacy/ua-mtx-merge/` and are never deleted. **`SmartKeyAccount` stays as it is:** no twin, its own address-form `mtxExecute` and named entries; "the wallets keep the address surface" in Q1 above now means `SmartKeyAccount` only. Why: the merge removes twins on SCaaS contract wallets as it does on tokens; external wallets only display the typed data. Cost: new wallet bytecode, typehashes, `typed_ops.json` rows and KATs (`mandate_pay_kat.json`, `mandate_revoke_kat.json` to legacy); the node's wallet rows become `ua_metatx` jobs and the auto-pay path signs the named UA entries; a wallet shows `bytes32` for `from`, `delegate` and `payee`; the flat builders `mtxPayUnderMandate(token, …)`, `mtxRevoke`, `mtxExecuteAsOwner`, `mtxExecuteAsOwnerRaw`, kept by the owner on 2026-11-01 (CTR-ACC-05's 2026-11-02 Change), go to legacy as second signed entries of their operations (controller, plan MD-11(a); owner confirmed 2026-11-05). Source: owner 2026-11-04; [spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md) §2.7, R32, §10 Q6; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md` T3b, MD-11.

The rewrite of the component docs to the merged forms (the Change lines of R1–R47, this rule's normative home, the operator note) has no draft and is the rest of T19; until then this entry and its Changes are the text of the merged forms.

### CTR-MTX-31 — The pay entries are the ERP interface: the key adds up, a refund is a reverse payment, lanes are free
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-05 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-31 · superseded-by: —

**Status.** BUILT on the EVM, branch `ua-mtx-merge`, T37 `3740b85e` (free lanes, `PayMeta` on every pay entry), T42 `9e3cf553` (the node's pay jobs), T83 `ba280ade` (`payNo` as `bytes32`, the pay records); UNAUDITED. Tests `test/metatx/PayLanes.t.sol`, `PayRecords.t.sol`. The non-EVM families keep their pay-once lane until their own rounds.
**Why.** Owner O1: pay functions connect to external sales and ERP systems, and `entryRef` with its metadata is the reconciliation key; O3: one document may be paid in parts, and whether it is fully paid is the ERP's call; O12: the generic transfer path stays open and reconciles off chain.
**Cost if wrong.** A contract-side pay-once would refuse a legitimate second instalment; a reconciler that does not add the amounts of one key books a partial payment as complete or a refund as income.
**Source.** `superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-pay-meta-tax.md` §1 PT-1, §2.2, §2.3 (owner rulings O1, O3, O12, 2026-11-05).

### CTR-MTX-32 — Service pull: a contract's custody by the payer's one signed transfer
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-09 · normative: contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-32 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A contract that must take a payer's SCaaS tokens into its custody and run its own logic in the same transaction does it by a service pull: the payer signs one `UAMetaTransfer` (`to` = `relayer` = the service, `MODE_RESTRICT_RELAYER`, fee `NONE`, `entryRef` = the operation's EIP-712 digest in the service's domain), the service checks the spec's §3.3 steps 1–9 and calls `mtxExecuteTransfer` itself. The EVM token needs no change (verified on kinds 0–13 and Hedera). The owner's answers of 2026-11-09 to the spec's §13, all as recommended:
- **Q1 B.** One generic node kind `service` (NODE-JOB-25): its rows come from operator config, checked against the contract's `servicePullEntries()` in both directions; the node builds the calldata from named fields by the declared EIP-712 type under C3's bounds and reads the pulled token from the contract. No service is named in node code; an address has one kind, both ways.
- **Q2 A.** One signature (only `t`); the request carries `<Op>`'s typed data beside it. The blind-commitment residual is accepted as for `PayMeta` (CTR-MTX-26): a signer other than `ua-rs` shows "pay `value` to S" with `entryRef` opaque; `ua-rs` recomputes the digest from the typed data and refuses on a mismatch (its client rule lands with branch `ua-rs-sign`).
- **Q3 A.** The relayer is paid by `RelayFeeRouter` (CTR-MTX-27) or not at all; every pull is at fee `NONE`, fee 0, no fee recipient.
- **Q4 refuse.** A service refuses an `entryRef` it has seen (`ServicePullReplayed`): the reconciliation key `(token, payer, S, entryRef)` stays unique.
- **Q5 accept.** On the regulated kinds 8–13 a payout the token refuses stays owed, never redirected; a recorded `forceTransfer` on S drains the pooled balance, the shortfall falls on the last claimants, payouts fail closed; a service on a regulated kind states it in its own documentation.
Controller calls (the owner may override): C1 `entryRef` is the full EIP-712 digest; C2 one payer and one token per entry; C3 the node-relayable `<Op>` field types; C4 the gateway unchanged; C5 the balance-delta check always on; C6 the ids; C7 the names `ServicePullShape`, `ServicePullNotReceived`, `ServicePullReplayed`, `ServicePullFrozen`, `servicePullEntries`.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`: T77 `b9b130bb` (the reference service, test only, and its tests), T78 `9fe6253d` (vectors and the `clientkeys` builder), T79 `711f4f35` (the node kind `service`); SPECIFIED for third-party services and for `ua-rs` (T80, its client rule on branch `ua-rs-sign`). UNAUDITED.
**Why.** CTR-TOK-01 forbids allowances for EOAs and UAs; a service still needs "take X from the payer and run my logic, atomic and relayable". The pull keeps that and drops what an allowance adds: standing authority, an open amount, a window.
**Cost if wrong.** A service that skips a check of §3.3 can be paid for an operation it never ran, or run one it was not paid for; the wallet shows a payment, not the operation (Q2's residual).
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-09 (Q1–Q5 as recommended); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-service-pull.md` §3, §5, §8, §13.

## 18. Contracts — Token wrappers and factory

### CTR-TOK-01 — Only contracts call approve, are spenders, or call transferFrom
- old: R26 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-01 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — a Universal Account never grants or holds an allowance either (no `uaApprove`); contracts move a UA's funds only against signed, named intents (CTR-UA-27). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.4, UP-10, Q2.

**Why.** An allowance held or granted by an EOA is the classic drain vector; the owner narrowed the rule to the **caller** of `approve` as well, so an EOA never holds or grants an allowance on a SCaaS token in any form (no meta-tx `approve`, no permit). Contract accounts approve through their own call path, where their guards run; a `TradeOrder`'s `dex` must be a contract and nothing more (owner-accepted residual risk, CTR-DEX-19). Outside tokens are not ours: an EOA may approve our wrapper on USDT.
**Cost if wrong.** EOA phishing approvals drain balances; a gasless ERC-1271 `approve` would bypass Safe guards and thresholds.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-addendum-wallets.md:198`. Owner wording: "spender là hợp đồng" (the spender is a contract); `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A5, A6, §3 MG-7, §8 Q5.
Change (2026-11-09, group 3i, owner Q1–Q5): a contract that must take a payer's SCaaS tokens into its custody uses a service pull ([CTR-MTX-32](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-32)), never an allowance. Status: BUILT on the EVM (T77 `b9b130bb`: the token side unchanged, the reference service test only).

### CTR-TOK-03 — One factory OpenFactory; append-only kinds; chainUid check
- old: R130 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** With nothing deployed, the owner kept only the factory v2 code, renamed `OpenFactory`; the version catalogue stays append-only and the factory registers only implementations whose `chainUid()` equals its own, so a clone's domain salt has one source. The kinds are [CTR-TOK-21](contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-21) and the creation API [CTR-TOK-25](contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-25).
**Cost if wrong.** Two factories split provenance and tender checks; a mismatched implementation would mint clones whose signatures verify on no chain.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:66`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-4, MG-9, §7 (CTR-TOK-03/12 row).

Change (2026-10-20): owner rulings 2026-10-19 / 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z1) — the constructor takes `Canonical` (the
confidential verifiers, CTR-ZTH-20) and `registerImplementation` checks a confidential release against it
(`NotCanonicalVerifiers`); `deprecate` is immediate and `createToken` refuses a deprecated version (`VersionDeprecated`;

a later `usableFrom` notice period (plan 5g-Z2) is a small addition. Status: built, commit `690a295a` (plan Task 5g-Z1).

Change (2026-10-20): owner rulings 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z2) — **the factory deploys every release on a versioned
environment.** The constructor is `(registrar, chainUid, noticePeriod)` (5g-Z1's `Canonical` removed). The registrar
publishes per kind (and one DEX domain) a versioned, append-only, never-changed `Env {factory, chainUid, registry,
smartKeyAccountImpl, hedera, deps, libs, libCodeHashes}` (`publishEnv`, `publishDexEnv`; the factory's own factory and
`chainUid`, else `EnvInvalid`) and releases code with `deployTokenImplementation(kind, version, envVersion, initcode,
implArgs)` / `deployDexImplementation(version, envVersion, initcode, implArgs)`: the factory checks each library's code

records `Release {implementation, envVersion, envHash, usableFrom, deprecated}`; the events carry the env hash, the

usable `noticePeriod` seconds after its deployment (`VersionNotYetUsable`); the deploy's `NOTICE_PERIOD` defaults to
10 minutes on the SCaaS testnet, 3 days on 22776, 0 elsewhere. (2) **Library pins** (owner ruling 2026-10-20, confirmed):
`Env.libs` is the registrar's list of the libraries the release links, each pinned by code hash
(`LibraryCodeHashMismatch`); the factory does not parse the init code to compare the list with its link references.
(3) **Env binding** (owner ruling 2026-10-20: **no** to "`deployTokenImplementation` binds the kind's latest env"; the final
rule belongs to a later governance-matrix spec): interim, **controller proposal 2026-10-20, owner may override** —
`deployTokenImplementation` / `deployDexImplementation` take an explicit `envVersion` that must be published for that kind

defaults of item (1) above) and the review 5g-Z2 fixes. (1) `DeployBase` is safe by default: a fixed list of test / dev
