**Change (2026-11-10, owner ruling; BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`): the release entry points renamed.** Old: `deployImplementation(kind, version, envVersion, initcode, implArgs)` was the token-kind path and `deployRelease(id, envVersion, initSelector, interfaceId, initcode, implArgs)` the generic class path. New: the token-kind path is `deployTokenImplementation` (selector `0x276344e9` -> `0x7d847eae`), the generic class path is `deployImplementation` (`0x72fb13f7` -> `0x8968d1ae`); `deployDexImplementation` keeps its name. Arguments, checks, events (`ImplementationDeployed`, `DexImplementationDeployed`, `ReleaseDeployed`) and errors are unchanged. Renamed everywhere at once in current code and docs (`src/`, `test/`, `script/` with `script/onchain/`, `scaas-node/tests/e2e.rs`, the current docs, specs and plans, this register's older entries included); `legacy/`, `docs/history/`, `docs/research/` and the run records under `runs/` keep the names of their time. No selector table, audit row or client encodes either entry. The factory already deployed on the SCaaS testnet is immutable and keeps the old names; a factory built from this code answers only the new ones.
Change (2026-11-07, chain-neutral releases, CTR-TOK-29): the constructor takes the registrar only; `configureChain(chainUid, noticePeriod, govRouter, refBlock, refHash)` sets the chain's values once and every publish, deploy and creation entry refuses before it (`ChainNotConfigured`); envs carry no factory, `chainUid` or router, and `deployTokenImplementation` no longer reads a release's `chainUid()` (a release is chain-neutral; the clone's is checked after `initialize`). The deploy scripts and the sibling order of the deploy gate follow (T73 `bbcbbe85`). Status: BUILT (T71 `b61ac38d`, T72 `612981b9`, T73).

### CTR-TOK-04 — Conversion rate num/den, rounding favours contract
- old: R133 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Rates as `(num, den)` with rounding in favour of the contract keep reserves solvent under every rounding path.
**Cost if wrong.** Rounding in favour of users leaks value per operation and can drain reserves.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:84`

### CTR-TOK-05 — Internal reserve accounting and solvency invariant
- old: R134 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Internal reserve accounting ignores donations and forced sends, so the solvency invariant is checkable from the contract's own state.
**Cost if wrong.** Balance-based accounting lets an attacker skew rates with a donation.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:91`
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner ruling CTR-GOV-12): on a hybrid, a wrapped token with `maxSupply ≠ 0`, the solvency invariant is not claimed: `totalSupply() ≤ maxSupply` holds instead, `balanceOf_i ≥ reserve_i` stays, a mint adds no reserve, and `executeRate` runs every check but the supply comparison. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T9 `20620a1e`).

### CTR-TOK-06 — Fixed or timelocked adjustable rate at creation
- old: R135 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-06 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The issuer chooses at creation between a fixed rate and a timelocked adjustable one; holders see the choice before they wrap.
**Cost if wrong.** A silently adjustable rate is an admin key over holders' value.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:98`
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner ruling CTR-GOV-12): `collateralValue() ≥ totalSupply()` after a rate change holds except on a hybrid (CTR-TOK-05). Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T9 `20620a1e`).

### CTR-TOK-07 — Multi-underlying any-of with disable-only guardian
- old: R136 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Multi-underlying is any-of with a disable-only guardian: holders can always exit through any enabled leg and nobody can add a leg. Rejected: a weighted basket that mints from a group of tokens at fixed proportions — it needs price oracles and rebalancing, which the immutable design forbids.
**Cost if wrong.** A basket would introduce oracle and rebalancing risk into every wrap and unwrap.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:108`

### CTR-TOK-08 — Decimals are display only
- old: R137 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-08 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Decimals are display only; arithmetic uses raw units, so a decimals mismatch can never misprice a wrap.
**Cost if wrong.** Scaling by decimals inside the contract adds rounding paths and errors.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:115`

### CTR-TOK-09 — NormalToken holder burn, renounceable minter
- old: R141 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A `NormalToken` lets holders burn and its minter retire, which matches self-issued tokens; both are now the flags `BURNABLE` and `MINTABLE`, the minter a granted role whose holder may `renounceRole` ([CTR-TOK-22](contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-22)).
**Cost if wrong.** A non-renounceable minter is a permanent admin key.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:135`

### CTR-TOK-10 — Only creation-time visible admin exceptions
- old: R142 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-10 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Only publicly visible admin exceptions exist, so a holder can read every power over a token before acquiring it. Features stay creation-time ([CTR-TOK-22](contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-22)); the earlier creation-time-only roles are superseded by roles the owner grants and revokes (owner ruling), all public on chain.
**Cost if wrong.** Hidden or later-added powers would make provenance meaningless.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:138`
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-08, -12, -13): no role moves balances except under `FORCE` or `MODERATE`, on public balances, chosen at creation (neither built); a hybrid's issuer mints unbacked units under `maxSupply`. Status: hybrid BUILT on branch `governance` (T9 `20620a1e`); `FORCE` and `MODERATE` SPECIFIED.

### CTR-TOK-11 — Fee-on-transfer-out and rebasing underlyings unsupported
- old: R143 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-11 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Fee-on-transfer-out and rebasing underlyings break 1:1 accounting; they are refused rather than half-supported.
**Cost if wrong.** Supporting them silently would make reserves drift from supply.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:144`

### CTR-TOK-12 — Voluntary v2 migration; domain read per token
- old: R146 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-TOK-03, CTR-MTX-02

**What it said.** v1 clones and factory v1 stayed untouched beside v2 and holders migrated voluntarily; clients read the domain and pay lane per token.
**Why.** Nothing is deployed, so the v1 line is deleted instead of migrated (CTR-TOK-03); reading the domain per token survives in CTR-MTX-02.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:156`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A4, §7.

### CTR-TOK-13 — Multi rates adjustable per leg, default off
- old: R147 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-13 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Per-leg adjustable multi rates are an issuer option, off by default.
**Cost if wrong.** Default-on adjustability would surprise holders of plain wrappers.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:160`

### CTR-TOK-14 — Gasless wrap through permit is planned only
- old: R149 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-TOK-20, CTR-MTX-19

**What it said.** A gasless wrap through an EIP-2612/Permit2 op was planned only.
**Why.** Gasless wrap is now `mtxExecute(wrap)` under an allowance on an outside underlying (CTR-MTX-19) or `mtxWrap` by signature for a SCaaS underlying (CTR-TOK-20); no permit op is needed.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:184`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §7 (CTR-TOK-14 row).

### CTR-TOK-15 — Open factory: anyone creates tokens
- old: UD:§20 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-15 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An open factory means anyone can create tokens or wrap any token; SCaaS is not a gatekeeper.
**Cost if wrong.** Spam tokens exist; provenance getters (CTR-TOK-17) let clients filter them.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:1079`

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-19 (plan 5g-Z1, CTR-ZTH-20) — the factory stays open for token creation; what the
creator no longer chooses is a confidential token's verifier: it is fixed by the implementation release (constructor
immutables, registered only on the factory's canonical set), and the creator picks it only by picking the version. Status: built, commit `690a295a` (plan Task 5g-Z1).

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z2) — the confidential release's verifiers are the `deps` of the env
version the registrar names at `deployTokenImplementation` (CTR-TOK-03 Change of 2026-10-20), immutables of its code by
construction; the creator still picks them only by picking the version. Status: built on branch `rev2-zether-z2`, commit `0f88e66f` (plan Task 5g-Z2).

### CTR-TOK-16 — getWrapper keyed by creator and underlying
- old: UD:§20.3 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-16 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Wrappers are looked up by `(creator, underlying)`, so two creators never collide and no global "official" wrapper exists. Three lookups answer three questions: getWrapper(creator, underlying) is A's xDAI wrapper; getWrapperCount / getWrapperAt list all of A's xDAI wrappers (one per curve or fee schedule); deployCountFor / deployedFor list every zDAI wrapper of every creator so the market can compare A with B. There is no uniqueness on `underlying` alone and no name or symbol review: `zDAI-A` and `zDAI-B` coexist normally.
**Cost if wrong.** A global wrapper slot invites squatting.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:1210`

### CTR-TOK-17 — Provenance getters instead of gatekeeping
- old: UD:§20.4 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-17 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Every token answers immutably who created it and from which implementation; clients decide trust instead of the factory.
**Cost if wrong.** Clients that ignore provenance can be shown look-alike tokens.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:1255`

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-19 (plan 5g-Z1) — provenance gains `isRegisteredToken(token)` (made from a registered
version, `version ≠ 0`); a version-0 token is unvetted code and clients and the gateway treat it so. For confidential
tokens the factory is the published source of the canonical verifiers (CTR-ZTH-20) instead of a client-side list. Status: built, commit `690a295a` (plan Task 5g-Z1).

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z2) — the factory publishes a confidential token's verifiers through its
release: `releaseOf(kind, version)` gives `envVersion` and `envHash`, `envOf(kind, envVersion).deps` the addresses (5g-Z1's
`zetherVerifiers` / `pqzVerifier` views are removed with `Canonical`). Status: built on branch `rev2-zether-z2`, commit `0f88e66f` (plan Task 5g-Z2).

### CTR-TOK-18 — Factory is the critical immutable artifact
- old: UD:§20.6 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-18 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The factory is the most critical immutable artifact: every clone inherits its code choices.
**Cost if wrong.** A factory bug is inherited by every token created through it until a new factory ships.
**Source.** `research/_USER-DECISIONS.md:1288`

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z2) — the chain and verifier checks leave the factory for the
implementations' `initialize`: a Zether token reverts `VerifierUnsupportedOnThisChain` when the release's transfer
verifier's `isSupportedOnThisChain()` is false or unanswered (`ZetherLib.init`, was the factory's `_checkZether`), and
outside a dev chain (`ZetherSafety`); a PQZ token runs `PqzSafety` (was also `_checkPqz`). The factory keeps one generic
gate, `setKindEnabled(kind, on)` (registrar; it replaces `setZetherEnabled` / `setPqzEnabled`); **controller proposal,
owner may override:** the plain kinds start enabled, the confidential kinds disabled, and `setKindEnabled` itself runs
no chain check (the token's `initialize` does). Status: built on branch `rev2-zether-z2`, commit `0f88e66f` (plan Task 5g-Z2).

### CTR-TOK-19 — Multi wrap checks only its own leg's reserve
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-19 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The reserve rule (CTR-TOK-05) stays per leg: `wrap`/`addReserve` on leg A check only leg A's `balanceOf ≥ reserve`, and a shortfall on another leg is disclosed and alerted on instead of blocking intake. Rejected: checking every leg on a multi `wrap` and `addReserve` (at most 8 `balanceOf`, as `executeRate` already does) — it would amend CTR-TOK-05.
**Cost if wrong.** After one leg loses backing, new deposits into a good leg mint at par into an under-backed pool and early exiters take the good assets those deposits brought; the mitigation is off-chain (per-leg backing alerts, issuer pausing intake by communication, wallets showing per-leg backing).
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:596` (owner decision 2026-10-06, implementation review L3); `history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md:925` (the open question it answers)

### CTR-TOK-20 — Signature wrap of a SCaaS underlying (mtxWrap)
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-20 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — `uaWrap(u, UATradeOrder, auth)`: the same wrap by signature with a UA order pulled by the underlying's `uaTrade`, minting to a `bytes32` destination (derived: `_uaMint`); event `UAWrapped`. SPECIFIED (UA-5b). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.3.

Change (2026-10-13): built as ruled (UA-5b): `uaWrap` in `WrappedToken` / `WrappedLib`. Controller ruling, confirmed by the owner 2026-10-13: it emits `UAWrapped` only (no `Wrapped`), the leg check is ERC-165 on `IUALedger` before the pull (C5b-9). Source add: plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-ua5b-trade-dex.md`.

**Why.** An EOA holding a SCaaS underlying cannot approve the wrapper, so the owner accepted a signature wrap: the holder signs a `TradeOrder` in the underlying's domain naming the wrapper as `dex`; the wrapper pulls through the underlying's `mtxTrade`, checks the received amount and mints in the same call, paying the relayer from the order's `fee`.
**Cost if wrong.** Without it, holders of SCaaS underlyings could never wrap (or fund Zether) without a contract account.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A9, §3 MG-7b.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner decision 6 of 2026-10-31, TS-D16, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C2, C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): a wrap by signature is a `WrapOrder` (the 12 `TradeOrder` fields with `receiveToken -> wrappedToken`, `receiveAmount -> minMinted`, `dex` dropped), entry `mtxWrapOrder(address underlying, WrapOrder, bytes sig)` / `uaWrapOrder(address underlying, UAWrapOrder, UASig)`, so `mtxWrap` is the named entry of `wrap(uint256)`. The underlying's order digest hashes `dex == receiveToken` as `WrapOrder`, every other order as `TradeOrder`. The wrap, unwrap, burn and reserve entries (`mtxWrap`, `mtxWrapLeg`, `mtxWrapToUA`, `mtxAddReserve`, `mtxUnwrap`, `mtxUnwrapLeg`, `mtxUnwrapToUA`, `mtxBurn` and `ua*` twins) are named typed entries; the flat `uaUnwrap` went to `legacy/typed-signing/` (owner 2026-11-01).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R39; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `mtxWrapOrder(address underlying, ITradeToken.UAWrapOrder o, IUARegistry.UASig auth)` is today's `uaWrapOrder`; `WrapOrder` and `CancelWrapOrder` are no longer in `src`, and their `typed_ops.json` rows retire (MD-7).

### CTR-TOK-21 — One implementation per kind; the token tree
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-21 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Two axes: the kind is code (`NORMAL`, `WRAPPED` with 1–8 legs, `NORMAL_ZETHER`, `WRAPPED_ZETHER`; four PQZ kinds reserved), the features are flags; the tree is `MetaTxBase` → `ERC20MetaTx` → `MetaTokenBase` → kinds. Single and Multi merge (the leg count says which); Hedera is a deploy-time `IS_HEDERA`, not a child contract; every token can trade. The built code carries three generations side by side and the Zether token duplicates a second wrapper tier.
**Cost if wrong.** Per-combination contracts multiply audits and overflow EIP-170 (today `ZetherToken` is 4,363 B over); a creator could not pick "single underlying, payable off, confidential".
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §1, §2 (T1, T3, T9, T10, T13), §3.

Change (2026-10-20, owner): **the reserved kinds `NORMAL_ZETHER_PQZ` and `WRAPPED_ZETHER_PQZ` are dropped** (a token carries at most one confidential layer; a holder who wants both uses two tokens). Ids 6 and 7 are not reused for anything else; the enum entries go with the `mtxShield` / `mtxUnshield` rework (no layer argument needed; CTR-ZTH-45 change) — all chains are test-only. Specs to update with it: token-wrappers.md kind table, pq-zero-knowledge.md, contracts/README.md. Status: decided; code change with plan Task 5h.

The kind table in token-wrappers.md and the contracts/README picture caption were updated; the SVG pictures still show the reserved boxes (docs follow-up). Status: decided (owner); built.

Unchanged and checked: the ABI (selectors, events, errors), the storage layout and the runtime and creation bytecode without the CBOR metadata of every `src/` contract (119). Why: the names say what the kind is (a plain issued token, a wrapper), not what it lacks. Cost if wrong: a second rename; tooling that read the old deploy keys must re-deploy or re-read. ### CTR-TOK-22 — Features are flags: features, lockedFeatures, owner, roles, disableFeature
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-22 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One administration word chosen at creation (bits 0–8: `PAYABLE`, `MINTABLE`, `BURNABLE`, `RATE_ADJUSTABLE`, `WRAP_DISABLEABLE`, `FREEZE`, `FORCE`, `PAUSE`, `ALLOWLIST`); per flag the creator picks locked or disableable (the owner may clear it once, never set it). Owner ruling: issuers administer through one `owner` (optional; candidate OpenZeppelin `AccessControlDefaultAdminRules`, decided in P1) who grants and revokes the roles and disables disableable flags, and can give everything up: after `renounceOwnership()` role holders keep their roles, so an unchangeable token means revoking every role first. The built `renounceMinter`, `renounceRateAdmin`, `renounceGuardian` correspond to the holder's `renounceRole`, `disableControls` to `disableFeature`. Validation lives in the token's `initialize` (`FeatureInvalidForKind`, `LockedNotSubset`, `RoleWithoutFeature`); `PAYABLE` is default off; `PAYABLE` and `BURNABLE` have no role and are always locked (`disableFeature` reverts `FeatureLocked(bit)`); the token refuses flags 5–8 on a confidential kind; a minter never mints into a shielded balance.
Change (2026-10-09): `PAYABLE` and `BURNABLE` have no role and are always treated as locked; `disableFeature(PAYABLE|BURNABLE)` reverts `FeatureLocked(bit)`.
**Cost if wrong.** Per-class powers cannot express a mix; an unvalidated factory-side check would let `createTokenUnregistered` bring a token with inconsistent roles.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §2 (T2, T5, T8, T11), §5.
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-01 with its Change, -02, -04, -06, -10 with its Change, -12, -18): the flag table and the administration bullet follow `GovernanceBase`. Old rule: an `address` owner in `AdminLib` grants and revokes at once, flags 5–8 regulated, bits 0–63 SCaaS's, 64–127 the application's and 128 and above refused. New rule: the owner and every holder are UA ids; a new holder or a wider `Grant` takes two calls within `[eta, eta + grantDelay]`; `cancelGrant`; `renounceOwnership` reverts while a bit that is not locked has a live root; `hasRole` means listed, not able to act; bit 1 on a hybrid, bit 9 `DENYLIST`, bit 17 `RESCUABLE`, bit 21 `MODERATE`; bits 0–127 SCaaS's, 128–255 the application's, none refused; views `grantDelay`, `pendingGrant`, `lastProposedAt`, `holderCount`, `grantOf`, `validBits`. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T3–T10b, T11); bits 5–10 and 21 SPECIFIED.
Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3s, [CTR-GOV-24](#ctr-gov-24--kyc-bit-28-allowlist-and-denylist-lists-held-in-the-token-enabled-at-once); status: BUILT (ua-mtx-3s)): on the regulated kinds bits 8, 9 and 28 may be set after creation by the admin's `enableFeature`, at once; 8 and 9 are then never cleared (`disableFeature` refuses `FeatureNotDisableable`); `lockedFeatures` may hold 8, 9 or 28 while unset, which fixes the bit off (`enableFeature` refuses `FeatureLocked`). Every other flag unchanged: set at creation, cleared once, never set.
Change (2026-11-11, controller call under the owner's leave of 2026-11-10, quoted in [CTR-GOV-24](#ctr-gov-24--kyc-bit-28-allowlist-and-denylist-lists-held-in-the-token-enabled-at-once)'s Source; group 3s, after Fable's review; status: BUILT (ua-mtx-3s)): the grant rule "a role only on a set bit" (`RoleWithoutFeature`) is relaxed for bits 8 and 9 only: a role on them may be granted, and its holder may edit the list, while the bit is off and not locked off, so a list is written before `enableFeature`; at init the issuer seat takes each of them for which the "enableable" predicate of CTR-GOV-24 holds.

### CTR-TOK-23 — Hedera is IS_HEDERA, not a child contract
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-23 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Hedera is a per-chain variant, so each implementation carries an immutable `IS_HEDERA`; when set the signature check takes the HIP-632 path and `WrappedLib` associates HTS underlyings fail-closed (`HederaLib`). The three Hedera children and four copies of the override go for about 0.5–1 KB per implementation.
**Cost if wrong.** Hedera children triple the deployable set and keep four copies of one override in sync by hand.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §2 (T3, T13), §3.

### CTR-TOK-24 — External libraries, ERC-7201 namespaces, size budget
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Heavy logic moves to external libraries linked at deploy (`TradeLib`, `PayLib`, `AdminLib`, `WrappedLib`, `ZetherLib`, `HederaLib`); the transfer hot path and the per-transfer administration check stay inline. Each module keeps state in its own ERC-7201 namespace so libraries never overlap; each token implementation is capped at 20,480 B (about 4 KB of room for later streams) and CI fails above it.
**Cost if wrong.** Without the split the rewrite does not fit EIP-170 (24,576 B); shared storage between libraries would corrupt silently.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §1, §4.

Change (2026-10-31, controller record under the owner's code-size rule of 2026-10-21): **`UARegistry.init` is a size-baseline entry**, 53,736 B of init code (runtime 46,734 B, under the 65,536 B ceiling). The explicit registry ABI took it past EIP-3860's 49,152 B, the limit `scripts/size_gate.py` still checks; it is under Amsterdam's 131,072 B, which the test chains run. An entry only records the ratchet; it changes no rule. Status: built in typed-signing R1b, re-recorded with the later `register` ruling (CTR-UA-36).

Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C0, controller record under the owner's code-size rule of 2026-10-21; status: decided, the following line; commit: typed-signing C0, the `main` merge commit follows): **the full Part C entry list does not fit the two wrapped confidential kinds without a lever, so the TS-D18 stop rule applied and C1 waits.** A compile-only mock of the token side of C2, C3, C4 and the C6 relay fee ends `WrappedPqzToken` about 11.9 KB and `WrappedZetherToken` about 12.8 KB over the 65,536 B ceiling; every other contract stays under. Above the ceiling the assembler also widens every jump target to PUSH3, about 5.2 KB more on the raw figures (82,726 B and 83,448 B). Moving the `nonReentrant` body into shared private functions frees about 9 KB per wrapped token at no gas cost, and with the init path and the selector table behind external libraries every contract fits (61,378 B and 61,704 B). No lever is on the branch. The spike keeps `MtxPipelineLib.preNamed` over the existing pipeline envelope, so one function serves both paths, and adds `uaShield` beside `mtxShield` so the UA path of the pattern is tested (controller calls, owner may override). The baseline holds the spike's sizes, a ratchet as before.
Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, status: decided, built in typed-signing C2–C4; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): size levers for the named entries: lever 2 (one shared `nonReentrant` body, `private` `_enter` / `_exit` in `MetaTxBase`) and lever 1 (the init path and the selector table of the wrapped confidential kinds behind external library calls). `optimizer_runs` stays 200 and `via_ir` stays off. Real code above about 64.5 KB on a wrapped kind stops for the owner; lever 3 (views behind `fallback`) or B′ is the reserve. Figures: `docs/research/evm-size-levers.md`.
Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, status: decided, built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): `uaExecute` is general, so non-token contracts may take UA-signed calls later. New `abstract contract UAMetaTxBase is MetaTxBase` holds the registry reference and the UA pipeline; its fee hook refuses a fee ≠ 0 by default, and `ERC20MetaTx` overrides it with the UA ledger. `MetaTxBase`, `SmartKeyAccount` and `MandateWallet` carry no UA code. A non-token contract reads `_ticketSubject()`, because `_msgSender()` is `UA_POOL` for every derived subject.
Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, status: decided, built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands; replaces the controller call to remove it): `executeMetaTransaction` stays in `MetaTxBase` and `IMetaTx`, beside `mtxExecute`, on every contract as today; it signs `address from`, so it does not belong in `UAMetaTxBase`. `mtxExecuteWithFee` still goes to `legacy/typed-signing/`. The entry shares the EIP-1776 name only: selector `0x47aea5b5`, against `0x0c53c51c` of the common `executeMetaTransaction(address,bytes,bytes32,bytes32,uint8)`; ERC-1776 itself defines no such function.
Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, status: decided, built in typed-signing C2's review fix round; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the flat `uaUnwrap(bytes32 from, …)` overload moves to `legacy/typed-signing/`, the named `uaUnwrap(UAEnvelope, …, UASig)` replaces it. Controller correction, owner may override: `mtxCancelNonce` is declared in `IMetaTx`, and the id is re-pinned.
Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, status: decided): `UARegistry` is not split. The earlier ruling of the same day for R1′ + R2 is replaced after measurement: under legacy codegen the external wrapper keeps the ABI encoders, so R1′ leaves `UARegistry` at 39,288 B with +10,457 B in total and needs a pointer cast past the view checker; the one-library form does not fit a 60M block. R2 alone (`UARegisterLib`: registry 28,048 B, library 31,257 B, every transaction under 60M, `register` about +6 k gas, total bytes +27 %) is the reserve, for a chain near BSC's 70M. `fallback` stays rejected.
Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C2, controller calls, owner may override; status: decided, built in typed-signing C2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): (1) `UAMetaTxBase` also holds what `_mtxCtx` and a non-token reader need: the immutables `_SMART_KEY_CLONE_CODEHASH` and `IS_HEDERA`, and the views `registry`, `uaNonce`, `uaDigest`. (2) `IUALedger` keeps all its functions, so its ERC-165 id stays; `ERC20MetaTx` therefore spells out the five joins (`registry`, `uaNonce`, `uaDigest`, `uaExecute`, `uaBatch`, +57 B per token), and `IZetherToken` no longer inherits `IUALedger`, since that second path would ask every Zether contract for the same five. An inherited function is not part of an interface id, so no id moves; `ZetherStatements` reads `registry()` through `IUALedger`. (3) The default `_uaChargeFee` reverts `MetaTxUnknownMode(mode)`, the address path's refusal on a contract without a balance. `supportedModes()` rules both paths (`CallFacts.supported`, C2 review), so a non-token at 0x03 refuses every fee mode on `uaExecute` as on `mtxExecute`, a fee of 0 included, and the hook is reached only by a contract that claims a fee mode. (4) `mtxCancelNonce` is on `MetaTxBase` and declared in `IMetaTx`, like every entry on every contract (owner 2026-11-01, C2 review; the first pass left it out on a brief that meant only `executeMetaTransaction`): `type(IMetaTx).interfaceId` 0xf6695913 -> 0x2f1aa7fe on every token kind, pinned by `test_iMetaTxIdPinned`; the wallets answer no ERC-165. (5) On a named `ua*` entry a native id signs with `UASig.signature`; `keyData` and `members` are ignored there, as they are unsigned and carry no authority. (6) Named `ua*` entries reach the registry through the new `MtxPipelineLib.preNamedUA`, which passes the `UASig` as it came; `preNamed` keeps `bytes auth` for the address path and `uaShield`. (7) The flat `uaUnwrap(bytes32 from, address underlying, …)` of `MetaTokenBase` went to `legacy/typed-signing/` in the C2 review (owner 2026-11-01): it duplicated the named `uaUnwrap` / `uaUnwrapLeg`. `mtxWrap(address, TradeOrder, bytes)` stays beside `mtxWrap(Envelope, …)` until C6 renames it (TS-D16); tests read that selector through `IWrapOrder`. (8) C2 review, for a non-token on `UAMetaTxBase`: `uaCancelNonce`, `uaCancelDigest` and the `scaas.ua.ledger` storage struct move there (same slot, same field order; `balance` stays the ledger's, `cancelUsed` is every contract's), seven joins on `ERC20MetaTx`. `cancelNonce` refuses a sender of `UA_POOL` with `MtxSelectorNotAllowed` rather than act on the subject: refusing is smaller, and `MetaNonceCancelled` has no field for a derived id. `_subject()` gives an op body the ticket subject, else the caller padded. `_requireValidSignature` on `UAMetaTxBase` runs `MtxPipelineLib.requireSignature` under `_mtxCtx`, so a non-token's address path takes the HIP-632 and clone rules; a token's `_execute` never reaches it.
Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C3, controller record under the owner's lever ruling of 2026-11-01; status: decided, built in typed-signing C3; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): **lever 1 is on `WrappedZetherToken`, in a new library `ZetherWrappedLib`.** Real figures: the kind ends at 60,759 B with the lever and 64,475 B without it (−3,716 B; the library 4,958 B). Without it the kind is 25 B under the 64.5 KB stop line with C6 still to add entries, so it is not well under and the lever is needed. `MetaTokenBase.initialize` calls a new hook `_initRaw(initArgs)`, whose default decodes `TokenConfig` and calls `_init`; `WrappedZetherToken` overrides it to hand the raw bytes to `ZetherWrappedLib.init`, and `mtxSelectors()` returns `ZetherWrappedLib.selectors()`. The library is in the link closure of `WRAPPED_ZETHER` only (`DeployBase`, `Catalogue.closureLibs`), so `NORMAL_ZETHER` keeps its closure and `ZetherLib` keeps no DELEGATECALL; `LinkClosure.test_libraryOpcodes` pins exactly 2 for it (`WrappedLib.initToken`, `ZetherLib.init`). `WRAPPED_PQZ` is C4's. Figures: `docs/research/evm-size-levers.md` §9. `NormalZetherToken.init` joins the size baseline at 55,218 B, as `UARegistry.init` (past EIP-3860, under Amsterdam's 131,072 B, which the test chains run).
Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C3, controller calls, owner may override; status: decided, built in typed-signing C3; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): classical Zether on the explicit parameters. (1) The direct ops take `ZetherSingle` / `ZetherMulti` / `ZetherBurn` and `proof` (Appendix X.3); their signed overloads and `ua*` twins live on `ZetherLayer` / `WrappedZetherToken` only, not in `IZetherToken`, so `IZetherToken.<op>.selector` stays unique for the allowlist. (2) `IConfidentialToken` keeps the events, `mtxShield` and `mtxRollOver`; `IConfidentialWrappedToken` keeps `Unwrap` and `mtxWrapShield`. The packed signatures moved unchanged to `IPqzToken` and a new `IPqzWrappedToken` until C4; the Zether form is in a new `IZetherWrappedToken`. PQZ code changes: those two interfaces and the base list and import of `WrappedPqzToken`, nothing else. (3) `ZetherLib` takes the structs itself: a point's `abi.encode` is its 128 bytes, so statement and record are assembled without a packed payload in between (old vs new bytes pinned by `test_zetherTransferExplicitStatementBytes` on every prover row, `test_zetherTransferStoredBytesUnchanged`, `zether-cross`). The fold's preconditions in `docs/research/zether-msm-crypto-review.md` hold unchanged: every point of the statement reaches the MSM, `fee < 2^64` and `0 < amount ≤ maxShielded` are checked before the header. (4) `MemoSaltMismatch`, `AuthNotEmpty` and `AccHintNotEmpty` go, they cannot occur any more; `BadPayload` remains for a `sealedMemo` of the wrong length and now carries that length. (5) `BadPoint` is in `IZetherToken`'s ABI. (6) `ERC20MetaTx._namedCall` and `UAMetaTxBase._namedCallUA` are added for an entry whose struct words are not its call's arguments; `_uaMetaOf` and `_uaSettle` are private, so `UAMetaTxBase` had to change; a non-token path is not affected. (7) `Env.domainSeparator` is filled on every op, for the owner digests; `mtxUnshieldUnwrap` takes `_env()` and sets the direct binding itself, so `_envUnwrap` goes. (8) The signed transfer entries return `bytes32` as Appendix X.3 says, the others `bytes memory` as the C0 spike. (9) zether-prover keeps its packed `payload` field and builds `directCalldata` on the explicit ABI (`transfer_single_call`, `transfer_multi_call`, `unshield_call`); only `directCalldata` moved in its vectors. (10) `zetherOwnerAuth` in clientkeys goes to `legacy/typed-signing/`: the owner ops take `UASig` (`zetherOwnerSig`). The packed surface is kept, not built, in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/typed-signing/ZetherPacked.sol` and `clients/zether-prover/legacy/typed-signing/envelope_packed.rs`.
Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C6, controller calls, owner may override; status: decided, built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): trade, DEX, receiver fee, relay fee and UA cancel on typed structs (TS-D19), `typed_ops.json`'s rows run under each token's and the DEX's own domain. Calls taken where the plan left a choice:

- **`uaTrade`, `uaInvalidateNonces` and the UA transfer entries take `UASig` too (Appendix X row 9).** `uaWrapOrder(address, UAWrapOrder, UASig)` hands its `auth` to the underlying's `uaTrade`, and `uaPayReceiverFee` hands its `payerAuth` to the typed UA pipeline, so keeping `bytes auth` there would have meant re-encoding a `UASig` into the old blob, or a second pipeline. `uaExecuteTransfer`, `uaBatchTransfer` (`UASig[]`), `uaTransfer`, `uaTransferWithFee`, `uaPay`, `uaPayMeta`, `uaTrade`, `uaCancelOrder`, `uaInvalidateNonces`, `uaCancelNonce`, `uaPayReceiverFee` and `RelayFeeRouter.uaRelay` all do; `MtxPipelineLib.preTransferUA` is the UA half of `preTransfer` and `authorize` takes `UASig`. `uaExecute`, `uaBatch` and `uaShield` keep `bytes auth` (owner table). `clientkeys` `buildUaPayMeta` encodes the `UASig`.
- **`DexLeg` (Appendix X row 20) replaces `Leg`, and `ExchangeLeg` takes the same members.** With `uaTrade` on `UASig` the DEX has to hold one, so the opaque `bytes order` / `bytes sig` of a leg become `TradeOrder order`, `UATradeOrder uaOrder`, `bytes sig`, `UASig auth`; the members of the other shape stay zero and nothing reads them. A dirty address word in a leg now reverts the whole `mtxSettle` at the outer re-encoding of the settlement, where `abi.decode` used to fail only that settlement inside its self-call: the submitter's own malformed calldata, caught by its simulation.
- **The token digests of an order go through one `TradeLib.orderHash(c, ua)`:** `dex == receiveToken` hashes as `WrapOrder` / `UAWrapOrder`, every other order as `TradeOrder` / `UATradeOrder`, and `pulled` stays keyed by that digest. A `DexOrder` nests `hashStruct`, always the `TradeOrder` form. `TradeLib.cancelHash` is a public library function (a rare path, four type strings the tokens need not carry).
- **Views.** `cancelOrderDigest(TradeOrder)`, `cancelUAOrderDigest(UATradeOrder)`, `receiverFeeDigest(MetaTransfer, …)`, `uaReceiverFeeDigest(UAMetaTransfer, …)` and on the DEX `cancelDexOrderDigest(sellToken, TradeOrder)` replace the views over a digest, since a nested struct hashes the struct, not its digest. A wrap order's cancel digest comes from the same `cancelOrderDigest`, by `dex == receiveToken`. No `relayFeeDigest` view: the size, and the client builds it.
- **`relayer` of `RelayFee` is read as `msg.sender`, not passed (C1's table).** So `msg.sender != relayer` is refused by the signature: a caller other than the router hashes itself and gets `MetaTxBadSignature`. The router's old shape refusals (`entryRef`, lane, nonce, fee mode, bound relayer) cannot occur any more, the token builds those fields; `_shape` keeps the payee-is-the-executor refusal and the target's code. A payment for another target, call or chain now fails at the signature, after the target call ran, and the revert unwinds it, where `RelayFeeShape` used to fire before the call. `mtxRelayFee` / `uaRelayFee` are in `IERC20MetaTx` / `IUALedger`, so both ERC-165 ids move, and are not `PAYABLE`-gated, as `mtxExecuteTransfer` was not.
- **`typed_ops.json`: the C6 rows take values the chain accepts.** `typed-ops-vectors.mjs` sets `ReceiverFee`, `UAReceiverFee`, `WrapOrder`, `UAWrapOrder` and the cancels to real orders by the row's key instead of fillers, so they execute rather than stop at a shape check. No type string or typehash moved. `UACancelNonce` keeps its filler derived `ua`: the test holds the registry to the exact digest.
- **`checkTradeOrder` refuses every order with `dex == receiveToken`, whatever the `dexes` list says,** and loses its `wrappers` option; `checkCancel` refuses `CancelOrder` / `CancelUAOrder` of such an order.

Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C7 and its review round, controller call, owner may override; status: decided, built in typed-signing C7; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): client reproducers of the typed op digests. (1) Only `clients/clientkeys` and `clients/zether-prover` build an EVM op digest of a struct that the typed ops moved; `ua-rs`, `ua-py`, `ua-go`, `ua-cs`, `ua-dart`, `ua-c`, `ua-cxx` and `ua-qt` build the portable records (typed since P7), the registry arguments (R1 / R2), `relay_ref` (a router ref, not a signed struct; `relayref.json` unchanged) and, in `ua-rs`, `ua_auth_digest` under the registry domain, so no code moved there. (2) `zether-prover` has the JSON command `typedDigest` (`typed::typed_digest`): the typed digest in the token's own domain of every one of the 47 Zether rows of `typed_ops.json`, the transfers, unshields, wraps, roll-overs, owner ops, receiver and relay fee, orders and cancels and their `UA*` twins; `args` is a nested struct hash and `proof`, `sealedMemo` are hashed `bytes`, as the contract hashes them. The hashing is one generic encoder over the type strings of one table (`typed::OPS`), so no per-op code exists and a new row is a table line; each field of the message is a named JSON member. `tests/typed_ops.rs` runs every `zether` row of the vector and asserts the count (47) and the exact list of rows left out. (3) The rows the prover leaves out are the 27 without a `zether` domain: `PrepareAcc` / `UAPrepareAcc` (token entries), the MandateWallet and SmartKeyAccount ops and `Execute` (signed by their owners' keys), the 24 PQZ rows incl. `PqzAuth`, and `CancelDexOrder` (the DEX's domain). `PqzAuth` has no client builder on this branch beyond `clients/clientkeys`: PQZ ops come from `e2e.py` and the node. (4) `zether-prover` has the command `namedCall`: a build's packed `payload`, `proof` and `beneficiary` plus the envelope fields become the named relayed entry (`mtxConfidentialTransferSingle`, `mtxConfidentialTransfer`, `mtxConfidentialTransferCompact`, `mtxUnshield`, `mtxUnshieldUnwrap` with `Envelope e` first and `bytes sig` last): the typed `message`, the `digest` a wallet signs and, with `sig`, the calldata, equal to the vector's calldata. The `UA*` twins are digest-only (`typedDigest`): the prover has no `uaExecute` binding builder. `ownerAuth` signs the owner ops' digest as before. The generic `envelope` command and `MetaTransaction` digest stay, as `executeMetaTransaction` stays, and the prover's direct calldata is byte-identical (`ZetherProverCross` passes through the real binary).
Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C8, controller calls, owner may override; status: decided, built in typed-signing C8; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): scripts on the named entries. (1) `script/pqz/e2e.py` keeps its two generic relayed transfers (TS-D14: the generic path stays, and it is what `debit_min_gas` is pinned on) and adds sections 5b and 6b, every PQZ op once on its named entry; the two sets of calls share the same proof-building code. (2) The struct digest comes from clientkeys (`OP_BUILDERS`, as the portable messages do), the calldata from the script's own encoders, so a `typed_ops.json` row checks the encoders independently of the client; the row's digest checks the script's mapping of its positional arguments to the struct's fields. (3) One PQZ holder in the scenario is an msig, so `registerMsig`, a `MemberSig[]` PoP and `UASig.members` run as `pqzAuth` and as an envelope signature; it is registered after the per-kind list checks, which stay as they were. (4) `uaShield` keeps `bytes auth` (owner table, 2026-11-01), so the msig holder is shielded by a direct `mtxShield`. (5) `script/ZetherE2E.s.sol` gets a payer EOA derived from a fixed label that only signs; the deployer relays for a fixed fee. Its signed ops are single, Compact multi and unshield; `ZetherUnshieldUnwrap` and the `ua*` twins are not in it (`namedCall` has no UA form, the C7 entry). (6) `DeployBase` keeps its code; its comment's size figures follow the baseline, `_requireReleaseGas`' formula is untouched. No script deploys a registry generation 2.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing N1, controller calls, owner may override; status: decided, built in typed-signing N1; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the node's EVM job API on the named entries. (1) **One table, one generic encoder** (`scaas-node/src/typed.rs`) instead of one `sol!` call per entry as the plan said: a row is a struct and the entry's argument plan, `alloy` `dyn-abi` (already in the tree) encodes, one `hash_tuple` hashes; the pattern of `zether-prover` `typed::OPS` (C7). Every row is pinned against `typed_ops.json`. `sol!` stays for what the venue and the guard read. (2) **`contract` is a job field**: an entry does not fix its domain (`mtxUnwrap` is on three kinds) and the node may not read a view for the digest, so the op names `token`, `zether`, `pqz`, `wallet`, `account`, `dex` (`registry`, `factory` for the plain rows). A wrong claim on a native signer is `BAD_SIGNATURE`. The calldata does not carry `contract`, and a derived UA's or contract signer's claim cannot be checked here, so the **in-flight key is two keys held together: the typed digest and `keccak(to ‖ data)`**, both free or neither; one call never flies twice under another claim. (3) **Plain entries are rows too**: hex `call` jobs carried the registry's writes, `deploy`, `mtxExecuteAsOwner` and the DEX entries, so refusing hex on every kind means each is named JSON (`kind = call`, `op`). The venue's settlement and DEX cancels reach the client as `op` instead of `calldata`; scaas defines the interface, consumers follow. (4) **The wallet's four flat builders stay beside the named entries** (owner ruling 2026-11-01, "The named builders stay"; the first N1 build dropped two of them, corrected in the N1 review): `mtxPayUnderMandate(token, …, validUntil, sig)`, `mtxRevoke`, `mtxExecuteAsOwner`, `mtxExecuteAsOwnerRaw` are plain rows, the guard allows them on a bound non-token contract, and `op.struct` names the overload of `mtxPayUnderMandate` (`PayUnderMandate` the named form, `mtxPayUnderMandate` the flat one). The kill switch's `mtxRevoke` job keeps its path; their lanes are the contract's. The named `mtxPayUnderMandate(Envelope, …)` and `mtxDelegateRevoke` run on the mandate lanes at nonce 0, refused `MANDATE_LANE` otherwise. (5) **`MetaTransfer` jobs keep their explicit struct** (`metatx` / `m`, `struct = transfer`, no hex) with an optional `contract` for the digest, default `token`; `struct = call` (`MetaTransaction`) is refused. `Table`, `self_call_ok`, the `mtxSelectors()` read and `SELECTOR_NOT_ALLOWED` on EVM go to `legacy/typed-signing/`: no job reaches them. The contracts keep the generic entries (owner 2026-10-31); the mesh digest still reads `Mtx::Call` (mesh is not a job kind). (6) **Gateway**: `POST /v1/op {chain, op}` beside `/v1/metatx`, default closed: after the parse the old door, a registered token (NODE-GW-01, NODE-GW-03; controller ruling on the N1 review, the first build took every row, so `deploy`, `register*`, `mtxSettle` and wallet rows cost the lane free gas). The rule is "an entry reaches `/v1/op` only if the old door allowed it", and the old door had no UA path, so a `ua*` entry on a registered token is refused too (`FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED`, controller ruling on the N1 review); it goes as a `ua_metatx` job. The signature pre-check runs in `Guard::check`, so every lane runs it too: a native 65-byte signature that does not recover and whose signer has no code is `BAD_SIGNATURE`, nothing simulated. Any other length (a 64-byte Hedera account signature, HIP-632, CTR-MTX-25) is the contract's to judge. (7) **`RELAY_FEE_SHAPE`** keeps only "the payee is the executor": the `RelayFee` struct signs the rest. A relay fee is the entry `mtxRelayFee` / `uaRelayFee` with a named `call`; the node sends the router's `relay` / `uaRelay` to the signed `relayer`, never the token's entry. A relay fee cannot relay a relay fee. The inner op is parsed without the lane's `fee_recipient`: the payer hashed those bytes, so an unbound inner `relayer` / `feeRecipient` is 0, and a client hashes it as 0. The brief's `{underlying, wrapped, recipient, minOut}` is `mtxUnwrapLeg`; `mtxUnwrap` has no `underlying` (`typed_ops.json`). (8) Indexer unchanged: Parts C added no event, `MetaTransactionExecuted.digest` is the typed digest; for a receiver fee the outer `ReceiverFee` digest is the in-flight key and `meta.digest` the payment's `MetaTransfer` digest, which is what the chain emits. (9) `op.validUntil` narrows a deadline the chain enforces, never extends it (the minimum); a cancel has none, so there it stands alone. (10) The node reads no digest view; `node-e2e-anvil` keeps the contract as a live oracle for the local digests (`mtxDigest`, `mtxTransferDigest`, `uaTransferDigest`, an emitted `MetaTransactionExecuted`), and pins the plain rows' argument names and order against forge's ABI.

Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, later the same day, replaces "`UARegistry` is not split" above; status: decided, built in typed-signing R2, the registry split, not the plan's Part R Task R2; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): **`UARegistry` is split in two: `UARegistry` keeps the views and `requireAuthorized`, `UARegistryLib` takes `cacheExpandedKey`, every `register*`, `storePqzPop`, `setPqzKey` and `setKemKey`.** R2 alone: no R1′ (the views stay in the registry) and no `fallback`, which stays rejected. A behaviour-preserving refactor: the 53 selectors, the ABI, every digest, event and error stay; code location, addresses, gas and sizes move. The name is `UARegistryLib` (the spike's `UARegisterLib`). The figures are in `docs/research/evm-size-levers.md` §8.

Controller calls, owner may override:

- **The immutables reach the library as the spike's three words,** appended by `_lib` after the forwarded calldata (`_cfg(kind)`, `_cfg(0x0142)`, the clone codehash) and read from the end of the calldata; the rest calls back the getters on `address(this)`. No caller's byte reaches those words, and solc's library call protection refuses a direct call of every entry. The one difference from the pre-split code, malformed calldata only, is kept and pinned by `test_nestedOffsetReadsAWordAsItsOwnArgument`: an offset inside a struct is checked where it is read, and the library's calldata is 96 B longer, so an offset aimed at a word reads it as that caller's own argument, where the pre-split code reverted. What it can read is public, and the call is the one a well-formed call with those bytes would be. Closing it means walking every nested field in the stubs, an estimated 600–1,000 B (not measured) and gas per element, for no security gain. Accepted in the R2 review: no strict end check.
- **The rules used by both sides moved once, not twice:** `_capped`, the native rule (`_byCode` + `_1271`, now `UAStore.byCode`) and the starvation rule (`_viaPredecessor` + `_starved`, now `UAStore.via`) are one copy in `UAStore`, with the storage and the bytes helpers. Only `_msig` and `_memberOk` exist on both sides, and neither copy has the `portable` branch: `requireAuthorized` here, a portable record's signature in the library. The ua8-soroban minimal rule (U8S-D1) therefore lands in `UARegistryLib._msig`.
- **A derived `msig` member on the portable path goes through `requireAuthorized` on `address(this)`,** a new frame per member, the spike's form; the library holds no member's verifier address. The verdict is the same: the member's kind was checked against its record at registration.
- **The constructor refuses a registry whose library has no code (`UAConfig(0)`).** New, and not in the spike: a raw DELEGATECALL to an empty account succeeds, so every write would be a silent no-op. The library cannot leave once it is there (no SELFDESTRUCT, pinned).
- **`SSTORE2WriteFailed` is declared on `UARegistry`, not on `IUARegistry`,** so no other contract's metadata moves.
- **Gate:** `_requireReleaseGas("UARegistryLib")` and `require_release_gas("UARegistryLib")` beside the registry's. The formula `runtime × 1,530 + 2^24` stays, so the library's gate asks more than its transaction costs by simulated gas (figures in §8). A chain at a 60 M block is still refused by the gates of the registry's library and of `NormalToken`.
- **`scripts/size_gate.py` measures every library of `src/` from its artifact:** forge's report lists no library without a view function in its ABI, so `UARegistryLib` would have had no ratchet. It knows a library by solc's call protection at the head of the runtime. `AdminLib`, `PqzBurnLib` and `PqzTransferLib`, the other libraries the report leaves out with external functions, join the baseline as ratchets, so a library's entry stays although it fits (R2 review).
- **`msig` minimal form in `UARegistryLib._msig` (U8S-D1, owner 2026-10-31; built, typed-signing M2 port of ua8-soroban 5383ac7b; status: built).** The stored `msig` signatures (`pop` v2, `kem`, `pqz-key`) are accepted only when `T >= N && T - w_min < N` (one pass keeps the smallest slot weight); the check is after the old threshold test, error `UAPoP` / `UAUnauthorized` as before. `UARegistry._msig` (transaction authorisation, not stored) keeps its rule. Declared difference against `UARegistryPreSplit`: a redundant stored `msig` set the pre-split registry accepts, the split registry refuses; the `test_diff` scenario holds no such row, so it reports none. `UARegistryLib` 31,315 -> 31,358 B (+43) with this rule.
- **`msig` member acceptance (owner 2026-11-02; status: built, typed-signing Task MA).** See [CTR-UA-37](#ctr-ua-37--listing-in-an-msig-is-no-consent-a-member-accepts-and-only-accepted-members-count-at-verify).

The pre-split source is frozen in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/typed-signing/UARegistryPreSplit.sol`, the other side of `test/ua/UARegistrySplit.t.sol` and `UARegistryUA8Test.test_split_portableRowsSame`.
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-01, -19): `scaas.governance` joins the namespaces and `scaas.token` keeps identity only; `AdminLib` is `GovernanceLib`; the regulated namespace is named `scaas.regulated`, not built. Above every limit and baseline row the size gate holds the ceiling 131,072 B runtime and 262,144 B init, and the contracts above 65,536 B are the pinned list `_above64KiB`. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T2 `7edcad34`, T3 `7825361b`).
Change (owner 2026-11-04, `ua*` / `mtx*` merge; status: SPECIFIED, not built): the 2026-11-01 exception recorded above, "`uaExecute`, `uaBatch` and `uaShield` keep `bytes auth` (owner table)", is reversed by [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) (spec row R47): the merged `mtxExecute`, `mtxBatch` and `mtxShield` take `UASig`; `executeMetaTransaction` keeps `bytes signature`. Built by the merge, not here.
Change (owner 2026-11-09, T66b spec §11 (d), (f); supersedes the owner's ruling of 2026-11-01 of one registry library recorded above; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, T66b 3.1 `cb4abd33`, 3.1b `83cfa8b8`, 3.1c `b2ec0d85` and `23955351`, 3.1d `d1842a58`; UNAUDITED): **the registry is a trio, `UARegistry` and two libraries split by domain** ([contracts/accounts.md](contracts/accounts.md), the registry bullet above CTR-UA-37). R-1 first: the registry's `pure` views whose code a library already holds forward through `_libPure(lib, sel)`; R-2 (whole writers moved into the registry) was dropped, its first move (`storePqzPop`) grew the pair by 1,784 B. `UARegistryCoreLib` keeps the `register` forms, the `msig`, `acceptMembership`, `requirePortable`, `registrationOf`, `uaCount`, `uaOf`, `keyHashOf` and four delegation-only helpers; `UARegistryAuxLib` takes the writes after registration (`setPqzKey`, `storePqzPop`, `setKemKey`, `cacheExpandedKey`), the reads off the hot path and the five `*Digest` views (3.1d), and runs the shared helpers of the core by one nested `DELEGATECALL` each (3.1c, the registry's three appended words forwarded; one level, Aux to core only), which relaxes "one `DELEGATECALL` per operation" to one from the registry plus one nested hop per shared helper; `UARegistryLib` retires to `legacy/` (`a1353950`). Runtime: registry 28,165 B, core 33,685 B, Aux 20,192 B, each under its 57 M line; asked as their own transactions 48.03 M, 56.64 M and 34.04 M (T66b 4.4). Execution gas old -> new: `setKemKey` +8.1 k, `setPqzKey` +12.9 k (two nested calls, to keep the check order), `storePqzPop` +29.0 k, `cacheExpandedKey` +5.9 k; charged gas unchanged where the EIP-7976 floor binds (`storePqzPop`, an ML-DSA-65 `setKemKey`). Deploy order core, Aux, registry. Deferred by the owner 2026-11-09 (to be weighed later): further core -> Aux moves, in the order `acceptMembership`, `registrationOf` and `uaCount`, `uaOf` and `keyHashOf`, then only if needed `registerFrost`, `registerMuSig2`, `registerWebAuthn`.


### CTR-TOK-25 — Creation API: createToken, createTokenUnregistered, TokenConfig, TokenCreated
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-25 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One `TokenConfig` (name, symbol, decimals, features, lockedFeatures, owner, roles, initial supply, legs, rate, confidential parameters) replaces the per-kind `initData`; `CREATE2` clone and `initialize` in one call; one `TokenCreated` event; registry views `isToken`, `isDex` and `versionOf`; `createDex` and `DexConfig` (CTR-DEX-24); one `IOpenFactory` and one `IFactoryToken`.
**Cost if wrong.** Per-kind encodings keep a second parsing surface in the factory, node and clients; a deployed-but-uninitialized clone can be front-run.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` §7.

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-19, option (a) (plan 5g-Z1) — `createTokenUnregistered` refuses every confidential kind
(`UnregisteredConfidentialKind`, kinds 2–7) and stays for the plain kinds, recorded as version 0 and flagged unvetted
(`isRegisteredToken` false); `ConfidentialConfig.verifier` must be 0 (the release's verifier, CTR-ZTH-20; the field stays
until the creation API is replaced in plan 5g-Z2). Status: built, commit `690a295a` (plan Task 5g-Z1).

Change (2026-10-20): owner rulings 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z2) — **generic creation API.** `createToken(kind, version, bytes
initArgs, salt)`, `createTokenUnregistered(kind, implementation, bytes initArgs, salt)` (plain kinds only) and
`createDex(version, bytes initArgs, salt)`; every implementation answers `initialize(address creator, uint64 version,
bytes initArgs)`; the kinds of this repository decode `initArgs = abi.encode(TokenConfig)`, `SCaaSDex`
`abi.encode(DexConfig)`; the factory never reads `initArgs`. **Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (confirmed): `initialize` takes no
`Env`**, and the split stays explicit — the implementation carries what never changes for it (the `Env` in its
constructor: verifiers, registry, chain, libraries), each instance carries its own configuration from `initArgs`
(rates, features, roles, the confidential settings). `ConfidentialConfig.verifier` is removed (7 fields). The factory's
index and the one `TokenCreated` read the token's `underlyings()`, `features()`, `lockedFeatures()` and `owner()` after
`initialize`; `createToken` refuses an unknown, deprecated or not-yet-usable release and a disabled kind (`KindDisabled`).
Status: built on branch `rev2-zether-z2`, commit `0f88e66f` (plan Task 5g-Z2).
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-01 with its Change, -04, -06, -12): `TokenConfig.owner` and the initial holders are UA ids (`bytes32`); `TokenConfig` gains `grantDelay`, `rescueTo` and `maxSupply`, each fixed at creation. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T7 `c2525e28`, T9 `20620a1e`, T10 `dc9bfde0`, T10b `ac29de05`).
Change (2026-11-07, factory index and chain-neutral releases, CTR-TOK-27, CTR-TOK-29): the creation order is CREATE3 (with the instance's `ChainEnv` appended to the clone's code) → `initialize(creatorId, …)` → the post-init `chainUid()` check → the index record → the event; `predictAddress(creatorId, class, kind, salt)`; `TokenCreated` and `DexCreated` carry `bytes32 indexed creatorId` (the signing UA through the router); the index record replaces the per-token info behind the registry views. Status: BUILT (T67 `658f684f`, T71 `b61ac38d`, T72 `612981b9`, T76 `e8ca069b`).

Change (owner 2026-11-11, group 3t, [CTR-PQZ-36](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36); status: BUILT on `ua-mtx-3t`, UNAUDITED): `TokenConfig.conf` gains `uint64 verifierFee` and `uint64 verifierFeeMax` after `proofStore`, so the encoding of every kind's `TokenConfig` moves (all chains test-only: no alias); every kind but an `OFFCHAIN` PQZ token requires both 0 (`ConfigFieldForOtherKind(4)`, or `PqzVerifyConfigInvalid()` on a `PRECOMPILE` PQZ token).
