### CTR-TOK-27 — The factory indexes every contract it creates, in its own state
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-27 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `OpenFactory` keeps one record per contract it creates, never changed or deleted: `Created {addr, creatorId, ownerUA, contractClass, kind, version, createdBlock, createdAt}`, and per class the lists all, by owner UA at creation (never 0) and by creator. Views `infoOf`, `contractsPage`, `contractsOfOwner`, `contractsOfCreator`: `(page, total)`, oldest first, `n ≤ MAX_PAGE = 100` (`PageTooLarge`), `n = 0` the count, `from ≥ total` an empty page, `ClassUnknown`. Class ids `uint16`: 0 not made here, 1 `TOKEN`, 2 `DEX`, 3 `PQCHAT`, 4–65535 the registrar's. The owner list is a claim (the owner right after `initialize`, not now): wallets show `version ≠ 0` and the creator; releases are not indexed.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`: T67 `658f684f`, the creator ids T71 `b61ac38d`; tests `test/v2/FactoryIndex.t.sol`. Gas (`GovGas`): `createToken` 1,446,879 → 1,805,428, `createDex` 3,416,944 → 4,006,661 (T67); with CREATE3 and the env (T72) 2,183,102 / 4,383,367. UNAUDITED.
**Why.** Owner 2026-11-07: "no event filtering, because events are lost" (history expiry): a wallet or indexer must find every contract a factory made by `eth_call` alone.
**Cost if wrong.** Three slots and three list pushes per creation; an index whose owner list is read as an authority would mislead (hence a claim, shown with the creator).
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-07 (factory index spec Q1–Q6 as recommended); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-factory-contract-index.md` §2–§7; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md` T67, T69.

Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3r; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3r`, UNAUDITED): **the factory keeps no owner information.** The record is `Created {addr, creatorId, contractClass, kind, version, createdBlock, createdAt}` (two slots); no owner list and no `contractsOfOwner`; `TokenCreated`, `DexCreated` and `InstanceCreated` carry no owner; `FactoryInfo` is six words (192 B) without `ownerUA` (owner, Q4); the factory reads no owner or admin of what it creates. The current admin is the contract's `admin()`, its history the contract's own `AdminTransferred` events. Old: `ownerUA` in the record, the list by owner UA at creation, the owner field of the three events. Why: an owner can transfer or renounce, so a recorded owner goes stale; the creator, class, kind, version, block and time do not move. Source: owner 2026-11-10; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md` §3; CTR-GOV-23.

### CTR-TOK-28 — The generic catalogue: a new contract class or kind without a factory change
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-28 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A generic release is `ReleaseId {contractClass ≥ 3, kind, version}` (0–2 `ClassReserved`: tokens and the DEX keep their typed paths). Registrar only: `publishClassEnv`, `deployImplementation(id, envVersion, initSelector, interfaceId, initcode, implArgs)` (checks code, `factoryInfo()` 224 B naming this factory and the release's id, owner 0, initialized; ERC-165 `0x01ffc9a7` and `interfaceId`, not `0xffffffff`; `validateEnv`; the body modules), `deprecateRelease`, `setClassKindEnabled` (a new `(class, kind)` starts off). Anyone: `createInstance(id, salt, initCall)`, the catalogued initializer only, value 0, on the fresh clone only, then `factoryInfo()` and `chainUid()` checked, the record, `InstanceCreated`; `creating()` (EIP-1153) names the creator during a creation. No unregistered generic path; not a node job. Names (owner 2026-11-10): the generic deploy entry is `deployImplementation` (was `deployRelease`), the token-kind one `deployTokenImplementation` (was `deployImplementation`); `ReleaseIsDeprecated` is the error the spec calls `ReleaseDeprecated` (an error cannot share the event's name).
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`: T70 `a01f3e8d`, `ee9c85c8`; the rename `157062b7`; tests `test/v2/FactoryGenericKind.t.sol` (a kind added without factory code). `createInstance` 1,826,732 gas (T70). UNAUDITED.
**Why.** Owner 2026-11-07: "`OpenFactory` must be built so that later the admin can easily add another kind / implementation"; the factory is immutable, so the extension point must be in it from the start.
**Cost if wrong.** A class's code is the registrar's trust root, as for tokens: the factory proves the release's code, env, initializer, interface and `chain_uid`, not that its logic is sound.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-07 (Q7–Q12 as recommended), 2026-11-10 (names); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-factory-contract-index.md` §8.

### CTR-TOK-29 — Chain-neutral releases: one address per release on every chain, the chain's values in each clone's code
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-29 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `OpenFactory(registrar)` has the same bytes everywhere; `configureChain(chainUid, noticePeriod, govRouter, refBlock, refHash)` runs once (the genesis hash whenever the EVM can prove it, a reference block's hash, the router's `chainUid()`; every other entry refuses before it, `ChainNotConfigured`). Release init code and envs carry no chain value; the factory appends each instance's `ChainEnv {chainUid, registry, govRouter, smartKeyAccountImpl, hedera, deps, params}` to its clone's code, read by `EXTCODECOPY`, never an immutable; `initialize` without it reverts `EnvMissing`, the implementation signs nothing (`ChainUidZero`). Every creation is CREATE3 with `s = keccak256(abi.encode(creatorId, class, kind, salt))`, `predictAddress(creatorId, class, kind, salt)`, the clone's `chainUid()` checked after `initialize`. Through the chain's router the creator is the signing UA (S3: `mtxCreateToken`, `mtxCreateDex`, `mtxCreateInstance`; `RouterSubjectZero`).
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`: T71 `b61ac38d`, T72 `612981b9`, T73 `bbcbbe85` (deploy), T74 `7c460398` (two chains, the CREATE3 KAT), T76 `e8ca069b` (S3); tests `test/v2/ChainNeutral.t.sol`, `ChainNeutralFactory.t.sol`, `test/governance/GovRouterCreate.t.sol`. Cost: `mtxTransfer` +636 to +646 gas, `transferToUA` +1,311 to +1,400, the router's `mtxMint` +682; every kind +0.8 to +1.2 KB. UNAUDITED.
**Why.** Decisions A and B, option I (owner 2026-11-07): the factory, the libraries and every release at one address on every chain, so a release is verified once; the chain's values cannot be immutables of shared code.
**Cost if wrong.** One `EXTCODECOPY` of the 138-byte head per signed call; a clone made outside the factory has no env and refuses.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-07 (option I, S3 the signing UA, §10.3 Q1–Q8); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-chain-neutral-releases.md` §2–§6, §11 (Fable review).

Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3r; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3r`, UNAUDITED): the constructor is `OpenFactory(bytes32 admin)` with a native first admin (CTR-GOV-23), the release list's `registrar` row becomes `admin`, and `configureChain` also takes the router's code hash, requires the router's `registry()` non-zero with code and the router's `SmartKeyAccount` clone hash equal to its registry's. **The factory is the chain's directory** (option (a): write-once, one address per name, no versions), **with no constants** (owner, same day): every entry is written once with its code hash checked at the write: the router at `configureChain`; `RelayFeeRouter` (under a constant salt whatever `DEPLOY_SALT` is, reused when already there; its executor read as its `EXECUTOR()`, code hash checked at the write), `ComplianceRegistry` (the SCaaS deploy's, one issuer policy among many; naming it confers nothing), `SmartKeyAccountFactory` and `ZetherStatements` through `setChainEntries`; `uaRegistry()` is the router's `registry()`, and every env publish refuses another registry or a `SmartKeyAccount` implementation other than the router's (bound from `configureChain` on, before any env). One view per entry and `directory()`, a named struct; no key map. Not entries: libraries, body modules, releases, an env's `deps`, per-DEX children (`DexPuller` through `dex.puller()`). Why no constants: with no `bytecode_hash` set, the metadata would tie the factory's address, so every release's, to every byte of a singleton's source closure (`RelayFeeRouter.sol`, `MetaTxLib.sol`, `IUARegistry.sol`, …); the factory's address now depends on its own code and its first admin only. Source: owner 2026-11-10; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md` §5.2, §13; Fable review 2026-11-10 (P2-2, P2-6, P2-7, P3).

### CTR-TOK-30 — Body modules: every body but the ERC-20 core runs in a DELEGATECALL module of its kind
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-09 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-30 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Every deployed contract, libraries included, must fit one transaction of 60 M (`asked = (regular + state) × 1.05`, regular × 1.05 < 2^24, the EIP-8037 inclusion rule), and the token kinds were 33,889–73,511 B (57–124 M asked; eleven of the twelve above 60 M). With lever L in its forward form each kind keeps its typed entry points, its ERC-20 core and the one guard, and forwards every other body by `DELEGATECALL` to a body module of its own kind (P pipeline / named transfers / pay, T trade, A admin, W wrapped and regulated, Z Zether, Q and Q2 PQZ; the DEX's D its governance), so no rule, selector, event, error, digest or storage slot moves.
**Cost if wrong.** A module that behaves differently from the body it replaced (a hook missing in its core, an immutable unset) changes a rule silently; a stub that leaves the guard set blocks the next call into the token in the transaction; a swapped or foreign module runs another kind's code. Hence the implementation's constructor checks every module, the env pins their code hashes, the factory refuses a module outside the env, and the differential test per entry, the path tests and the mutants. A release costs more transactions per chain (4–7 per kind, each ≤ 60 M) and a forwarded call pays about one warm `DELEGATECALL` frame.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-07 (lever L in its forward form, per-kind modules and their release cost accepted, the PQZ calldata cost accepted: [CTR-GOV-19](#ctr-gov-19--build-first-on-the-scaas-testnet-at-a-higher-code-size-ceiling-reduce-later)'s Change); owner rulings 2026-11-09, `superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-t66b-library-organisation.md` §11 (a)–(j), reviewed by Claude Fable 5.1 (§14); plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-ua-mtx-merge.md` task T66b; `research/evm-library-organisation.md`. Owner 2026-11-11, in chat, on the review of spec 3t (`superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-verifier-fee.md` R6): "Hỏi trước khi tách." (ask before splitting).
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge` (T66b: the split `3a837c85`, rule 4 `abc9b6ce`, `3e00abf3`, the DEX's D `5a8fccda`, the pay cut `f2a06f15`, the deploy wiring and `ModuleNotPinned` `1c7f59a0`, the faces' events and errors `82d57bc7`, the tests of spec §10 `6ec405b9`, `7d55ed52`, `de280186`, the mutants 21 of 21 killed `5af1f0ff`, pins `a9d38e4b`, the size gate `816f226d`); UNAUDITED. The legacy token tree is in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/` (`d142b57c`).

Rulings recorded here (owner 2026-11-09, spec §11; status: decided, built as stated):

- **(a) The DEX:** its 22 governance entries are forwarded into the admin module D now (`SCaaSDex` 34,929 -> 32,991 B, D 6,459 B).
- **(b) The module count:** about 59 token modules accepted; built 55 (Q splits into Q and Q2 on kinds 5 and 13 only), each ≤ 60 M.
- **(c) The four-set gate** passes with the three known-red `test_gas_rollMax_relayedFullTx` rows listed (n2048-kmax1024, n2304-kmax4096, n2816-kmax65536) and their figures reported; `ROLL_MAX` stays 96 / 80 / 64 / 32, its move decided later.
- **(e) Room for later governance:** no separate governance module now. A later governance version grows `GovernanceLib` first (14,513 B; margin line 33,903 B ≈ 57 M asked, hard line 35,694 B ≈ 60 M). When a kind's A passes 33,780 B (≈ 57 M; hard 35,570 B ≈ 60 M) it splits into A (init, tables, token meta, mint / burn) and G (the governance entries); the DEX's D the same.
- **(g) Pay stays in P, one per kind:** a P that passes 33,780 B splits into P and P2 (pay, relay fee); none does (the largest P 30,783 B). A shared pay module (one regulated module for 10–13, or one per family) is recorded for a later switch; the T66b 4.4 comparison found the twelve per-kind pay bodies different apart from immutables and metadata (each kind's hooks are compiled in), so a shared module needs those hooks as data.
- **(h) C0:** `test_c0_gasNamedVsGeneric`'s bound `named < generic + 2,000` becomes `+ 7,000`: the named `mtxUnwrap` (module W, library call) 160,958 -> 160,749 gas, the generic `mtxExecute(unwrap)` (module P, pipeline compiled in) 163,269 -> 154,866.
- **(i) The split overhead of a relayed PQZ op** (two more frames, each copying the envelope): `test_splitOverhead_dataSizeBound`'s bounds are the measured figures plus about 10 %, PQZL 9,000 -> 99,000 (largest 90,196, n2048-kmax1024 mldsa65), PQZH 14,000 -> 335,000 (largest 303,659, n2304-kmax4096 mldsa65) (`0fcbb2c3`).
- **(j) `debit_min_gas`** at the measured value at every set: [CTR-PQZ-14](#ctr-pqz-14--disclosure-only-by-zero-knowledge-proof)'s Change of 2026-11-09.

**Change (2026-11-10, owner: "fix it so every class is checked"; BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`; UNAUDITED): every class's release is module-checked.** `OpenFactory` checked a release's `modules()` against its env's `libs` only on the token-kind and DEX paths; the generic class path (`deployImplementation`, e.g. `PqChat`, class 3) did not, so a generic release could name a module outside its env (`PqChat` checks its module's code and `FACTORY()` itself, but the guarantee belongs to the factory, under one rule for every class). Now `deployImplementation` runs the same `_checkModules` (`ModuleNotPinned`, `ModulesUnreadable`). Every release of every class answers `modules()`, an empty list allowed, and the answer is fixed by its code (immutables or constants, never storage), because the factory reads it once, at the release; every in-repository class reads immutables only (the twelve token kinds, the DEX, `PqChat`). No path registers an implementation the factory did not create: the three release paths are registrar-only and `CREATE2` the init code in the factory (`createTokenUnregistered` registers nothing and checks at each creation). The factory already deployed on the SCaaS testnet is immutable and keeps the old behaviour; the check applies to releases registered on a factory built from this code. Cost: `OpenFactory` 29,225 -> 29,238 B runtime, its deploy asked 49,280,339 -> 49,301,224 gas (NET-EVM-11, under 60 M); evidence `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-10-ua-mtx-merge-generic-modules.txt`.

**Change (owner 2026-11-10, before the SCaaS testnet reset 2; amends this rule and the body-modules spec §4.2 (`superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-t66b-library-organisation.md`); status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3p`, group 3p; UNAUDITED): the body modules are split by function on every kind.** Old: W held the wrapped entries and the regulated powers together (on 9, 11, 13 one module of 32,226–33,407 B, W 13 373 B under the 33,780 B line), and Q's split was named Q2. New: the letters are A admin, P pipeline / pay, T trade, **W wrap only**, **R regulated only** (group id 12), Z Zether, Q PQZ, **S** the PQZ state, setters and views (Q2's id 8 kept). Kinds 8, 10, 12 rename their W to R; kinds 9, 11, 13 split their W into W (wrap) and R, one more module per release (55 -> 58 token modules); kinds 5 and 13 rename Q2 to S. R holds the regulated layer's 14 entries on every regulated kind (`RegulatedBase`'s and the kind's `disableFeature`: `canReceive`, `disableFeature`, `forceTransfer`, `freeze`, `freezeOf`, `isFrozen`, `operatorTransfer`, `order`, `pause`, `recordOrder`, `regulatedConfig`, `revokeOrder`, `unfreeze`, `unpause`); the wrap bodies a regulated kind restates (`rescue`, `underlyings`) stay in W, and the compliance hooks wrap and unwrap call are internal and stay compiled into W. No rule, selector, event, error, storage slot or call count moves (one hop: a module never calls another), and the token ABI is unchanged; `modules()` lists the modules by group id (R last: P, T, A, W, R on 9; P, T, A, Z, R on 10; P, T, A, Q, R on 12; P, T, A, W, Q, S, R on 13). Built in the generator (`script/modules/gen_faces.py` `R_ENTRIES`, `S_SETTERS`; faces, modules and `script/KindModules.sol` regenerated, `--check` clean); `DeployBase` and the scripts read `kindModuleNames`, `basebook.py` and `pq.py` match the letters P, T, A, W, R, Z, Q, S. Sizes old -> new (runtime B): W 9 32,226 -> 27,239, W 11 33,216 -> 28,229, W 13 33,407 -> 28,420 (each -4,987); R 9 / 11 / 13 new 11,999 / 11,999 / 12,048; R 8 / 10 / 12 11,778 / 11,778 / 11,820 (the old W 11,778 / 11,778 / 11,827); S 5 / 13 = the old Q2 18,216 / 19,038; the faces of 9, 11, 13 22,932 -> 23,250, 26,672 -> 26,992, 29,474 -> 29,795 (a fifth or seventh module: its immutable, check and `modules()` slot), every other face unchanged. Deploy gas, each module its own CREATE2 transaction (asked = (regular + state) x 1.05): R 20,168,205–20,621,622, W 9 / 11 / 13 46,074,538 / 47,732,694 / 48,052,643, S 30,949,943 / 32,336,022, the faces of 9 / 11 / 13 39,517,662 / 45,797,882 / 50,512,802 plus the factory frame; all within 60 M, regular x 1.05 < 2^24 (`smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-10-ua-mtx-3p/probe/Probe3p.t.sol`). Pins moved old -> new: `size-baseline.json` (the three faces and the three W above), `test/v2/module-opcodes.json` (W 9 / 11 / 13 DELEGATECALLs 26 -> 21, R [8, 0] new, the renamed rows unchanged), `test/modules/Modules.t.sol` module rows 55 -> 58; the storage layout pins do not move (each module has its core's layout). Tests: `test/modules/Groups.t.sol` (R and S hold exactly their entries, W and Q none of them, every stub of every face reaches its own module); the mutants are in `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-10-ua-mtx-3p/summary.txt`.

Change (owner 2026-11-11, on the review of spec 3t, [CTR-PQZ-36](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36); status: in force): **ask before splitting.** No module is split and no size lever applied without asking the owner: when a module or library passes its notice line, or a lever looks needed, the work stops, the measured sizes are reported and the owner decides. Old: a module that passes 33,780 B splits along its domains (rulings (b), (e), (g) and the splitting rule of `contracts/token-wrappers.md`) as a step of the work; new: the split is the owner's call each time. The owner's words are on this entry's Source line.

### CTR-TOK-31 — Wrap and unwrap limits on the hybrids of the wrapped kinds
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-31 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** On a hybrid (`maxSupply ≠ 0`) of kinds 1, 3, 5, 9, 11, 13, bit 25 `WRAP_LIMIT` lets the owner set per leg a short and a long fixed wrap window and the same two for unwrap (per id, plus an optional token-wide cap), the net rule (an id unwraps at most what it wrapped, net) and its linear decay over `decayDays`; bit 26 `WRAP_LIST` a wrapper and an unwrapper list; bit 27 `REDEEMER` an exemption from the net rule, a scalar power whose excess is a use of its grant. A pure-wrap token refuses the three bits at creation. A wrap-side relaxation or an unwrap-side tightening waits the factory's `noticePeriod()`; the rest applies at once.
**Why.** A state-issued hybrid (the owner's example: a kVND CBDC, 100 billion minted, citizens wrapping a foreign stablecoin) needs to bound the reserve's inflow and outflow per person and in total, to let people redeem their own money, and to keep foreign currency that stays unused as liquidity; holders keep an exit window before the unwrap side tightens.
**Cost if wrong.** A path that moves reserve without the count would let a signature bypass a limit the direct call obeys; an unwrap tightening at once would be a pause of redemption, which the repository refuses elsewhere (CTR-TOK-07, CTR-GOV-17); a bare role read for the redeemer would leave an expired or revoked grant exempt.
**Source.** Owner rulings 2026-11-10, `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-wrap-limits.md` (R1–R25 with the spec, R26 and R27 on Fable's review the same day). In full:
- **R1** two independent limits per direction, each `(amount, period)`, a short and a long one, each off at 0; a wrap fits both wrap limits, an unwrap both unwrap limits. **R2** fixed windows, not sliding. **R3** per user, plus an optional token-wide cap. **R4** "unwrap ≤ own net wrapped", a separate option, default off. **R5** a wrapper list and an unwrapper list, managed by a role. **R6** the owner sets them through `GovernanceRouter`; on the wrap side tightening applies at once, relaxing waits. **R7** one slot per user packing the windows and the net amount. **R8** the bodies in module W.
- **R9** a separate `redeemer` role exempt from the net rule (merchants). **R10** Sybil accepted. **R11** the net entitlement decays over time, switched apart from the net rule (after a year half, after two years nothing in the owner's example).
- **R12** hybrids only; issuer mints never count. **R13** holder protection: on the unwrap side tightening waits the notice, relaxing applies at once; the decay follows the unwrap side; membership and a redeemer's revoke at once. **R14** the subject's quota, never `msg.sender` of a relay; the net credit to the id credited. **R15** per leg in the leg's units. **R16** the fixed-window burst accepted. **R17** amounts are the underlying moved. **R18** no new stop. **R19** views, events, pre-checks as specified. **R20** everything off by default; the bits at creation. **R21** the delay is the factory's `noticePeriod()`. **R22** quanta, one slot, windows in minutes. **R23** the decay linear to zero over one horizon. **R24** the weighted-average start. **R25** a round trip refreshes the start: accepted and disclosed (confirmed at the build's start).
- **R26** (Fable P1-2) the weighted start is an absolute minute stored as `uint64`, in the one slot by repacking: window starts 21 bits (periods up to `2^20 − 1` minutes), used counts 19 bits (`perUser ≤ 2^19 − 1`), `base` 32 bits. **R27** (Fable P1-1) bit 27 is scalar on the six wrapped kinds; the write phase runs `GovernanceUse.use(REDEEMER, holder, excess)`.
- Bit 27 is refused on pure-wrap tokens like 25 and 26 (confirmed at the build's start). **Q17** (the shielded id of the confidential kinds is not always the public id): ruled (a) by the owner 2026-11-10, disclosed, no new rule. **R26 accepted** by the owner 2026-11-10 with its bounds: a window start 21 bits (a period ≤ `2^20 − 1` minutes, ≈ 728 days), a used count 19 bits (≤ 524,287 quanta per user per window).
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-wraplimit` (group 3l, plan T97–T104); UNAUDITED; reviewed in design by Claude Fable (approve with fixes, applied).

### CTR-TOK-80 — No EOA approve lockdown
- old: R4 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-TOK-01

**What it said.** An earlier design did not lock EOA approvals.

## 19. Contracts — Accounts and mandates

### CTR-ACC-01 — SmartKeyAccount clones; salt binds key and guardian
- old: RS4-1 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-01 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Counterfactual clones with a salt binding the first key and the guardian give a predictable address that nobody else can claim.
**Cost if wrong.** A salt of the key alone would let anyone deploy the account with a hostile guardian.
**Source.** `history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md:11`

### CTR-ACC-02 — Signature is keyIndex, Merkle proof, sig
- old: RS4-3 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-02 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One signature encoding `(keyIndex, proof, sig)` covers single operations and Merkle batches for both key types.
**Cost if wrong.** Two encodings would double the parsing and test surface.
**Source.** `history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md:19`

### CTR-ACC-03 — Guardian recovery adds a key after two days
- old: RS4-4 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Guardian recovery adds a key after a two-day delay that any existing key can cancel, so a lost device is recoverable and a rogue guardian is visible.
**Cost if wrong.** An instant recovery would let a compromised guardian take the account.
**Source.** `history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md:23`

### CTR-ACC-04 — Authenticator signCount is not checked
- old: RS4-5 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Synced passkeys report a zero or non-monotonic signCount; checking it would lock out legitimate users.
**Cost if wrong.** A cloned authenticator is not detected by the counter; the account relies on device security instead.
**Source.** `history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md:27`

### CTR-ACC-05 — 400k ERC-1271 cap only for SmartKeyAccount clones; salted account domain
- old: RS4-10 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Only `SmartKeyAccount` clones, identified by codehash, get the 400 k ERC-1271 cap that the Solidity P-256 path needs; everything else keeps 50 k. The account's domain carries `salt = chain_uid` from the factory, so its address differs per chain.
**Cost if wrong.** A global 400 k cap lets any contract wallet grief relayers with expensive validation.
**Source.** `history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md:43`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-4.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call; status: documented; built in typed-signing C5; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the named entries of `SmartKeyAccount` and `MandateWallet` are signed in the same salted account domains and take the same ERC-1271 cap rule; `SmartKeyAccount` entries carry `AccountSig {keyIndex, proof, signature}`.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) Q6 and MD-11, spec row R32; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge` (T3b), UNAUDITED): the mandate wallets' named entries are signed over `UA<Op>` in the wallet's salted domain; `MandateWallet` passes `smartKeyAccountImpl_ = address(0)`, so a contract signer keeps the 50 k ERC-1271 cap (MD-11 (c)); the flat builders kept on 2026-11-01 are in legacy (MD-11 (a), owner 2026-11-05). `SmartKeyAccount` is unchanged.

### CTR-ACC-06 — Delegated payment uses MandateWallet, no allowance
- old: R25 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/mandates.md#CTR-ACC-06 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — owner, delegate and payees may be UAs (CTR-ACC-12; SPECIFIED, UA-5c). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.12, Q8.

**Why.** Delegated payment through a dedicated `MandateWallet` (`mtxPayUnderMandate`) with per-token limits never exposes the payer's main balance to an allowance; a mandate is not an allowance, since the wallet, a contract, is the token's caller. The wallet's domain is salted with a deployer-chosen `chain_uid`, so the node checks it before relaying.
**Cost if wrong.** An allowance-based mandate would be an unlimited spender on the payer's tokens.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-addendum-wallets.md:196`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-3, MG-4, MG-7.
Change (2026-10-08): `MandateWallet` is a `MetaTxBase` contract: the delegate signs a `MetaTransaction` with `data = payUnderMandate(token, payee, amount, entryRef)` or `revoke(token, epoch)`, fee `NONE`; the typed `PayUnderMandate`/`RevokeMandate` go; named entries keep their signatures and derive their lane (`"scaas.mandate.pay"`/`"scaas.mandate.revoke"`, nonce 0). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G3, §3 GC-6.
Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — **mandate periods are fixed windows on the grid of the mandate's start** (the second code review, on-chain part (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-sol`; triage W-A…W-S in `pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, row W-L; report `V2-claude-ua-account-wallet.md` V2-4). `MandateWallet.payUnderMandate` reset an ended period to `periodStart = now`, so the first payment after an idle stretch opened a window where the delegate chose; now `periodStart += ⌊(now − periodStart) / periodSeconds⌋ · periodSeconds`, the window that holds `now`, so the boundaries stay on the grid `setMandate` (or a reset) started and the owner can compute them. A fixed window still admits `maxPerPeriod` just before and again just after a boundary — at most `2 · maxPerPeriod` within any `periodSeconds`, as before; the grid does not remove that, and the triage's "no double cap across a boundary" needs a rolling window, i.e. the payment history on chain (rejected: unbounded storage and gas per payment). `mandates.md` CTR-ACC-06 states the semantics and tells an owner who needs a hard bound per `periodSeconds` to set half the cap. Test `test_period_windows_stay_on_the_grid` (fails on the old reset). Deployed bytecode: `MandateWallet` (and `HederaMandateWallet`). Status: **done** (`a59168c5`).
Change (2026-10-19): **owner ruling W-L — the fixed period grid is accepted.** The owner accepts the grid of fixed windows as built (`a59168c5`, merged in the 5g integration `b37a49cf`): a delegate can spend `maxPerPeriod` just before and again just after a boundary, so at most `2 · maxPerPeriod` within any `periodSeconds`, as mandates.md CTR-ACC-06 documents; no rolling window (it needs the payment history on chain: unbounded storage, or a ring buffer with a payment-count cap). An owner who needs a hard bound per `periodSeconds` sets half the cap, or a shorter period with a proportional cap (P/2 with cap/2 gives at most 1.5× over any interval of length P). Status: **ruled** (owner, 2026-10-19); mandates.md says so.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) Q6 and MD-11, spec row R32; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge` (T3b), UNAUDITED): `MandateWallet` is a `UAMetaTxBase` contract with one signed entry per operation over `UA<Op>`: the delegate signs `UAPayUnderMandate` (`mtxPayUnderMandate`) and `UADelegateRevoke` (`mtxDelegateRevoke`), the owner `UASetMandate`, `UASetPayee`, `UARevokeMandate` and `UAExecute`; the lanes stay `mandatePayLane(entryRef)` / `mandateRevokeLane(token, epoch)`, nonce 0, as the signer's `batch`. The 2026-10-08 sentence "named entries keep their signatures" is reversed: the flat builders and `mandate_pay_kat.json` / `mandate_revoke_kat.json` are in legacy (MD-11 (a)); `executeMetaTransaction` refuses every call (MD-11 (b)). Normative text: [mandates.md §1](contracts/mandates.md#CTR-ACC-06).

### CTR-ACC-07 — Signed mandate revocation bound to epoch
- old: CR-ADW-1 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/mandates.md#CTR-ACC-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A signed revocation (`mtxRevoke`, renamed from `revokeWithSig`) bound to an epoch revokes every outstanding mandate signature at once and works gaslessly.
**Cost if wrong.** Without the epoch a revoked delegate could replay an older mandate.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-addendum-wallets.md:296`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-3.
Change (2026-10-08): the epoch travels in the revoke data, `revoke(token, epoch)`, on the lane `keccak256("scaas.mandate.revoke" ‖ token ‖ epoch)`. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-6.
Change (2026-10-30, owner ruling; branch `ua-soroban` T6b): the rule now also covers the Soroban mandate (one rule on every family): `epoch(token)`, +1 on every `mtx_set_mandate` and revoke, signed in the delegate's `mtx_revoke` and `mtx_mandate_pay` (`StaleEpoch = 13`), and the owner may pass any epoch to `mtx_revoke` (unchecked, as the EVM owner revoke has no epoch). NEAR, Algorand, Cosmos and Solana follow in their own family rounds. Details: NET-SOR-21.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller call; status: documented; built in typed-signing C5; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the named `mtxPayUnderMandate(Envelope, …)` and `mtxDelegateRevoke(Envelope, …)` stay bound to the mandate epoch (`test_mandateEpochBound`) and run on `mandatePayLane(entryRef)` / `mandateRevokeLane(token, epoch)` at nonce 0 (node and clients; the node refuses any other lane, `MANDATE_LANE`). The flat `mtxPayUnderMandate(token, …)` and `mtxRevoke` stay (owner 2026-11-01).

### CTR-ACC-08 — Passkey subjects, Merkle batch, account key lifecycle
- old: R31(account) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-08 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Retail subjects use passkeys they already have; Merkle batching gives one biometric prompt for many lines; one grammar and check order apply in every family.
**Cost if wrong.** Per-family WebAuthn checks drift, and one lax family (suffix origin, crossOrigin) becomes the phishing target.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md:519`

### CTR-ACC-09 — SmartKeyAccount kept as optional option (b)
- old: R307 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `SmartKeyAccount` stays available as option (b) for users who want a stable address across key rotation.
**Cost if wrong.** Removing it would force every rotation to move funds.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:238`

### CTR-ACC-10 — SmartKeyAccount key management is a MetaTransaction signed by the account itself
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-10 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `SmartKeyAccount` moves onto `MetaTxBase` like every SCaaS contract (owner G3); its keys include passkeys with no address, so the account itself is `from` and verifies the signature against its own key set (owner G9); the typed `OwnerCall` and its single nonce go, the lanes and vectors are shared with every contract.
**Cost if wrong.** An account that signed as one of its keys could not use passkeys; a separate owner struct keeps a second digest rule and nonce space alive.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G3, G9, §3 GC-6.
Change (2026-11-01, typed-signing C5; controller calls, owner may override; status: built on the branch, the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): `SmartKeyAccount` and `MandateWallet` (with `HederaMandateWallet`) take the named typed entries of TS-D14, the account's six with `AccountSig`, on the `typed_ops.json` rows. Calls taken in building them:

- **The named builders stay.** `mtxPayUnderMandate(token, …, validUntil, sig)`, `mtxRevoke`, `mtxExecuteAsOwner` and `mtxExecuteAsOwnerRaw` sign the generic `MetaTransaction`, so they add no digest, and TS-D14 keeps that path. `mtxPayUnderMandate` is now an overload; its derived lanes hold only on the flat form. The named form's `batch` is the signer's: a signature cannot move lanes, since `batch` is signed, and `refUsed` and `epoch` stop a new signature by the delegate for the same payment or revoke.
- **`Execute` runs in `src/wallet/WalletExecute.sol`, an abstract `MetaTxBase` both wallets inherit.** `_named` takes one `args` for the struct and the call, which a hashed `bytes data` cannot be, so this holds the typehash and builds the digest and the call; it runs `MetaTxBase._run`, now `internal`, so there is one pipeline. A token overrides `_execute` and `_named`, so `_run` stays dead code there and no token grows; only the metadata hash moves, so the CREATE2-derived KATs are regenerated. No storage or selector changes.
- **`AccountSig` reaches `_isValid` as the calldata tuple itself.** A dynamic tuple in calldata is `abi.encode(keyIndex, proof, signature)`, so the entries pass that slice as `bytes` to the unchanged pipeline, with no second decoder.
- **Rows.** An account signs as itself, so its rows run on an account placed at the row's `from`. `AddKey` and `RotateKey` carry filler keys: they run past digest, signature and nonce and stop at `BadKey`; a valid key through both entries is in `NamedWallets.t.sol`. No vector moved.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller calls, owner may override, owner ruling 2026-11-01 for the flat builders; status: documented; built in typed-signing C5; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): `SmartKeyAccount` has named entries `mtxAddKey`, `mtxRemoveKey`, `mtxRotateKey`, `mtxSetGuardian`, `mtxCancelRecovery` and `mtxExecute(Envelope, …)`, each with `AccountSig`; `MandateWallet` has `mtxSetMandate`, `mtxSetPayee`, `mtxRevokeMandate`, `mtxPayUnderMandate`, `mtxDelegateRevoke`, `mtxExecute`. `Execute` is the one generic struct, kept because the call is inherently arbitrary (`src/wallet/WalletExecute.sol`). The four flat builders `mtxPayUnderMandate(token, …)`, `mtxRevoke`, `mtxExecuteAsOwner`, `mtxExecuteAsOwnerRaw` stay: they sign the generic `MetaTransaction`, add no digest, and `mandate_pay_kat` / `mandate_revoke_kat` depend on them.

### CTR-ACC-11 — The multi-key contract account is SmartKeyAccount in every chain family
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-ACC-11 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** "Smart" marks a contract account and "key" its many keys; the old name said nothing a reader could use. One name in every family (EVM `SmartKeyAccount` and `SmartKeyAccountFactory`, the Solana, Sui, Aptos and Soroban equivalents) is renamed in code in phase P4, all at once.
**Cost if wrong.** Two names live side by side in code and docs for longer than P4; a half-renamed family reads as a different contract.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` T15.

### CTR-ACC-12 — A UA may own, delegate and receive under a MandateWallet
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-13 · normative: contracts/mandates.md#CTR-ACC-12 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `bytes32` owner, delegate and payees with the generic UA pipeline of `MetaTxBase` let a UA use a mandate without a wallet-specific signature path; a derived owner gets no ERC-1271 answer because callers cap 1271 at 50 k gas (a PQ check needs up to 5.95 M) and a 1271 answer would be a generic signing oracle for a UA key (CTR-UA-10 layer 1).
**Cost if wrong.** A derived owner cannot pay by hand through ERC-1271; it acts through `uaExecute(execute(…))` on the wallet.
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-13 (Q8); `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.12, O7.
Change (owner 2026-11-04, `ua*` / `mtx*` merge; status: SPECIFIED, not built): **superseded in form by [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30)** (its Q6 Change). The ids stay as this rule says: `bytes32` owner, delegate and payees, every authority check on the subject as an id, a native payee paid by `payWithFee` and a derived one by `payWithFeeToUA`, no ERC-1271 answer for a derived owner, `HederaMandateWallet` following with HIP-632 on the native branch. The form changes: the wallets get merged entries, not twins. Each wallet operation has one signed entry `mtx<Op>(UAEnvelope, …, UASig)` for native and derived signers alike; `uaExecute`, `uaPayUnderMandate`, `uaRevoke` and `uaExecuteAsOwner` are not built, and a derived owner acts through the merged `mtxExecute`, not `uaExecute(execute(…))`. A native signer needs no registry; a derived one goes through `UARegistry.requireAuthorized`. Built in the merge round (plan T3b); `contracts/mandates.md` is rewritten there (T19).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) Q6 and MD-11, spec row R32; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge` (T3b), UNAUDITED): the rule is BUILT in the merged form, not as `ua*` twins: constructor `(bytes32 owner, bytes32 chainUid, address registry, bool hedera)`, `_subject()` checks, a native signer by its own key without a registry call, a derived one through the registry (`UALedgerOff` at 0); tests `test/wallet/MandateWalletMerged.t.sol`, `NamedWallets.t.sol`. Normative text rewritten in [mandates.md](contracts/mandates.md#CTR-ACC-12).
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O11, controller call C5 (T37 `3740b85e`): the wallets' pay entries (`payUnderMandate`, `mtxPayUnderMandate`) take `PayMeta` last, unsigned and bound by the signed `entryRef` (`UAPayUnderMandate` unchanged); the wallet's own `refUsed[entryRef]` is the wallet's rule, untouched by O3; new KAT and CREATE2 addresses (`test/wallet/MandateWallet.t.sol`).

## 20. Contracts — DEX

### CTR-DEX-01 — Complete DEX with token-verified orders and no allowances for SCaaS tokens
- old: R35(contract) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-01 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An off-chain persistent book with on-chain settlement gives exchange UX without custody. The owner moved order verification into the sell token (role-free `TradeOrder`, funds only into the named DEX), kept both paths, and made the DEX pay out and end every call with unchanged balances; the fee rate is the signed one.
**Cost if wrong.** Trusting the book for prices would let the operator fill against users; DEX allowances keep EOA approvals alive.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md:554`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A7, A10, §3 MG-8.
Change (2026-10-08): the same `TradeOrder`s can also be executed against AMM pools — multi-hop routes, cycles — through `mtxExchange` (CTR-DEX-20), with the surplus paid to the signers (CTR-DEX-21). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §1, §2 S3, §3 DS-1.

### CTR-DEX-02 — Cancel signatures never expire; per token and per DEX
- old: RS5-10 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-02 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Cancel signatures (`CancelOrder`, `InvalidateNonces`) never expire, so a cancellation cannot lapse before the order does; they now live on each sell token (`mtxCancelOrder`, `mtxInvalidateNonces` per order lane) and on the DEX for outside-token orders.
**Cost if wrong.** An expiring cancel could resurrect an order the signer withdrew.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:119`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.2, MG-8.4.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller calls, owner may override, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): nested cancels `CancelOrder(TradeOrder order)`, `CancelUAOrder`, `CancelWrapOrder`, `CancelUAWrapOrder`, `CancelDexOrder(DexOrder order)`; the `pulled` key stays the order digest; the cancel carries no deadline of its own (controller call, `op.validUntil` of the job stands alone).

### CTR-DEX-03 — Admin set once at creation: list markets and set the fee split
- old: RS5-1 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The admin, set once at creation (CTR-DEX-24) with no setter, has two powers — `setMarket(base, quote, listed)` and `setFeeSplit(relayerSharePpm, treasury)` — and changes who receives fees and in what proportion, never the amount, which comes only from the signed `fee`.
**Cost if wrong.** An admin that sets the fee amount could raise it on resting orders; any custody power is custody by another name.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:398`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A15, §3 MG-8.3.
Change (2026-10-08): `admin` is written once by `initialize` of a factory-made clone, no longer an immutable (CTR-DEX-24); two more powers, `setExchangeTarget` (list or delist an exchange target or executor) and `setListedOnly` (DEX-wide listed-only mode, default off); neither touches funds or a fee amount (CTR-DEX-23). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §2 S1, S2, §3 DS-6.
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-01 with its Change, CTR-GOV-04): the DEX is on `GovernanceBase`. Old rule: one `admin`, set once, no transfer, no renounce, holding all four powers. New rule: one `owner`, a UA id (`bytes32`), with a two-step transfer and a renounce; `setMarket`, `setExchangeTarget` and `setListedOnly` run under bit 11 `LISTING`, `setFeeSplit` under bit 12 `FEE_ROUTING`; `initialize` gives a non-zero owner both bits, and a new holder waits `grantDelay`; a UA that is no native account acts through the chain's `GovernanceRouter`; still never the fee amount. CTR-DEX-12, -18 and -23 name the holder of `LISTING` where they named the admin. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T3 `7825361b`, T7 `c2525e28`, T10b `ac29de05`, T11 `ea9f4e9d`).

### CTR-DEX-04 — IOC closed on chain at its single pull
- old: RS5-3 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An IOC order is pulled once and `pulled[h] = amount` at that pull, so its remainder cannot fill later; Path B implies IOC.
**Cost if wrong.** A dangling IOC remainder could fill at a stale price.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:402`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.2.

### CTR-DEX-05 — FOK is minFill = amount, checked on chain
- old: RS5-4 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Fill-or-kill is the order's `minFill = amount` with nothing pulled yet, enforced by the token (Path A) or the DEX (Path B, outside legs), so a partial fill can never settle.
**Cost if wrong.** Trusting the book for FOK lets a buggy matcher partially fill.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:404`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A13, §3 MG-8.1.

### CTR-DEX-06 — Relayer FIXED fee pro-rata, rounds down
- old: RS5-6(relayer-fee) · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-DEX-17

**What it said.** A separate per-order relayer fee (`FeeMode`, `fee`, `feeToken`, `feeRecipient`) was charged pro-rata per fill and rounded down.
**Why.** The owner replaced it with one signed DEX fee rate whose relayer share the DEX pays per its admin split (CTR-DEX-17).
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:407`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A15, §7 (CTR-DEX-06 row).

### CTR-DEX-07 — MetaTxDex kept as unrouted legacy
- old: RS5-7 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-DEX-16, CTR-DEX-01

**What it said.** `MetaTxDex` stayed deployed as an unrouted legacy two-leg settlement over `trade` op legs.
**Why.** The trade op is gone with the op dispatch; `SCaaSDex.mtxSettle` covers its fill-or-kill case, so `MetaTxDex` is deleted.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:409`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.4, §7 (CTR-DEX-07 row).

### CTR-DEX-08 — SCaaSDex caps ERC-1271 gas by codehash
- old: RS5-14(contract) · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-08 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The DEX's own signature checks (outside-token legs, DEX-domain cancels) cap ERC-1271 gas by codehash (400 k for `SmartKeyAccount` clones, else 50 k) and refuse to run with too little gas left; SCaaS legs get the same cap inside their token.
**Cost if wrong.** Uncapped 1271 lets a signer grief the settler; a 63/64 starvation could fake a failed check.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:431`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.4.
Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — **an outside token cannot forge the starvation errors** (the second code review, on-chain part (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-sol`; triage W-A…W-S in `pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, row W-O; report `V3-claude-common-metatx-dex.md` V3-01). `mtxSettle` re-raises a settlement's `SigCheckGasStarved` / `UAVerifyGas` for the whole call; an admin-listed outside token (or an ERC-777-style hook behind a payout) could revert with those bytes, so one counterparty voided a relayer's whole batch. Fix at the source: no call the DEX makes into a token returns the token's revert data — the puller pulls by `trySafeTransferFrom`, `_send` / `_sendTo` pay by `trySafeTransfer`, `_bal` reads `balanceOf(this)` by a one-word `staticcall`; each failure reverts `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)`. Only the DEX, a SCaaS token (factory-registered code, no hooks) or the registry can then raise the two errors, so the re-raise rule stays and a real starvation still reverts the whole call. Deviation from the triage ("honour them only when the DEX frame itself is low on gas"): a real `UAVerifyGas` can come back with most of the gas (a `mldsa65` hold of 5.95 M refused at its start; caps up to `verifyBudget`, 12 M), so a threshold sound for real starvations lets a forger through on every batch below ≈ 6–13 M gas, and a tighter one turns real starvations into `MatchFailed`, which the node drops (NODE-DEX-06); the source fix has neither problem. Cost: the `MatchFailed` reason of a failed token call is `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)` instead of the token's own error, for every token the DEX calls, SCaaS tokens included (`_send` / `_sendTo` / `_bal` serve all tokens): an outside token's `ERC20InsufficientAllowance(puller, …)`, and a regulated SCaaS payout's `Frozen` / `NotEligible` / `TokenPaused`, now all read `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)` (the venue's NODE-DEX-11 pre-check carries the regulated attribution); a returnbomb token now returns one word. Tests: `test_forgedStarvationFromAnOutsideToken_isOnlyMatchFailed` (pull, payout, balance read × both selectors: only that settlement fails, the other settles); the existing starvation tests unchanged. Deployed bytecode: `SCaaSDex` (and the `DexPuller` it deploys). Status: **done** (`c65f897e`). Follow-up (5g integration, branch `rev2-chain-int`; review of W-O F1 / F2; controller proposal, owner may override): (1) a token call that returns **no data** (it ran out of gas, or the token has no code) reverts **empty** again, so `MatchFailed`'s reason stays empty, which the node and the client contract read as `out_of_gas` (NODE-DEX-06, dex-venue.md, TODO P2b-2, the ERP connector contract); anything else reverts `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)` (`SCaaSDex._tokenFailed`, used by `_send` and `_bal`; the same check inline in `DexPuller.pull`). Empty data matches neither starvation selector, so a token still cannot forge one. Test `test_starvedOutsideTokenCall_isAnEmptyMatchFailed` (pull, payout, balance read run out of gas: empty reason, the other settlement settles; fails before the follow-up), `test_forgedStarvationFromAnOutsideToken_isOnlyMatchFailed` still passes. (2) The texts (this entry, dex.md, the `mtxSettle` comment, asset-suite.md) say "every token" instead of "outside token" and list the regulated-reason loss above. Bytecode: `SCaaSDex` 22,953 B, `DexPuller` 643 B. Status: **done** (`5de4be5a`).

### CTR-DEX-09 — Non-EVM settlement bound to the relayer
- old: RS5-15(non-evm) · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Non-EVM settlement is bound to the relayer, so a third party cannot front-run a matched pair.

### CTR-DEX-10 — min_nonce capped by family word width
- old: RS5-19 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-10 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `min_nonce` is capped by each family's word width so a maker cannot brick its own nonce space by overflow.
