### CTR-DEX-11 — DEX fee rounds up, once per order per settlement
- old: RS5-21 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-11 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `dexFee = ceil(receiveFill · fee / 10⁶)` on the order's aggregate received amount in a settlement, so many small fills cannot evade the fee by rounding and the token's `FeeAboveSigned` bound holds for a taker filled by several makers.
**Cost if wrong.** Round-down lets dust fills trade fee-free; per-maker ceilings could exceed the signed bound.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md:455`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.3.

### CTR-DEX-12 — Managed market venue contract and arbiter
- old: R214(contract) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-12 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A managed market is an `SCaaSDex` instance whose admin is the venue operator's multisig; the regulated token's own checks arbitrate on chain, and a settlement that slipped through intake fails alone.
**Cost if wrong.** Mixing managed rules into the open DEX would gate everyone.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-asset-suite-design.md:176`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.3.

### CTR-DEX-13 — TradeOrder: one role-free struct for every leg
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-13 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner modernized the earlier `MtxTradeOrder` with the old field names: `from`, `receiveToken`, `amount`, `receiveAmount`, `minFill`, `fee`, `relayer` (the matching party), `dex` (the only puller and recipient), `destination` (accepted by the owner), `flags`, `batch`, `nonce`, `validUntil`, signed in the sell token's salted domain. No role and no counterparty field: taker or maker is arranged at settlement, and `relayer` decides who may match.
**Cost if wrong.** Role fields freeze an order's side; a counterparty field duplicates `relayer`; an unsigned price on escrow legs lets the DEX set it.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A10, A12, A14, §3 MG-8.1.

Change (2026-10-31, owner ruling on the typed-signing plan): **`TradeOrder.batch` and `nonce` keep their names in Part C.** They are the order lane (`minNonce`), separate from the meta-tx lane (`nonces`), so the named entries' `Envelope.batch` / `nonce` do not rename or merge them. Why: the fields already say what they are in the order's own struct, and a rename would churn every order digest and vector for nothing. Cost if wrong: two different lanes share a field name, told apart by the struct. Status: decided; no code change.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R37; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): `TradeOrder` for every outside leg; a SCaaS token leg is a `UATradeOrder` ([CTR-DEX-26](contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-26) shape 1).

### CTR-DEX-14 — Minimum fill: the signer's minFill for every order in a settlement, no protocol floor
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-29 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-14 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner 2026-10-29: the 50 % protocol floor (`MIN_FILL_PPM = 500_000`, owner 2026-10-08: effective minimum `max(minFill, ceil(amount / 2))` on the sold side and `receiveFill · 10⁶ ≥ receiveAmount · MIN_FILL_PPM` on the received side, for the taker and every maker) is dropped. Every order in a settlement fills at least its signed `minFill` or closes its remainder (`sellFill == amount − pulled[h]`); `minFill = 0` is valid, `minFill = amount` is fill-or-kill, `minFill > amount` stays `BadMinFill`; there is no received-side line (it follows from the sold side and the price limit). The floor was a fixed number the signer could not lower, and its reason ("no order is matched as junk"; a small fill forces a maker to re-create its order) did not hold: a partial fill leaves the remainder resting, fee splitting is already closed by the fee round-up (CTR-DEX-11), the relayer that pays the gas is the venue node, and a signature is verified once per order whatever the fill. The floor did harm: a large order at the best price showed as liquidity only takers of half its size could take (a cheap fake wall), small takers were pushed to worse prices, users split orders (more signatures and verifies), a Path A order was locked to two fills, and partial coincidences of wants (the four matching modes, research note `research/dex-matching-modes.md` §5–§6) were impossible. Junk fills become venue policy (NODE-DEX-15: no leg below the market's `min_base_amount` unless it closes, no settlement worth less than its gas; `depth` / `ticker` keep large-`minFill` orders out of best bid / ask) and clients default `minFill` to the market's minimum size (CLI-SGN-35). The non-EVM programs never had the floor. Status SPECIFIED; the built code (`TradeLib`, `SCaaSDex` Path B, the node's `min_fill`, clientkeys) still applies 50 % (Transitional). All chains are test-only: no migration.
**Why an amount, not a percentage** (owner question 2026-10-30): `minFill` is an absolute sell-token amount signed in the order. It means the same in every settlement of a partly filled order (a percentage would have to say "of the original amount" or "of what remains", and the second changes after each fill); it states the signer's real constraint (do not fill me below X tokens: a smaller fill is not worth its fee and gas); the chain checks it with one comparison, no ppm arithmetic or rounding; a wallet that thinks in percent signs `minFill = amount · p`; and it covers fill-or-kill (`minFill = amount`) and any fill (`minFill = 0`). The removed 50 % floor was exactly a protocol-wide percentage.
**Cost if wrong.** If dust fills turn out to matter on chain, the venue policy is the only guard against them, and an order signed with a small `minFill` can be filled in small pieces by an open (`relayer = 0`) submitter at that submitter's gas cost (the maker still gets its price, the fee rounds up). With the floor kept: fake walls at the best price, worse prices for small takers, split orders, no partial CoW / hybrid.
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-29 (chat; research note `research/dex-matching-modes.md` §6.3). Earlier rule: owner 2026-10-08, `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A13, §3 MG-8.1.
Change (2026-10-30): **built** in the DEX round (branch `dex-round`, task T1 the code, tasks T2–T13 the rest of the round). What: `TradeLib.record` and `SCaaSDex._calc` Path B refuse `move != amount − pulled && move < minFill` and nothing else, there is no received-side line, `MIN_FILL_PPM` is gone, the node's `min_fill` is the signed `minFill` (T11), clientkeys shows it as signed (T14), an anvil e2e settles a fill below half an order (T13, T13 fix). Options weighed (DEX spec row 1, "minimum fill"): keep the 50 % floor, or the signer's `minFill` only; the round builds the owner's 2026-10-29 choice and re-decides nothing. Why: the dropped floor made fake walls, pushed small takers to worse prices and ruled out partial coincidences (the Why above). Cost if wrong: dust fills (the venue policy of NODE-DEX-15 is the only guard); tokens and DEXes made before the new releases keep the floor until redeployed (all chains are test-only, no migration). Who: owner 2026-10-29, built as ruled. The pre-round code and the two floor tests are kept in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/dex-round/` (owner: backup, not delete). Test consequence: the old step of the e2e `dex_order_book_settles_partial_fills_persists_and_cancels` that expected a below-half bid to be cancelled was removed because it described the old floor (cancel, persistence and failed-commit steps remain tested) — a controller call at the T13 review, cost if wrong: none.


### CTR-DEX-15 — The sell token verifies the order and moves funds only into dex
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-15 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — step 4 is skipped when `pulled[h] ≠ 0` (verified at the first pull or cancel; `h` binds every field), on the token and on the DEX's outside legs; `minNonce` is keyed by `bytes32` (natives padded: same slots), one floor for `TradeOrder` and `UATradeOrder`. SPECIFIED (UA-5b). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.6, UP-12, O6, Q6.
Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — **on-chain review W-S, SOL-02 (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-pqz`, commit `fb7600cb`; U SOL-02, P3):** the price limits `move · receiveAmount > receiveFill · amount` (`TradeLib.record`, Path A) and `sold · receiveAmount > recv · amount` (`SCaaSDex._calc`, ESCROW, CTR-DEX-16) are compared over 512 bits (`TradeLib.mulGt`, `Math.mul512`): the same verdict for every input whose products fit (fuzzed against the plain products), `PriceLimit` instead of a panic past 2^256. SOL-01 (floor rounding dust of `pqzUnshieldUnwrap`, favours solvency) and SOL-03 (`PqzSafety` / `ZetherSafety` chain allowlists, 22776 added at its launch gate) recorded as by design. Bytecode: `TradeLib` (+85 B), `SCaaSDex` (+58 B). Tests `test_pathA_priceLimit_hugeAmounts`, `testFuzz_mulGt`, `test_mulGt_past2pow256`, `test_pathB_priceLimit_hugeReceiveAmount`. Status: **done** (`fb7600cb`, merged `734b9c76`).

**Why.** `mtxTrade` checks the caller is the named contract `dex`, the relayer binding, expiry, order lane, flags, amounts, the fee cap, the signature and `pulled[h] < amount`; on Path A it also checks fill, overfill, minimum, price and fee figures against the signed values; it moves funds to `dex` only, so no allowance is needed and a signer reads one address to know where its funds can go.
**Cost if wrong.** A token that trusts a caller-chosen route or recipient turns every order into a permit.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A7, §3 MG-8.2, §12 (C1, H7, M1), §13 (N-M1).
Change (2026-10-08): `o.receiveToken == address(this)` is allowed (a cycle order sells X for more X on the exchange path); `SelfOrder` stays for `from` and `dex`; known flags gain `LISTED_POOLS = 4`, which the token does not interpret. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §2 S3, §3 DS-2.
Change (2026-10-27): **review C6-5 (controller proposal, owner may override)**: an order with `nonce ≥ 2^128` is refused at the pre-check (`NonceAboveCap(orderHash)`): no lane floor could ever reach it (`minNonce` is capped at `2^128`, CTR-DEX-02), only a per-order cancel would. The node's intake (`scaas-node` `dex.rs`) and `clientkeys` `checkTradeOrder` refuse it the same way. Status: **done** (review2 T6 `4623478d`, T7 `1b26e5ff`).
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller calls, owner may override, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the token's cancel entries take the nested structs (TS-D19) and `tradeOrderDigest` hashes `dex == receiveToken` as `WrapOrder`; `mtxCancelOrder(TradeOrder, sig)` tells a wrap order by that rule; views `cancelOrderDigest(TradeOrder)`, `cancelUAOrderDigest(UATradeOrder)`.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R38; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the token-side entry is `mtxTrade(ITradeToken.UATradeOrder o, IUARegistry.UASig auth, ITradeToken.TradeFill f)`, today's `uaTrade` body; `TradeOrder` stays for outside legs.

### CTR-DEX-16 — mtxSettle: everything through the DEX, balances unchanged
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-16 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — legs become tagged (`{sellToken, shape, order, sig, fill}`, shape 0 `TradeOrder`, shape 1 `UATradeOrder`); the UA rules are CTR-DEX-26. SPECIFIED (UA-5b). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.7, O3, Q5.

**Why.** One taker against many makers per settlement: check, match at maker prices, pull every leg into the DEX, pay every destination, fee share and refund in the same call, then assert the DEX's balance of every token unchanged. One choke point and one invariant replace per-party delta checks, which misfire on shared addresses; listing only exact-transfer tokens makes conservation catch a misbehaving token.
**Cost if wrong.** Payments outside the DEX would leave the token trusting a fill it cannot see; dust or donations could be paid out.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.3, §12 (M1, M3), §13 (N-M3).
Change (2026-10-08): outside-token legs are pulled through the `DexPuller` (CTR-DEX-22). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §3 DS-4.
Change (2026-10-27): **review C6-8, the controller rulings of the P2b build recorded in full (owner may override)**: (1) there is no `checkOrder` view on the DEX: the dex.md §10 reads are the intake (P2b-2, `f4afbcac`); (2) `MatchFailed` keeps the first 256 bytes of a settlement's revert data (`MAX_REASON`) and `SigCheckGasStarved` reverts the whole call (P2b-2, `f4afbcac`). Status: **done** (built in P2b-2; recorded in review2 T8).
Change (2026-10-27): **review C6-1 (controller proposal, owner may override)**: every call the DEX or its puller makes into any token (`balanceOf`, `transferFrom`, `transfer`, `TokenCall`) is forwarded at most `TOKEN_GAS = 500,000` gas, so a hook or hostile token cannot burn the gas a later capped verify needs; running out is an ordinary failed call with empty return data (`MatchFailed`, the node's `out_of_gas`). The README row offered a per-settlement gas budget and / or this cap; only the cap was built: a `Settlement.gas` field changes the ABI the node and `clientkeys` encode. Cost if wrong: a token whose transfer needs more than 500,000 gas cannot settle on the DEX. Status: **done** (review2 T6 `49769894`).

### CTR-DEX-17 — One signed fee rate; the DEX distributes it per the admin split
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-17 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner kept one fee field, `fee` (ppm, ≤ 1 %), on what the signer receives in any role; the DEX charges at most that, once per order per settlement, and splits it at once between the submitting relayer and the treasury. There is no separate relayer fee; maker/taker pricing is node intake policy.
**Cost if wrong.** Several fee fields multiply what a signer must check; fees kept in the DEX break conservation.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §2 A15, §3 MG-8.3.
Change (2026-10-27): **review C6-8 (controller ruling of P2b-1, owner may override)**: `FeeSplitInvalid` refuses a treasury of 0 or the DEX at `initialize` / `setFeeSplit` unless the relayer share is 100 %, so no share can stay in the DEX; the `FeeWouldStick` check the first design named is not built (P2b-1, `27b9e92a`; conservation backstops). Status: **done** (built in P2b-1; recorded in review2 T8).

### CTR-DEX-18 — Outside-token legs: the same order, checked by the DEX
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-18 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A token SCaaS does not control cannot verify a `TradeOrder`, so the DEX does, with the same checks, as a `DexOrder` in its own salted domain with `o.dex == this`, its own `pulled`/`minNonce`, no `ESCROW`, and a pull under the party's allowance; token kinds come from the listing (via the factory's provenance), never from the leg.
**Cost if wrong.** A leg-declared kind could send a fallback-only "token" down the `mtxTrade` path; unchecked outside legs would trade at any price.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-8.4, §13 (N-M2).
Change (2026-10-08): the pull is `DexPuller.pull` under the party's allowance to the puller, never to the DEX, so an exchange interaction cannot spend a user allowance (CTR-DEX-22). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §3 DS-4.
Change (2026-10-27): **review C6-4 (controller proposal, owner may override)**: on the exchange path a receive-only outside token with a transfer fee pays signers below their signed floor and conservation does not catch it (the DEX measures its own balance; the fee comes out of the recipient's side); the settle path pulls both tokens and is safe. The loss is bounded by the token's fee. Recorded in dex.md (CTR-DEX-18, -21): list exact-transfer tokens only, delist a token that shows a fee; a recipient-balance check was not built. **Review C6-9**: `setMarket` refuses `base == quote` and a zero token (`BadMarket`). Status: **done** (documented in review2 T8; C6-9 built in review2 T6 `4623478d`).
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller calls, owner may override, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the DEX's cancel is `CancelDexOrder(DexOrder order)` nested (`cancelDexOrderDigest(sellToken, TradeOrder)`); a leg is `DexLeg` / `ExchangeLeg` with typed members instead of opaque `bytes order` / `bytes sig` (Appendix X row 20, controller call): a dirty address word in a leg reverts the whole `mtxSettle` at the outer re-encoding.

### CTR-DEX-19 — dex must be a contract, nothing more (owner-accepted residual risk)
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-19 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The owner decided against a token-side DEX registry or codehash allowlist: the token requires only that `dex` is a contract and consults no registry (the factory's `isDex`, CTR-DEX-24, is advisory, for clients and the node). A phishing contract named as `dex` can take the signed amount; the mitigations are off chain — clients warn and by default refuse to build or sign for a `dex` off the chain profile's DEX list (for `mtxWrap`: a registered wrapper), wallets show `dex`, and the node routes only to listed DEXes.
**Cost if wrong.** A user who overrides the client refusal and signs for a malicious contract loses the signed amount.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §4, §8 Q5, §13 (N-H1).
Change (2026-10-08): wording only — the token consults no registry; the factory's advisory `isDex` (CTR-DEX-24) is for clients and the node.
Change (2026-11-11, Fable review B P2-1; controller call under the owner's leave; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-fix-contracts`, UNAUDITED): the bound "takes the signed amount" was not true: `restorePulled` gave capacity back without the tokens, so a hostile `dex` could loop pull, restore, pull and take the signer's whole balance within `validUntil`. The restore now moves the tokens back ([CTR-DEX-27](#ctr-dex-27--mtxhybrid--mtxhybridvia-the-book-and-a-route-in-one-call-the-takers-unsold-remainder-refunded-and-its-capacity-restored)); the rule's bound holds again.

### CTR-DEX-20 — mtxExchange: TradeOrders executed against AMMs, multi-hop and cycles
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-20 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** On a chain with AMM liquidity an order the book cannot match can still fill at or above its signed price, a route through several pools can beat one pool, and a signer may want a cycle X→…→X. The owner wanted no new signed struct: the same `TradeOrder` is executed by the node's own algorithm instead of against `makers[]` — (a) `mtxExchange`, the DEX calling each interaction itself (CoW model), (b) `mtxExchangeVia`, a submitter-named executor (UniswapX model); `receiveFill` is a floor, one plan is atomic, and `ExchangeLegSettled` carries `limitReceive` so a client verifies the result without trusting the submitter. Named `mtxExchange` by the owner (first `mtxSolve`).
**Cost if wrong.** Without it AMM liquidity stays out of reach and every order without a book counterpart waits; a DEX-specific router per AMM kind would need new contract code for every venue.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §1, §2 S3, S5, S7, §3 DS-1.
Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — **DEX and metatx hygiene** (the second code review, on-chain part (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-sol`; triage W-A…W-S in `pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, row W-Q; report `V3-claude-common-metatx-dex.md` V3-04 a–f). (a) **Sweep rule, no accounting**: the DEX holds nothing between calls; a balance that reaches it outside a settlement or plan (a mistaken transfer, a fee an interaction earns, e.g. `mtxWrap`'s fee minted to the DEX as submitter) belongs to nobody, and the next exchange-path submitter may move it through an interaction in any token outside its plan (plan tokens must end at their snapshots); dex.md CTR-DEX-20 says so; explicit accounting rejected (bytecode and gas for funds the protocol never puts there). (b) `sellToken == receiveToken` on the exchange path stays allowed — **refuted as a finding**: a cycle order sells X for more X through AMM routes by design (CTR-DEX-20 "multi-hop and cycles", dex.md CTR-DEX-15 step 1, CLI-SGN-37's cycle label; `test_exchange_profitableCycle_xToX`); the settle path refuses it because a book match of X against X is meaningless. A refusal was tried and reverted on that test. (c) `_classify` is **not** re-checked per leg: `deprecate` only marks a version (CTR-TOK-18), a per-leg check costs two factory calls per leg, and making a listed token outside voids every order signed in its token domain — the DEX admin's call, by re-listing (dex.md CTR-DEX-18). (d) Factory doc drift fixed (token-wrappers.md kinds table, CTR-TOK-18 registrar powers, CTR-TOK-25, §6.2; `IOpenFactory`'s enum comment): kinds 4–5 are built behind the PQZ gate, 6–7 reserved; the registrar also has `registerDexImplementation` and `setPqzEnabled`. (e) `mtxWrap` emits `Wrapped(destination or from, u, received, minted − fee)` and `uaWrap` `UAWrapped(to, u, received, minted − fee)` (field renamed `from` → `to`, same topic hash): the credited party and what it got; the return value stays the gross `minted`. (f) `nonReentrant` on `payWithFee`, `payWithFeeToUA`, `mint`, `mintToUA`, the role and owner functions (`MetaTokenBase`), `disableWrap`, `proposeRate`, `cancelRate`, `executeRate`, `disableFeature` (`WrappedToken`) and `SmartKeyAccount.initiateRecovery` / `completeRecovery`; CTR-MTX-18 names the exceptions (`initialize`; the plain ERC-20 `transfer` / `approve` / `transferFrom`, which make no outside call). None of them made an outside call, so no live path closes; the rule becomes true. The `WrappedZetherToken` / `WrappedPqzToken` overrides of `disableFeature` and `executeRate` (zether/, pqz/, open on this branch) got the guard in the 5g integration (`7b507c3a`; test `test_reentryIntoTheRestatedAdminEntriesRefused` in `ZetherWrapped.t.sol` and `PqzWrapped.t.sol`: a hook leg re-entering either mid-pull gets `Reentrancy`, before `NotOwner`; +265 B each, `WrappedPqzToken` 60,105 B against the 65,536 B test-chain limit). Tests: the `Wrapped` / `UAWrapped` assertions of `MtxWrap.t.sol` / `UAWrap.t.sol`; `test_native_reentryIntoEveryEntry_isRefused` (13 entries re-entered from a native payout, all `Reentrancy`); `test_executeCannotReenter` (the recovery entries). Deployed bytecode: `SCaaSDex`, every token implementation, `SmartKeyAccount`. Status: **done** (`0fd4cc65`).
Change (2026-10-30): a failing interaction of a path (a) call no longer "reverts with its data": every path (a) entry (`mtxExchange`, `mtxHybrid`, the batch) reverts `InteractionFailed(uint256 index, address target, bytes reason)` with at most 256 bytes of the target's revert data and copies no return data on success (T2; CTR-DEX-28 has the full decision). Options: bubble the target's revert data (built until now) or wrap it. Why wrap: a hostile target could revert with the `SigCheckGasStarved` or `UAVerifyGas` selector and take a whole batch down, and a returnbomb could drain a plan's frame. Cost if wrong: debugging reads one more ABI layer; executor (path (b)) failures stay unwrapped. Who: owner-confirmed 2026-10-30. Four existing tests moved to the wrapped shape.


### CTR-DEX-21 — The exchange surplus goes to the signers, on chain
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-21 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Output above the floors belongs to the signers (owner): per receive token the excess over the floors and Path B refunds is split pro rata by floor, the remainder to the last leg; any other leftover reverts; the surplus pays no DEX fee. With strict conservation and fixed floors alone, a better-than-quoted AMM output would revert the plan.
**Cost if wrong.** A surplus left to the submitter turns every quote buffer into the submitter's income; a leftover assigned arbitrarily would hide route bugs.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §2 S4, §3 DS-3.

### CTR-DEX-22 — DexPuller: the DEX holds no user allowance
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-22 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An exchange interaction runs as the DEX, so any allowance the DEX held could be spent by `outsideToken.transferFrom(victim, attacker, x)`. Outside-token holders approve an immutable puller that only the DEX can call, and the DEX calls it only after its own `DexOrder` checks (CoW's vault-relayer pattern).
**Cost if wrong.** An allowance on the DEX itself makes every open-mode interaction a theft path for every outside-token holder.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §3 DS-4, §4.
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner ruling CTR-GOV-06): `DexPuller.rescue(token)`, by anyone, pays a stray balance to the puller's immutable `rescueTo` (0 = no rescue); the DEX itself takes no `rescue` entry, CTR-DEX-20 stands. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T10 `dc9bfde0`).

### CTR-DEX-23 — What an exchange interaction may call; listed targets by flag or admin mode
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-23 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Interactions may target any contract by default (owner), except the DEX and the puller, and never with the `mtxTrade` selector (else a victim's resting order naming this DEX could be pulled with an invented fill and the amount moved out while conservation balances). The owner wanted both guards on targets: the signer's `LISTED_POOLS` flag per order and the admin's DEX-wide listed-only mode; the listing then applies to every target and to an executor, whose inner calls the DEX cannot see.
**Cost if wrong.** Without the selector block, any resting order is drainable; without a listing option, a signer who distrusts unknown pools has no on-chain guarantee.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-dex-exchange-design.md` §2 S1, S2, S5, §3 DS-5, DS-6.
Change (2026-10-27): **review C6-8, the controller rulings of P2c recorded in full (owner may override)**: (1) `increaseAllowance(address,uint256)` and Permit2 `approve(address,address,uint160,uint48)` are refused as `ForbiddenSelector` on every interaction target, as `mtxTrade` / `uaTrade` are; (2) every allowance an `approve` interaction granted is set back to 0 after the last interaction; (3) `receivedFloor` is the gross floor (before the DEX fee), so the company books `receivedFloor − dexFee + surplus`. Other allowance-raising calls (e.g. `increaseApproval`) are neither refused nor reset (review C6-10: documented, conservation bounds a call, the admin lists targets accordingly). Status: **done** (built in P2c `dbf27a5e`; recorded in review2 T8).

### CTR-DEX-24 — Factory-made DEX clones; the DEX registry is advisory
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `OpenFactory.createDex` makes an `SCaaSDex` clone with `admin` written once by `initialize` and the `DexPuller` deployed by `initialize`; `isDex` serves clients and the node, and tokens never consult it, because requiring a factory-made DEX would give the factory admin too much power over trades (CTR-DEX-19 unchanged).
**Cost if wrong.** If tokens required `isDex`, the factory admin could stop trading; without the registry, clients and the node have no on-chain list of genuine DEX versions.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-token-tree-design.md` T12, §7.

Change (2026-10-20): owner 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z1) — `deprecateDex(version, reason)` (registrar, immediate,
`DexImplementationDeprecated`) and `isDexDeprecated`; `createDex` refuses a deprecated version (`DexVersionDeprecated`);
DEXes already made are untouched. Status: built, commit `690a295a` (plan Task 5g-Z1).

Change (2026-10-20): owner rulings 2026-10-20 (plan 5g-Z2) — `createDex(version, bytes initArgs, salt)` with
`initArgs = abi.encode(DexConfig)` and `SCaaSDex.initialize(creator, version, initArgs)`; the DEX release is deployed by the

`SmartKeyAccount` implementation and the linked `TradeLib` from the env; the explicit `envVersion` is the interim
controller proposal of CTR-TOK-03, owner may override) and is usable after the notice period
(`DexVersionNotYetUsable`). Status: built on branch `rev2-zether-z2`, commit `0f88e66f` (plan Task 5g-Z2).
Change (2026-11-04, governance T17; owner rulings CTR-GOV-01 with its Change, CTR-GOV-04, CTR-GOV-06): `DexConfig.owner` is a UA id (`bytes32`), `DexConfig` gains `grantDelay` (≤ 30 days) and `rescueTo`, both immutable; ownership moves by `transferOwnership`, no longer "written once"; `DexCreated`'s last field is `owner`. Status: BUILT on branch `governance` (T7 `c2525e28`, T10 `dc9bfde0`, T10b `ac29de05`).
Change (2026-11-07, CTR-TOK-27, CTR-TOK-29): the DEX's record is in the factory index (class 2, kind 0) and `isDex` / `dexVersionOf` read it; `DexCreated` carries `bytes32 indexed creatorId`; the DEX's chain values come from its clone's code (`chainEnv()`, `SMART_KEY_ACCOUNT_IMPL()`, `GOV_ROUTER()`), its release takes `(factory_, implArgs)` only. Status: BUILT (T67, T71, T72).

### CTR-DEX-25 — UATradeOrder: a UA's order, verified by its token
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-13 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-25 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): built as ruled (UA-5b): `UATradeOrder`, `uaTrade`, `uaCancelOrder`, `uaInvalidateNonces` and the views in `ITradeToken` / `ERC20MetaTx`, `TradeLib` on one internal form with `bytes32` `minNonce` (one floor per id both ways), verify once on both paths (CTR-DEX-15 step 4), purpose `trade` in `UAKinds` and the six UA libraries, `uatrade_kat.json`. Controller rulings, confirmed by the owner 2026-10-13: the `ua*` trade functions revert `UALedgerOff` while the ledger is off, a padded native `from` included (C5b-2); one internal order form, a `TradeOrder` read as a `UATradeOrder` in memory (C5b-1). Source add: plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-ua5b-trade-dex.md`.

**Why.** `TradeOrder.from` is an `address`, so a UA needs its own struct (`bytes32 from`, `bytes32 destination`) in the sell token's domain, signed under the new purpose `trade`; the token runs CTR-DEX-15 unchanged on the fields both structs share, moves the fill by `_uaMove`, and shares `minNonce` by id. Widening `TradeOrder` for everyone was rejected: native wallets keep displaying an `address`, and existing vectors and node encoders stay.
**Cost if wrong.** Two order structs for clients, node and vectors.
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-13 (Q3, Q4); `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.6 (UP-11), O2, O4.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller calls, owner may override, TS-D19; status: documented; built in typed-signing C6; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): `CancelUAOrder(UATradeOrder order)` nested; `uaTrade`, `uaCancelOrder`, `uaInvalidateNonces` take `UASig` (Appendix X row 9, forced by `uaWrapOrder` handing its `auth` to the underlying).
Change (owner 2026-11-04, `ua*` / `mtx*` merge; status: SPECIFIED, not built): two parts are reversed by [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30). Spec row R9: C5b-2 ("the `ua*` trade functions revert `UALedgerOff` while the ledger is off, a padded native `from` included") becomes "only a derived seller needs the ledger; an all-native trade runs at `registry() == 0`". Spec row R12: the rationale "Widening `TradeOrder` for everyone was rejected …" becomes "A SCaaS token leg is a `UATradeOrder`, native or derived; `TradeOrder` and its vectors stay for outside legs" (the token's `mtxTrade` is today's `uaTrade`). The Rule text and `contracts/dex.md` are rewritten by the build.

### CTR-DEX-26 — UA legs: tagged legs in SCaaSDex, one book
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-13 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-26 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): built as ruled (UA-5b): tagged `Leg` / `ExchangeLeg`, shape-1 legs on SCaaS ledger tokens pulled by `uaTrade`, payouts and Path B refunds to derived ids by `transferToUA`, `UALegSettled` / `UAExchangeLegSettled`, `UAVerifyGas` re-raised, `uaTrade` refused in interactions; the node sends shape-0 legs and indexes `UALegSettled` (its UA intake, `bytes32` book and PQ gossip after UA F5, C5b-11). `SCaaSDex` is 23,493 B, under EIP-170, so it does not join the size baseline (C5b-14; the cost line above expected it to cross). Controller rulings, confirmed by the owner 2026-10-13: `SelfTrade(bytes32)` (C5b-3), `LegShapeUnknown(uint8)` (C5b-4), "ledger on" = the listing's `tokenKind == SCaaS` and `registry() ≠ 0`, no ERC-165 (C5b-5), a derived destination checked only by the receive token's `transferToUA` at the payout, so an unregistered one is `MatchFailed` (C5b-6), shape-0 bytes after the 13 words ignored (C5b-7). Measured: two `mldsa65` legs 12,124,252 transaction gas; three revert `UAVerifyGas`. Source add: plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-ua5b-trade-dex.md`.

**Why.** Extending `SCaaSDex` in place (a `shape` tag and an encoded order per leg) keeps one book in which UA and native orders match; UA legs only in SCaaS ledger tokens, payouts and refunds to UAs by `transferToUA`; `UAVerifyGas` reverts the whole `mtxSettle` as `SigCheckGasStarved` does, so a starved submitter cannot turn a valid order into `MatchFailed`; `uaTrade` is refused in interactions as `mtxTrade`. A second DEX implementation was rejected: two books, no cross-matching.
**Cost if wrong.** The `Leg` / `ExchangeLeg` ABI changes (nothing deployed); the DEX crosses EIP-170 (size baseline; owner: Glamsterdam); PQ legs bound a settlement to the EIP-7825 cap, so the node packs settlements by kind.
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-13 (Q5); `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.7, O3.

Change (2026-11-10, owner; BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`): **the `p256` / `webauthn-p256` verify cap is 400,000**, the registry's value (`DeployBase`'s `KindConfig` for both kinds), not the classical row's 50,000. The table of [contracts/dex.md](contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-26) splits the row: `p256`, `webauthn-p256` 400,000 (≈ 31 legs per 16.78 M transaction, ≈ 28 on Hedera: an estimate with the `ed25519` row's leg work); the classical row (`bip340`, `secp256k1`, a native id) keeps ≤ 50,000. The node's `verify_cap` (the budget of `LIQUIDITY_TOO_LARGE`, [NODE-DEX-19](node/dex-venue.md#NODE-DEX-19)) reads the same: 40 `p256` SCaaS inputs need 17,000,000 gas, above the 2^24 transaction cap, and are refused before any simulation; 39 fit (`guard::tests::liquidity_pre_checks`).

### CTR-DEX-27 — mtxHybrid / mtxHybridVia: the book and a route in one call; the taker's unsold remainder refunded and its capacity restored
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-27 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner 2026-10-29 (research note `research/dex-matching-modes.md` §8.1): matching mode 3 — makers first, the rest of the taker outside — gets its own entry in addition to `mtxExchange` plans. Decisions, each with its options, choice, cost if wrong and who:
- **Hybrid on chain.** Options: `mtxExchange` plans only; a new entry only; both. Choice: both — `mtxExchange` plans stay (tests only, no ABI change), and `mtxHybrid` / `mtxHybridVia` are new: the contract computes each maker's price as `mtxSettle` does (`⌈fill · receiveAmount / amount⌉`) and the surplus goes to the taker only; the planner uses `mtxHybrid` for mode 3 on a listed market and `mtxExchange` plans for CoW / ring and every other shape. Who: owner 2026-10-29. Status: built.
- **Plan shape.** Options: the research sketch `{ref, taker, makers[], outsideSell, outsideFloor}` or the sketch plus `address[] extraTokens`. Choice: plus `extraTokens` (intermediate hop tokens that pass through the DEX, snapshotted, as `ExchangePlan`); `makers` may be empty, `outsideSell` may be 0 (book only; the planner then uses the cheaper `mtxSettle`); no new error for either. Cost if wrong: an `extraTokens` nobody uses costs one empty array word. Who: controller proposal, owner may override. Status: built.
- **Events.** Options: a new `HybridSettled` event or reuse. Choice: reuse — each maker `LegSettled` / `UALegSettled`; the taker `ExchangeLegSettled` / `UAExchangeLegSettled` with `receivedFloor = Σ maker sold + outsideFloor`, `surplus` = the output above `outsideFloor`, `limitReceive` as today; the makers' `LegSettled` / `UALegSettled` are read by the watcher and indexer today, the taker's `ExchangeLegSettled` / `UAExchangeLegSettled` come with P7 / the `OrderRouter` (NODE-DEX-04, SPECIFIED). Cost if wrong: an indexer that wants `outsideFloor` alone derives it (`receivedFloor − Σ maker sold`). Who: controller proposal. Status: built.
- **A route that leaves part of the taker's sell unspent.** Options: give it to the makers pro rata (CTR-DEX-21), refund the taker, or revert. Choice (owner 2026-10-30, with the clarification of the same day): **refund the taker, only if what it really sold still satisfies its signed order** — the leftover goes back to the taker's `from` fee-free; the sold part must be above 0 (`ZeroFill`), at least its `minFill` (`BelowMinFill`; a fill-or-kill taker can never be refunded) and at a price no worse than its limit (`PriceLimit`), else the whole hybrid reverts (no partial-refund path); makers never receive the leftover and keep their own `minFill` / limit as in `mtxSettle`; a leftover above `outsideSell`, or the sell token below its expected balance, stays `ConservationBroken`; tests are required (built: 51 tests in `DexHybrid.t.sol`). Cost if wrong: a planner that mis-sizes `outsideSell` reverts the hybrid at the relayer's gas. Status: built.
- **Capacity restored** (owner 2026-10-30, follow-up; controller design, owner may override). The refunded part is fillable again under the same signed order: after paying the refund the DEX calls the sell token's `restorePulled(order, amount)` (and the `UATradeOrder` overload for a UA taker; on the DEX's own state for an outside-token taker; skipped for IOC). The token checks `msg.sender == o.dex` and `amount ≤` what this DEX pulled for the order hash in this transaction (a transient EIP-1153 counter that `TradeLib` bumps on every pull), lowers `pulled[h]` and the counter, errors `RestoreExceedsPull(h)`, event `PullRestored(h, amount)`. Alternative rejected: leave the refunded part counted in `pulled[h]` — a resting taker's order could then be closed after selling only its `minFill`, with no funds lost but a surprising lost capacity. Cost if wrong: one more token entry point (the DEX is the only caller; both selectors are `ForbiddenSelector` in interactions); tokens before the new release do not have it.
- **Self-trade and pool listing in a hybrid.** Options: the exchange path's rules or `mtxSettle`'s. Choice: `mtxSettle`'s self-trade rule (no maker's `from` equals the taker's; makers may share a signer), because a hybrid is a book settlement plus a route; `LISTED_POOLS` is read from the taker only (or the admin's `listedOnly`): the route cannot change what a maker gets. Cost if wrong: a maker that wants listed pools only cannot force it in a hybrid (it still gets its exact price). Who: controller proposal.
- **Fees of a hybrid.** Options: as `mtxSettle` or as the exchange path. Choice: makers as `mtxSettle` (`⌈receive · fee / 10⁶⌉` on their exact receive); the taker once on its floor (`Σ maker sold + outsideFloor`), the surplus fee-free (CTR-DEX-21), the relayer share to `msg.sender` (CTR-DEX-17). Who: controller proposal following CTR-DEX-17 and -21.
- **Typed data.** Options: a new signed struct for hybrid or batch plans, or none. Choice: none — plans are submitter-built over the existing signed `TradeOrder` / `UATradeOrder` / `DexOrder` (owner 2026-10-29: no extra signature); `trade_kat.json` and `uatrade_kat.json` do not move. Who: owner (research note §6.1).
- **EIP-7702.** Options: new guards on the new entries or none. Choice: none new — the entries follow owner rulings D1–D5 of 2026-10-30 (CTR-UA-24) as `mtxSettle` / `mtxExchange` do: a designator signs with its own key only, submitters and relayer bindings are open roles, targets are solver-chosen and bounded by conservation. Who: owner rulings 2026-10-30.
- **Non-EVM families.** Options: change in this round or unchanged. Choice: unchanged — none had the floor, none has an exchange path, 1 × N follows with the `OrderRouter`. Who: owner 2026-10-29 (research note §6.3, §8.4).
- **Vectors.** Options: regenerate what moves or hand-patch. Choice: `dex_order_kat.json` regenerated with `WRITE_KAT=true` (18 CREATE2-derived keys moved) plus three encoding-only keys (`hybrid_calldata`, `hybrid_via_calldata`, `exchange_batch_calldata`; 19 → 22 keys); `trade_kat.json`, `uatrade_kat.json` and `metatx-parity.json` unchanged. Who: controller proposal (precedent: the token-rename regeneration, owner 2026-10-30). Regenerated again after main (the UA registry changed there) was merged in (task T17: the addresses moved, the three new keys unchanged in form) and after the final review's allowance-reset fix (final fix wave: CREATE2-derived keys only).
- **Deployment.** Options: migrate or redeploy. Choice: redeploy, no migration (all chains are test-only): a new `TradeLib` means new token releases (a release pins the library's code hash) and a new `SCaaSDex` a new DEX release; tokens made before keep the 50 % floor until redeployed; the SCaaS testnet takes them in its next roll-out (TODO step 5). Who: owner (all chains test-only; 7622 may be reset).
**Cost if wrong.** Without the entry a mode 3 order is two transactions (IOC and FOK cannot span them) or an `mtxExchange` plan whose maker floors the submitter chooses; with it `SCaaSDex` carries about 2 KB more code (the size is recorded in `size-baseline.json`).
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-29 (research note `research/dex-matching-modes.md` §8.1) and 2026-10-30 (the refund, its clarification, the restored capacity); `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-dex-round-design.md` (section 0 rows), rows on the hybrid, plan shape, events, the unspent remainder, self-trade, fees, typed data, 7702, non-EVM, vectors and deployment.
Change (2026-10-30): **built** (DEX round, branch `dex-round`): task T3 (`mtxHybrid` / `mtxHybridVia`; the exchange helpers split into `_snap` / `_checkPulled` / `_route` / `_excess` / `_conserve` and take a `submitter` parameter, stack pressure in a memory struct, `via_ir` stays off), T4 (the taker's refund under its own bounds, `_takerSoldCheck`, `restorePulled`, both selectors forbidden in interactions), T4 review fixes (a no-op cancel clears the pull counter), T6 / T6 fix (modes 3 and 4 proven on `mtxExchange` plans), T8 (invariant suite), T9 / T9 fix (KAT, gas, size). Measured (`vm.lastCallGas` regular gas): `mtxHybrid` 1 × 1 + one hop 407,134, 1 × 2 481,385, `mtxSettle` 1 × 1 306,813 in the same setup. Size: `SCaaSDex` 27,252 B runtime (first `size-baseline.json` entry); the spec expected about 26.5–28 KB.
Change (2026-10-30): controller ruling, owner may override — **both `restorePulled` selectors are `ForbiddenSelector` in `_interact`** (T4 security ruling at the T3 review). What: the token's `restorePulled(TradeOrder,uint256)` (`0x58c18f87`) and `restorePulled(UATradeOrder,uint256)` (`0x8c4a5df6`) are refused in every interaction of `mtxExchange` and `mtxHybrid`, with tests; the wrapper path was checked (a wrapper is the `o.dex` of an underlying order, but nothing can make it call `restorePulled`). Why: an interaction runs as the DEX, which is `o.dex`, so a submitter's interaction `token.restorePulled(order, fill)` would lower `pulled[h]` of a leg pulled in the same transaction and over-sell it. Cost if wrong: none — the selectors are refused as `mtxTrade` is. Task T4.
Change (2026-10-30): controller ruling, owner may override — **the size baseline is ratcheted for the six token kinds too, in T9** (not only for `SCaaSDex`). What: `size-baseline.json` gets `SCaaSDex` 27,252 B and the runtime and init sizes of the six token kinds that grew by about 0.7–0.8 KB with `restorePulled` (e.g. `NormalToken` 38,100 → 38,916; `WrappedPqzToken` 61,046 → 61,748 runtime), all under the ceiling 65,536 B. Why: the ceiling is 65,536 B and the baseline is a ratchet (owner 2026-10-21); no micro-optimisation (owner 2026-10-11 / 2026-10-21). Cost if wrong: the size gate stays red until T9, nothing else. Task T9.
Change (2026-10-30): controller ruling, owner may override — **spec section 4.2 step 6's sentence "the token cannot be told to give capacity back" is amended in T16** with the docs, to the `restorePulled` rule above (the owner's follow-up of the same day post-dates it); the DEX spec also gets the matching amendments of its executor and out-of-gas lines (CTR-DEX-29, CTR-DEX-28). Cost if wrong: one stale spec line until then. Task: dex-round T16.
Change (2026-10-30): controller ruling, owner may override — **sequencing in one worktree**: the clientkeys task (T14) and the next contract task never commit in the `dex-round` worktree at the same time (one worktree, one index); a short wait is the cost if wrong. Also: the new anvil e2e of T13 uses its own gateway port 18653 (anvil 18652) — the plan's fixed 18651 collided with the existing DEX e2e (a plan defect found at the review); cost if wrong: none. Task: dex-round T13 fix.
Change (2026-10-30): controller calls of the plan (**plan decisions, owner may override**; recorded by T16), each: what / why / cost if wrong.
(1) *Legacy copies*: the pre-round `src/trade/TradeLib.sol`, `src/dex/SCaaSDex.sol`, `src/dex/ISCaaSDex.sol` and the floor tests (`test_minFillPpm_halvingEncodesIt`, `test_minFill_oddAmountRoundsTheHalfUp`) are copied to `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/dex-round/` (not built), with a line in `legacy/README.md` — superseded code is backed up, never deleted (owner); cost if wrong: a few unbuilt files (task Setup).
(2) *Test files*: new suites `test/v2/DexHybrid.t.sol`, `DexBatch.t.sol`, `DexModes.t.sol`, `UniswapExecutor.t.sol`, `DexInvariant.t.sol`, `test/fork/UniswapFork.t.sol`, mocks in `test/helpers/MockUniswap.sol`, the floor cases edited in place; cost if wrong: a rename.
(3) *One self-call helper*: `mtxSettle` and `mtxExchangeBatch` share one private loop helper (self-call, 256-byte reason copy, starvation re-raise); `mtxSettle`'s behaviour is unchanged and its tests are the check; cost if wrong: a few duplicated lines (the review found the ~6-line loop repeated in both).
(4) *Internal helpers take `submitter`*: `_exchangeIn`, `_exchangeOut`, `_payExchange` get a `submitter` parameter instead of reading `msg.sender` (needed by `exchangeOne`); stack pressure goes into a memory struct, never `via_ir` (it would move every CREATE2-derived vector); cost if wrong: a refactor.
(5) *The unreachable price check*: the `PriceLimit` check on the taker's sold part is implied by the token's check at the pull, so it is one internal function `_takerSoldCheck` and its case is tested through a harness (`test/helpers/HybridHarness.sol`, a `SCaaSDex` subclass); cost if wrong: one harness file.
(6) *Junk-fill policy scope*: the node builds NODE-DEX-15's per-leg `min_base_amount` rule and the `min_fill` bucket; the clause "no settlement worth less than its gas" needs plan pricing and stays SPECIFIED for the `OrderRouter` (step 6); cost if wrong: see NODE-DEX-15.
(7) *No executor deploy script*: none of our chains has Uniswap; `UniswapExecutor` is deployed by the fork test only; a deploy script and the `uniswap_executor` deployment key come with the first chain that has Uniswap; cost if wrong: a script written later.
(8) *The fork test is outside the gate runner*: it needs an RPC; the controller runs it once and commits the log (block and outcome, no URL); forge invariant tests print `[PASS] invariant_…` without `(`, so a reviewer checks them in the forge log, not the `named-tests` gate; cost if wrong: a manual step.
(9) *Hybrid internals*: steps 2–7 of the hybrid reuse the exchange path's snapshot / pull / route / distribute / conservation code with the makers' floors computed on chain; the excess of the sell token is not distributed — it is the unsold remainder; cost if wrong: a longer code path to audit.
Change (2026-11-11, Fable review B P2-1; controller call under the owner's leave; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-fix-contracts`, UNAUDITED): **the restore is the refund.** What: the token's `restorePulled` moves `amount` from `o.dex` back to `o.from` after lowering `pulled[h]` (`_restorePulledBody`: `_uaMove(pad(o.dex), o.from, amount)`); `SCaaSDex._hybridOut` no longer adds a SCaaS taker's restored leftover to its own refund (an IOC or outside-token taker is still refunded by the DEX), so the taker's `UAExchangeLegSettled.refund` leaves it out and the token's `PullRestored(h, amount)` reports it. Why: with a restore that moved nothing, a hostile `o.dex` looping pull → restore → pull took more than the signed `amount` (CTR-DEX-19's bound). Options: a per-transaction gross counter (refused: `inTx` is transient and the loop also runs across transactions) or tokens and capacity together. Cost if wrong: a dex that spent the pulled tokens can no longer restore (it reverts, as it should). Tests: `test_restorePulled_hostileLoopBounded` (five loops, the signer loses `amount`), `test_restorePulled_needsTheTokensBack`; `test_restorePulled_boundedByThisTxPull`, `test_restorePulled_uaOrder` follow.
Change (2026-10-30): controller resolution at the T8 review — **Path B never rests**: the DEX spec says fill-or-kill, IOC and Path B are whole (one settlement), so the invariant suite's handlers build a Path B order as one-shot, not as a resting order refilled later; cost if wrong: the invariant campaign does not cover a Path B order across settlements (it cannot exist).
Change (2026-10-30): **gates of the round** — owner 2026-10-25 ("full gate only for core"): only the affected steps ran, through the runner `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-10-30-dex-round-gates.sh` (logs `runs/2026-10-30-dex-round-<step>.txt`): forge (the whole suite) at the committed set `n2304-kmax4096` only, so the gas pins were checked at that set only (DX21), the size gate, `docs_check`, `cargo clippy` + `cargo test` of `scaas-node`, its anvil e2e, clientkeys `npm test`, and the named-tests guard; no pqz-core gate, because no core or set parameter changes. Task T17 (after main was merged in): forge 1,681 passed / 0 failed / 11 skipped, sizes 0 errors, cargo 460 passed / 0 failed (the Algorand artefacts built once in the worktree), anvil e2e 6 passed, clientkeys 155 tests (153 passed, 2 skipped), named-tests 128 names / 0 problems; T17 also fixed UADeploy `test_C5_1`, which now prices `SCaaSDex` at its baseline size (broken since T9 added the entry). Final fix wave (after the allowance-reset fix and main merged in again): forge 1,682 passed / 0 failed / 11 skipped, sizes 0 errors, docs 0 errors, cargo 460 passed / 0 failed, anvil e2e 6 passed, clientkeys 155 tests (153 passed, 2 skipped), named-tests 129 names / 0 problems; every step rc 0. With it the controller's earlier ruling "main is brought into `dex-round` by merge, never rebase" (made so that cited branch hashes stay valid) is **withdrawn** as moot: the branch may be merged with or rebased onto main. Who: owner (the withdrawn ruling was the controller's). Status: current (no branch hashes); withdrawn (merge only). Task: dex-round T16 fix.
Change (2026-10-30): controller ruling, owner may override — **T17's task review is folded into the T18 whole-branch review** (its focus names the merge resolution, the gate runner and the `test_C5_1` fix): the whole-branch reviewer reads the same diff. Cost if wrong: none beyond one combined pass. Status: done. Task: dex-round T17 / T18.

### CTR-DEX-28 — mtxExchangeBatch: independent plans in one transaction, a failing plan isolated; InteractionFailed wraps a failing interaction
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-28 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner 2026-10-29 (research note `research/dex-matching-modes.md` §7.2, §8.3): a batch now, not later. Decisions, each with options, choice, cost if wrong and who:
- **Batch now.** Options: later or now. Choice: now, in the same round as `mtxHybrid` and the mode 3 / 4 tests: one self-call per plan, a failing plan emits `ExchangeFailed(ref, reason)` (at most 256 bytes of the plan's revert data), the starvation errors (`SigCheckGasStarved`, `UAVerifyGas`) are re-raised whole as in `mtxSettle`, `NothingSettled` when no plan succeeds. Who: owner 2026-10-29. Status: built.
- **Form** (owner-confirmed 2026-10-30). Options: path (a) only or path (a) and (b) items; parallel arrays or an item struct. Choice: path (a) only, parallel arrays `mtxExchangeBatch(ExchangePlan[] ps, Interaction[][] xs) returns (bool[] ok)` (the owner's sketch), `LengthMismatch` on unequal lengths; no `mtxHybridBatch` and no executor items (add when the planner shows the need). Cost if wrong: one transaction per executor plan or hybrid until then. Status: built.
- **A failing interaction** (owner-confirmed 2026-10-30). Options: bubble its revert data (as built) or wrap it. Choice: wrap — every path (a) entry reverts `InteractionFailed(uint256 index, address target, bytes reason)` with at most 256 bytes of the target's revert data and copies no return data on success. Needed so that a hostile target cannot forge `SigCheckGasStarved` / `UAVerifyGas` and take a whole batch down, and so a returnbomb cannot drain a plan's frame. It changes CTR-DEX-20 step (4)'s wording "a failure reverts with its data". Cost if wrong: debugging reads one more ABI layer. Status: built.
- **EIP-7702 and relaying.** The batch follows owner rulings D1–D5 of 2026-10-30 as the other entries do (no new guard; the submitter is an open role); it is a relayer entry over user signatures with the fee possibly 0; nothing assumes gas price 0 or a chain block limit (the bound is EIP-7825). Who: owner rulings 2026-10-30, 2026-10-20, 2026-10-21.
**Cost if wrong.** Without the batch a relayer sends one transaction per plan; without the wrap one hostile target ruins a batch. Gas: batch overhead 7,298 per plan (measured), bounded by EIP-7825 per transaction; a gas-burning target fails its own plan and later plans may run out of gas at the relayer's cost, simulated first.
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-29 / 2026-10-30; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-dex-round-design.md` (section 0 rows), rows on the batch, its form and the failing interaction.
Change (2026-10-30): **built** (DEX round, branch `dex-round`, task T2 `InteractionFailed`, task T5 the batch with `exchangeOne` and `ExchangeFailed`; the T4 review fixes m1 / m2 were made in task T5 and belong to CTR-DEX-27): `DexBatch.t.sol` 12 tests, four `InteractionFailed` tests in `DexExchange.t.sol`; `SCaaSDex` 27,252 B after the batch (+1,448).
Change (2026-10-30): a review minor of the batch (T5), resolved by wording and a node fix — a gas-burning target inside a later plan reads `InteractionFailed(i, target, "")`, not an empty `ExchangeFailed` reason, so the spec's section 5 and NODE-DEX-04 are amended: the node's classifier (`revert_name` → `guard::reason_is_out_of_gas`; T12, T12 fix) reads both as `out_of_gas`; the `ExchangeFailed` watcher is SPECIFIED. Controller call, owner may override; cost if wrong: an out-of-gas plan shown as a failure with a reason.
Change (2026-10-30): final review fix, controller (owner may override) — **the allowance reset after a path (a) route is a capped token call that drops the target's revert data** (W-O, as `_send`). What: `_route` sets every allowance an `approve` interaction granted back to 0 by `TokenCall.ok(token, approve(spender, 0))` (at most `TOKEN_GAS`, at most one word of return data) and on failure `_tokenFailed` (empty data, or `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)`), instead of OZ `forceApprove`, which re-reverted with the target's whole revert data. Why: a target that grants `approve(x, n > 0)` and reverts `approve(x, 0)` with the bytes of `SigCheckGasStarved` made `exchangeOne` revert with that selector, which `mtxExchangeBatch` re-raises, so one plan took the whole batch down (final review part A, important finding 1; pre-existing on main, where `mtxExchange` is one plan). The other token calls of the exchange, hybrid and batch paths were checked: `_send`, `_bal` and the puller were already capped and data-dropping; an `approve` interaction (the approve-up before the route) is wrapped `InteractionFailed`; the calls into SCaaS tokens (`mtxTrade`, `uaTrade`, `restorePulled`, `transferToUA`, the digests) are factory-made code that may raise the starvation errors. Test `test_batch_resetForgesStarvation_onlyThatPlan` (only that plan fails, `ExchangeFailed(ref, SafeERC20FailedOperation(target))`, the other settles; before the fix the whole batch reverted `SigCheckGasStarved(1, 2)`). An honest token sees the same call (`forceApprove` with value 0 is one `approve(spender, 0)`). `SCaaSDex` 27,252 → 26,967 B runtime (size baseline ratcheted); `dex_order_kat.json` regenerated (17 CREATE2-derived keys moved, 22 keys). Cost if wrong: a reset failure reads `SafeERC20FailedOperation(token)` instead of the token's own error. Status: done. Task: dex-round final fix wave.

### CTR-DEX-29 — UniswapExecutor, the reference executor, and the opt-in Uniswap fork test
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-29 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Controller proposals (owner may override), each with options, choice and cost if wrong:
- **Reference executor.** Options: none, one per Uniswap version, or one contract. Choice: one contract, `UniswapExecutor`: v3 pool callback and v4 `unlock` hops, exact-input, the whole balance of a hop's input token spent, holds nothing after a call, callable only by its DEX, no admin, no upgrade; v2 and v3 routers stay on path (a); not deployed on 7622 (no Uniswap there). Cost if wrong: more hop kinds (flash swaps, solver inventory) are later executors. Status: built (5,536 B runtime).
- **Uniswap fork test.** Options: CI against a public RPC, opt-in by an environment URL, or a local Uniswap compiled from source. Choice: opt-in — Ethereum mainnet forked at a block pinned in the test (`FORK_BLOCK = 22,000,000`), the RPC URL only from `SCAAS_FORK_RPC_URL` (never in the repo, a commit or a run log), skipped when unset, CI never runs it, foundry's fork cache makes re-runs offline. Real Uniswap bytecode is the point of the test and CI cannot depend on a paid RPC (owner constraint: no paid RPC in CI, no secrets). Cost if wrong: CI never touches real Uniswap; the mocks and the executor's unit tests stay the CI coverage. Status: built; run once 2026-10-30, 9 of 9 passed.
**Cost if wrong.** As listed per decision.
**Source.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-dex-round-design.md` (section 0 rows), rows on the reference executor and the fork test.
Change (2026-10-30): **built** (task T7 the executor and its 12 unit tests, task T10 the fork test and its run log `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-10-30-dex-round-fork.txt`).
Change (2026-10-30): controller ruling, owner may override — **the executor returns unspent `tokensOut` (the taker's unsold sell token among them) to its DEX** instead of requiring them at zero. What: at the end of `exchangeCallback` the executor sends its whole balance of each `tokensIn` and any unspent balance of each `tokensOut` to the DEX, and raises `Leftover(token)` only for intermediate hop tokens, so it ends at 0 in every token; the DEX spec's section 9 sentence "every `tokensOut` balance must be zero (`Leftover`)" is amended accordingly in T16. Why: the owner's hybrid rule of 2026-10-30 (the taker's unsold remainder is refunded) post-dates that sentence, and `test_hybrid_refund_viaExecutor` requires the unsold sell token to come back; the DEX's conservation check stays the guard. Cost if wrong: a two-line revert in the executor. Task T7; the review accepted it.
Change (2026-10-30): owner 2026-10-30 — **the fork RPC is the public archive endpoint dRPC** (no key, archive state confirmed at block 21,800,000; its URL is not written here), passed only as `SCAAS_FORK_RPC_URL` in the controller's run command and never written to a repo file, commit or log; the run log records the block and the outcome only. Cost if wrong: a re-run needs another archive endpoint (any that serves the pinned block works). Run: 9 passed, 0 failed, rc 0, log committed in T10 run log.

### CTR-DEX-30 — Liquidity: one signed LiquidityOrder through the DEX, outcomes only
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-30 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A SCaaS token refuses `approve` from an EOA or a UA (CTR-TOK-01, CTR-UA-27), so no AMM router can pull a deposit.
Owner rulings 2026-11-10 (the liquidity spec §2): reuse the DEX's machinery, no adapter per AMM (R1); a signed typed
`LiquidityOrder` in the DEX's domain, the UA form (R2); SCaaS inputs pulled by the token's new DEX-only `mtxLiquidityPull`
in module T of every kind, a new token release (R3, R9, Q2 = yes), outside inputs and positions by the `DexPuller`; outcome
checks only (R4); withdraw as an order that gives the LP or the position (R5); the body in a new DEX module (R6); module
names by domain, `SCaaSDexLiquidityModule` and `SCaaSDexD` renamed `SCaaSDexGovernanceModule` (R7); no `mtxLiquidityVia`
yet (R10, Q3 = not now). Controller choices the owner may override: C1 the DEX's domain, every verifier recomputes `h`; C2
the UA purpose `trade`; C3 the minimum net of the fee, measured at the DEX and again at the recipient; C4 the fee on ERC-20
outputs only; C5 cancel by lane and expiry only; C6 kinds from the DEX's record; C7 the puller pulls a position by its
unchanged `pull`; C8 the rule ids; C9 at most eight inputs, outputs and extra tokens; C10 no `RelayFeeRouter` wrap in this
round (relayed directly at its signed relayer / fee, fee 0 included). Fable's review (approve with fixes) and re-check
(approve) are applied (spec §19, §19.1). Build choice (ua-mtx-liquidity): a token without code at the snapshot holds 0
(the plan's own interaction creates a v2 pair).
**Cost if wrong.** A new token release and DEX release; nothing deployed is upgraded, all chains test-only.
**Source.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-dex-liquidity.md`.
Change (2026-11-10): **built** on branch `ua-mtx-liquidity` (UNAUDITED): `SCaaSDexLiquidityModule`, `SCaaSDexCore`,
`LiquidityLib`, `mtxLiquidityPull` on the twelve kinds, `test/liquidity/`, `liquidity_kat.json`, `clientkeys`, the node row.
Change (2026-11-10, owner): the size stop of spec §9.3 (`SCaaSDex` 33,628 B, over its 33,594 B margin by 34 B) is resolved by
lever (a) (the liquidity views already in the module: 0 B) then lever (b): `mtxCancelOrders`, `mtxInvalidateNonces` and their
digest views move into the liquidity module behind typed stubs. Measured: `SCaaSDex` 32,809 B, the module 19,055 B, module T
17,418-20,219 B per kind, module A +27 B, the faces +154-181 B; `size-baseline.json` moved in its own commit. Status: done.

### CTR-DEX-31 — A received position is bound by a signed, listed reader
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: contracts/dex.md#CTR-DEX-31 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Ownership of an ERC-721 position proves who holds it, not what it holds: a hostile submitter can mint the deposit
into its own position and hand over dust. Owner 2026-11-10, Q1 = A (R8): a signed and listed read-only reader per
position-manager family binds the signed pool, range and minimum liquidity; `exchangeTarget` carries the reader role beside
the target and executor roles (Fable P3: safe, no separate map now).
**Cost if wrong.** A reader per family (≈ 40 lines of views); a wrong reader fails closed (`PositionMismatch`).
**Source.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-dex-liquidity.md` §7.

### CTR-DEX-80 — Fill-or-kill two-leg MetaTxDex settlement
- old: R3 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-DEX-01, NODE-DEX-01, INT-ERP-12

**What it said.** The first design settled two `MetaTxDex` legs fill-or-kill.

### CTR-DEX-81 — DEX fee on received side rounds down
- old: RS5-6(dex-fee) · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-DEX-11
