### CTR-ZTH-94 — Zether token bodies run in `ZetherLib` / `ZetherWrappedLib`
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-03 · normative: contracts/zether.md#CTR-ZTH-94 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner ruling 2026-11-03: move the Zether token function bodies into the existing libraries, shared code into `ZetherLib`,
wrapped-only code into `ZetherWrappedLib`. No new library (no `ZetherOpsLib`). Goal: smaller `NormalZetherToken` and
`WrappedZetherToken` deploy transactions, so that they deploy on public chains (ETH about 60 M gas per block, BSC about 70 M) under
EIP-8037 (a transaction fits only if regular + state gas fits the block; about 1,606 gas per byte of code), and further below the
64 KiB ceiling (EIP-7954). Built on branch `zether-lib`, commit `1c8b57f3` (status: built, not merged; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands):
the transfer, single and unshield ops, their signed and `ua*` forms and the typehashes of those forms run in `ZetherLib`; the
unshield-unwrap op and its signed forms in `ZetherWrappedLib`; `NormalZetherToken`'s init path and `mtxSelectors()` table in
`ZetherLib` (size lever 1, as C3 did on the wrapped kind). A moved entry keeps its declaration on the token and hands the library
its own calldata (no Zether struct coder stays in the token); `mtxShield`, `mtxWrapShield`, the roll-overs and the views stay.
No selector, ABI, typehash, event, error or storage slot changes; `ZetherLib` keeps no DELEGATECALL, `ZetherWrappedLib` two.
**Figures.** Runtime (init): `NormalZetherToken` 52,874 → 47,470 B (56,446 → 51,042), `WrappedZetherToken` 62,305 → 58,407 B
(65,887 → 61,986); `ZetherLib` 19,690 → 26,131 B (now a `size-baseline.json` entry, over EIP-170), `ZetherWrappedLib` 4,958 →
11,471 B. Deploy transaction, regular + state gas: `NormalZetherToken` 84.9 M → 76.3 M, `WrappedZetherToken` 100.0 M → 93.7 M,
so neither fits a 60 M or 70 M block yet (about 37.3 KB and 43.5 KB of runtime fit; the base kinds are 37,487 B and 48,278 B);
`ZetherLib` 41.9 M and `ZetherWrappedLib` 18.5 M fit both. Gas per call against main (forge, deterministic): the direct transfers
−0.3 K to −4.6 K (one calldata copy instead of an ABI encode), `mtxUnshield` +0.1 K to +0.2 K; the signed and `ua*` forms cost
between +1.0 K and +1.9 K at the median, at most +17.0 K (`mtxConfidentialTransferCompact` signed at `M = 8`, 26.1 M gas: the library builds the op call and
the token reads it back); `mtxUnshieldUnwrap` / `uaUnshieldUnwrap` signed +1.0 K median; `NormalZetherToken.initialize` +5.7 K once
per clone; `mtxSelectors()` +13.2 K, an `eth_call`. No gas pin and no KAT moved.
**Why.** The bodies were already thin calls into `ZetherLib`; what the token still carried per op was the ABI encoding of its
calldata structs (to call the library and to build a signed entry's struct words and op call). Forwarding the calldata removes
those coders from both kinds; the decoders of the entries' own arguments stay, since the ABI is the token's.
**Cost if wrong.** A library split can change storage, `this`, `msg.sender`, return data or the guard: the libraries run by
DELEGATECALL in the token's context as before, write only the token's namespaces, call nothing back, and every existing test
passes unchanged. On malformed calldata only, a `ZetherMulti` offset aimed at a word the token appends reads that public word
(`test_nestedOffsetReadsAnAppendedWord`).
**Source.** Owner ruling 2026-11-03; measurements and the plan in [research/zether-library-split.md](research/zether-library-split.md).

## 24. Contracts — Universal Account

### CTR-UA-01 — Refuse BLS keys and signatures at infinity
- old: RS2-18 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-01 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** BLS keys and signatures at infinity make the pairing trivial; refusing them prevents a fake BLS custody that lets `x` alone spend.
**Cost if wrong.** Accepting infinity lets anyone pass a BLS check.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-03-zether-design.md:618`

### CTR-UA-02 — UA is a key-derived identifier, not a contract
- old: R290 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-02 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A UA is an identifier derived from key data, like an EOA for every scheme: free, deterministic, the same on every chain, with nothing to deploy.
**Cost if wrong.** A contract per account costs a deploy per user per chain and is upgradeable state.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:93`

### CTR-UA-03 — 32-byte kind-tagged ids in canonical form
- old: R291 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** 32-byte kind-tagged ids never collide with 20-byte native ids; a 20-byte truncation would allow a 2^80 grind between an EOA and a multisig policy.
**Cost if wrong.** 12 more calldata bytes per id (192 gas).
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:100`

### CTR-UA-04 — keccak256 for ids in every family
- old: R292 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-04 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One hash (keccak256) with native support in every family gives the same id on every chain.
**Cost if wrong.** Different hashes per family would give different ids for one key.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:113`

### CTR-UA-05 — Fixed kind table per registry generation
- old: R293 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The kind table is fixed per registry generation; a mutable table would be an admin key over every account.
**Cost if wrong.** New schemes wait for a new generation and new token implementations.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:117`
Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — **gen 1 starving behind gen 2 is `UAVerifyGas`, never a verdict** (the second code review, on-chain part (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-sol`; triage W-A…W-S in `pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, row W-M; report `V2-claude-ua-account-wallet.md` V2-5). `_viaPredecessor` / `_zetherViaPredecessor` turned every gen-1 revert except a 4-byte `UAVerifyGas` into `false`, so gen 1 running out of gas before its own hold (its pre-hold work: record SLOAD, `abi.decode(auth)`, `uaOf` / `uaMessage` keccaks, `SSTORE2.read`) came back `UAUnauthorized`: fail-closed, but a relayer is told "bad signature" instead of "more gas" (T-AUTH-4). Now both read `g = gasleft()` before the call and also re-raise `UAVerifyGas` for a revert with no data while `gasleft() < g / 63` (gen 1 used up all it was given, i.e. ran out of gas; any other gen-1 revert returns its unused gas and stays a failed check). Deviation from the triage's wording ("a minimum-gas guard before the hand-off"): a constant guard must cover gen 1's pre-hold work, which grows with the caller's `auth` (an `msig` with PQ member signatures), so no constant is sound; the check after the call needs none. Edge: an `auth` whose decoding alone exceeds the gas supplied reads `UAVerifyGas` too (still fail-closed). Tests: `test_W_M_gen1OutOfGas_isUAVerifyGas_aCheapRevertIsAVerdict` (a gen 1 that burns all its gas behind gen 2: `UAVerifyGas` on both hand-offs, `UAUnauthorized` on the old code; a gen 1 that reverts at once with no data stays `UAUnauthorized`); `test_W_M_gen1StarvedBeforeItsHold_isUAVerifyGas` (a 5 k–300 k gas sweep with the real p256 path never yields `UAUnauthorized`; it passes on the old code too: there the gas gen 2 keeps is too little to finish any verdict, so the misclassification needs a gen 1 whose pre-hold work is large, e.g. a big `auth`). Deployed bytecode: `UARegistry` (only a gen 2 takes the path; none is deployed). Status: **done** (`17c72d62`).

### CTR-UA-06 — Native kinds unregistered; derived kinds register first
- old: R294 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-06 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-17): owner — kinds are the same on every chain, so **every derived kind is registrable on every chain whose registry has its verifier, also where the key is a native account**; the native key's registered id is the derived `keccak256(TAG(kind) ‖ key_data)`, separate from its native id and the same on every chain (`ed25519` 0x0102 no longer "native elsewhere"). New derived kind **`secp256k1` 0x0108** (owner 2026-10-17, controller design): `x ‖ y` (64), ECDSA over the 32-byte `ua_msg`, sig `r ‖ s ‖ v`, low-s, `v ∈ {27, 28}`, keyHash group `secp256k1` over x (one key, one purpose with `bip340` / MuSig2 / FROST), `Secp256k1Verifier` (cap 50 k), enabled on every chain's gen-1 registry; registry slot 19; vectors appended (kinds.json, signatures.json, metatx3.json, uatrade_kat.json); all six clients. Native kinds stay without records and outside the per-kind list (CTR-UA-29).

**Why.** Native kinds need no registration; derived kinds register once per chain, which is where PoP and one-key-one-purpose are enforced and typos revert.
**Cost if wrong.** One registration per chain (~75 k gas on bn254).
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:125`

### CTR-UA-07 — PoP binds the UA, its attributes and the proof hash (portable, no chain)
- old: R295, UA:Q10, typed-signing:TS-D1, typed-signing:TS-D2, typed-signing:TS-D3, typed-signing:TS-D6, typed-signing:TS-D7 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-07 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Every record field follows from signed data (since UA-8 the PoP covers the UA, the PQZ key hash, the KEM record hash and the PQZ proof hash, with no chain, chain uid or registry; first over chain, registry, UA and `authRef` with the authority co-signing, changed by UA-6 and UA-8 below), so registration is relayable and front-running yields the same record or a revert.
**Cost if wrong.** A field taken from `msg.sender` or left unsigned would turn front-running into capture.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:133`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1407`

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 (U4): the last word of the PoP digest is the PQZ key hash (`0` without a PQZ key), no longer `authRef`; no authority co-signs (purpose `authref` removed). The signer's PoP covers the hash, so a front-runner cannot strip or swap the PQZ key; every other record field is implied by the signed key data. See CTR-UA-30. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-25 / 2026-10-30): **UA-8 — the PoP is portable** (owner 2026-10-25, spec P1/P2; the encoding and the single signed digest are controller calls, owner may override; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua8-portable-registrations.md`). The chain key, `chainUid` and registry address leave the digest; the registry accepts only the new form. (a) **Encoding** (plan decision *Encoding* [UA8-D1], controller call, owner may override): every UA-8 digest is `keccak256` of 32-byte words in `abi.encode` order — `portablePopDigest = keccak256(abi.encode(PURPOSE_POP_V2, ua, pqzKeyHash, kemRecordHash))`, `registrationDigest = keccak256(abi.encode(portablePopDigest, pqzPopHash))`, `kemRecordDigest = keccak256(abi.encode(KEM_RECORD_TAG, ua, uint256(version), keccak256(kemPk)))` (the version a big-endian 32-byte word); for 32-byte fields `abi.encode` equals the concatenation, so every family gets the same bytes from its keccak256. Tags: `PURPOSE_POP_V2 = keccak256("scaas.ua.purpose.pop.v2")`, `PURPOSE_KEM = keccak256("scaas.ua.purpose.kem.v1")`, `KEM_RECORD_TAG = keccak256("scaas.ua.kem-record.v1")` (the spec's formula tag is renamed `KEM_RECORD_TAG` so it is not read as a purpose), and for the PQZ key record `PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY` / `PQZ_KEY_RECORD_TAG` (see CTR-UA-16). Status: decided; built in `UAKinds` and the JS reference, commits `6f72d0ba`, `6572e679`, `e8a6a711` on branch `ua8`. (b) **One signed digest for every kind** (plan decision *One signed digest* [UA8-D2], controller call, owner may override): the signer's `pop` — and each member of a PQ-eligible `msig` — signs `uaMessage(kind, PURPOSE_POP_V2, registrationDigest)`, so one signature covers the UA, both attribute hashes and the proof hash; the spec's P3 text "members sign `uaMessage(MSIG, POP_V2, portablePopDigest)`" is corrected to `registrationDigest` (ruling A1-c1: the bare `portablePopDigest` would leave the proof hash signed by nobody). The `R_REG` proof is over `portablePopDigest` (its message must not contain its own hash). Zether (`0x0141`) and the group kinds keep their schemes, only the message changes; a non-PQ-eligible `msig` keeps the empty `pop`. Status: decided; built in `e1b33079` (`UARegistry`), `f0796dba` (zether-prover). (c) **Native `msig` members are chain-free** (ruling C7, controller call, owner may override; it overrides the plan's first reading "native members stay chain-bound, valid only on their own registry"): a code-less EOA member signs the EIP-191 `personal_sign` of `memberDigest` for the three portable purposes only (`pop` v2, `kem`, `pqz-key`; 65-byte `r ‖ s ‖ v`, low-s), a member with code (EIP-7702 delegate, contract wallet) answers ERC-1271 over the same digest (portable only where that wallet exists with the same behaviour), every other purpose stays EIP-712 `UAAuth` (CTR-UA-24, CTR-MTX-14) — why: the owner's "a UA does not depend on the chain" and the spec's P3; cost if wrong: wallets show a `personal_sign` prompt instead of a typed-data view for the registration. Status: decided; built in `6f72d0ba`, `6572e679` (vectors), `e1b33079` (`_sigOk` restricts the rule to the portable purposes), clients `f2769577`, `4d35490b`, `9e1f2357`, `844933cc`; the `_sigOk` purpose guard that restricts the rule to the portable purposes came in `fd4719d2` (ruling A5-m3; `e1b33079` had no guard).

Change (2026-10-30): **owner ruling R-7702 — EIP-7702 members on the portable path follow CTR-UA-24 — SUPERSEDED the same day by owner ruling D1 (next change)** (owner 2026-10-30, final review of UA-8, part 2 O3 / part 1 owner item 4). A native `msig` member with code, signing for a portable purpose (`pop` v2, `kem`, `pqz-key`), is checked like `_native`: the EIP-7702 designator ⇒ the root key's ECDSA over the `personal_sign` hash of `memberDigest` first, then ERC-1271 through the delegate; other code ⇒ ERC-1271 only. It supersedes controller ruling A5-m m2 (built in A5: any code ⇒ ERC-1271 only), under which a member delegated on one chain and not on another had a `pop` that was not portable between them. Why: CTR-UA-24 says the base key of a 7702 account stays root wherever a native id is verified, `msig` members included; the portable path should not be the one exception. Cost if wrong: none for security (the root key controls the account at protocol level anyway); one more branch in `_nativePortable`. Status: superseded by D1 (below); built in `cc965914`, replaced in `0c113cfc` (no history rewritten).

Change (2026-10-30): **owner ruling D1 — a 7702 designator account signs by its own key only, never ERC-1271** (owner 2026-10-30, after the 2026-10-29 EIP-7702 hot-wallet drain: "an EOA must really sign — no delegation at all; an EOA must not run code"; EIP-7702 rulings D1–D5, audit `research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md`). In the registry, on both native paths (`_native` for `requireAuthorized`, `_nativePortable` for an `msig` native member signing `pop` v2, `kem` or `pqz-key`; one `_byCode`): no code or the EIP-7702 designator `0xef0100 ‖ delegate` ⇒ ECDSA by the account's own key only (over `uaAuthDigest`, resp. the `personal_sign` hash of `memberDigest`), never ERC-1271 through the delegate; other code ⇒ ERC-1271 only. It supersedes ruling R-7702 (designator: root-key ECDSA first, then ERC-1271), the 2026-10-28 rule for the registry, and, like R-7702, controller ruling A5-m m2 (any code ⇒ ERC-1271 only), so a member delegated on one chain and not on another still signs one portable `pop`. Why: a delegate's ERC-1271 lets whatever code the account is delegated to — a sweeper delegate after one phishing signature — forge every registry authorization of the account. Cost if wrong: a delegated wallet's session keys or passkeys cannot sign for a registry id; its base key still can. Status: decided (owner); built on `ua8`: `cc965914` (R-7702) → `0c113cfc` (portable path, D1) → `128becef` (`requireAuthorized`, shared `_byCode`). The address path (`SigCheck.isValid`, `MetaTxBase`, `MtxPipelineLib`'s native `from`, `RelayFeeRouter`, the DEX and the node's DEX venue `valid_sig`, clientkeys `signDigest`) followed on branch `no7702` (`5ddc577d`..`dad611dc`; CTR-UA-24 change of 2026-10-30, rulings D1–D5).

Change (2026-10-31, owner decisions 2 and 8 of 2026-10-31, exact strings controller call, owner may override; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`, decisions [TS-D1], [TS-D2], [TS-D3], [TS-D6], [TS-D7]): **the portable records are typed EIP-712 structs.** Domain `EIP712Domain(string name,string version)` = (`"SCaaS UA Portable"`, `"1"`), no chain id, no verifying contract, no salt, separator `DS_P = 0x9a2c390d4dc940ccdb5fa6b21e673e87159bdd99aeef22ea791bcea9efc64ca1`. Structs `UAKemRecord(bytes32 ua,uint64 version,uint8 scheme,bytes32 kemPkHash)`, `UAPortableRecord(bytes32 ua,uint16 kind,bytes32 pqzKeyHash,UAKemRecord kem)`, `UARegistration(UAPortableRecord record,bytes32 pqzPopHash)`, `UAPqzKey(bytes32 ua,bytes32 pqzKeyHash)`, `UAPqzKeyRecord(UAPqzKey key,bytes32 pqzPopHash)`, typehashes pinned in accounts.md CTR-UA-07 and in every library; `typed(s) = keccak256(0x1901 ‖ DS_P ‖ hashStruct(s))`. Only `UAPortableRecord` carries `kind`, the registering kind, as `uint16` (no string, no parameter-set field; the name comes from `kindName`, CTR-UA-35). The `ua_msg` wrapper and the purpose tags are kept and not bumped (test-only chains: no old signature can verify under the new digests): `pop` signs `uaMessage(kind, PURPOSE_POP_V2, typed(UARegistration{record, pqzPopHash}))`, `R_REG` proves over `uaMessage(0x0142, PURPOSE_POP_V2, typed(record))`, the Zether PoP over the `0x0141` registration with no PQZ key and the zero KEM record. "No KEM record" is `UAKemRecord{ua, 0, 0, 0}` [TS-D2], replacing `kemRecordHash = 0`. It **supersedes the encoding of decision (a) of the 2026-10-25 / 2026-10-30 change** ([UA8-D1]: `abi.encode` of words under `KEM_RECORD_TAG` / `PQZ_KEY_RECORD_TAG`, tags and raw digests now in `legacy/typed-signing/`) **and ruling C7's `personal_sign`** in decision (c) (CTR-UA-33, change of this date). Views [TS-D6]: `portableDomainSeparator`, `portableRecordDigest(ua, kind, pqzKeyHash, kemRecordHash)`, `kemRecordHash(ua, version, kem)`, `registrationDigest(ua, kind, pqzKeyHash, kemRecordHash, pqzPopHash)`, `kemRecordDigest(ua, version, kem)`, `pqzKeyDigest(ua, pqzKeyHash)`, `pqzKeyRecordDigest(ua, pqzKeyHash, pqzPopHash)`. Vectors [TS-D7]: `portable.json` (version 2, `typed` section, `typedData` per row), `signatures.json`, `pq_signatures.json`, `structures.json`, `groups.json`, `r33_keys.json` regenerated, pre-round copies in `legacy/typed-signing/`; the `pqzPop` values stay fillers, the real `R_REG` proofs are made at run time by `e2e.py`, and `pqz-core` is unchanged (the message stays 32 bytes). Why: a wallet shows a typed record's fields, where `personal_sign` of a hash shows nothing the user can check (CTR-MTX-14), and a record stays chain-free with a domain of only `name` and `version`. Cost if wrong: a hardware wallet that refuses a domain without `chainId` cannot sign a record (no Ledger / Trezor test first, owner decision 3); every family hashes the same words, so a later change of a struct regenerates every vector. Status: built in typed-signing P1, P2, P3, P4, P6, P7, P8 (`UAKinds`, `UARegistry`, clientkeys, ua-rs, the wrappers, the reproducers, zether-prover, `e2e.py`); Soroban typed-signing P5, NET-SOR-17.

### CTR-UA-08 — Rogue-key defence chosen per aggregate kind
- old: R296, UA:Q3 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-08 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Each aggregate kind uses its native rogue-key defence, checked on chain: per-member PoP for `msig`, KeyAgg for MuSig2, DKG PoKs for FROST.
**Cost if wrong.** Off-chain facts (share distribution, distinct parties) stay attestation-only and must be shown as such.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:148`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1391`

### CTR-UA-09 — Structures commit to members; verification goes two levels
- old: R297 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Structures commit to sorted members and nest one level, which bounds gas and avoids cycles.
**Cost if wrong.** Two-level governance uses `SmartKeyAccount` or Safe as a member.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:159`

Change (2026-11-02, **owner ruling**, CTR-UA-38): an `msig` may hold `msig` members, verification goes two levels only; "a member may not itself be a structure" goes. MuSig2 and FROST stay members. Bounded gas stays, and `SmartKeyAccount` or Safe as a member stays as another way.

### CTR-UA-10 — One key one purpose: registry, tags, EOAs
- old: R298(2-3-4) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-10 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — new purpose `trade` (`scaas.ua.purpose.trade.v1`) for the `UATradeOrder` digest, the `CancelOrder` digest over a UA order hash and the `UAInvalidateNonces` digest (CTR-DEX-25); the registry is unchanged (it takes any purpose tag), the constant joins `UAKinds` and the six UA libraries. SPECIFIED (UA-5b). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.6, O4, Q4.

**Why.** One key = one purpose in four layers (derivation, registry `keyOwner`, tagged messages, EOA rules) prevents cross-scheme nonce leaks and signing oracles.
**Cost if wrong.** A foreign wallet reusing an EOA key for `bip340` remains undetectable on chain.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:166`

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6: purpose `authref` is removed (with `PURPOSE_AUTHREF`, `scaas.ua.purpose.authref.v1` and the co-sign step); purpose `pop` wraps `popDigest(ua, pqzKeyHash)`; purpose `zether-auth` keeps its bytes and covers only the PQZ `authDigest` (classical Zether spends by its proof alone); purpose `zether-owner` is signed by Schnorr with `x` through `requireAuthorized` (the Zether UA is a SIGNING UA). One key = one purpose gains the PQZ key: it decrypts and proves, the signer's key authorizes. Spec §5. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits 9c2cbc5c; clients 294a4688..8b93de4e).

### CTR-UA-11 — keyHash per curve group, not per kind
- old: R299 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-11 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `keyHash` per curve group makes all kinds over one group share a namespace, so the same key cannot register under two kinds.
**Cost if wrong.** A per-kind keyHash allows the same key under two kinds.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:173`

### CTR-UA-12 — Tagged message for every derived-UA signature
- old: R301 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-12 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Every derived-UA signature is over a tagged message with kind and purpose, so cross-kind and cross-purpose replay die at the hash; native signers sign EIP-712 `UAAuth`, never a raw hash.
**Cost if wrong.** One extra keccak (~60 gas).
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:188`

### CTR-UA-13 — No key rotation inside a UA
- old: R302, RS2-9, UA:Q1 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-13 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A UA is immutable: new key data is a new UA; rotation moves funds. A rotatable policy kind was rejected for v1 because it brings back an admin-like mutable record.
**Cost if wrong.** Membership changes of a corporate `msig` require moving funds.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:202`, `history/specs/2026-10-03-zether-design.md:597`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1385`
Change (2026-11-06, owner rulings O1–O7, R1–R6; group 3g, CTR-UA-42): **the PQZ key attribute is versioned, not rotated in place.** The UA stays immutable (no key rotation inside a UA); its PQZ key gains versions v ≥ 1, each added once and never replacing an earlier one, and the holder migrates its balance to the new version. Status: BUILT on EVM (T51 `3f80f072`, T54).

### CTR-UA-14 — Each function accepts only the kinds it needs
- old: R303, UA:Q4, UA:Q5, UA:Q7 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-14 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — UA parity (CTR-UA-27): the DEX, `MandateWallet` and (when built) regulated tokens open to registered SIGNING UAs through UA forms; the address-typed ABI is unchanged; the earlier plan of a UA-ledger allowance `uaApprove` and an `SCaaSDex` v2 with `bytes32 maker` is dropped (no UA ever grants or holds an allowance, Q2; UA orders are `UATradeOrder`s in the one `SCaaSDex`, CTR-DEX-25/26); the role and admin functions stay as they are, their holders gasless through their own contract account (Q1). Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §6 Q1, Q2.

**Why.** Each function accepts exactly the kinds it needs; native-address functions keep their ABIs and Zether UAs can neither receive on v3 nor sign through `requireAuthorized`.
**Cost if wrong.** UA holders need v3 tokens; deployed v1/v2 clones stay native-only.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:207`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1394`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1396`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1400`

Change (2026-10-20, owner; UA-6 Q1 / U8): **the Zether kind joins the SIGNING set, not MEMBER**: `requireAuthorized` accepts `zether-bls12381` for every purpose (verifier `ZetherSchnorrBls12381Verifier`, `auth.keyData` empty as a stored kind), `_checkTo` accepts it as a UA-ledger receiver, and parity (CTR-UA-27) applies; it stays out of MEMBER (a hot key the wallet holds in software for every balance read) and out of the PQZ holder set. Domain separation unchanged: Schnorr hashes `"SCAAS-ZETHER-SCHNORR-V1" ‖ R ‖ Y ‖ uaMessage(kind, purpose, digest)`, proofs have their own transcripts. The closed sets are now ZETHER = {0x0141}, SIGNING = every derived kind including 0x0141, MEMBER = SIGNING single-key kinds except 0x0141 plus the native kinds; the clauses "Zether `authRef`" and "a Zether UA can never be a v3 receiver nor sign through `requireAuthorized`" are deleted. Status: decided; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits 9c2cbc5c, c4ece459).

### CTR-UA-15 — Registry is monotonic and admin-free
- old: R304 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-15 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A monotonic, admin-free registry lets tokens rely on a record forever and nobody can repoint a key. Rejected: the early shared-registry sketch (`SchnorrPublicKey {x, y}`, `register(x, y, sig)`, `schnorrAddress = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(x, y))`) — corrected to kind-tagged ids, a PoP with domain tag, chain and registry, on-curve and subgroup checks, and no upgrade path.
**Cost if wrong.** A compromised derived key is handled like a compromised EOA: move funds.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:215`
Change (2026-11-06, group 3g, CTR-UA-42): **the later additive writes are per key version.** Old: "a PQZ key to a record without one (`setPqzKey`, once)", "the PQZ proof (`storePqzPop`)". New: `setPqzKey(ua, version, …)` adds each `(ua, version)` once and `storePqzPop(ua, version, pqzPop)` the proof of a version; nothing is changed or removed, so the registry stays monotonic. Status: BUILT on EVM (T51 `3f80f072`, T54).

### CTR-UA-16 — The Zether key is the UA; the PQZ key is an attribute of a PQ signer
- old: R305, UA:Q2 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-16 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Zether kinds bind only the encryption key; authorization is an immutable `authRef` (self, native or SIGNING UA), so spend authority stays separate from decryption.
**Cost if wrong.** `authRef` cannot rotate; a timelocked rotation was rejected.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:219`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1389`

Change (2026-10-20, owner): **the Zether key is the UA and the PQZ key is an attribute of a PQ signer** (CTR-UA-30): the immutable `authRef`, its co-signature and the rule "a BLS UA on the curve of `Y` is refused" are removed; classical Zether spends by its proof alone and signs every other write by Schnorr with `x` (a leaked `x` is a full loss, accepted); a PQZ holder is a single-key `mldsa44` / `mldsa65` / `fndsa512` UA or a PQ-eligible `msig`, the key is given once in `register` and cannot be added later. UA-6 U3, holder set (controller proposal, owner may override): `slhdsa128s` is **not** a direct holder (not in the owner's list; a 7,856-byte signature and a ≈ 1.4 M gas cap on every spend) but counts as PQ weight inside an `msig`, as built; every other kind, Zether included, reverts `UAPqzHolder`. The same-curve-BLS DDH concern becomes a wallet derivation rule (separate trees, already true). Spec §2–§5. Status: decided (owner rulings) / proposal (U3); built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-25 / 2026-10-30): **UA-8 — the PQZ key's proof is optional, the key carries `proven`** (owner 2026-10-25, spec P8 "the balance-key proof is optional"; the rest controller calls, owner may override). (a) **An unproven PQZ key claims nothing** (plan decision *Unproven PQZ key* [UA8-D8]): no `keyOwner` entry and no `0x0142` list entry until the key is proven; the `keyOwner` check (`UAKeyInUse`) and the list append happen when the key becomes proven (`register` with a checked proof, or `storePqzPop` on a registry with the verifier); on a registry without the PQZ verifier (`0x0142` slot empty) a PQZ key is accepted unproven (formerly `UAKindDisabled(0x0142)`). Why: if unproven keys claimed the key, anyone could list a victim's PQZ key without a proof and block the victim. Status: decided; built in `e1b33079`, `b7ba0284`. (b) **PQZ tokens read `proven`** (plan decision *PQZ tokens* [UA8-D9]): new view `pqzKeyOf(ua) → (address ptr, bytes32 pqzPopHash, bool proven)`; `PqzCore._keyPtr` refuses an unproven key with the existing `AccountNotRegistered(ua)` (no new token error); `recordOf` keeps its shape and returns the pointer for unproven keys too (a directory). Status: decided; built in `da0529a9`. (c) **`setPqzKey` and "one PQZ key per UA"** (ruling A1-I1, controller call, owner may override; spec P4/P9 extended): a signed, portable, write-once `setPqzKey(ua, pqzKey, pqzPopHash, sig)` accepted only when the record has no PQZ key, so the PQZ key stays "set once" per chain and copyable — otherwise an old copied registration without the key would permanently deny it on that chain; cost if wrong: one more write path. Client rule, documented: a UA uses **one PQZ key, ever** (a UA that signs two PoPs with different PQZ keys can diverge across chains; a generation-1 registry can still take a different `setPqzKey` key after generation 2 holds one for a gen-1 record, because gen 1 cannot see gen 2 — gen 2 and its tokens use gen 2's key, gen 1's can never be proven). The record: `PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY = keccak256("scaas.ua.purpose.pqz-key.v1")`, `PQZ_KEY_RECORD_TAG`, `pqzKeyDigest = keccak256(abi.encode(PQZ_KEY_RECORD_TAG, ua, pqzKeyHash))`, `pqzKeyRecordDigest = keccak256(abi.encode(pqzKeyDigest, pqzPopHash))`; the signer signs `uaMessage(kind, PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY, pqzKeyRecordDigest)`, the `R_REG` proof is over `uaMessage(0x0142, PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY, pqzKeyDigest)`. Check order `UAUnauthorized` (id not held) → `UAKindDisabled(0x0142)` (gen 2 in front of a gen 1 that enables it) → `UAPqzHolder` → `UAPqzKeySet` → `UAKeyData` / `UAPqzPopHash` → signature (ruling A4-c2). Status: decided; built in `6572e679` (JS), `b7ba0284` (registry), `aa4a22cb`, `844933cc` (clients). (d) **One invariant for generations** (rulings A5-I1 and A6-I1, controller calls, owner may override): a UA's PQZ attachment (the `setPqzKey` key, the proof, `proven`, the `keyOwner` of proven PQZ keys, the `0x0142` list slot) lives in the oldest generation that enables `0x0142`, while the record stays where it was registered; so a gen 2 whose gen 1 enables `0x0142` refuses a PQZ key (`UAKindDisabled(0x0142)`, before the holder check — a non-holder's key gets `UAKindDisabled`, not `UAPqzHolder`), and a gen 2 that enables it in front of a gen 1 that does not accepts `storePqzPop` / `setPqzKey` for a gen-1 record (an exception to "writes go to the generation that holds the record"). Status: decided; built in `fd4719d2`, `a41dc869`. (e) **Empty proofs are refused and written bytes are logged** (ruling A6-m): an empty `pqzPop` in `storePqzPop`, and a proof hash of `keccak256("")` in `register` / `setPqzKey`, revert `UAPqzPopHash`; `UAPqzPopStored`, `UAPqzKeyAdded` (and `UAKemKeySet`) carry the written bytes, and `register`'s stored proof is carried by `UARegistered` (so `UAPqzPopStored` carries empty bytes then, ruling A6-f1). Status: built in `b7ba0284`, `a41dc869`. (f) **Large registrations split** (ruling A11-f and the 60 M statement of rule *No zero-gas assumption*): a registration with the proof in the call is 84.8–109.1 M gas (regular + state, measured), more than a 60 M block, so the client registers without `pqzPop` and calls `storePqzPop` (45.6–57.5 M) when `eth_estimateGas` of the full call is above `gasLimit·1023/1024` or fails (the full path only when the estimate is at most `gasLimit·1023/1024`); status: built in `10214629`, `2a453057`, `5a970b4c` (`e2e.py`); `e2e.py --split` forces the split path so it can run on the SCaaS testnet too (ruling A12-r2, built in `b884d64f`); a relayer compares the estimate with min(block gas limit, its per-transaction cap) (owner ruling R-node 2026-10-30, see CTR-UA-31). **Watch item for fs3 Task 13** (ruling A11-watch): the gas figures use the `rreg` stand-in for the verifier; with the real `R_REG` verify (≈ 3.65 M) `storePqzPop` at `n2816-kmax65536` is ≈ 59.9 M, right at a 60 M block (`n2304-kmax4096` has about 7 M headroom) — measure first on a chain with a 60 M block (the SCaaS testnet, 200 M, takes the full path and is not affected); the gen-2 variant (`storePqzPop` on a gen 2 that enables `0x0142` for a gen-1 record, 57,729,122 with the stand-in) is ≈ 60.1 M, above a 60 M block (final review 2026-10-30, m1; recorded in `TODO.md`). (g) **Cross-set copies: `setPqzKey` may replace a key this chain can never prove** (owner ruling R-cross-set, 2026-10-30, final review of UA-8 part 1 I2, option (c)): because a registration is portable, anyone can copy a UA's registration with a PQZ key of one parameter set (say `n2304-kmax4096`) to a chain that runs another (say `n2816-kmax65536`); there the chain's `R_REG` verifier and `PqzCore._keyPtr` refuse the length, so the key can never be proven, and before this ruling `setPqzKey` (`UAPqzKeySet`) and `register` (`UAAlreadyRegistered`) left the UA without PQZ on that chain for good. Now `setPqzKey` may replace a stored PQZ key **only when its length is not this chain's PQZ set's key length**; keys of this chain's set stay write-once. As built: the stored key is replaced only when it is unproven, slot `0x0142` has a verifier, and its length ≠ `PqzSet.PK` (this build's set, the verifier's own check); without the verifier nothing is replaced. The replacement emits the ordinary `UAPqzKeyAdded` (no new event or error); `UAPqzKeySet` is now raised only when the stored key stays. A replaced `register` key is kept for `registrationOf` (the record still returns the `register` arguments and stays copyable); a replaced `setPqzKey` key is overwritten and survives only in its log. A gen 2 with the verifier replaces gen 1's other-set key in its own attachment (gen 1's record untouched). The client rule "one PQZ key per UA, ever" becomes "one PQZ key per UA per PQZ parameter set". Why: a third party must not be able to strand a UA's PQZ use on a chain; the other options of the review — (a) a documented rule "one parameter set on every chain a UA uses", which nobody can enforce, and (b) the registry refusing other-set keys where it has the verifier, which conflicts with "one PQZ key per UA, ever" and with keys stored unproven as directory entries — were not chosen. Cost if wrong: one more write branch; on that chain the record then names the new key (the replaced one stays valid on the chains of its own set). Status: decided (owner); built on `ua8` in `cc965914` (tests `test_ua8_crossSetKeyReplaced`, `test_ua8_crossSetRightSetKeyStays`, `test_ua8_crossSetGen2ReplacesGen1Key`).

Change (2026-10-31, owner decision 2 of 2026-10-31; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`, TS-D3): **the PQZ key record is typed.** `setPqzKey`'s signature is over `uaMessage(kind, PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY, typed(UAPqzKeyRecord{UAPqzKey{ua, pqzKeyHash}, pqzPopHash}))` and a later key's `R_REG` over `uaMessage(0x0142, PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY, typed(UAPqzKey{ua, pqzKeyHash}))`, under the CTR-UA-07 domain; `PQZ_KEY_RECORD_TAG` is legacy. `storePqzPop` of a `register` key reads the kind from `kindOf(ua)` (a gen-1 record on its gen-2 host included), because the `R_REG` record now carries `kind`. `setPqzKey` takes a `UASig` (CTR-UA-36). Why: the same readable record as the PoP. Cost if wrong: every family reproduces the struct hashes byte for byte; the vectors pin them. Status: built in typed-signing P1, P2, P3, R1.

Change (2026-11-04, owner, CTR-UA-39 Q2): **`mldsa87` (0x0134) is a holder** of a PQZ key and a KEM record where the kind is enabled. The holders are single-key `mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `mldsa87`, `fndsa512` and a PQ-eligible `msig`; `slhdsa128s` stays out (its reasons, a 7,856 B signature and ≈ 1.4 M gas a spend, do not describe `mldsa87` on a precompile: 4,627 B, ≈ 0.25 M estimate). A PQZH value token's single-key holder list (`PqzCore._creditKey`, owner 2026-10-27 C0-2) takes it too. Status: decided; built on `mldsa87`.

Change (2026-11-04, owner, CTR-UA-40 Q2): **`fndsa1024` (0x0135) is a holder** of a PQZ key and a KEM record. The holders are single-key `mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `mldsa87`, `fndsa512`, `fndsa1024` and a PQ-eligible `msig`; `slhdsa128s` stays out. A PQZH value token's single-key holder list (`PqzCore._creditKey`) takes it too. Its spend fits: `setKemKey` ≈ 9.0 M (estimate: `fndsa512`'s 6.5 M + the verify difference 2.46 M), a PQZ debit adds its ≈ 4.8 M authorization. Status: decided; built on `mldsa87` (`a57da111`).
Change (2026-11-06, owner ruling R2; group 3g, CTR-UA-42; and owner ruling R3 of group 3f, CTR-PQZ-30): **version 0 is write-once without exception, and the token view names the version.** Old (owner 2026-10-30, ruling R-cross-set): a stored unproven key of another set's length could be replaced once by `setPqzKey`. New: a second version 0 reverts `UAPqzKeySet` whatever its set; a new key is a version v ≥ 1 (CTR-UA-42); `pqzKeyOf(ua)` returns `(version, ptr, pqzPopHash, proven)` of the current version. "PQZ tokens accept only proven keys" now reads "`PRECOMPILE` PQZ tokens"; an `OFFCHAIN` token accepts an unproven key of this set's length, which its verifier checks off chain (CTR-PQZ-30). Status: BUILT on EVM (T51 `3f80f072`, T54; 3f T44 + T45 `2cce490d`).

### CTR-UA-17 — Verify through registry; large keys stored once
- old: R306 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-17 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The registry does lookup and check in one call; small keys travel in calldata, large keys (PQ, MuSig2/FROST group keys) are stored once.
**Cost if wrong.** No token-side cache in v1: one cold call (~2.6 k) per check.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:229`

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 (U1, U6): the optional PQZ key of a PQ signer is stored as a separate SSTORE2 pointer beside the record (returned by `recordOf`), not as `keyPtr`; the `Record` keeps one slot; `keyOf(ua)` keeps returning the signer's own stored key (ML-DSA `pk`, Zether `Y`, …). Zether `Y` is stored so that `keyOf` serves storage-only recovery and its signed writes carry only the signature. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits 9c2cbc5c, 8889a21b, a01ed25e).

### CTR-UA-18 — Derived-UA balances in a separate bytes32 ledger in the base
- old: R308 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-18 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Derived-UA balances live in a separate `bytes32` ledger, shown to ERC-20 tools as the `UA_POOL` sub-ledger, keeping `Transfer` replay equal to `balanceOf`; the ledger lives in the one base, so every tier has it.
**Cost if wrong.** Naive indexers see one large `UA_POOL` holder.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:243`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-9.

### CTR-UA-19 — UAMetaTransaction has its own typehash in the token domain
- old: R309, UA:Q11 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-19 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** `UAMetaTransaction` has its own struct and typehash because `from` is `bytes32`; it is signed in the token's one salted domain (version `"1"`, `chainUid` the implementation's immutable) and keeps explicit shapes (transfer, `pay`, `unwrap`), since a `bytes32` sender cannot run a self-call.
**Cost if wrong.** Clients build two struct shapes; a separate domain version would add a second salt source.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:255`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1410`; `history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md` §3 MG-9, §7 (CTR-UA-19 row).
Change (2026-10-08): both UA structs (`UAMetaTransaction`, `UAMetaTransfer`) share the token domain; the split is CTR-UA-26. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G8, §3 GC-9.
Change (owner 2026-11-04, `ua*` / `mtx*` merge; status: SPECIFIED, not built): "the registry … 0 = the ledger is off: every `ua*` reverts `UALedgerOff`" is reversed by [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) (spec row R9): the UA structs are the token's signed structs for every merged operation, and at `registry() == 0` only a derived side reverts `UALedgerOff`; a call whose every side is native runs. The Rule text and `contracts/accounts.md` are rewritten by the build.

### CTR-UA-20 — Optional VC layer; on-chain anchor deferred
- old: R310 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-20 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The credential layer is optional; contracts consume only `ComplianceRegistry` flags. The on-chain anchor is deferred because nothing reads it and it would leak metadata.
**Cost if wrong.** No public holder/issuer co-statement in v1; the evidence bundle carries it privately.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:264`

### CTR-UA-21 — Holder binding by account-signed presentation
- old: R311, UA:Q14 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-21 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Holder binding is a presentation signed by the account under purpose `vp` (SD-JWT VC + KB-JWT `alg: scaas-ua`), ideally by a dedicated identity UA.
**Cost if wrong.** External SD-JWT verifiers accept these presentations only if they implement `scaas-ua`.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:271`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1415`

### CTR-UA-22 — Breaking dev-only migration from Zether registry
- old: R312 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-22 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Migration from the built Zether registry is breaking and dev-only: the old registry and `AuthScheme` leave the build (backed up in `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/ua3/`, UA-3), Zether accounts re-register.
**Cost if wrong.** Dev balances are recreated by scripts; no production data exists.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:278`

### CTR-UA-23 — PQ and ed25519 kinds on every EVM chain
- old: R313, UA:Q9 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-23 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-11): owner — (1) ML-DSA signs `pq_msg = keccak256(TAG(kind) ‖ ua_msg)` with the empty FIPS 204 context instead of `ua_msg` with `ctx = kind_tag`: EIP-8355 always uses the empty context and EIP-8051 takes a 32-byte message, so only a 32-byte digest carrying the tag fits both; key data and UA ids unchanged, vectors change in P6; chain 7622's `MLDSA65` becomes EIP-8355's layout. (2) New kind `slhdsa128s` (0x0133, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s, FIPS 205, pk 32 B, sig 7,856 B, same `pq_msg`), the hash-based backup if lattices fall: pure Solidity on SHA-256 `0x02` (no SLH-DSA precompile EIP), enabled on public chains only after P6 measures its gas against the per-transaction cap and `UA_VERIFY_BUDGET`. Both SPECIFIED (P6). Source add: owner, 2026-10-11; `research/pq-eips-vs-scaas.md` Q1, Q4.

Change (2026-10-15): controller proposal (owner may override) — P6f D3 / D5: on the SCaaS testnet the UA ML-DSA kinds verify through `MLDSA44` at `0x5caa500000000000000000000000000000000012` and `MLDSA65` at `0x5caa500000000000000000000000000000000013` (EIP-8355 layout, empty context, gas 49,000 / 68,000 + 6 per message word); on the copy `UAMldsaVerifier(0x0130 / 0x0131, …)` picked the precompile (`PRECOMPILE()` = the address) and verified the `pq_signatures.json` rows. The gen-1 registry on the SCaaS testnet is redeployed with them in P6g.

Change (2026-10-31): owner ruling 2026-10-31 — the UA kinds follow the same principle as PQZ and classical Zether: no chain-id lock; a kind is enabled wherever the chain meets its requirement. `DeployBase` drops its dev-chain flag (31337 / 1337, plus 7622 for the PQ kinds): `bls-bn254-minsig` is enabled wherever `UAPrecompileProbe` passes the bn254 G2 check (was: private chains only), and the PQ signing kinds `mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `fndsa512`, `slhdsa128s` wherever the kind's gen-1 cap is at most half the chain's `UA_VERIFY_BUDGET` (this rule's bound; was: the dev chains and the SCaaS testnet only) — all four at the 12 M budget, while Hedera's 10.5 M leaves `mldsa65` (cap 5.95 M) off. The verifiers are pure Solidity under the EIP-170 limit (largest `UAMldsaVerifier` 11,234 B), so code size never disables a kind; the registry itself already needs a 64 KiB code-size chain. `zether-bls12381` stays off Hedera (no Zether token can exist there). Status: done on branch `zether-ungate`.

Change (2026-10-31): owner ruling 2026-10-31 — the condition "an audit is required before any public chain enables the PQ verifiers" is removed from deployment: deploying and enabling the PQ signing kinds (`mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `fndsa512`, `slhdsa128s`) is not gated by an audit; they keep the label UNAUDITED, as classical Zether and PQZ do. The 50 %-of-budget rule stays as it is. On Hedera `mldsa44` is usable only if its expanded-key cache step fits Hedera's 15 M per-transaction cap (12.76 M measured on an osaka anvil, not measured on Hedera). The audit of the PQ verifiers stays an open TODO, no longer a deploy precondition. Status: done on branch `zether-ungate` (docs only; `DeployBase` never checked an audit).

Change (2026-10-31): owner ruling 2026-10-31 — the PQ-kind enable threshold of the deploy script changes from cap ≤ 50 % to cap ≤ 66 % of the chain's `UA_VERIFY_BUDGET` (the 50 % rule of the previous entries stays as history). `DeployBase._pqKindFits` checks it integer-exact as `cap * 100 <= budget * 66` (12 M: 7.92 M; Hedera 10.5 M: 6.93 M); the registry's own `cap <= budget` check is unchanged. Reason: a kind at 66 % of the budget is ~46 % of the per-transaction gas (the budget is 70 % of the cap), which leaves the rest for the operation. Effect: all four PQ kinds are enabled at the 12 M budget and on Hedera (`mldsa65`, cap 5.95 M, was off there). Caveat: on Hedera `mldsa65` plus a heavy operation such as relay fee + mandate can come close to the 15 M per-transaction cap. Status: done on branch `zether-ungate`.

Change (2026-10-31): owner ruling 2026-10-31 — `ed25519` gets the same wording as the PQ kinds: the audit is not a deploy gate; it keeps the unaudited label. `DeployBase` has always enabled it on every chain, so this only aligns the docs (accounts.md §1.9 and S15) with the code. Status: done on branch `zether-ungate`.

Change (2026-10-31): **gen-1 kind gate, owner ruling 2026-10-31 option (a)** — "every gen-1 deploy carries every kind the chain can run (`DeployBase` already does; add a gate that refuses a gen-1 deploy missing an EIP-2537 kind the probe passes; no `UARegistry` change)". Built as `DeployBase._checkGen1Kinds(IUARegistry reg, bool bls, bool isHedera)`, called in `_deployUARegistry` after the registry's constructor and before the `chainUid()` gate: it requires `reg.generation() == 1` and, when `UAPrecompileProbe` passes EIP-2537 (`bls`), `kindEnabled` for `schnorr-bls12381` 0x0105, `bls12381-minsig` 0x0106 and, except on Hedera (no Zether token can exist there, `ZetherLayer`), `zether-bls12381` 0x0141; otherwise the script reverts `gen-1 registry: EIP-2537 kind <k> the probe passes is missing` before anything is broadcast. Without EIP-2537 nothing is required; a probe whose RPC call fails counts as no EIP-2537 (the stated rule only; refusing a deploy whose probe call fails is the owner's open alternative, plan `2026-10-31-ua8-soroban` open question 2). Soroban half (controller call, owner may override; no code): Soroban kinds are compiled into the registry and there are no generations — a new kind is a new registry deployment with new tokens bound to it (S16) — so the rule is written down only: "a Soroban registry meant to stay (mainnet) is deployed from a build carrying every kind built for Soroban at that time" (so after `zether-soroban`). Normative: accounts.md §1.9 "Gen-1 kind gate". Tests: `UADeploy.t.sol` `test_gen1KindGate_refusesMissingZether`, `_refusesMissingSchnorrBls`, `_noBlsPasses`, `_hederaExempts0141`, `_deployPathRunsIt`. Who: owner 2026-10-31 (the EVM gate); controller (the Soroban rule). Status: built, ua8-soroban G1 (the `main` merge commit is added when it lands).

Change (2026-11-04, owner, CTR-UA-39 Q1 / Q4; the rule applied, unchanged): `mldsa87` (0x0134) is a PQ signing kind under this rule. Its pure-Solidity verifier would need a cap ≈ 8.8 M (least working gas 8,763,152 on the cached expanded key; 31.9 M on the FIPS 204 key), over 66 % of every budget (7.92 M; Hedera 6.93 M), so the kind is **disabled wherever no ML-DSA-87 precompile is probed** and has no expanded-key cache; where the EIP-8355 probe passes (`0x14`, or `0x…5caa0014` on the SCaaS testnet) it is enabled with the precompile path's cap (0.25 M, an estimate until T-GAS measures it). The `mldsa87Gas` value of the testnet precompile is provisional (≈ 102,000) until a calibration run the owner allows. Status: decided; built on `mldsa87`.

Change (2026-11-04, owner, CTR-UA-40 Q1 / Q5; the rule applied, unchanged): `fndsa1024` (0x0135) is a PQ signing kind under this rule, **enabled on every EVM chain in pure Solidity**: the measured verify (4,728,382 gas on the UA row, 4,932,967 at the largest NIST KAT message) is 41 % of 12 M and 47 % of Hedera's 10.5 M, so it passes the 66 % rule (7.92 M / 6.93 M) everywhere. Its gen-1 cap is **5,250,000, provisional** until T-GAS measures the worst case (the KAT maximum + 6.4 %, the margin of `fndsa512`'s 2.5 M over its 2.35 M); `_pqKindFits` passes it on every budget ≥ 7,954,546. No precompile anywhere: no EIP defines a Falcon-1024 one (EIP-8052 is Falcon-512 only, no address), and the SCaaS testnet gets none (Q5: .NET has no Falcon; pure Solidity passes). Status: decided; built on `mldsa87`.

**Why.** PQ signing kinds and ed25519 are enabled on every EVM chain (owner), verified by precompile where probed or pure Solidity, each within a measured per-chain cap; an over-budget kind is disabled, never registrable-but-unusable.
**Cost if wrong.** PQ checks cost real money on public L1s (≈ $36–240 per ML-DSA-65 check at 10 gwei).
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:281`, `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:1404`
Change (2026-11-06, group 3f, CTR-PQZ-28): **applied.** An `mldsa44` / `mldsa65` PQZ verifier on a chain without the ML-DSA precompile verifies on its cached expanded key within the registry's cap, so it runs `expandKey` first (uncached `mldsa65`, ≈ 18.9 M, is over the registry's 5.95 M cap and over 2^24). No code change.

### CTR-UA-24 — EIP-7702 EOAs are native; classify by code
- old: R331 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An EIP-7702 delegated EOA keeps its base key as root, so its ECDSA is accepted; since the owner rulings D1–D5 of 2026-10-30 its delegate never authorises (no ERC-1271 through the delegate) and a delegated caller is refused, because a sweeper delegate after one phishing signature would otherwise sign or act for the account. Classification is by code at verify time (until 2026-10-30: ERC-1271 through the delegate was a fallback).
**Cost if wrong.** Smart-EOA users lose delegate signing and direct calls while delegated (they use relayed `mtx*` signed by their key, or clear the delegation); if a future EIP lets 7702 accounts disable the base key, a new registry generation must follow it.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md:355`

Change (2026-10-30, owner ruling R-7702, superseded the same day by D1): the rule also holds on the UA-8 portable path — an `msig` native member signing for `pop` v2, `kem` or `pqz-key` over the chain-free `memberDigest`: empty code ⇒ ECDSA over its `personal_sign` hash; the EIP-7702 designator ⇒ that root-key ECDSA first, then ERC-1271; other code ⇒ ERC-1271 only. It superseded controller ruling A5-m m2 (any code ⇒ ERC-1271 only on that path). Built in `cc965914`; replaced in `0c113cfc`.

Change (2026-10-30, owner ruling D1, amends this rule for the registry): in the registry (`requireAuthorized` and `msig` native members on both paths, one `_byCode`) a 7702 designator account is checked by ECDSA with its own key only, **never ERC-1271** through the delegate; empty code likewise ECDSA; other code ERC-1271 only. Why, cost and full text: CTR-UA-07, change of 2026-10-30 (D1). Built on `ua8`: `cc965914` (R-7702) → `0c113cfc` (portable path) → `128becef` (`requireAuthorized`). The address path (`SigCheck.isValid` and its callers, `RelayFeeRouter`, the node's DEX venue `valid_sig`, clientkeys `signDigest`) followed on branch `no7702` (next change).

Change (2026-10-30, owner rulings **D1–D5** — owner 2026-10-30, after the 2026-10-29 EIP-7702 hot-wallet drain: "an EOA must really sign — no delegation at all; an EOA must not run code"; status: current, decided (owner); built on branch `no7702`: `5ddc577d` (D1, `SigCheck`), `6bb05818` (D2, D3), `955f5337` (D4, D5), `684f5643` (DEX KAT and size baseline), `b76b168c` (clientkeys, CLI-SGN-40), `dad611dc` (node)): a 7702 designator is an EOA **everywhere**: own-key ECDSA only, never ERC-1271 (D1, now also on the address path, CTR-MTX-25); a designator direct caller is refused `CallerDelegated` wherever a caller is authority (D2, D3, CTR-MTX-18); no relay target or native unwrap recipient is a designator (D4, CTR-MTX-27); deployer- and registrar-chosen code must be a contract (D5, CTR-TOK-03). The registry and the tokens now apply one 7702 rule. Supersedes the 2026-10-28 rule "delegate-only signatures on both paths" (CTR-MTX-27 change of that date) and, with it, the "address path still open" wording of the R-7702 / D1-registry changes. Cost: one warm EXTCODESIZE per guarded call (313 gas), +352 per bound relayed item; token runtimes −91 to −95 B (`MtxPipelineLib` −164 B, `WrappedLib` +126 B, `RelayFeeRouter` +74 B, `OpenFactory` +183 B; `size-baseline.json` ratcheted). Chain level: NET-EVM-07. Non-EVM analogues: NET-ALL-83 (D6 dropped).

Change (2026-10-31, cross-reference, no change to this rule): the chain-bound native rule stands as it is (`requireAuthorized` over `uaAuthDigest`, by code at call time). On the portable path only the digest moved: an `msig` native member signs the record's typed digest instead of the EIP-191 `personal_sign` of `memberDigest`, by the same `_byCode` (an EOA or an EIP-7702 designator by ECDSA with its own key only, other code by ERC-1271). See CTR-UA-33, change of this date. Status: built in typed-signing P3.
