### CTR-UA-26 — The UA path splits into UAMetaTransaction and UAMetaTransfer
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-26 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): owner — the UA allowlist grows with parity: `unwrapToUA` and `burn` (UA-5a), `zetherShield` and the confidential ops under the UA envelope binding (UA-5c); `approve`, `mtxTrade` and `uaTrade` stay refused in every `ua*` function — a UA trades by a signed `UATradeOrder`, not by a UA-ledger allowance. SPECIFIED. Source add: owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.1, UP-8, UP-10.

**Why.** The UA ledger carried the same token-shaped `to`/`value`/`data` struct as the address path; splitting it the same way (owner G8) gives one model everywhere: a generic call for the UA allowlist and a typed transfer/payment, sharing the one nonce map.
**Cost if wrong.** Two meta-tx models — split on the address path, mixed on the UA path — for clients, node and vectors.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §2 G8, §3 GC-9.
Change (2026-10-19): controller — **a cancel is not bound to the nonce it cancels: recorded, no change** (the second code review, on-chain part (plan Task 5g, branch `rev2-chain-sol`; triage W-A…W-S in `pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, row W-P; report `V3-claude-common-metatx-dex.md` V3-02). `uaCancelDigest` covers `(chainid, chainUid, token, ua, batch, validUntil)` and `uaCancelNonce` bumps the lane from whatever it is (the native `cancelNonce` meta-tx likewise), so a relayer that withholds a cancel can submit it later and void the next envelope on that lane (`MetaTxBadNonce`). Griefing only — nothing moves, the signer re-signs — and conformant to accounts.md ("each signature cancels once"). Binding the nonce (`uaCancelDigest(…, nonce)` with `_nonce == nonce`, `cancelNonce(batch, expected)`) changes the `metatx-cancel` digest, six clients and the KAT vectors; not done. Wallets: a cancel's `validUntil` no later than the envelope it targets, shown as "bump this lane once", not "cancel envelope n". Status: **recorded** (owner may order the binding).
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R7; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): the signed path has two structs, a generic `UAMetaTransaction` and a typed `UAMetaTransfer`, under the `mtx*` names, and they take native and derived ids; the `ua*` names and the sentence that `uaExecuteTransfer` mirrors `mtxExecuteTransfer` go (nothing is left to mirror).

### CTR-UA-27 — Parity: every native-id operation is open to a registered SIGNING UA
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-13 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-27 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner decisions of 2026-10-13 on the UA parity design: a derived UA of any SIGNING kind, PQ included, can do every operation a native id can — as a subject through a signed UA form (`ua*`, the UA allowlist, `UATradeOrder`, the generic UA pipeline of `MetaTxBase`) and as a receiver through a `bytes32` form credited in the UA ledger. Q1: the role and admin functions (token owner and role holders, DEX `admin`, factory creator and `TokenConfig.owner`/`roles`/`initialHolder`, `SmartKeyAccount` keys and guardian, `addReserve`, a one-call UA-source `zetherWrapShield`) stay as they are, with no UA counterpart — their holders still act gaslessly through their own contract account (`SmartKeyAccount` / `MandateWallet` `execute`, fee `NONE`, NODE-JOB-01, NODE-JOB-19). Q2: no UA ever grants or holds an allowance. Q10: regulated tokens key compliance by `bytes32` when built. Phases UA-5a / 5b / 5c.
**Why.** A UA never sends a transaction, so without a UA form for every subject and a `bytes32` form for every receiver a PQ-key UA could not trade, wrap in one step, receive from a mandate or use a Zether token without keeping a classical key — the reason UAs exist. Separate structs and events keep every address-typed ABI, vector and indexer unchanged; the allowlist/dedicated-function split reuses the self-call where the body needs only `_msgSender()`. Role functions stay off every allowlist because a signature check would skip a minter contract's caps or a Safe's guards (CTR-MTX-19); the owner keeps them as they are since their holders are gasless already through their own contract account. An allowance for UAs was rejected: an EOA has none on a SCaaS token (CTR-TOK-01), and every pull already has a signed, named intent.
**Cost if wrong.** Each operation has two forms to build, test and vector (code size grows; owner: no size work before Glamsterdam); a UA cannot hold a role directly, so a UA-only holder who needs a role deploys a contract account.
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-13; `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §1–§6 (UP-1…UP-6, UP-8, UP-10; Q1, Q2, Q10).
Change (owner 2026-11-04, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30) with its Q6 Change; status: SPECIFIED, not built): the parity rule holds, by construction (spec R8), but three parts now read wrong for tokens, the router and the mandate wallets. The subject's signed form is the one merged `mtx*` entry of each operation, which takes native and derived ids, not a `ua*` twin beside an address form (the generic UA pipeline is the merged `mtxExecute`; on `MandateWallet` the `bytes32` ids of CTR-ACC-12 come through merged entries, not `uaExecute`). The Why's "separate structs and events keep every address-typed ABI … unchanged" no longer holds there: the address forms go to legacy and a native subject signs the `UA…` struct. The Cost's "each operation has two forms" becomes one form per operation. `SmartKeyAccount` keeps its address form. `contracts/accounts.md` is rewritten by the build (T19).

### CTR-UA-28 — A native caller credits a derived UA in one call
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-13 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-28 · superseded-by: —

Change (2026-10-13): built as ruled (UA-5a): `_uaMint`, `wrapToUA`, `unwrapToUA`, `mintToUA`, `payWithFeeToUA`, `burn` and `unwrapToUA` on the UA allowlist (CTR-UA-26) and `uaPayReceiverFee` (CTR-MTX-05) are BUILT; the spike's controller rulings C5a-1…C5a-14 settle build details (task split, one wrap body, check order, fixtures, gas method, vector parameters) and change no rule. Source add: plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-ua5a-receivers-wrap.md`.

**Why.** Every `address` receiver of a direct path gets a `bytes32` form (`wrapToUA`, `unwrapToUA`, `mintToUA`, `payWithFeeToUA`, beside `transferToUA`), each crediting through `_uaMove` (a mint is a move from 0), so a wrap reaches a UA in one call instead of `wrap` + `transferToUA` and a mandate can pay a UA payee. `wrapToUA` is on the address allowlist only (a UA holds no outside underlying); `unwrapToUA` pays a SCaaS ledger leg by `transferToUA` and is on both allowlists. The `UnwrappedToUA` event and the ERC-165 test for a ledger leg were controller rulings, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-13.
**Cost if wrong.** Four more entry points per kind; a leg that falsely reports `IUALedger` can only cheat the unwrapper who chose it (the exact balance delta still holds the wrapper's reserve).
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-13 (Q9); `history/specs/2026-10-13-ua-parity-design.md` §4.2, §4.3, §4.5 (UP-9).
Change (2026-11-10, ua-mtx-merge T19; pay-meta-tax spec §10; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge`, UNAUDITED): owner O11 (T37 `3740b85e`): `payWithFeeToUA` takes `PayMeta` last; `entryRef == metaPayId(meta)`.

### CTR-UA-42 — PQZ key records per (ua, version): version 0 as before, versions v ≥ 1 strictly sequential and signed by the UA, current the highest eligible
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-42 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A UA's PQZ key is kept per `(ua, version)`. Version 0 is today's record byte for byte (`UAPqzKey` / `UAPqzKeyRecord`, `PURPOSE_POP_V2` / `PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY`) and write-once without exception (R2: ruling R-cross-set's replacement retired; a second version 0 reverts `UAPqzKeySet`). A version v ≥ 1 needs version 0 and `v == latest + 1` (`UAPqzKeyVersion`), the UA's own `UASig` (m-of-n `members` for an `msig`, never `keyData`) over typed `UAPqzKeyVersionRecord{UAPqzKeyVersion{ua, version, pqzKeyHash}, pqzPopHash}`, and its own `R_REG` proof over `uaMessage(0x0142, PURPOSE_PQZ_KEY, typed(UAPqzKeyVersion))`. A per-UA marker `pqzKeyUsed[ua][h]` keeps a UA's versions distinct (`UAKeyInUse`, on every registry kind; a gen-2 host reads gen 1's); `keyOwner` per proven version; the `0x0142` list once per UA. `current` is the highest eligible version (proven; without the verifier, this build's set length with its proof bytes stored), moved only when proof bytes are stored (`register` with `pqzPop`, `storePqzPop`), never down, with `UAPqzKeyCurrent(ua, version)`. Views `pqzKeyOf` (four words: version, ptr, pqzPopHash, proven), `pqzKeyAt`, `pqzKeyLatest`, `pqzKeyUsed`, `pqzPopOf(ua, v)`, `pqzKeySigOf(ua, v)`, the two pure digests. Host rules 1–4 (spec §2.3). KV-14: this release's registry generation on every chain. UNAUDITED.
**Status.** BUILT on EVM (plan T51 `3f80f072`, T54; tests `test/ua/PqzKeyVersions.t.sol`, `test/ua/UAStoreLayout.t.sol`, `test/pqz/PqzKeyVersionsToken.t.sol`, invariants `test/pqz/invariant/PqzVer{Handler,Invariants}.t.sol`, T56 `e1336e60`: J1–J6, J9, J10 at the four sets; 48 mutants over T51–T56, every one killed). Other families: PLANNED, each in its own round. The draft of this rule was numbered CTR-UA-41, which the owner's verifier-naming rule of 2026-11-10 took first.
**Why.** O1–O7 and R1–R6 (owner 2026-11-06): a PQZ key must be replaceable after an operator change or a share holder leaving, without changing the UA (CTR-UA-13: the UA itself never rotates); each version proven on its own so no proof is evidence for another key.
**Cost if wrong.** A version accepted out of sequence or with a reused key would let a debit name a key nobody proved, or carry one version's proof to another; a `current` that could move down would strand credits sent to the higher version.
**Source.** owner rulings O1–O7, R1–R6 (2026-11-06); spec [superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-key-versions.md](superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-key-versions.md) §2, §6.1, §12 (KV-1 … KV-5, KV-14); reviews [Codex](research/pqzver-codex-review.md), [Fable](research/pqzver-fable-review.md). Measured at T51 (history, before T66b's split): deploy gas `UARegistryLib` 60.83 M → 63.08 M, `UARegistry` 50.62 M → 53.51 M.

## 25. Contracts — Post-quantum Zether

### CTR-UA-29 — The registry keeps an on-chain list of the UAs of each kind
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-17 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-29 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Wallets choose decoys for PQZ and classical Zether multi-recipient transfers among the UAs of the token's kind; event logs may be pruned on a long-running chain, the registry state is not, and a UA serves many tokens, so the list lives in the registry (`uaCount`, `uaAt`, `uaPage`, `uaIndex`; every kind including `msig` (owner 2026-10-17); native ids are not listed). Controller design accepted by the owner: the index in the record's free 40 bits, ≈ +27 k gas per registration, gen 2 forwards gen-1 kinds.
**Cost if wrong.** ≈ 27 k gas on every registration and 25,602 B of registry code (over EIP-170; test chains allow 64 KiB) for a list wallets could otherwise rebuild from logs while the logs exist.
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-17 (TODO.md "UA Registry: on-chain index of UAs per kind"); branch `ua-index`.

Change (2026-10-19): controller proposal (owner may override) — on-chain review W-C (`pqz-core/research/code-review-2026-10-19/U-agy-chain.md`, V2-1): **a decoy selection rule for wallets** — decoys only from UAs active in the token within the look-back window, weighted by recency, never registered after the wallet's last sync point, at most a fixed share per `authRef` group; threat S30 in accounts.md. Spec only, no bytecode. Status: written (`66654e3`); wallet code in P6h.

Change (2026-11-07, owner): the token-activity filter of the decoy rule is an **option**, not mandatory; the default draws decoys uniformly from the kind's list up to the wallet's last sync point (never UAs registered later); the filter (activity, recency, holder-authorised moves) can be enabled, with the sybil trade-off stated to the holder.

Change (2026-10-19): owner rulings on the on-chain review (both proposals accepted): **W-J** the `secp256k1` kind (0x0108) verifies ECDSA over the raw digest, so an EOA-held key signs it only through `eth_sign` (against S23) — recorded as a residual risk in the S23 row; an EIP-191 `personal_sign` variant (new verifier, vectors, six clients) after P6. **W-K** `MandateWallet.isValidSignature` / `HederaMandateWallet` accept the owner's ECDSA over any digest (ERC-7739 class) — documented beside `SmartKeyAccount`'s limitation in accounts.md; no wrapping. Status: recorded in the spec.

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U11, **the PQZ-capable list**: each UA stays in its kind's list (`msig` included); a PQZ holder is also appended to the list of key `0x0142`, read with the same `uaCount(0x0142)`, `uaAt(0x0142, i)`, `uaPage(0x0142, …)`, so PQZ decoy legs come from one anonymity set of recipients that all have a PQZ key (a per-kind filter would leak which kind the real recipient is); no reverse index, `Record.index` stays the kind-list position; ≈ +27 k gas per holder registration; it lives in the generation that enables 0x0142. Classical Zether decoys keep the `0x0141` list. **The decoy rule of the 2026-10-19 Change loses its `authRef` clause** (no on-chain grouping is left to cap with one key per UA): it keeps "active in the token within the look-back window, weighted by recency, never registered after the wallet's sync point"; threat S30 now records that a sybil decoy set costs one PQ registration per decoy (≈ 5 M gas, free on the SCaaS testnet, bounded by node sponsorship quotas, CTR-UA-25). Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).
Change (2026-11-06, group 3g, CTR-UA-42): **the `0x0142` list takes a UA once, whatever its number of key versions, and a wallet never draws a decoy with a pending version** (a latest version of this set's length not yet eligible); UAs without a recent `UAPqzKeyCurrent` come first. Status: BUILT (registry T51 `3f80f072`; `clientkeys` `pqzDecoyCandidates`, test `pqz-versions.test.js`).

### CTR-UA-30 — A UA is one signature-verifying entity; a PQZ key is an attribute of a PQ-signing UA
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-20 · normative: decisions.md · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner rulings 2026-10-20 on the research note `docs/research/ua-identity.md`: (1) **a UA is one entity that
can verify signatures** (a native account, a single key of any kind, BLS, a multisig m-of-n, …); ids keep the current
derivation (CTR-UA-02 / -03: native ids as-is or zero-padded, derived ids `keccak256(keccak256(tag) ‖ key_data)`).
(2) **Classical Zether: option (A) — the Zether key is itself the UA** (as the zether-dev `ZetherAccount.register(y, c,
s)` with `yHash`, in SCaaS form `keccak256(keccak256(tag) ‖ Y)` with the kind tag): the key signs by Schnorr with `x`,
the Zether proof authorizes a spend ("self" mode kept); its public balance and its confidential account share that id.
(3) **PQZ: the PQZL public key is an attribute of a PQ-signing UA only** (`mldsa65` / `mldsa44`, later `fndsa512`, or a
`msig` whose non-PQ members' weight is below the threshold — the CTR-PQZ-12 rule; classical signers may not carry a PQZ
key), **supplied in `register`** (no separate attach function), with the `R_REG` proof of knowledge bound to chain,
registry and the UA id; immutable. (4) **An encryption key belongs to one UA only**, multisig included (the existing
`keyOwner[keccak256(GROUP ‖ key)]` map, `UAKeyInUse`). Consequences: the `pqz-mlwe` UA kind (0x0142) and its `authRef`
go (the id 0x0142 stays as the PQZ scheme id); the PQZ account, its fees (CTR-PQZ-06 change) and its public balance live
under the signing UA's id; for a multisig the PQZL secret is a single view / prove key, spends need the m-of-n
signature. The research note's option to drop Zether "self" mode is withdrawn by (2).
**Why.** One identity per holder for public and confidential balances; the PQZ key cannot sign compactly (an `R_REG`
proof is ≈ 40 KB), so it rides on a PQ signer; Zether keys can sign, so the single-key account stays simple.
**Cost if wrong.** Registry, verifiers, the `R_REG` message, the PQZ token state keys and every UA client change
(test chains only; the `R_REG` change rides the 16k `proofSystemId` bump).
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-20 (chat rulings on `docs/research/ua-identity.md` §8: PQ signers only, keys in `register`, Zether option (A)). Status: decided, not built (UA-6, before plan Task 5h).

Change (2026-10-20, owner): **definition — a UA is the actor (person, organization, device or group) that signs and is accountable for a write to a smart contract, tokens included**. Reads need no UA. Consequence (controller reading, consistent with rulings (2)–(4)): anything that cannot sign a write is not a UA but an attribute of one — the PQZ key (attribute of a PQ signer); a classical Zether key is a UA because it signs (Schnorr by `x`) and its proof authorizes the spend. Recorded in README §6. Status: decided.

Change (2026-10-20, owner): **the Zether `authRef` is removed entirely** (no optional spending co-signer): a Zether key UA authorizes its spends by its proof alone and signs its other writes (`zetherRollOverSigned`, `zetherSetRollOverMode`, `pop`) by Schnorr with `x`; a leaked `x` is a full loss (funds and privacy), accepted (analysis `research/shield-and-key-reuse.md` §1). Removed in UA-6 with the PQZ `authRef`: the record field, `authPop`, purpose `authref`, `UAAuthRef`, `survivesEncKeyLeak` for Zether. Status: decided, built in UA-6.

Change (2026-10-20, owner; UA-6 design question Q1): **a Zether key UA may sign every write**, like any signing UA (follows the UA definition above: the actor that signs and answers for a write) — its Schnorr signature by `x` authorizes UA-ledger transfers, trades and every other `requireAuthorized` path, and its public balance is spendable that way; `zether-bls12381` joins the SIGNING set (not an `msig` member, cannot hold a PQZ key). UA-6 spec decision U8 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-ua6-encryption-key-attributes.md`, branch `ua6-spec`). Status: decided; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits c4ece459, 97fe4778).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U1, **record and storage**: the `Record` keeps its one slot (kind, registeredAt, keyPtr, index); the PQZ key is a second SSTORE2 pointer in a new mapping `_pqzKey[ua]`, written once inside `register`, never in the id; the PQZ key claims `keccak256(GROUP("pqz-mlwe") ‖ pqzKey)` in the existing `_keyOwner` map for every holder, `msig` included (`UAKeyInUse`, ruling (4)); the registry hard-codes no key length (`UAPqzVerifier.verifyPop` refuses any key that is not exactly `PqzCt.PK` bytes with every coefficient `< q`). Removed: the `_authRef` mapping, the `authPop` argument, the `recordOf` second return value as `authRef`. Source: UA-6 spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-ua6-encryption-key-attributes.md` §2. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U2, **`register` shape**: one function `register(kind, keyData, pop, pqzKey, pqzPop)`, the pair empty for every UA but a PQ holder (`pqzPop` empty iff `pqzKey` empty); same selector for every kind, the argument slots of the removed `(authRef, authPop)` pair reused; a separate `registerWithPqzKey` rejected (two entry points for one record). Steps (cheap first): kind enabled, key data, id, single-key keyHash or `msig` members and gas bound, PQZ attribute (`UAKindDisabled(0x0142)`, `UAPqzHolder`, `UAKeyInUse`), the signer's PoP, `R_REG`, store. Spec §3. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U4, **one digest for both proofs**: `popDigest(ua, pqzKeyHash) = keccak256(abi.encode(POP_TAG, chainKeyHash, chainUid, registry, ua, pqzKeyHash))`, the built function with its last word renamed from `authRef`; `pqzKeyHash = keccak256(GROUP("pqz-mlwe") ‖ pqzKey)`, or `0` without a PQZ key (so every UA without one keeps today's PoP bytes and every classical vector stays valid). The signer's PoP and the `R_REG` proof use it under the kind tags `TAG(kind)` and `TAG(0x0142)`: a front-runner can neither strip nor swap the key, and a proof made for another UA fails. Spec §3. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U5, **a PQ-eligible `msig` signs its registration**: an `msig` whose non-PQ weight is below its threshold always registers with its m-of-n `abi.encode(MemberSig[])` over `uaMessage(MSIG, POP, popDigest(ua, pqzKeyHash))` (purpose `pop`), with or without a PQZ key, because an unsigned registration would let anyone fix the structure first without the key, forever. A classical-dominant `msig` can never hold a PQZ key, so its `pop` stays empty (no change). Spec §3. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U6, **interface after UA-6**: `UARegistered(ua, kind, keyData, address pqzKey)` carries the 20-byte pointer, not 16 KB of log data (≈ 0.13 M gas saved); `recordOf(ua)` returns `(Record, address pqzKey)` (0 = none; a gen-2 registry forwards it), wallets read the key with `eth_getCode` minus the leading `STOP` byte; new error `UAPqzHolder(ua)`; removed `UAAuthRef`, `requireZetherAuthorized`; `kindEnabled(0x0142)` and `verifyCap(0x0142)` answer for the `R_REG` verifier; no `pqzKeyOf` view. Spec §3.2. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U12, **UA ledger and public balances**: the PQZ public balance, the fees of CTR-PQZ-06 (2026-10-20), the source of `pqzShield` and the target of an unshield to oneself live under the signing UA's id in the token's UA ledger, spent by that UA's ML-DSA / `msig` signature; a Zether account's public balance sits under its Zether UA id, spendable by Schnorr with `x`. `_checkTo` needs no change beyond `UAKinds.isSigning`; the sentence "a Zether kind never receives" is deleted. Spec §8. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits 9c2cbc5c, 8889a21b, a01ed25e).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U13, **`R_REG`, `proofSystemId` and the 5h dependency**: `R_REG` absorbs a 32-byte message; the relation, the statement layout, `UAPqzVerifier`, the precompile and `statement_register.json` do not change, only the pre-image of the message (the signer's id and the key hash instead of the PQZ id and `authRef`). The change has no `proofSystemId` of its own: it rides the 5h bump (the "16k" id with the B-1 transcript fix, K_MAX = 16,384, q = 2^50 − 42,310,535, owner rulings 2026-10-20) in the roll-out of plan fs3 Task 13; until then the SCaaS testnet keeps today's registry. Spec §9. Status: proposal (the q value and the 5h bump: owner rulings); built in UA-6 / 5h (branch `ua6`, commit 9c2cbc5c; the 5h bump rides plan Task 5h).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U14–U16, **clients, node, vectors**: the ten client libraries (`ua-rs`, `ua-c`, `ua-cxx`, `ua-qt`, `ua-dart-frb`, `ua-dart`, `ua-py`, `ua-go`, `ua-cs`, clientkeys `ua.js`) move rows 0x0140 and 0x0142 out of `KINDS` (0x0142 stays in a `SCHEMES` table so `tag`, `ua_msg`, `key_hash` work while `ua_of` refuses it), `is_zether(k) = k == 0x0141`, `is_signing` adds 0x0141, new `is_pqz_holder` and `msig_pqz_eligible`, `authref` leaves `PURPOSES`, `pop_digest` takes `pqz_key_hash`, new `pqz_reg_message`; the clientkeys register flow builds `(pqzKey, pqzPop)` from the sealed PQZ leaf; `clients/zether-prover` drops `authSig`/`authDigest` and the bn254 build. Node (spec only, nothing built reads the registry): the route body becomes `{chain, kind, keyData, pop, pqzKey?, pqzPop?}`, the node recomputes the key hash and never verifies `R_REG` locally, the route body limit rises from 64 KiB to 160 KiB (a PQZL holder registration is ≈ 49 KB binary, ≈ 100–108 KB as hex), the record cache reads `recordOf → (Record, pqzKey)`. Vectors: `kinds.json` (0x0140 out, 0x0142 to `schemes`, `authref` out, holder and `pqz_reg_message` rows), `structures.json` (PQ-eligible `msig` rows), `signatures.json` / `pq_signatures.json` / `groups.json` (`authRef` fields dropped: every one is zero, so PoP bytes do not move; holder PoP rows over a non-zero hash), `metatx3.json` (a Zether-UA row); PQZ statement vectors unchanged. Spec §10. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits bf68718a, c12a38e9 [e2e]; 93c5ead2, 1e961aea, 67ef75bc [prover, clientkeys]; 1d24da92 [vectors]; 35036846, c159cf56, 40a8f2ba, 7e2016ef, 7419d7ef [ua-py, ua-go, ua-cs, ua-dart]; 294a4688, a0a66940, da649535, fc0a9a21, 26d9775c, 8b93de4e [ua-rs, ua-c, ua-cxx, ua-qt, ua-dart-frb]; final fix wave 872a6251).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U17–U19, **size gate, gas, tests**: `scripts/size_gate.py` on `UARegistry` (over EIP-170 since CTR-UA-29; allowed on the 64 KiB test chains) and the Zether / PQZ implementations and libraries, expected to shrink, no size work (owner: wait for Glamsterdam), the baseline ratchets down where it shrinks. Gas measured with forge `--isolate` and logged in `smartcontracts/evm/runs/<date>-ua6-gas.txt` (registrations with and without a PQZ key, a PQ-eligible `msig`, `requireAuthorized` on a Zether UA, the Zether and PQZ spends without the registry auth call). Tests `test_UA6_*`: holder registration with and without a key; strip / swap (`UAPoP`); `R_REG` over another UA's digest; the same PQZ key on two UAs (`UAKeyInUse`); non-holders (`UAPqzHolder`); PQ-eligible `msig` without `pop`; `pqzKey` where `0x0142` is disabled; gen-2 forwarding; `uaCount(0x0142)` order; a Zether UA signing, receiving, refused as a member; Zether spends with no `authSig`; the PQZ transfer from an ML-DSA and an `msig` holder; a leg or auditor without a key. The `authRef` suites go to `legacy/ua6/`. Spec §10. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commits 740fbe06, 872a6251).

Change (2026-10-20): controller proposal (owner may override) — UA-6 U20, **migration**: none (all chains test-only; mainnet 22776 not launched). The registry ABI, the Zether entry points and every client change at once; the SCaaS testnet gets the new gen-1 registry (with `UAPqzVerifier` in slot 0x0142 on the 16k id), the PQZ and Zether tokens and the e2e accounts by `smartcontracts/evm/script/pqz/e2e.py` in plan fs3 Task 13 (back up, reset, deploy; controller may do this on the SCaaS testnet); other dev chains redeploy on their next reset; no record is carried over. Spec §10. Status: proposal; built in UA-6 (branch `ua6`, commit 740fbe06 for the docs).
Change (2026-10-20): controller ruling (owner may override) — UA-6 in-branch rulings, recorded in full (branch `ua6`, ledger `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-ua6-encryption-key-attributes/progress.md`). (1) **`uaExecute(zetherShield)` is allowed on both Zether kinds**: scope addition, the brief's test requires it; it is the first bullet of CTR-ZTH-51; small ABI surface to revisit in UA-5c (commit c4ece459). (2) **Rollover and mode changes accept a registered Zether UA only** (owner ruling 2026-10-20, replacing the controller ruling that accepted any id passing `requireAuthorized`, commit c4ece459): `zetherRollOverSigned` and `zetherSetRollOverMode` revert `AccountNotRegistered(ua)` for any other kind or an unregistered id, before `requireAuthorized`, even with a valid signature; asserted in `test_ownerOpsZetherUaOnly` (the commit after 47515612 titled "owner ops accept a Zether UA only"). (3) **ua-c ABI version stays 1**: the kind rows 0x0140 / 0x0142 and the purpose `authref` are removed, which is binary-compatible; the behaviour change is accepted on the test chains (commits a0a66940, da649535, final fix wave). (4) **The deciding `slhdsa128s` msig vector case**: a PQ-eligible `msig` with an `slhdsa128s` member is decided by a generated vector row and test, so its PQ weight is no longer undecided (commit 67ef75bc, vectors 1d24da92). (5) **`UAKinds.uaOf` refuses 0x0142** with `UAKindNotDerived` in code (it calls `_requireDerived`; `tag()` and `groupName()` keep `_requireTagged`), matching accounts.md, CTR-PQZ-13, the spec and all ten clients; `UARegistry` +9 B, baseline ratcheted; asserted in `test_UA6_pqzNotAKind` (commit 872a6251). (6) The Zether UA no longer signs the purposes `member` and `zether-auth` in the clients: no contract accepts them from a Zether UA (final fix wave). Status: controller ruling; built in UA-6.
Change (2026-10-20): review dispositions of the UA-6 reviews (CTR-UA-30, plan Task 10). Per-task reviews: Task 1 clean (minors folded into Tasks 4/9); Task 2 clean (verifyPop key-length check confirmed; minors deferred to Task 9); Task 4 clean; Task 5 one Important (bare `expectRevert` in `test_v3FeeUA`), fixed in a01ed25e; Task 3 one Critical (`e2e.py` NameError on a deleted dict), fixed in c12a38e9; Task 6a two Important (the `slhdsa128s` PQ weight undecided, `zether-read-balance` bn254-only) plus minors, fixed in 67ef75bc; Task 8, Task 6b (native and Rust) and Task 9 clean. Final whole-branch review (988e15f8..7524be45): 0 Critical, 4 Important (the e2e `uaIndex` check on the 0x0142 list; stale `authSig` selectors in zether.md CTR-ZTH-34 and the metatx.md allowlist; `uaOf(0x0142)` accepted; these decisions lines without commits and rulings) and minors 1–8; fixed in the final fix wave (872a6251 and following) except: gas optimisation of registration (owner: no size or gas optimisation now), the `isDerived` simplification and the `_CFG13` rename, which are skipped. Residuals kept open: `ua-qt` and `tst_ua.qml` uncompiled (no Qt6 on the host), no evm test exercises a real `R_REG` proof (the verifier is a stand-in in `UARegistryPq`: cover with the 16k regeneration or the fs3 Task 13 e2e), `script/pqz/e2e.py` first real run on a PQZ chain in fs3 Task 13. ### CTR-UA-31 — A registration is portable: same bytes on every chain, every field in state, `checked`
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-25 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-31 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner request 2026-10-25: "when an account is registered in `UARegistry` on Ethereum, anyone can take exactly that information and
register it on another chain: a UA account does not depend on the chain (its transactions do). The KEM keys likewise." Scope: every family
(owner 2026-10-29); the order of families EVM → Soroban → NEAR → Cosmos / Sui / Aptos / Solana → Algorand → TON, **plans for steps 1–2 only**
(owner 2026-10-29: do steps 1 and 2 first); PQ verification per family and the relayer-checked mode wherever a chain cannot verify (owner 2026-10-29,
spec P10 / P11). The design rulings of the spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-ua8-portable-registrations.md`, by date, all **owner 2026-10-25**
unless marked (the spec calls P1–P9 "controller proposals, owner may override" and marks which parts the owner stated):
**P1** the PoP is portable (CTR-UA-07); **P2** one `register(kind, keyData, attrs, pop, pqzPop)` with everything in one call, anyone may submit
(owner: "not two steps"), and **"store all of it"** — `pop`, `pqzPop`, the KEM record and its signature in contract state as SSTORE2 blobs, so a
registration is rebuilt from state when logs are gone; **P3** what must match — the same kind enabled in the target generation (a PQ kind needs its
verifier there; a PQZ key does *not* need the PQZ verifier, it is stored unproven — the spec's first sentence "a PQZ key on a chain without the
verifier reverts like a disabled kind" is superseded by P8, corrected in the spec 2026-10-30), `msig` members sign `registrationDigest` (ruling A1-c1, CTR-UA-07);
**P4** only the KEM key changes, the PQZ key is set once (owner), any order, no revocation (owner); **P5** a version names the same key on every
chain (owner); **P6** `keyOwner` uniqueness stays per chain, for signer keys and proven PQZ keys (owner); **P7** the KEM record in `UARegistry`,
signed, versioned, stored with its signature (owner; CTR-UA-32); **P8** the balance-key proof is optional (owner; CTR-UA-16); **P9** the later writes
`setKemKey` and `storePqzPop` are mtx-style, chain-free and without a fee, relayable by anyone (owner: no `mtxRegister` / `mtxSetKemKey` /
`mtxStorePqzPop` forms — there is no token to take a fee from); **P10** every family (owner 2026-10-29); **P11** per-family PQ verification and the
relayer-checked mode (owner 2026-10-29 for NEAR `mldsa65` via the host function, Algorand `fndsa512` after AVM v14, Cosmos / Soroban / Sui in part).
**Plan decisions of 2026-10-30** (all controller calls, owner may override; status decided; built on branch `ua8`, not merged, not pushed; the label in
brackets is the plan's, never used here without its content):
- *Encoding* [UA8-D1] and *One signed digest* [UA8-D2] — see CTR-UA-07 (commits `6f72d0ba`, `6572e679`, `e8a6a711`, `e1b33079`).
- *Native `msig` members stay chain-bound* [UA8-D6]: the plan's first reading — a native member signs the registry's EIP-712 `uaAuthDigest` (CTR-UA-24
  unchanged: an EOA never signs a raw digest), so a PoP whose signing set has a native member is valid only on its own registry; derived members are
  portable. **Overridden by ruling C7** (CTR-UA-07 (c)): a native member signs chain-free with `personal_sign` for the portable purposes; the EIP-712
  path remains for everything else. Status: superseded by C7 before being built (the first A1 draft, `6f72d0ba`, already carries C7).
- *Every field in state, chunked* [UA8-D7]: `register` stores `abi.encode(keyData-rest, pop, kemVersion)` (`keyData` once: the stored-kind key stays in its
  existing `keyPtr`, ruling "no second copy"), `pqzPop` and each KEM version's `pk ‖ sig` as SSTORE2 chunks of at most `BLOB_CHUNK = 32,768` B (the largest
  `msig` PoP the gas bound admits on a chain with a larger `verifyBudget` exceeds one 64 KiB code blob); `registrationOf(ua)` returns exactly the `register`
  arguments (the initial `attrs.kemVersion` is stored with the blob, ruling C2, so the view is exact after later `setKemKey`s); the PQZ key keeps its own
  single pointer (`PqzCore` checks its code length). Status: built in `e1b33079`.
- *`checked` on EVM is derived, not stored* [UA8-D10] with ruling C8: every part the EVM registry stores is verified on chain, except a PQZ proof not yet
  proven. Code points shared by every family (in `portable.json`): `NONE = 0`, `CHAIN = 1`, `RELAYER = 2` (+ the relayer id). `checkedOf(ua) → (pop, pqzPop,
  kem)` = `(CHAIN, proven ? CHAIN : NONE, KEM record stored ? CHAIN : NONE)` — an unproven proof reads `NONE` (not yet stored or not yet checked) — and
  the events carry them where the verdict varies — as built, `UARegistered` emits all three (`checkedPop`, `checkedPqzPop`, `checkedKem`) and `UAPqzPopStored` emits `checkedPqzPop`; `UAPqzKeyAdded` has no `checked` field (NONE until its `UAPqzPopStored`) and `UAKemKeySet` has none (CHAIN on EVM); this is how ruling C8's "the same values in the events" was realised (the plan's first wording "the events carry `proven` not `checked`" is replaced by C8). This is the EVM form of spec P11.3. Status: built in `e1b33079`, `b7ba0284`, `13c74c23`.
- *Generations* [UA8-D11]: gen 2 forwards the new views (`registrationOf`, `popOf`, `pqzPopOf`, `pqzKeyOf`, `pqzKeySigOf`, `checkedOf`, `kemKeyOf`, `kemKeyAt`) to

  record) — refined for the PQZ attachment by CTR-UA-16 (d). Indexers read **both generations** (gen 2 emits PQZ events for UAs registered in gen 1). Status: built

- *Legacy* [UA8-D13] (owner rule "backup, not delete", ruling C9): the pre-UA-8 `UARegistry.sol`, `UAKinds.sol`, `IUARegistry.sol` are copied to

- **Owner rulings of 2026-10-30** (final whole-branch review of UA-8 step 1; built on branch `ua8` in the final fix wave, `e6cdc13e` … `128becef`):
  - **R-node — the node relays all four registry writes, built now.** The node's call table (`CALL_TABLE` then, the `PLAIN` rows of `typed.rs` with `guard.rs` since, [NODE-JOB-19](node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-19)) gets a row for each of

- Process rulings that shaped the build (recorded for traceability): the PQZ attach step moves into the registry task (C1, built `e1b33079`); every commit compiles — the portable digests
  and the new interface land beside the old `popDigest` and the old path is removed in the registry commit (C3, `e1b33079`); `portable.json` carries PQZ rows for all four sets,

**Why.** A UA is derived from key data and is the same on every chain; only its registration depended on the chain. A portable PoP lets anyone place the
same record elsewhere, from logs or from state, so a UA works on a new chain without its owner; transactions stay chain-bound (CTR-UA-24).
**Cost if wrong.** The registry's PoP, interface and storage change again; all ten UA libraries and the vector file move with it (test chains only: no migration).
Registration state grows (every field stored; a PQ registration with a stored proof is 84.8–109.1 M gas and splits across two calls on a 60 M block).

### CTR-UA-32 — KEM (chat) key records: signed, versioned, write-once in any order, never revoked
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-25 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-32 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner rulings 2026-10-25 (spec P4, P5, P7): the KEM (chat) key is the one attribute a UA may change; a new key is a record `(ua, version, pk)` signed by the UA
over a chain-independent digest, stored by anyone on any chain **in any order** (a lower version may be stored after a higher one, because others may still use it);
each `(ua, version)` is written once; **there is no revocation** (a key that has been on chain stays public forever; the highest version only says which is the latest);
a version names the same key on every chain (client rule, final review 2026-10-30 m4: one KEM key per KEM version, the initial record included — two signed registrations with different initial `(kemVersion, kemPk)` diverge across chains, and write-once means nothing can repair it); **one scheme only — ML-KEM-1024 + X25519** (the X-Wing-style combiner with ML-KEM-1024, public key 1,600 B, ciphertext
1,600 B, shared secret 32 B; the contract accepts only 1,600-byte keys); **several keys per UA (one per device) later** — one first, storage keyed `(ua, keyId)` with
`keyId = version` so `addKemKey` changes no layout; **only PQ kinds may hold a KEM key**; **no one-owner check** (a KEM record carries no proof of possession of the KEM
secret, so a uniqueness check would let anyone who sees a key first list it under their own UA and block the real owner on that chain; a UA that lists someone else's key
gains nothing — it cannot decrypt); every version needs the UA's signature and the signature is stored with it. Plan decisions of 2026-10-30, **controller calls, owner may
override**, status decided, built on branch `ua8` (not merged):
- *KEM versions start at 1* [UA8-D3]: `attrs.kemVersion = 0` with an empty `kemPk` means "no KEM record" (spec P2 "0 = absent"); `kemRecordHash = kemRecordDigest(ua,
  kemVersion, kemPk)`, 0 without a record; `setKemKey` refuses version 0 (`UAKemVersion`). Built in `e8a6a711`, `e1b33079`, `13c74c23`.
- *The initial KEM record travels with `register`* [UA8-D4]: stored as version `attrs.kemVersion` with an **empty `sig`** — its consent is the registration `pop`, which covers
  `kemRecordHash`; `kemKeyAt(ua, v)` returns `sig = ""` for that version; it reaches another chain only through that chain's `register` (which must carry the same record, or
  the `pop` fails). Built in `e1b33079`.
- *A KEM signature has the `pop` format* [UA8-D5]: `setKemKey(ua, version, kemPk, sig)`: `sig` is the kind's raw signature for a single key, `abi.encode(MemberSig[])` for an
  `msig` (members under `member`; a code-less native member by `personal_sign`, ruling C7; an EIP-7702 designator member likewise by `personal_sign` with its own key only, a contract member by ERC-1271, CTR-UA-24 as amended by owner ruling D1 2026-10-30), over `uaMessage(kind, PURPOSE_KEM, kemRecordDigest(ua, version, kemPk))`, verified
  against the stored key data; the same bytes on every family (a family that decodes `msig` signatures parses this ABI layout). Check order: `UAUnauthorized` (id not held) →
  `UAKemHolder` → `UAKemVersion` → `UAKemKeyLength` → signature (`UAUnauthorized`). A front-runner holding a quorum's signatures can submit another valid subset first (the stored
  `sig` differs; key, version and id do not): accepted. Built in `13c74c23`.
- *KEM holder set* [UA8-D12]: the UA-6 U3 kinds (`mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `fndsa512`) plus a PQ-eligible `msig`; the `msig` PQZ debit gas bound (CTR-PQZ-12, `TX_GAS_CAP`) applies to the
  PQZ key only; other kinds revert `UAKemHolder(ua)`. Built in `e1b33079`, `13c74c23`.
- *KEM vector keys* [UA8-D15]: the vector KEM keys are real `ML-KEM-1024 ek ‖ X25519 pk` (1,568 + 32 B, X-Wing order) from fixed seeds; the contracts check the length only (the scheme
  is UA-7's). Built in `6f72d0ba`.
**Why.** Chat sessions (UA-7) wrap a session key to each member's KEM key; the key must be discoverable on every chain, signed by the UA, and copyable like the registration.
**Cost if wrong.** A second scheme or a revocation mechanism would change the record and the digest; several keys per UA add `addKemKey` with no layout change.
**Source.** owner, 2026-10-25 (spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-ua8-portable-registrations.md` P4, P5, P7; UA-7 spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-ua7-pq-e2e-sessions.md`); plan 2026-10-30 (A1, A4, A5, A7). Status: decided; built on branch `ua8`, not merged. UA-7 reads the key with `kemKeyOf(ua)` / `kemKeyAt(ua, version)`.

Change (2026-10-30): **the KEM key record carries a scheme id — the first byte of `kemPk`** (owner 2026-10-30; the design below is the controller's, owner may override). Rule: `kemPk = scheme byte ‖ key`. **Scheme 1** = ML-KEM-1024 + X25519 (X-Wing order): `kemPk = 0x01 ‖ ek (1,568 B) ‖ X25519 pk (32 B)` = **1,601 B**. **Scheme 2** is reserved for ML-KEM-1024 + HQC + X25519 (after FIPS 207) and is **not enabled**: the registry refuses it like any unknown id. HQC itself is not built now. Registry check order (EVM `UARegistry._checkKemPk`, every client the same): empty `kemPk` → `UAKemKeyLength(0)`; first byte not an enabled scheme (0, 2, 3 … 255) → new error `UAKemScheme(uint8 scheme)`; enabled scheme but not its exact length → `UAKemKeyLength(length)`. `kemRecordDigest` is unchanged (it already hashes `kemPk`, so the scheme byte is signed); the ABI of the existing functions is unchanged (one error added). Why: a later hybrid scheme with HQC then needs no new registry generation and no new record format — only an enabled id and its length; a registry that does not know the id refuses it, so a key of an unknown scheme is never stored. Test-only chains: no migration and no compatibility path (the 1,600-byte keys of the earlier test vectors are in `smartcontracts/vectors/ua/legacy/portable.json`). Status: decided (owner 2026-10-30); built on branch `kem-scheme` — clientkeys `90c79186`, EVM registry + forge tests + size baseline (`UARegistry` 36,868 → 37,066 B), the Rust, C, C++, Qt, Go, Python, C#, Dart and Dart-FRB clients and these docs in the later `kem-scheme:` commits; not merged (merge before the UA-Soroban registry task, whose `Kem(ua, version)` stores 1,601-byte keys). The 1,600 B of the CTR-UA-32 text above and of the earlier UA-8 spec and plan records is the pre-scheme length (history).

Change (2026-10-31, owner explicit-parameter rule; shape controller call, owner may override; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`, TS-D3, [TS-D11]): **the KEM record is typed and the key is explicit.** A record signs `uaMessage(kind, PURPOSE_KEM, typed(UAKemRecord{ua, version, scheme, kemPkHash}))`, `kemPkHash = keccak256(kemPk)` over the 1,601 assembled bytes, `scheme = kemPk[0]`; `KEM_RECORD_TAG` is legacy. Every ABI place of the key takes `struct KemKey {uint8 scheme; bytes mlkemEk; bytes32 x25519;}`: `UAAttrs.kem`, `setKemKey`, `kemKeyOf`, `kemKeyAt`, `UAKemKeySet`, `kemRecordHash`, `kemRecordDigest`. The registry assembles `scheme ‖ mlkemEk ‖ x25519` for storage and hashing, so stored bytes and digests stay those of `kemPk`. Why: the explicit-parameter rule; a key is two cryptographic objects plus a scheme id. Cost if wrong: ABI churn only, the bytes are unchanged. Status: built in typed-signing P1, P2, P3, R1.

Change (2026-10-31, owner rulings, KEM items 1–3 on the plan): **the `register` KEM key is version 0, and the key is hash-committed only when the transaction does not fit.** (1) `register` takes no KEM version (`UAAttrs.kemVersion` is gone): its key is always version 0, the first record; `setKemKey` adds versions ≥ 1. It replaces "versions start at 1" [UA8-D3], [UA8-D4]. "No KEM key" is told by the record: `UAKemRecord{ua, 0, 0, 0}` is absent, a present version-0 record has `scheme ≠ 0`; `kemKeyOf` returns the highest stored version and `kemKeyAt(ua, 0)` the `register` key; `register` no longer writes `_kemMax`. (2) Normally `register` carries the full `KemKey`. Only when the full call is over the largest calldata whose EIP-7976 floor fits the EIP-7825 cap (`REGISTER_CALLDATA_LIMIT` = 261,909 B) does the client send `attrs.kem` = scheme only and `attrs.kemPkHash = keccak256(kemPk)`; the PoP signs the same `UAKemRecord{ua, 0, scheme, kemPkHash}`. X0 found one case, an `mldsa65` UA with a PQZ key, its `R_REG` proof and a KEM key at `n2560-kmax16384`: 262,116 B in full, 260,548 B committed (1,361 B headroom), the fill 2,020 B. (3) No separate `storeKemKey`: `setKemKey(ua, 0, kem, UASig())` fills a committed key, open to anyone, `sig` must be empty, after `keccak256(kemPk) == kemPkHash` (new error `UAKemKeyHash(ua)`); version 0 not committed reverts `UAKemVersion(ua, 0)`. Until filled, `kemKeyOf` / `kemKeyAt(ua, 0)` return nothing and `checkedOf`'s `kem` is `NONE`; `registrationOf` keeps the committed form so a copy is byte-identical. The key always ends up in contract state. The registration blob drops its always-0 KEM-version word (`abi.encode(keyRest, pop)`, was UA8-D7's three fields). Why: one less argument a client can get wrong, and a registration that fits one transaction at every set. Cost if wrong: a committed key is unusable until someone fills it; clients send the two calls together. Status: built in typed-signing P1b (clientkeys, ua-rs, reproducers, wrappers, `UARegistry`), R1 (`kemPkHash`, the fill), R2; the same rule on Soroban in `ua8-soroban` B2 / B3.

Change (2026-11-01, owner ruling, whole-branch review PRV M1, option (a)): **a front-run of `register` may land the hash-commit form; clients repair it, no contract check.** The full and the hash-commit form of a KEM key sign the same `UAKemRecord`, so anyone can front-run a full `register` with the commit form of the same `pop`. No contract check is added: a calldata bound in the contract would tie it to one chain's limit. A front-run yields the same record, its hash-commit form, or a revert. Client rule: after `register`, or on `UAAlreadyRegistered`, read `registrationOf`; when `attrs.kemPkHash != 0` and `kemKeyAt(ua, 0)` is empty, send `setKemKey(ua, 0, key, UASig())`. Status: built on `typed-signing`: the contract comment and the forge tests in `8a8ecbf3`, the pure helpers clientkeys `kemRepair` and ua-rs `kem_repair` in `163f668f`; the reproducers and wrappers build the same call with their `setKemKey` builders, no helper of their own.

Change (2026-10-31, owner ruling, KEM item 4): **`setKemKey` never overwrites a stored key.** Every version, 0 included, is write-once: a version that holds a key reverts `UAKemVersion(ua, version)`, a new key always goes to a new version ≥ 1, and older versions stay readable through `kemKeyAt`, so old ciphertexts keep decrypting. No replace, delete or rotate-in-place path, on EVM and on Soroban alike. Why: never lose ciphertext; a holder of an old key must still decrypt. Cost if wrong: none found; a leaked key stays listed, as "no revocation" above. Status: built in typed-signing R1 (tests on version 0 stored by `register`, version 0 after a fill and a stored version ≥ 1); Soroban in `ua8-soroban` B3.
Change (owner 2026-11-05, confirmed 2026-11-07; plan T66a part 2; status: BUILT on EVM and Soroban, UNAUDITED): **an `msig` holds no KEM key.** Old: the KEM holders were the single PQ kinds plus a PQ-eligible `msig` (UA8-D12). New: the single PQ signing kinds only (`mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `fndsa512`, `mldsa87`, `fndsa1024`; on Soroban the first three); an `msig`, PQ-eligible or not, reverts `UAKemHolder` at `register` (a whole or a hash-committed key) and at `setKemKey`, before any signature; a PQ-eligible `msig` still holds a PQZ key. Senders seal to each accepted member's own KEM key. Vectors: `portable.json` `msig-pq/<set>` without a KEM key (`kemRecords` 15 → 12), the negatives `msig-with-kem/<set>` and `msig-kem-record` (`UAKemHolder`), `nested.json` `msig-nested-pq` without one; the old files in `smartcontracts/vectors/ua/legacy/ua-mtx-merge/t66a/`. Operators: a client on the old builders that registers an `msig` with a KEM key gets `UAKemHolder`. Commits `c33a69dd`, `a6c4cdd7`, `d9187276` (registry, builders, `ua-rs` and its bindings, the node's check), `65afdcff` (Soroban); legacy copies `a8f58ca3`.

### CTR-UA-33 — The registration event carries `popHash`; `msig` members sign without key data; WebAuthn blobs canonical only
- old: typed-signing:TS-D4 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-33 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner ruling 2026-10-30, two parts, one rule on every family (owner: never split a rule by chain kind). **A.** The
registration event — `UARegistered` on EVM, `UaRegistered` on Soroban, the equivalent on any other family that emits one —
carries `popHash = keccak256(pop)` (`keccak256("")` for an empty `pop`) instead of the `pop` bytes. `pop` stays in contract
state, readable through the existing views (`popOf`, `registrationOf`; it was already stored, CTR-UA-31), so nothing is lost;
every other `register` argument (`keyData`, `attrs`, `pqzPop`) and the three `checked` values stay in the event. **B.** In
`auth = abi.encode(MemberSig[])` (`MemberSig {uint16 index; bytes keyData; bytes sig}`) — and in the `pop`, `setKemKey` and
`setPqzKey` signatures of an `msig`, which have the same format — every **registered** member carries an **empty**
`keyData`; the registry reads the member's key from the member's own record. Native members already carried empty key data
(R12); ML-DSA and the other stored kinds already did (CTR-UA-17, `vk` at `keyPtr`). B extends "empty, read from the record"
to the classical kinds (0x0100–0x0108: `webauthn-p256`, `p256`, `ed25519`, `bip340`, `schnorr-bn254`, `schnorr-bls12381`,
`bls12381-minsig`, `bls-bn254-minsig`, `secp256k1`), which sent their key data and were checked by
`uaOf(kind, keyData) == id`. A non-empty `keyData` for a registered member is refused, as CTR-UA-17 did for ML-DSA.

As built on EVM (controller calls, owner may override): (1) a classical member's key is read from its registration blob
`_reg[ua] = abi.encode(keyRest, pop, kemVersion)` (UA8-D7: `keyRest` is the whole key data of a non-stored kind; its
`keyPtr` is 0), a stored member's from `keyPtr` as before. Only the `keyRest` bytes are read (its length word at 0x60 and
its bytes from 0x80 of chunk 0, `SSTORE2.read(ptr, start, len)`), never the blob's `pop`: a member chooses its `pop`'s
length (a `webauthn-p256` pop has no upper bound), so reading the whole blob would let one co-signer push every check of
the `msig` past the per-member bound (review fix I1). (2) The rule is tied to the purpose `member` inside
`UARegistry._derived`: `requireAuthorized(id, PURPOSE_MEMBER, digest, auth)` takes `abi.encode(bytes(""), sig)` for every
derived id and refuses key data (`UAUnauthorized`). Why tied to the purpose and not only to the `msig` path: a gen 2 hands a
member of a kind it does not enable to gen 1 through gen 1's `requireAuthorized` under `member`; with the empty key data gen 1
reads its own record, so gen 2 needs no read of gen 1's blob and no new view. Every other purpose keeps
`auth = abi.encode(keyData, sig)` for a classical kind (single-key authorization is unchanged). (3) `MSIG_MEMBER_GAS`
35,000 → 45,000: reading the member's key from storage (cold SLOADs of the blob pointers, EXTCODECOPY) raised the worst
measured member overhead (cold, `--isolate`, a member handed to gen 1) from 19,987 to 28,544 (30,599 with the first
whole-blob read); + the caller's hold for a 400 k cap (11,349) = 39,893, rounded up to 45,000 (kept from the first build:
5 k spare, and the cap calibrations below stay). `test_T_GAS_memberPopSizeFree`: members registered with a 40,000 B `pop`
cost exactly what canonical ones cost and the at-budget structures still authorize within the bound. The `msig` structure bound (register step 4) and the PQZ-holder bound
(CTR-PQZ-12) use the new figure, so a few structures right at a budget no longer fit (the largest `mldsa65` cap of the
2-of-3 PQ treasury at a 12 M budget: 5,921,000 → 5,911,000); `test_T_GAS_msigAtBudget` / `test_T_GAS_msigPqAtBudget`
authorize at the new bounds. (4) Launch note (review M4, for the 22776 checklist): a gen 2 of this code in front of a gen 1
built before CTR-UA-33 would hand `abi.encode("", sig)` under `member` and the old gen 1 would refuse every classical
member (`uaOf("") != id`); the gen-2 constructor probes gen 1's UA-8 views only. Not reachable on the test-only chains (all
redeploy together); a mainnet gen 2 must sit on a gen 1 with CTR-UA-33.

**C. WebAuthn signature blob canonical only** (owner ruling 2026-10-30, every registry). Rule: wherever a registry, or
the verifier it relies on, decodes the `webauthn-p256` signature `abi.encode(bytes authenticatorData, bytes clientDataJSON,
bytes32 r, bytes32 s)`, the input is refused unless it is byte-equal to its canonical re-encoding: head offsets 0x80 and
0x80 + 32 + pad32(len(authenticatorData)), each dynamic field = 32-byte length ‖ data ‖ zero padding, no trailing bytes.
Why: a lenient decoder gives one signature many byte strings, so a front-runner could register the same id with different
`pop` bytes and so another `popHash` (CTR-UA-07: identical record or revert), and the canonical-only `MemberSig[]` rule
(review m3) would not hold for a WebAuthn member. As built on EVM: `WebAuthnP256Verifier._fields` reads the two lengths at
their canonical places, requires the canonical total length and compares `keccak256(sig)` with the hash of the re-encoding;
it is the verifier's first check (before the rpIdHash, flags, clientDataJSON grammar and the signature), and `verify` and
`verifyPop` share it, so it covers `register`'s PoP, the portable `msig` records (KEM / PQZ key), `requireAuthorized`
(tokens, `msig` member slots). Follow-up `webauthn-clients` (owner 2026-10-30: every verifier of this blob agrees, so no
client accepts a blob a registry refuses): `SmartKeyAccount._verifyWebAuthn` (CTR-ACC-08) compares the blob with its
re-encoding right after `abi.decode` (a blob `abi.decode` cannot read reverts, which its ERC-1271 callers read as a
refusal); `clients/ua-rs` `verify` (`webauthn_fields`, also behind the C / C++ / Qt / FRB bindings, which do not export
`verify`) and the `clientkeys` reference verifier (`test/ua-verify.js` `webauthnFields`; `src/` only encodes) apply the
`_fields` rule as their first check. The pure ports (`ua-py`, `ua-go`, `ua-cs`, `ua-dart`) and `scaas-node` decode no
WebAuthn signature; the non-EVM families carry the assertion in their own formats (NEAR Borsh `Auth`, Algorand tag 4,
Aptos `u16be(len ad) ‖ ad ‖ cd`, Sui struct, Solana precompile, TON cells, Cosmos JSON), not this ABI blob, so they are
left as they are. Shared vectors: `signatures.json` `derived[0].negatives` gained the eight `abi-*` rows (old file in
`vectors/ua/legacy/webauthn-clients/`). Soroban: built on `ua-soroban` (T2b `657e71ab`, test
`webauthn_blob_canonical_only`). Test: `EccVerifiers.t.sol` `test_WebAuthnCanonicalOnly` (trailing byte, each offset
shifted, non-zero padding after each field, each length word beyond the data, fields swapped with offsets fixed up; RED on
the old decoder). Status: decided (owner 2026-10-30); built on `msig-pophash` in `80be9314`; clients, `SmartKeyAccount`,
shared vectors and the real-verifier `msig` test (review M2) on `webauthn-clients` in `7b229c98` (ua-rs), `66210ae1`
(clientkeys), `24d3df61` (SmartKeyAccount), `e3e25b35` (vectors), `4c6def75` (M2). Soroban still has to read the new rows:
`ua-registry` `src/test_verify.rs` `kind_webauthn_p256_negatives_fail` (branch `ua-soroban`).

NEAR and Algorand (inventory 2026-10-30): no UA registry and no registration event; an `msig` member there is a key id
inside the structure, never registered (no member record exists), and its signature carries its key in the family's own auth
format (NEAR Borsh `Auth`, Algorand tag 4). A and B have nothing to apply to there; no change. Cosmos, Move, Solana and TON
have no `msig` and no registry. Soroban is changed on its own branch (`ua-soroban`).

**Why.** The UA-Soroban T0 hard gate (2026-10-30) measured an `msig` of 3 ML-DSA-65 members putting 17,228 B of contract
events on Soroban, over the network's 16,384 B contract-events limit, because the registration event carried the whole `pop`
(its ML-DSA-65 member signatures, 3,309 B each). The hash keeps the event small on every family while the state keeps the bytes; empty member key
data shortens every `msig` authorization by each classical member's key and makes "the key comes from the record" one rule
for every member kind.

**Cost if wrong.** An indexer that rebuilt a registration from the log alone now also reads `popOf` (or `registrationOf`);
`msig` authorizations pay ~10 k gas more per classical member on EVM (the storage read), and the per-member bound is 10 k
higher. Test-only chains: no migration, no compatibility path; the earlier vector blobs are in
`smartcontracts/vectors/ua/legacy/msig-pophash/`.

**Source.** owner, 2026-10-30 (UA-Soroban T0 hard gate; task brief `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-30-msig-pophash/task-brief.md`).
Status: decided (owner); built on branch `msig-pophash` (not merged; merge before `ua-soroban`): vectors and the clientkeys / ua-rs reference verifiers `17357941`, EVM registry + forge tests + gas pins + size baseline (`UARegistry` 37,066 → 37,181 B; 37,365 B after fix I1) `6d7010cb`, these docs `d531f769`; the review fixes (I1 key-only read, M1, M3, M4) in the `msig-pophash fix:` commit after it.

Change (2026-10-31, owner decision 4 of 2026-10-31, derived and contract member details controller call, owner may override; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`, [TS-D4]): **a native `msig` member of a portable record signs the typed digest; members are typed.** An EOA member (code-less or the 23-byte EIP-7702 designator, its own key only) signs the digest `eth_signTypedData_v4` returns for the record, 65-byte `r ‖ s ‖ v`, low s, replacing `personal_sign(memberDigest)` (ruling C7); a contract member answers ERC-1271 `isValidSignature(typedDigest, sig)`. The structure is bound by the record's `ua`, the operation by its struct type, so the native path needs no `memberDigest`. Derived members keep `memberDigest` under `member`, unchanged. Chain-bound member authorisations (`requireAuthorized`, `UAAuth`) are unchanged (CTR-UA-24). `MemberSig[]` is passed explicitly: `registerMsig`'s `pop` and `UASig.members` are typed, never `abi.encode`d into `bytes` ([TS-D12], CTR-UA-36); the stored bytes stay `abi.encode(members)`, so `popOf` and `pqzKeySigOf` read as before, and the canonical-encoding check of review m3 falls away because the registry re-encodes what it decoded. On EVM rule B now reads `UASig.keyData` empty under `member`, where it read `abi.encode(bytes(""), sig)`. Why: an owner rule, a wallet shows the record. Cost if wrong: a wallet that cannot sign typed data cannot be a native member of a portable record. Status: built in typed-signing P1, P2, P3, P6, P7 (typed digest), R1 (`MemberSig[]`, `UASig`).

Change (2026-11-03, **owner ruling**, built on `msig-nested`; part A, EVM, kind `msig` only): an `msig` record keeps no `pop` bytes. State keeps `keccak256(pop)` of the exact bytes the registry hashed (the `abi.encode(MemberSig[])` it assembled from the typed list) and one write-once `keccak256` per slot of the `pop`, of that member's signature object (the slot's `sig`, or an `msig` member's `abi.encode(InnerSig[])`), written with the slot's accepted bit, so each member can check its own signature; `memberSigHashOf(ua, index)` returns it, gen 2 forwards it, gen 2's constructor probes it. The bytes go in one event per slot, `UAMemberSig(bytes32 indexed ua, bytes32 indexed member, uint16 index, bytes32 purpose, bytes sig)`, `purpose` = `PURPOSE_POP_V2`, in index order, before `UARegistered`; the same store and event take a later acceptance (CTR-UA-37). `popOf(ua)` keeps its selector: for an `msig` it returns the 32-byte `keccak256(pop)` as its `bytes`, empty for an empty `pop` (no hash written then), and `registrationOf`'s `pop` is the same; a reader tells by the record's kind. Single-key and derived kinds keep their `pop` in state and `popOf` returns its bytes, unchanged. "From state alone" no longer holds for an `msig`: the record is state plus its events, and a copy rebuilds the `pop` from the events in `index` order, checks each slot against `memberSigHashOf` and the whole against `popOf`, and sends `registerMsig`, which verifies. The node keeps and serves those bytes (NODE-IDX-08, SPECIFIED). Staging: every other family keeps storing an `msig`'s `pop` until its round. Two forms the owner ruled the same day and replaced, recorded so the record is whole: one whole-`pop` hash with `popOf` empty; the `pop` of every kind to a hash. Vectors: each `msig` registration row of `portable.json` and `nested.json` gains `memberSigHashes`. Measured, regular + EIP-8037 state gas, before -> after. `register` (`test_T_GAS_register_ua8PerKind`, the pins): `msig-classical` 166,104 + 1,115,370 -> 166,172 + 1,115,370 (an empty `pop`: no hash written; +68 is the dispatcher, one selector renamed); `msig-pq-native` 308,120 + 6,941,610 -> 318,100 + 1,262,250; `msig-pq/n2048-kmax1024` 3,468,184 + 83,874,600 -> 3,468,184 + 73,250,280 (the regular figure is the calldata floor's, so the log bytes do not show in it; -10,624,320 state at every set); `mldsa65#1` 387,992 + 9,232,020, unchanged. Nested (`test_registrationCostRows`, `--isolate`, n2304-kmax4096): `mldsa65 200k [16x2]`, 32 signatures, 111,040 B of `pop`: 9,226,918 + 171,757,800 -> 9,673,506 + 1,262,250; `[16x3]`, 48, 166,528 B: 14,378,528 + 257,269,500 -> 14,695,013 + 1,409,130, so it now fits a 200 M block; 16 flat slots: 4,373,284 + 88,449,300 -> 4,846,552 + 3,514,410; `slhdsa128s` 8 flat: 12,211,414 + 100,542,420 -> 12,600,386 + 2,290,410; `[1x8]`: 12,604,938 + 102,294,270 -> 13,026,362 + 2,192,490. `acceptMembership` (`test_acceptanceCostRows`): a native member, 65 B, first bit of the word: 58,776 + 97,920 with nothing kept, 97,867 + 578,340 with the bytes in SSTORE2 -> 75,621 + 195,840; an `msig` member, a two-leaf list, 384 B, a later bit: 124,083 + 0, 164,803 + 968,490 -> 144,751 + 97,920. Sizes: `UARegistry` 29,498 -> 29,429 B, `UARegistryLib` 35,596 -> 35,918 B; no token moved. Tests: `test_popMemberSigHashes`, `test_copyReplaysTheStoredAcceptance`, `test_ua8_copyFromState`, `test_nestedVectors_registrations`. Mutants, each killed: the wrong bytes hashed, the hash at the wrong index, the event without the bytes, an `msig` `pop` still stored, a second write over an index, `popOf` the hash of other bytes.

Change (2026-11-08, owner, status: decided, to be built in plan task T66b part 5 on `ua-mtx-merge`; reverses the 2026-11-03 "no `popSlotsOf`"): an `msig` record also keeps a **bitmap of the slots that signed its `pop`** (one word, written at `register`), and the registry gains the typed view `popSlotsOf(ua) → (uint16[] index, bytes32[] hash)`; `popOf` stays `keccak256(pop)`. State alone then tells which slots signed the `pop` and which accepted later, so a copier (CTR-UA-31) no longer rebuilds that set from logs; the bytes still come from the `UAMemberSig` logs or the node keeper (NODE-IDX-08). Every family: Soroban in the same task, NEAR and Algorand in their UA rounds.
Change (2026-11-08, owner; plan T66a part 5; status: BUILT on EVM and Soroban, UNAUDITED): **the `pop` slot bitmap and `popSlotsOf`, as decided above, are built.** EVM: `UAStore.Layout` slot 19 `popSlots` (appended; slots 0–18 unmoved, `UAStoreLayout.t.sol`), written once at `register`, never by `acceptMembership`; `popSlotsOf(ua) → (uint16[] index, bytes32[] hash)`, empty for an empty `pop` and any other id, gen 2 forwarding gen-1 records; `popOf` unchanged. Soroban: `Key::PopSlots(ua)`, `pop_slots_of(ua) → (Vec<u32>, Vec<BytesN<32>>)`. NEAR, Algorand: their UA rounds. Gas: `register` of `msig-pq-native` (318,601 + 1,262,250) → (330,779 + 1,360,170), the new word. Tests `test_popSlotsOfFromVectors`, `test_popSlotsOfLaterAcceptanceSetsNoPopBit`, `test_nestedVectors_popSlotsOf`. Commits `4cbe89cd`, `00414d6f`, `65afdcff`.

### CTR-UA-34 — Relayer-checked mode: a listed relayer checks what the chain cannot, the record says so, nothing it marks authorises
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-29 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-34 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Where a chain cannot verify a part of a registration (the PQ signature of `pop` or of a KEM record, the PQZ proof), the part is stored only through a listed relayer that checked it off chain, each part carries `checked = none | chain | relayer(id)`, everything needed to re-check is stored and clients re-verify, and a relayer-checked record never authorises anything on that chain. Six rules (UA-8 spec P11, owner rulings P10 and P11 of 2026-10-29); Soroban is the first family to run it, EVM does not.
**Why.** Owner 2026-10-29: the relayer must carry a share of the responsibility; the UA id is a hash of the key data, so identity is never taken on the relayer's word. Soroban's form, the changes to the spec's reading (mixed `msig` keeps `signable`, "delist" means a new registry, `KeyR`, `kem_key_at`, `checked_of`) and the open questions are in CTR-UA-34 and in the entries of `ua8-soroban` B4, B7b and B8 under NET-SOR-17.
**Cost if wrong.** A listed relayer that stores a bad record takes one write-once slot on that chain only (rule 6); wrongly relaxing rule 5 would let an unverified key authorise.
**Source.** owner 2026-10-29; the UA-8 spec P11; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-ua8-soroban.md` (U8S-D8) and the UA-8 plan Part B (UA8-D18 to D20). Status: built on Soroban, ua8-soroban B4, B6, B7b; every other family SPECIFIED in its own UA round. The `main` merge commit is added when it lands.

### CTR-UA-35 — kindName: the registry answers a kind id's name
- old: typed-signing:TS-D5 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-35 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `UARegistry.kindName(uint16 kind) external pure returns (string)` = `UAKinds.name(kind)`, in `IUARegistry`. Every id of the kind table answers, enabled or not: a name table, not an enablement view. An unknown id reverts `UAKindUnknown(kind)` (the existing behaviour of `UAKinds.name`, no new path; controller call, the owner kept this default 2026-10-31, open question 6 of the plan); an app reads a revert as "unknown".
**Why.** Owner 2026-10-31: `kind` is `uint16` only in every signed record, no string field; the name is looked up, and a public view gives an app that lookup without a copy of the table.
**Cost if wrong.** A new kind needs a new generation anyway (CTR-UA-05), so the table in the view cannot go stale on a deployed registry.
**Source.** owner 2026-10-31, plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`. Status: built in typed-signing P3 (`test_kindNameEveryKind`, `test_kindNameUnknownReverts`). No wrapper exports it: kind names stay in `kind_info`. Soroban `kind_name(kind: u32) -> String` (`KindUnknown` panic) comes in `ua8-soroban`; every other family's UA round answers it in NET-ALL-84.

### CTR-UA-36 — The registry's ABI is explicit: named typed parameters, no packed blob of several fields
- old: typed-signing:TS-D10, typed-signing:TS-D11, typed-signing:TS-D12, typed-signing:TS-D13 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-36 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner 2026-10-31, general: "every parameter is explicit, as in a REST / JSON / RPC API — no packed / opaque `bytes` that bundle several fields"; a genuine cryptographic blob stays `bytes` as its own named parameter. On the registry (shapes: controller calls, owner may override; each built in the task named):
- **`msig` [TS-D10].** `struct MsigMember {uint16 kind; bytes32 id; uint16 weight;}`, `struct MsigStructure {uint16 threshold; MsigMember[] members;}`, `registerMsig(MsigStructure structure, UAAttrs attrs, MemberSig[] pop, bytes pqzPop)`. The registry assembles the CTR-UA-09 bytes, so ids and every digest are the packed form's. `registrationOf` / `keyOf` return the packed bytes and `msigOf` the typed structure. `register(0x0120, …)` reverts `UAKeyData(0x0120)`: it has no place for `MemberSig[]`, so `msig` has one accepted form. Built in R1.
- **`KemKey` [TS-D11].** See CTR-UA-32. `UAAttrs {bytes pqzKey; bytes32 pqzPopHash; KemKey kem; bytes32 kemPkHash;}`. Built in R1.
- **`UASig` [TS-D12].** `struct UASig {bytes keyData; bytes signature; MemberSig[] members;}` replaces the `bytes auth` = `abi.encode(keyData, sig)` of `requireAuthorized`, and the `bytes sig` of `setKemKey` / `setPqzKey`: native `signature`; derived single key `keyData` (empty for stored kinds) + `signature`; `msig` `members` only, the structure from the record; any other field set is not authorized. A portable record's signature never carries `keyData`; stored bytes keep their form (`signature`, or `abi.encode(members)`). A signature that is one cryptographic object stays one `bytes signature` (owner 2026-10-31, open question 3 of the plan); ERC-1271 and Uniswap callbacks keep their ABI. Built in R1.
- **Typed key entries [TS-D13], Appendix X row 12.** `registerWebAuthn(WebAuthnKey{x, y, rpIdHash}, …)`, `registerMuSig2(uint16 kind, MuSig2Key{aggKey, memberKeys[]}, …)`, `registerFrost(uint16 kind, FrostKey{groupKey, threshold, FrostMember{commitments[], r, z}[]}, …)`, each reassembling the packed key data. Every other kind's key is one cryptographic object and stays `bytes keyData`. Built in R1b.
- **Explicit `kind` on `registerMuSig2` / `registerFrost`** (controller call, owner may override): secp256k1 and bn254 share one struct, so the entry takes the kind. Another kind, a point of the wrong length (33 B / 64 B) or a FROST member without exactly `threshold` commitments reverts `UAKeyData(kind)`; a disabled kind reverts `UAKindDisabled` first. Built in R1b.
- **`register` accepts the packed key data of `webauthn-p256` and the MuSig2 / FROST kinds too** (owner ruling 2026-10-31): for `0x0100` and `0x0110`–`0x0113` both forms are accepted, `register(kind, bytes keyData, …)` next to the typed entry; both give the same id and run the same `validateKeyData`. The explicit typed entries remain the recommended client path, and `registrationArgs` builds them. It overrides the controller call built in R1b, "packed `register` refused for these kinds, one accepted form", which was the explicit-parameter rule and no security fix. Only `msig` stays refused on `register`. Built in typed-signing R1c (643d9abd).
- **Typed views kept beside the byte views** (owner 2026-10-31): `msigOf`, `webAuthnKeyOf`, `muSig2KeyOf`, `frostKeyOf` stay next to `keyOf` / `registrationOf`, each empty for an id of another kind, forwarding gen-1 records on gen 2. Built in R1, R1b.
**Why.** A wallet, an auditor and a node read named fields; a packed blob hides which bytes are what. Selectors moved with the ABI: `register` `0x0c936361` → `0x4e229efb`, `setKemKey` `0x2d21c58e` → `0xa00cce2a`, `setPqzKey` `0xbde71760` → `0x3c6897f1`, `requireAuthorized` → `0x58d5ff4f`; new `registerMsig` `0x82b86a46`, `registerWebAuthn` `0xee03a1fe`, `registerMuSig2` `0xe1eddcdf`, `registerFrost` `0x7bd63410`; `storePqzPop` `0x7fac161a` unchanged. The node's call table has a row for each of the eight writes (`Rule::UaRegistry`; `pq_register` also reads `registerMsig`'s `pqzPop`).
**Cost if wrong.** More ABI surface and code: `UARegistry` runtime 38,152 → 46,734 B, init 53,736 B (CTR-TOK-24), and calldata of a head word per dynamic field; X0 measured it and only the case of CTR-UA-32 went over. The tokens keep `bytes auth` until Part C's C2; until then `UAKinds.uaSig` converts it (an `msig` told by `keccak256(TAG(msig) ‖ keyData) == ua`) and `PqzCore` resets the free memory pointer after the registry call, which adds about 0.9 KB per token (`WrappedPqzToken` 62,616 B of the 65,536 B ceiling at R1); C2 removes both.
**Source.** owner 2026-10-31, plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md` (TS-D10–TS-D13, Appendix X). Status: built in typed-signing R1, R1b, R2 (reproducers, wrappers, `e2e.py`, node call table). Legacy: `smartcontracts/evm/legacy/typed-signing/IUARegistryPacked.sol`, `IUARegistryPackedKeys.sol`. Soroban's explicit arguments come in `ua8-soroban`.

### CTR-UA-37 — Listing in an `msig` is no consent: a member accepts, and only accepted members count at verify
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-02 · normative: contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-37 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Owner 2026-11-02: registration stays as it is (a threshold signs a PQ-eligible `msig`, a classical-dominant one has an empty `pop`), each member may confirm later, and at verify only accepted members count. `msigOf` makes no claim that a member agreed; `memberAccepted(ua, index)` does; wallets and explorers show listed and accepted apart. `acceptMembership(ua, MemberSig{index, "", sig})`: anyone submits, the member signs the portable `UAMembership{ua, member}` (typehash `0x2ffb61cab130ef54f9af88d7255ca81c570651b2562c2c368286a1f43bfe5cb4`), a native member the typed digest or ERC-1271 over it, a derived member `memberDigest` under `member` with `PURPOSE_MEMBERSHIP`. One bitmap slot per `msig` (`Layout.accepted`, slot 15), written at registration from the stored `pop`; an empty `pop` writes nothing. Every verification but the registration's own `pop` refuses a `MemberSig` of an unaccepted slot, however good its signature. **Owner's correction of the same day: on a registry with this rule, until the accepted weight reaches the threshold the `msig` can authorize nothing, on any contract, for any purpose: payments, mandates, roles, orders, keys, records; a client computes the accepted weight from `msigOf` and `memberAccepted`, shows the `msig` as not active, and does not name it as a signer, party, role holder or payer until then** (SCaaS is not only tokens: this replaced a sentence about wallets taking funds). No decline, no leave: the id derives from the structure. No revoke: it could drop a held `msig` below its threshold and lock what it holds; the owner may add it later.
- **Scope (owner 2026-11-02).** Built on EVM. Soroban's twin is in progress on `ua8-soroban`. NEAR takes the rule in its own UA round: no registry, its `msig` counts member weight with no acceptance today. Algorand takes the rule in its own UA round: no registry, its `msig` counts member weight with no acceptance today.
- **Generations (controller, owner may override).** A gen-1 record on gen 2 is settled as `setKemKey` (UA8-D11): the bits live with the record, `acceptMembership` there is `UAUnauthorized`, the member accepts on gen 1; `memberAccepted` forwards, the verify is handed on, and `setPqzKey` on a gen 2 hosting the record asks gen 1 slot by slot, a failed call being `UAVerifyGas`, never a verdict.
- **Gas (controller, owner may override).** The read is once per authorization, so it is its own term of the registration bound, `MSIG_ACCEPTED_GAS = 2,500` (measured +2,236: `requireAuthorized`, `msig` 2-of-2, 49,634 -> 51,870), not `MSIG_MEMBER_GAS`. A record held here is one read in `UARegistry._msig` and one in `UARegistryLib._msig`, no call per member. A gen 2 hosting a gen-1 record pays one call to gen 1 per slot, 6,055 gas the first and 1,146 the next (`test_membershipGen2HostCallCost`): gen 1 has no getter for the word, and it is a write paying its own gas, outside `verifyBudget`. The largest treasury `mldsa65` cap the bound admits moves 5,911,000 -> 5,910,000. Sizes: `UARegistry` 27,997 -> 28,429 B, `UARegistryLib` 31,358 -> 32,667 B; `WrappedPqzToken` unchanged.
- **Names (controller, owner may override).** `acceptMembership`, `memberAccepted`, `UAMembershipAccepted`, `UAMembership`, `scaas.ua.purpose.membership.v1`. The node relays it as a ninth registry write, so a member needs no gas.

**Why.** A member could be listed without knowing it, and a classical-dominant `msig` then signs with a name that never agreed. A signature on chain from the member is the only evidence a contract can check; a bit keeps the verify at one read and never parses `pop`.

**Cost if wrong.** A `msig` with no `pop` is unusable until enough weight accepted, on each chain it is registered on: by design. `requireAuthorized` of an `msig` costs +2,236 gas; single-key kinds pay nothing (`PQZ_DEBIT_MIN_GAS` moved -88 only because two new selectors reordered the dispatcher: `requireAuthorized` 8 -> 6 comparisons, -44 on each of its two calls). No revoke means a member who regrets stays counted until a new structure replaces the old.

**Source.** owner 2026-11-02, brief `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-31-typed-signing/task-MA-brief.md`. Status: built in typed-signing Task MA on EVM, clients and node; Soroban's twin in progress on `ua8-soroban`; NEAR in its own UA round; Algorand in its own UA round.

Change (2026-11-03, **owner ruling**, built on `msig-nested`): the acceptance signature is kept in state. The spec review found that a `pop` using a slot of an inner `msig` accepted by `acceptMembership` could not be copied on its bytes alone: the bit is per registry and the signature was in no record. `acceptMembership` now stores it, SSTORE2, `acceptSig[ua][index]`, slot 16 of `UAStore.Layout`, write-once with its bit: `sig`, or an `msig` member's `abi.encode(InnerSig[])`; `membershipSigOf(ua, index)` returns it; a third party replays it on another registry, with no new signature. Slots of the `pop` stay exempt. Cost: a native acceptance 58,776 + 97,920 -> 97,867 + 578,340 regular + state gas; a two-leaf inner list 124,083 + 0 -> 164,803 + 968,490. `UARegistry` 29,211 -> 29,498 B and `UARegistryLib` 34,452 -> 35,596 B against the prototype, with the other review fixes. No registry layout pin exists; `test/v2/layout/` covers the tokens.
