### CTR-PQZ-27 — PQZ verifier mode: PRECOMPILE or OFFCHAIN, chosen per token at creation, immutable
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-27 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A PQZ token (kinds 4, 5, 12, 13) takes `ConfidentialConfig.pqzVerifyMode` at creation and never changes it: `PRECOMPILE` (0, the default, today's behaviour) or `OFFCHAIN` (1: a `PqzVerdict` signed by the token's verifier UA counts as a verified proof). No chain detection: a PRECOMPILE token without the precompile refuses as before (`UAVerifyGas`), an OFFCHAIN token never calls the precompile, on any chain. OFFCHAIN replaces soundness by trust in the named verifier UA; maximum loss `min(totalShielded, maxShielded) · shieldScale` public units (on 5 / 13 that much underlying in escrow). Authorization (CTR-PQZ-12), ciphertexts in state and the confidentiality of honestly formed data are unchanged; the PQZ verifier (off-chain) reads public bytes only and decrypts nothing (ARCH-POS-13). The Hedera env refusal stays in both modes. **UNAUDITED.**
**Status.** Contracts BUILT (T44 + T45 `2cce490d`): the three fields, byte 22 of `scaas.pqz` slot 0, the zero-dep release, OFFCHAIN init, `script/pqz/e2e.py`'s zero-dep form. The node (T47 `75ddccc4`, `fd2dfb2f`, `e50251b4`, `b3b31560`, `062133b6`), `clientkeys` (T46 `134560c1`, `e452b88f`, `8563eb78`) and the PQZ verifier (off-chain) (T48 `06e11d23`, `5d4a2780`): BUILT. Invariants T49 `9d7c2576`.
**Why.** O1: the mode exists for chains without the precompile, and "the same rule applies on every chain"; the default stays "option 1: not working". O2: in OFFCHAIN mode the proof is verified off chain and a verifier UA's signature counts as a verified proof. R1: PQZ only. R4: the maximum loss is stated (Fable P1-2).
**Cost if wrong.** A verifier that signs a false proof fabricates a balance under a UA it controls and drains the pool up to the maximum loss; a verifier that stops signing freezes every confidential balance of its token.
**Source.** Owner rulings O1, O2, R1, R4 (2026-11-06); names (owner 2026-11-07); spec [superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-attested-verify.md](superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-attested-verify.md) §2 (AV-1), §3 (AV-2), §10 rows 1, 7, 9; reviews [Codex](research/attest-codex-review.md), [Fable](research/attest-fable-review.md); threat T27 ([pq-zero-knowledge.md §12](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#threats)).

Change (owner 2026-11-11, group 3t, [CTR-PQZ-36](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36); status: BUILT on `ua-mtx-3t`, UNAUDITED): `ConfidentialConfig` gains `verifierFee` and `verifierFeeMax` (`OFFCHAIN` only; a `PRECOMPILE` token refuses a non-zero value with `PqzVerifyConfigInvalid()`), and the trust model shown at creation, in wallets and before a shield adds the fee, its cap and a pending increase. The maximum loss is unchanged: the verifier's fees leave the pool only as `totalShielded` falls.

### CTR-PQZ-28 — The verifier UA: kinds, frozen shape, fixed or transferable with notice, immediate revocation
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-28 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A verifier is accepted at init and at a proposal only if it is a native EOA (no code but the EIP-7702 designator), `secp256k1`, `p256`, `webauthn-p256`, `mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, or a one-level `msig` of those: kinds verifiable without a SCaaS precompile; a derived one must be registered on this chain. Its shape is frozen at assignment and recomputed on every OFFCHAIN check. Fixed: no transfer, no revocation. Transferable: the owner proposes, waits the factory's `noticePeriod()` (stored at init), and the same proposer confirms in the same owner generation; the epoch moves on every assignment. The owner may revoke a transferable verifier at once (freeze only). No governance bit; relayed through the `GovernanceRouter`, fee mode `NONE`.
**Status.** BUILT (T44 + T45 `2cce490d`: bodies, shape, events, the stubs, `pqzVerifyConfig()`, the router ops; the node's router rows T47 `75ddccc4`, `fd2dfb2f`, `e50251b4`, `b3b31560`, `062133b6`).
**Why.** O2: a fixed or transferable verifier chosen at init; a transfer changes the trust model, so it goes through governance and waits the notice. R4: revocation stops the trust root, never moves it, so it needs no notice. Q1 (owner 2026-11-06): **no** revocation of a fixed verifier ("fixed" means no owner power over it). C2: the mode is for chains without the precompiles, so its check needs none. C3 (Codex #2): a native slot that gains code or a slot accepted later must not change the policy without the notice. C4: moving the trust root is an ownership-level act; the governance pending runs on `grantDelay`, not the notice, so no bit of the SCaaS band is taken (Q4).
**Cost if wrong.** A verifier changed without notice re-opens the drain of CTR-PQZ-27; a lost fixed verifier freezes its token's confidential balances for ever (disclosed at creation).
**Source.** Owner rulings O2, R4, Q1 (2026-11-06); controller calls C2, C3, C4 in the approved spec; spec §4 (AV-3, AV-4), §10 rows 11, 12 (applied as they stand); 3e Q9 (the factory's notice period, set once by `configureChain`, CTR-TOK-29).

### CTR-PQZ-29 — The inline verdict: PqzVerdict last on every proof-carrying entry
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-29 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The verifier signs typed EIP-712 `PqzVerdict(address token,uint256 chainId,bytes32 proofSystemId,bytes32 statementHash,bytes32 proofHash,uint32 pqzVerifierEpoch,uint64 validUntil)` in the token's own domain under `PURPOSE_PQZ_VERDICT`; it travels as `PqzSignedVerdict pqzVerdict`, the last parameter of every proof-carrying entry (twelve on kinds 5, 13; ten on 4, 12) and of the verdict form of `verifyTransferAmount`, outside every `UA*` struct. PRECOMPILE tokens never read it. OFFCHAIN `_check` recomputes both hashes, checks the verifier, its shape and every field against storage and what it rebuilt, then the signature through `requireAuthorized`; nothing is stored. The verdict-less disclosure answers "cannot verify" (`PqzVerdictRequired()`) on an OFFCHAIN token.
**Status.** BUILT (T44 + T45 `2cce490d`: `_check`, the typehash pin, `PURPOSE_PQZ_VERDICT`, the entries, the disclosure form, `mtxSelectors()`, `selector_audit.json`; the measured effects ruled by the owner 2026-11-08, `9e23a3dc`: the verdict is the stack fallback `PqzSignedVerdict`, one parameter `pqzVerdict`, last, its empty encoding 480 B on a PRECOMPILE debit, kept (the array form `PqzSignedVerdict[]` considered and withdrawn the same day); the split-overhead bounds raised, PQZL 8,000 → 9,000 and PQZH 10,000 → 13,000 (`MtxSplitOverhead.t.sol`); a known limit of `n2048-kmax1024`, PQZH op 7 commit-reveal M = 4 without the auditor paid by an `mldsa65` UA, 16,786,328 > 2^24, M ≤ 3). Vectors file `verdict.json` and `clientkeys` BUILT (T46 `134560c1`, `e452b88f`, `8563eb78`); node BUILT (T47 `75ddccc4`, `fd2dfb2f`, `e50251b4`, `b3b31560`, `062133b6`). Left open by the owner then: `test_splitOverhead_dataSizeBound` measured 13,039 (`mldsa65`) and 13,055 (`fndsa512`) above the 13,000 bound at `n2304-kmax4096`; T66b's bounds (owner 2026-11-09: PQZL 99,000, PQZH 335,000) cover them.
**Why.** R2: no verdict book; the verdict inline as the last parameters, one `requireAuthorized` in `_check` with the existing `UAVerifyGas` shape, outside the subject's typed struct so no typehash moves. Codex #1: the epoch is signed, so a signature dies at every verifier change, A → B → A included. C1: `statementHash` over the exact bytes the token builds, field-by-field binding. The pair is one struct because the legacy code generator ran out of stack: the spec's sanctioned fallback (§5.3 "Stack"; the 3e `RelayPay` precedent), still explicit.
**Cost if wrong.** A verdict that fits another statement, proof, token, chain or epoch would accept a proof nobody checked.
**Source.** Owner ruling R2 (2026-11-06); owner 2026-11-08 (the measured effects); spec §5 (AV-5), §10 rows 5, 6, 8; Codex #1, #3, #7 and Fable P1-4 (closed by R2), Fable (a).

Change (owner 2026-11-11, group 3t, [CTR-PQZ-36](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36); status: BUILT on `ua-mtx-3t`, UNAUDITED): the statement a verdict hashes carries the verifier fee in its `fee` word, so a `VerifierFeeSet` makes every statement built before it stale: the op refuses (`AuthRejected`, and with a re-signed `pqzAuth` `PqzVerdictMismatch(3)`) and the holder re-proves; `PqzVerdict` and its typehash are unchanged.

### CTR-PQZ-30 — OFFCHAIN tokens accept unproven PQZ keys of the set length; the verifier checks them off chain
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-30 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** In OFFCHAIN mode every key read of a PQZ op (sender, recipients, auditor, shields, op 7 legs, rollover and prepare) and the auditor check at init take a stored key of this set's exact length, `proven` not required; PRECOMPILE requires `proven` as before. The PQZ verifier (off-chain) signs only when every key the statement names has its `pqzPop` bytes stored, its `R_REG` proof verifies over that path's and that version's message, and no other UA or version holds the same key; its cache is keyed by `(ua, version, pqzKeyHash)`.
**Status.** Contracts BUILT (T44 + T45 `2cce490d`); the verifier's checks BUILT (T48 `06e11d23`, `5d4a2780`).
**Why.** R3: an OFFCHAIN token accepts unproven keys; the verifier checks the `R_REG` proof and single ownership off chain. Given up (Fable (b)): `keyOwner` uniqueness and the `0x0142` list are not chain-readable for these holders; CTR-PQZ-12's holder rule stays the registry's at store time. 3g KV-12 (owner-approved 2026-11-06) adds the version to the check and the cache key.
**Cost if wrong.** A key nobody proved could take credits it can never spend; a duplicate key could carry a verdict to another account (closed on chain by 3g's per-UA marker and pairwise `KeyReused`).
**Source.** Owner ruling R3 (2026-11-06); spec §6 (AV-6), §10 row 4; 3g spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-key-versions.md` §5 (KV-12) and §10 row 11.

### CTR-PQZ-31 — PQZ state per (ua, version): credits to current, a stale version only migrates
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-31 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** PQZ state is kept per `(ua, version)`, `sendCounter` per UA (slot 12); credits go to the recipient's `current` version, read once (KV-7); debits name `keyVersion` after `fromUA` (captured once); a stale version only migrates (op 1 to the UA itself) or refreshes (`StaleKeyVersion`), above `current` `KeyVersionUnknown`, a transfer to oneself at `current` `SelfTransfer`, a key repeated between the parties `KeyReused`; `mtxRollOver(bytes32,uint64,uint256)` / `mtxPrepareAcc(bytes32,uint64,uint256)` (100 bytes static; the rollover reads no key, the prepare's key check covers it); `PqzRolledOver`, `Credited` / `Debited` with the version; the disclosure takes `keyVersion` (KV-11: it selects the key checked, it does not attest which version a leg was for).
**Status.** BUILT (T52 `7e8e2e6f`, `612971bd`, T53 `455f3e04`; invariants J1–J6, J9, J10 in `test/pqz/invariant/PqzVer{Handler,Invariants}.t.sol`, T56 `e1336e60`, 32 runs × 40 calls at the four sets, 48 mutants over T51–T56 killed). `ROLL_MAX` at `n2560-kmax16384` 12,581,335 gas, 1,577 under 0.75 · 2^24 (at 3g). Additive sender recovery BUILT as a reference test (`pqz-core/ffi/tests/recover_versions.rs`, trials `n + 2·m·n`); the wallet's own is `ua-rs`'s (SPECIFIED). Interface ids at 3g: `IPqzToken` 0xd37edfc5, `IZetherToken` 0xe65bc5f0 (PQZ no longer answers the 68-byte forms; `mtxRollOver(bytes32,uint256)` moved to `IZetherToken`). Sizes at 3g (history, before the T66b body modules): `NormalPqzToken` 47,714 B, `WrappedPqzToken` 57,026, kind 13 64,522 → 64,996, `PqzTransferLib` 19,724, `PqzBurnLib` 10,697. UNAUDITED.
**Why.** Owner rulings O1–O7 and R1–R6 of 2026-11-06: a UA keeps its id when its PQZ key rotates (an operator change, a share holder leaving); one rule on every chain; never lose ciphertext.
**Cost if wrong.** A credit to a stale version would strand funds under a retired key; a debit under the wrong version would spend another key's state.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-06 (O1–O7, R1–R6); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-key-versions.md` §3, §4, §10 rows 4–8, 17, 21, 23, §12 (KV-6 … KV-11).

### CTR-PQZ-32 — No version word in a PQZ statement or transcript
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-06 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-32 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The statement and the transcript carry no key-version word: the statement binds the key bytes; the `proofSystemId` is unchanged; migration confidentiality assumes honest, independent keys.
**Status.** BUILT by absence: the pqz vectors' statements are unchanged (J8, checked by the vectors).
**Why.** A version word would change every relation and need a new `proofSystemId` and a full gate for nothing the key bytes do not already bind.
**Cost if wrong.** Two versions with the same key bytes would be indistinguishable to a proof; closed by the registry's per-UA marker and the token's pairwise `KeyReused`.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-06; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-key-versions.md` §4, §12 (KV-13); research §7.3 (R1: no `keyVersion` in `PqzAuth`).

### CTR-PQZ-33 — Debit record: every pending slot kept, one record per debit
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-33 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Pending slots are never deleted (PP-1): no debit, rollover or clear deletes one. Each debit `(ua, k)` writes one record (`w0`, and `w1` when wide) naming its predecessor blob, `p`, `Δp`, the `proofStore` mode, and when wide `shieldIn`, `keyVersion`, `prevCounter`; the account's `lastDebit` is `k`; `T_k` is rebuilt from the one record (`T = prevBlob's (u, v_f) + Σ pending[p − Δp, p) + Trivial(shieldIn)`). View `pqzDebitRecord(ua, k)` → `DebitRecordView`.
**Status.** BUILT (T58 `201d4c95`, `e35d1d16`; invariants T64 `f2bd37ba`; integration with real proofs T65 `7d653925`). UNAUDITED. Readings (controller 2026-11-09, owner may override): `lastDebit` sits literally in the account slot 3g's `sendCounter` left (inner slot 2), which moves `accHash` / pending / `accWords` back by one (T52 had compacted them); `deltaP`'s build check is `K_MAX − 1 ≤ 65,535` (`PqzSet.DELTA_P_MAX`, a uint16 from `gen_set.py`): a first debit's `p` reaches `K_MAX − 1` by the units rule, so the spec's `K_MAX − 2` bound holds only for later debits. **`ROLL_MAX` open (owner):** the owner ruled a move to 112 / 96 / 64 / 48 on 2026-11-09 and reversed it the same day; `ROLL_MAX` stays 96 / 80 / 64 / 32 (`n2048-kmax1024` / `n2304-kmax4096` / `n2560-kmax16384` / `n2816-kmax65536`) until the owner decides; no Change line for a move. Since T58 a rollover deletes nothing, so `ROLL_MAX` is no longer the largest multiple of 16 under 0.75 · 2^24 for a relayed full transaction (the 2026-10-27 rule): at `n2304-kmax4096` `ROLL_MAX + 16` costs 12,536,214 ≤ 12,582,912. `test_gas_rollMax_relayedFullTx` (in `MtxSplitOverheadTest` and `PqzStatePinGasTest`) is the one known red at `n2048-kmax1024`, `n2304-kmax4096` and `n2816-kmax65536`, green at `n2560-kmax16384`; no test, pin or bound was edited to make it green.
**Why.** O1, R1: a holder or auditor must be able to rebuild any past debit's statement from state; deleting slots made the history unrecoverable.
**Cost if wrong.** State grows by the kept slots (one 32 B slot per credit) plus one or two words per debit; a rebuild without the record would need logs that EIP-4444 lets expire.
**Source.** Owner rulings O1, R1 (2026-11-07); controller calls C1, C2 and the 2026-11-09 readings; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-proof-path.md` §2, §9, §12; Change lines on plan 5h D4 (`_debit`'s deletion) and D8 (the rollover's), on CTR-PQZ-07; the state spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-pqz-state-redesign.md` §5.5's deletion no longer holds.

### CTR-PQZ-34 — ownTag and the key-version tail on every own debit, bound by memoHash
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-34 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every own debit carries `ownTag` (PP-3, the holder's HMAC over `chainUid ‖ token ‖ fromUA ‖ be32(sendCounter) ‖ keccak256(P(u) ‖ P(v_f))` under a key derived from the debited version's PQZ seed with label `PQZ/owntag/v1`; the contract checks no value); the op blob's tail is `ownTag ‖ kv(8·n) ‖ u8(n)`; `memoHash = keccak256(memo ‖ ownTag)` (HASH: `memo = salt ‖ sealedMemo`; BUNDLE, burn, refresh, unwrap: `keccak256(ownTag)`, were 0).
**Status.** BUILT (T59 `2a1f9d5e`, `0cc72669`, `90d857af`; node T63 `39fa296c`). `typed_ops.json`: the six PQZ debit rows `release: "3h"` (typehashes moved; relayer and fee recipient unbound at fee 0). `pq_kat.json`: the `ownTag` KAT (label `PQZ/owntag/v1`, versions 0 and 1) and the `memoHash` rows, shared with the no-oracle spec (C4). The no-oracle spec's §4.10 (a BUNDLE op 7 has `memoHash = 0`) holds for releases before 3h; a 3h release (C9) uses C3's formula; that spec carries its own Change line, and its reserved `ownTag` label is C4's. UNAUDITED.
**Why.** O2, R2: a holder recognises its own debits and their key versions from state alone, without a decryption oracle (ARCH-POS-13).
**Cost if wrong.** A client on the old formula computes another `memoHash` on a 3h release and its debit is refused; clients probe `proofStore()` to tell the release apart.
**Source.** Owner rulings O2, R2 (2026-11-07); controller calls C3–C5; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-pqz-proof-path.md` §3, §12.

### CTR-PQZ-35 — proofStore: NONE or LOG
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-07 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-35 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `ConfidentialConfig.proofStore` (after `pqzVerifierFixed`), 0 NONE / 1 LOG, `ProofStoreInvalid(uint8)` for 2 and above, slot 0 byte 23; the record's byte keeps the mode of its debit; under LOG every debit (op 1, op 7, burn, refresh, unwrap; PQZL and PQZH; PRECOMPILE and OFFCHAIN) emits one `PqzDebitProof(address indexed blob, bytes32 indexed ua, uint64 indexed sendCounter, bytes header, bytes proof)`. A non-PQZ kind refuses a set value (`ConfigFieldForOtherKind(4)`: plain kinds in `MetaTokenBase`, Zether on `ZetherLib`'s 3f line). The issuer changes it under bit 24 `PQZ_PROOF` (CTR-GOV-22). SSTORE2 for proofs dropped (owner 2026-11-07; spec Appendix A).
**Status.** BUILT (T60 `6dbb5d3d`, `c9e9575c`). `ZetherLib` +37 B kept (controller 2026-11-09: the one-condition refusal on the 3f line, `test_proofStore_zether_refused`): the Zether statement, vectors and gas pins unchanged (test/zether 441 passed; the eight plus-zero Zether rows as at `7558a364`: 86,106 / 86,084 / 69,133 / 69,133 / 46,434 / 46,456 / 142,438 / 142,450; invariant P7). The unsupported combinations (O13) are the table of [pq-zero-knowledge.md](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#pqz-unsupported), the wizard refuses them; one row is new under LOG (controller 2026-11-09): `n2560-kmax16384` PQZL op 7 M = 8 without the auditor, direct, 11,436,623 + 52,849,260 = 64,285,883 > the SCaaS testnet node's 64 M `max_gas_per_tx` (NONE 10,728,387 + 52,849,260 = 63,577,647 fits). Change note on spec §5's claim ("NONE and LOG fit wherever today's forms fit"): refuted for that row, holds for the other 281 of 282 pairs; 2^24 holds for every PQZL row under LOG; PQZH LOG costs 0 regular (the EIP-7976 floor hides it). UNAUDITED.
**Why.** O3, O9: an issuer may choose to keep every proof in the logs for audits, at a gas price; NONE costs nothing new.
**Cost if wrong.** A LOG token can hold a large debit in the node's queue (`PROOF_STORE_OVER_LANE_CAP`, NODE-JOB-24) until the issuer sets NONE or the job expires.

### CTR-PQZ-36 — The verifier fee: an OFFCHAIN token pays its verifier UA from the fee word, capped, raised only with notice
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-11 · normative: contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** (Summary; the normative text is [pq-zero-knowledge.md](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36).) An `OFFCHAIN` PQZ token (kinds 4, 5, 12, 13) adds its `verifierFee` once to every proof-carrying debit's `fee` word, `txFee + verifierFee + M·d`, and pays it from `SHIELD_POOL` to the current verifier UA; the immutable `verifierFeeMax` caps it; the admin lowers it at once and raises it only after the stored notice (`setVerifierFee`, `mtxSetVerifierFee`); on an `OFFCHAIN` token the direct binding word binds the fee in force.
**Status.** BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3t`, UNAUDITED (group 3t T0-T11; built beside 3s, merged by the controller at `0d6bc40c`): the contracts (config, init rows, the fee word, the payout and its regulated check, `TAG_DIRECT_MODE_VF`, `setVerifierFee`, the view, `mtxSetVerifierFee`), the tests of spec §15 (1)-(12), the invariants, real proofs at `fee ± 1`, `verifier_fee.json`, `typed_ops.json`, clientkeys, ua-rs, the node (the router row, `args.pqz_fee` and its pre-check, the `AuthRejected` / `PqzVerdictMismatch(3)` mapping after an indexed `VerifierFeeSet`, the indexer rows and the `pqz_verifier_fee` stamp), `scaas-pqz-verifier`'s `FEE_WORD_MISMATCH`, the matrix group `pqoff` (local run in the stacked gate), the mutants and the component docs (`smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-11-ua-mtx-3t/summary.txt`, `mutants.txt`). The normative text moved to [pq-zero-knowledge.md](contracts/pq-zero-knowledge.md#CTR-PQZ-36) (Fable P3-7(c)). Before: SPECIFIED; nothing built; the build follows 3s. Controller calls of 2026-11-11 under the owner's leave of 2026-11-10 (quoted under Source; spec §18, §19), tagged in the Rule: (1) the unit: `verifierFee` and `verifierFeeMax` are in shielded units, like `confidentialFee` and the fee word, and the payout is `verifierFee · shieldScale` public units; this interprets the ruling's "public units": at `shieldScale ≠ 1` the number a creator types is the public price divided by `shieldScale`; (2) the init range row uses the cap, so the setter checks only `next ≤ verifierFeeMax`; (3) a decrease during a pending increase cancels it (the `VerifierFeeProposed` is superseded, `VerifierFeeSet` is emitted); (4) the ruling's English rewrite of one `MetaTxLib.sol` comment leaves this item for a separate cleanup of the Vietnamese comments in `smartcontracts/evm/src` and `scaas-node/src`. Fable review 2026-11-11 (at `47cf777d`): approve with changes, no P0, 1 P1, 2 P2, 9 P3; every call decided by the controller under the same leave and applied in the spec (§19): the direct binding of `vf` (P1-1), the cancel by the current value (P3-1), the notice's limit disclosed (P2-2), `pqz_fee` optional on `PRECOMPILE` jobs and one source for the word off chain (P3-4).
**Why.** A verifier UA that checks every proof off chain is a paid service; its fee comes from the debit it verifies, through the fee word the proof already binds, so no relation moves and the pool pays out only what a hidden balance lost. The immutable cap bounds what an admin can take from holders, and is the price a holder accepts at shield; the notice helps only while the verifier keeps answering, so it protects against an admin who does not control the verifier.
**Cost if wrong.** An admin can raise every debit's cost to the cap after the notice (at once where the notice is 0, and within the notice too if it controls the verifier); dust below the fee cannot leave without a `shieldIn` top-up; a fee change, a decrease included, strands every op built before it; on 12, 13 a frozen, KYC-lapsed or listed-out verifier halts every debit while the fee is not 0, with no relief under admin 0.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-11, in chat, on the controller's proposal of the same day: "OK, vậy đi" (OK, go with it). Owner ruling 2026-11-11 on the Fable review's P2-1 (replacing the controller call on it), verbatim: "Giữ cách hiện tại. Vì nếu verifier bị chặn, họ không verify các giao dịch nữa thì cũng bị khóa như nhau." (keep the current way: if the verifier is blocked, it verifies no more transactions and the token is locked just the same): the verifier fee stays a direct payout to the verifier UA with its regulated checks (CTR-AS-25); on 12, 13 a blocked verifier halts debits while the fee is not 0, accepted and disclosed (T31). The controller's additions of the same day, after the owner asked whether `SHIELD_POOL` can be drained by continuous confidential transfers: the verifier fee is inside the proved fee, `totalShielded` and the pool move together, the invariant test, and the drain row (a lying verifier is the only path, bounded by the maximum loss of CTR-PQZ-27). The controller's calls (1) to (4) and the review calls, under the owner's leave of 2026-11-10: "tự động làm, không cần hỏi nữa" (do it automatically, no need to ask again). The owner on the review's size finding, 2026-11-11: "Hỏi trước khi tách." (ask before splitting; recorded under CTR-TOK-30). Spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-verifier-fee.md` §1, §3 to §9, §18, §19.

### CTR-PQZ-80 — PqzMetaTx: own mixin with op arguments sliced from calldata
- old: — · status: superseded · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: — · superseded-by: CTR-PQZ-21

**What it said.** `PqzToken` relayed through its own mixin `PqzMetaTx` with an `_executeOp` reading `m.data` as calldata slices (no self-call, `m.to = m.value = 0` else `PqzOpNotCanonical`), nonce spent with the fee after verify.

## 26. Networks — common model

### NET-ALL-01 — Pruning families keep executed lanes for H
- old: CR-PD-4(pruning), CR-R3-8(pruning) · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-01 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Families that prune executed lane state keep an executed lane for at least the horizon H after the op's `validUntil`.
**Why.** At-most-once payment per request holds only while the executed lane is remembered: GRAM measures `validUntil` from execution, not from lane creation, so state pruned earlier than the issuance horizon would let a sibling signature on the same lane execute again. The prune delays equal the 30-day horizon today, so ERP-issued terms are safe.
**Cost if wrong.** Issuers that sign terms on a lane beyond H get no pay-once guarantee.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md) line 901; [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 700.

### NET-ALL-02 — Contract-level meta-tx default on every network
- old: R30, UD:§1:eip1776, UD:§21.5 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-02 · superseded-by: —

Change: on EVM and Hedera the gateway runs a transfer, a payment or an allowlisted self-call of the token itself, never a call to another contract; signature-authorised entry points are named `mtx…`. Source add: §2 A1–A3, §3 MG-1, MG-3.
Change (2026-10-08): `mtxExecute` runs only allowlisted self-calls and token transfers/payments are `MetaTransfer`s (CTR-MTX-23); the non-EVM families sign the same two kinds (NET-ALL-26) and name signed entries `mtx` in their case (NET-ALL-28). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-1, NM-2.

### NET-ALL-03 — Head-of-line table and anti-lock test
- old: R62 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-05 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-03 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every adapter states how it avoids head-of-line blocking, and every family passes the anti-lock test.
**Why.** A sequence is strictly ordered, so one stuck transaction (fee below the mempool floor, or a nonce gap) blocks everything queued behind it; with a single key that means a dead relayer until someone intervenes, and one key also caps throughput at about one transaction per block.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 535.; [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 1538

### NET-ALL-04 — One WebAuthn grammar for every family
- old: CR-R3-1(grammar), RS4-2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** One WebAuthn rule and one bounded `clientDataJSON` grammar for every family.
**Why.** Verifiers had drifted apart: on Cosmos any page that could get an assertion for the rpId (a sibling subdomain, a related origin, a delegated iframe) could sign any operation, GRAM accepted any origin extending the stored one as a prefix, and elsewhere a cross-origin iframe yields assertions that carry the relying party's origin.
**Cost if wrong.** Cosmos dev passkey addresses change.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 630; [history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md](history/plans/2026-10-03-r3-passkey-seed.md) line 15.

### NET-ALL-05 — Key lifecycle stated per family
- old: CR-R3-6 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-05 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Key rotation and recovery are stated per family; every gap is listed, never implied away.
**Why.** The families do not offer the same lifecycle: a Cosmos passkey account is one key with no rotation, the Soroban guardian is only a seam, and a GRAM passkey cannot rotate and has no guardian, so a single blanket claim would hide real gaps.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 679.
Change (2026-10-08): EVM rotation runs through `mtxExecute` signed by the account (CTR-ACC-10). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-metatx-generic-call-design.md` §3 GC-6.

### NET-ALL-06 — Indexer filters registered contracts; empty stalls
- old: net-aptos:L1, net-solana:L1 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-06 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The indexer filters by the registered contracts in the family's own address form, and an empty list never advances the cursor.
**Why.** The Cosmos, Sui and GRAM reviews found indexers reading a static or wrongly formatted contract list; an indexer that advances with an empty or mismatched list moves past ranges it never really scanned.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 37; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 41.

### NET-ALL-07 — e2e fakes return real token ids
- old: net-aptos:L2, net-solana:L2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** End-to-end fakes return real token ids and refuse unregistered emitters.
**Why.** The GRAM and Hedera reviews found end-to-end tests that passed against fakes; a copy of the contract deployed elsewhere emits identical events, and only a fake that returns the real token ids and refuses strangers proves the indexer drops them.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 38; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 42.

### NET-ALL-08 — Payer signs every amount deciding delivery
- old: net-aptos:L3, net-solana:L3 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every amount chosen by the relayer that decides whether value arrives must be inside the payer's signature.
**Why.** The GRAM review found a relayer-chosen `forwardTon` amount that decided whether a signed payment arrived; any such amount outside the signature hands that decision to the relayer.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 39; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 43.

### NET-ALL-09 — Permanent submit refusals free the lane
- old: net-aptos:L4, net-solana:L4 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A permanent refusal at submit frees the lane at once
**Why.** The Cosmos and Hedera reviews found lanes held by submissions that could never succeed; resending the same bytes after a permanent refusal never passes, so holding the lane only blocks the jobs behind it.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 40; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 44.

### NET-ALL-10 — Crash-safe lanes never equivocate
- old: net-aptos:L5, net-solana:L5 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-10 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Lanes are crash-safe: no equivocation, no sequence used twice.
**Why.** The Sui review found that a restart could sign a second transaction on the same gas-coin version (equivocation); every family must show that a crash never yields two different transactions for one lane sequence.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 41; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 45.

### NET-ALL-11 — Multi-key accounts survive origin change
- old: net-aptos:L6, net-solana:L6 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Multi-key accounts with origins and a guardian survive an origin change.
**Why.** The Sui review found a one-key account that was bricked when the portal origin changed; several keys, an origin list and a guardian with a delay let the owner add the new origin or recover instead.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 42; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 46.

### NET-ALL-12 — Coins sent to accounts stay spendable
- old: net-aptos:L7, net-solana:L7 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-12 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Coins sent directly to an account or contract address stay spendable.
**Why.** The Sui, Cosmos and GRAM reviews found coins sent straight to an account or contract address that no code path could move, so they were stuck for good.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 43; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 47.

### NET-ALL-13 — No shared object serialises all markets
- old: net-aptos:L8, net-solana:L8 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-13 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** No shared object serialises all markets.
**Why.** The Sui review found one shared object serialising every market. A hot shared account runs its transactions one after another, hits per-account compute caps, raises local fees and is dropped under congestion, so unrelated operations of one subject end up waiting on each other.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 44; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 48.

### NET-ALL-14 — ERP verifies only keys it can prove
- old: net-aptos:L9, net-solana:L9 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-14 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A client verifies a signature only with a key it can prove belongs to the payer
**Why.** The GRAM and Sui reviews found signatures accepted from keys not tied to the payer. A key added later on chain cannot be checked by the ERP without an RPC call, so it answers "unknown" and the node's simulation decides; it never answers "valid" for a key it cannot prove.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 45; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 49.

### NET-ALL-15 — Lane state prunable, storage refunded
- old: net-aptos:L10, net-solana:L10 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-15 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Lane and nonce state is prunable and its storage is refunded.
**Why.** The GRAM review found lane and nonce tables that grow forever and keep charging storage; a permissionless prune that returns the storage deposit gives relayers a reason to clean up.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-aptos.md) line 46; [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 50.

### NET-ALL-16 — Never case-fold base58 addresses or ids
- old: net-solana:L11 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-04 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-16 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Base58 addresses and ids are never case-folded.
**Why.** Base58 is case-sensitive, and the ERP normalised addresses and transaction hashes with `.lower()`, which corrupts Solana addresses; transaction ids are therefore carried as `0x` plus 128 hex digits, which survive lowercasing.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md](history/specs/2026-10-04-net-solana.md) line 51.

### NET-ALL-17 — Asset suite on EVM and Hedera
- old: R215 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-17 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The asset suite is specified for EVM and Hedera only.
**Why.** EVM and Hedera run the same Solidity, so one implementation covers both; the other families first need their v2 wrapper work (NET-ALL-19) and then map the same rulings onto native mechanisms.
**Cost if wrong.** Nothing to undo.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-asset-suite-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-asset-suite-design.md) line 184.

### NET-ALL-18 — Tender on EVM and Hedera first
- old: R188 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-18 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The sealed-bid tender ships on EVM and Hedera first
**Why.** The tender verifies no signature, so the same bytecode runs on Hedera's smart contract service without a Hedera child, and Hedera-native bidders are handled by the deposit token; the other families need native designs.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-tender-sponsorship-shredding.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-tender-sponsorship-shredding.md) line 121.

### NET-ALL-19 — Wrappers v2 on EVM and Hedera only
- old: R145 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-19 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Token wrappers v2 are EVM and Hedera only
**Why.** Move and Solana need no wrapper for gaslessness because the subject account already holds any coin or asset; Cosmos, Soroban and GRAM keep their tier-1 tokens until wrappers there are designed with the same rate and reserve rules.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md) line 152.

### NET-ALL-20 — Per-family UA registries share kind table
- old: R314, UA:Q12 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-20 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** GRAM calls are asynchronous, and owner consent alone would let a wallet claim someone else's key. Owner-confirmed.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md) line 303; [history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md) line 1412.

### NET-ALL-21 — Non-EVM passkey owners = UA id, URN only
- old: R315, UA:Q13 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-21 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** A 20-byte form is exactly the truncation the UA id space forbids (2^80 collision work against secp256k1 accounts, CTR-UA-03); an account-shaped form invites native sends to a keyless address.
**Cost if wrong.** dev passkey accounts re-open; users copy a URN, not an address. Owner-confirmed.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md) line 311; [history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-universal-account-design.md) line 1413.
Change (2026-10-30, owner ruling 2026-10-30; status: current; first used by branch ua-soroban, task T4, clientkeys `soroban.js` `uaUrn`): the URN's `<kind>` segment is the kind's **name** as in `kinds.json` (e.g. `urn:scaas:ua:v1:webauthn-p256:<hex32>`), not the numeric code (`0x0100`); `<hex32>` is lower-case hex. Options were name (readable, matches the prose and the `KINDS` table of `ua.js`) or code (shorter, independent of a later rename); the owner chose the name. Cost if wrong: a kind rename changes its URN, so kind names are frozen once used in a URN. Every family's clients and wallets follow it.

### NET-ALL-22 — Chain identified by (chain_key, chain_uid); chain_uid salts every SCaaS domain
- old: R330 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-22 · superseded-by: —

Change: `chain_uid` is a constructor immutable of every SCaaS contract with a signature and the `salt` of every SCaaS EIP-712 domain, also bound into the confidential token's non-EIP-712 digests; CREATE2 deployer stated (addresses per chain for contracts that take `chain_uid`); fork limit stated (NET-ALL-25); Hedera block-0 hash stability check. Source add: §3 MG-4, §7 NET-ALL-22.
Change (2026-10-08): `chain_uid` (or the family identifier) is the `network` field of `MetaCall`/`MetaTransfer` (NET-ALL-26). Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-1.
Edit note (2026-10-08): `chain_uid` alone is not unique (Ethereum/ETC, Avalanche C-Chain/Fuji share a genesis), so a chain is `(chainId, chain_uid)`; pruned RPCs may not serve block 0, so deploy scripts and the node read `smartcontracts/evm/chain-uids.json`. Not a new id.
Change (2026-11-07, owner; chain-neutral releases, [CTR-TOK-29](contracts/token-wrappers.md#CTR-TOK-29); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-chain-neutral-releases.md` §9): **`chainUid()` comes from one of two sources, the same on every chain.** Old: a constructor immutable of every SCaaS contract with a signature (token implementations, the factory, the subject account factory, mandate wallets, the DEX, the registry). New: the factory and every factory-made contract are chain-neutral bytecode at the same address on every chain; the factory's `chain_uid` is written once by its registrar (`configureChain`, equal to the genesis hash whenever `BLOCKHASH(0)` / EIP-2935 can prove it, tied to the chain by a reference block hash), every token, DEX and generic instance carries the factory's value in its own code, appended at creation, and an implementation carries none (`chainUid()` = 0, it cannot sign); the registry, the governance router, the subject account factory, its accounts and the mandate wallets keep the constructor immutable. An instance's address depends only on the factory, the creator's UA id, the class, the kind and the salt (CREATE3). On a chain id shared by several live chains the factory is configured on each before any other registrar transaction there. Status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge` (T71–T74).

### NET-ALL-23 — Sui/Solana wallet signatures readable, passkey-first
- old: CR-WSF-1 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-23 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Solana and Sui wallet-key signatures: no blind blobs; origin binding through the passkey path or an opt-in account policy.
**Why.** Solana `signMessage` and Sui `signPersonalMessage` wallets write no requesting origin into the signed bytes, so any origin line a contract checked could have been written by the phishing page itself; a readable text rebuilt on chain at least lets the wallet show what is being paid, as with any wallet transaction on that page.
**Source.** [history/specs/round3-wallet-signing-formats.md](history/specs/round3-wallet-signing-formats.md) line 343.
Change (2026-10-08): the readable text is rebuilt from the `MetaTransfer`; a `MetaCall` renders its function, argument hash, network, expiry and digest, and clients decode the arguments before signing. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §4.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner 2026-10-31, one rule (owner 2026-10-25); status: documented; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): the EVM family's readable form is the typed EIP-712 struct of each operation (named structs and portable records); other families keep their readable forms and hash the portable records byte-identically; `0x0108` in MetaMask stays not built.

### NET-ALL-24 — Chain profile carries chain_uid and the DEX list
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-24 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Every SCaaS domain is salted with `chain_uid`, and the genuine DEXes are known only off chain (the token consults no on-chain DEX registry; the factory's `isDex` is advisory, CTR-DEX-24; owner 2026-10-08); the signer and the relayer need both values from a source they control, not from a server answer.
**Cost if wrong.** Clients sign with the wrong salt (every signature fails) or for a phishing `dex`.

Change (2026-11-09, group 3i, owner Q1 B): a chain profile also lists its services, the `chain_contract` rows of kind `service` (the node's `[[chains.services]]` today, [NODE-JOB-25](node/job-api.md#NODE-JOB-25)), advisory as the DEX list is: a client warns for a service off the list. ### NET-ALL-25 — A chain we run that forks becomes a new chain; no shared genesis hash
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-25 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Two branches of a fork share genesis, so `chain_uid` cannot separate them; a PoA chain re-created from the same genesis file repeats its hash. Owner ruling (2026-10-08): a fork of a chain we run gets a new chain id and `chain_key`; every private genesis carries a unique `extraData` nonce and a known genesis hash is refused.
**Cost if wrong.** Signatures made on one branch or one incarnation of a chain replay on the other.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §3 MG-4 (limits), §10 OQ3.

### NET-ALL-26 — Two signed kinds off EVM: MetaCall and MetaTransfer
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-26 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** SCaaS meta-transactions pay for any SCaaS function, not only transfers (owner, 2026-10-08); the non-EVM families mirror the EVM split into a generic `MetaCall` (function + hash of its arguments) and a typed `MetaTransfer` (`entry_ref` 0 = transfer, else payment) on one lane space per contract, with no fee field off EVM.
**Cost if wrong.** A closed op byte keeps every new gasless function (and every third-party contract) out of reach, and families drift from the EVM model.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §1, §3 NM-1, §6 Q4.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R30; status: SPECIFIED, text only, no non-EVM code moves in this round): the non-EVM `MetaTransfer` is each family's own struct and stays; it carries the fields of the EVM `UAMetaTransfer` ([CTR-MTX-23](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-23)), its `from` the family's native account in its own form; a derived subject signs the family's UA form.

### NET-ALL-27 — Verify generically, dispatch statically
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-27 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Move has no call by name and Solana declares every account up front, so the shared part is a per-family verifier library; each gasless function is a typed entry that calls it with its own name and argument hash; CosmWasm and GRAM use one `MtxExecute` message with internal dispatch. Owner: OK (2026-10-08).
**Cost if wrong.** One dispatching entry would need dynamic dispatch Move lacks, or a write-set Solana cannot declare.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §2, §3 NM-2, NM-4, §6 Q2.

### NET-ALL-28 — mtx names in every family, typed path at parity with EVM
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-28 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** One naming rule everywhere (owner, 2026-10-08, reversing "non-EVM families keep their op names"): `mtx_` snake case in Move, Soroban and Solana, `Mtx` Pascal case for CosmWasm and GRAM; `mtx_transfer`, `mtx_pay` (lane derived from the reference), `mtx_execute_transfer` and batch as on EVM; native-signer entries and chain standards (SEP-41, CW20) keep their names. Nothing is deployed outside test chains.
**Cost if wrong.** Signed and direct entry points look alike, and the node, clients and readers cannot tell them apart.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-2, NM-5, §6 Q1, Q4.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R31; status: SPECIFIED, text only): the EVM column of the parity table names the merged entries over `UAMetaTransfer`. One rule: per operation, a contract has its direct entry and at most one contract-verified signed entry, which takes every subject the chain's host cannot authorize for a call someone else submits (on EVM native and derived ids; on Soroban derived ids only, natives by host auth on the direct entry); on EVM a token also keeps the EIP-1776 alias `executeMetaTransaction` beside `mtxExecute` (owner 2026-11-01). NEAR and Algorand state their mechanism in their rounds.

### NET-ALL-83 — Non-EVM analogues of EIP-7702: recorded, not refused
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-83 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The ways a non-EVM family hands a key-holder account's authority to code (Algorand rekey to a LogicSig or app
and delegated LogicSigs, Aptos account abstraction and signer capabilities, Cosmos `authz` to a contract, TON W5
extensions / v4 plugins, NEAR `DeployContract` / full-access `AddKey` on the user's own account, Hedera contract keys;
none on Solana, Sui, Soroban) are residual risks with wallet guidance "never authorise code over your account"; SCaaS
contracts refuse none of them. Owner ruling 2026-10-30 (EIP-7702 follow-up, decision D6): first "on Algorand refuse a
rekeyed sender on sender-authorised key ops" (built on branch `no7702` as `86b099f1`, docs `f6700897`), then dropped
the same day on the controller's assessment and reverted (`c3f9e646`, `2be46f20`; after the rebase onto `main`:
`6a78779c`, `b2126567`, reverts `1e5d5ffc`, `57a03337`). Status: recorded (`644cb40a` on `no7702`).
**Why.** On Algorand a rekey is also the key-rotation mechanism (multisig, hardware key, the Falcon post-quantum
migration) and looks the same on chain as a rekey to code, so the refusal blocked legitimate and stronger accounts from
`add_key_native`, while the Algorand analogue that matters most (a delegated LogicSig, which can even rekey the victim
to an attacker key) stays undetectable; signature paths already verify the current authority, which code cannot be.
**Cost if wrong.** A rekeyed-to-LogicSig sender can still add a native key to its SCaaS record; the EVM rule
(EIP-7702 designators: own-key ECDSA only, no delegated caller) is unaffected.
**Source.** [research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md](research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md) §8, §6.3 D6; the D6 build report.

### NET-ALL-84 — One UA checklist for every family's spec
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-84 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every family's UA spec answers the 19-row checklist of networks/README.md NET-ALL-84 in its own §0 (or says
why a row does not apply): a shared answer that is the same on every chain, and a family-specific part that states the
chain's own mechanics. The rows come from the UA-Soroban spec's §0 (S1–S18, S13 split into classical Zether S13a and
PQZ S13b). Owner request 2026-10-30. Status: current (docs).
**Why.** The same questions must be asked of NEAR, Cosmos / Sui / Aptos / Solana, Algorand and TON as of Soroban, so
no family spec silently skips one, while the answers keep each chain's real mechanics.
**Cost if wrong.** A family whose mechanics do not fit a row explains why in its spec.
**Source.** The UA-Soroban spec, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` §0.

Change (2026-10-31, owner, typed-signing; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`): row 2 of the checklist now also asks for the typed portable records hashed byte-identically (CTR-UA-07; the typed EIP-712 form is the EVM family's readable form, other families keep their own, NET-ALL-23), explicit named registry arguments (CTR-UA-36) and a `kind_name` view (CTR-UA-35). It binds every family's UA round. The row count stays 19. Status: docs, typed-signing PD; Soroban `ua8-soroban`.
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; owner explicit-parameter rule 2026-10-31; status: documented; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): new checklist row 20, explicit parameters on every family, answered in each family's UA round (NEAR and Algorand separately); EVM answers it in CTR-MTX-29 and CTR-UA-36; Soroban's answer is the `ua8-soroban` branch's.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R15; status: SPECIFIED, a checklist question only): new row "Per operation, how many contract-verified signed entries, and which subjects take them?", answered per [NET-ALL-28](networks/README.md#NET-ALL-28); UA-Soroban: one, `ua_*`, derived ids only, natives by `require_auth` on the direct entry ([NET-SOR-20](networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-20)).

### NET-ALL-85 — A service pull on every family: one rule, each family's native form
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-09 · normative: networks/README.md#NET-ALL-85 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A service pull ([CTR-MTX-32](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-32)) is one rule on every chain: the payer signs once; the authorization is bound to the service as executor and to one operation, runs once, and expires; the service takes exactly the signed amount; and the payer never pays for an operation that did not happen (on the asynchronous families, NEAR and TON, an explicit refund). Each family uses its native executor binding: EVM and Hedera `mtxExecuteTransfer` with `relayer == msg.sender`; Soroban an auth tree rooted at `S.op(args)` with `pay` (`pay_ref` = the operation digest) as a sub-invocation, or `ua_pay` with `relayer = Some(S)`; NEAR `mtx_execute_transfer` with `op.relayer = S` and a refund in S's callback; Algorand an inner app call `mtx_execute_transfer` with `relayer == Txn.sender`; Solana a CPI to `relay_pay` with S's PDA as the lane signer; TON a `SignedOp` to the payer's jetton wallet with `relayer == sender`; Cosmos `ExecuteMsg::Relay` op `pay` by submessage. Sui and Aptos cannot do it with today's packages (Sui binds the relayer to `ctx.sender()`, Aptos's `relay_pay` is a `package entry fun`): each needs a token change in its own round.
**Status.** BUILT on the EVM and Hedera for the token side (no change), the reference service (test only) and the node kind `service` (group 3i, T77 `b9b130bb`, T78 `9fe6253d`, T79 `711f4f35`); Soroban, NEAR, Algorand SPECIFIED; Solana, TON, Cosmos, Sui, Aptos PLANNED. UNAUDITED.
**Why.** One rule on every chain (AGENTS); the spec's §9 reads each family's code for the binding it already has.
**Cost if wrong.** A family whose binding does not tie the authorization to the service would let anyone spend the payer's signed transfer outside the operation.
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-09 (spec Q1–Q5 as recommended); spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-service-pull.md` §9 (the file:line references per family).
