### NET-EVM-02 — Private reference chain id is 7622
- old: CR-PD-6, owner:2026-10-07:chain-7622 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-02 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The private reference chain is chain id 7622; its identity is the pair (chain id 7622, genesis hash `0x24e43dcbfc9624b23bf89409acd104d6e5671e2c41d8c192373d65519321c464`), profile `scaas-testnet`.
**Why.** Chain id 9000 is also Evmos Testnet, and replay protection is only as good as the chain id; the genesis hash pins the chain beyond the registry convention.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-design.md) line 918; [history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md](history/SCaaS-2026-10-07.md) line 39.
**Change (2026-10-31, owner ruling, branch `scaas-testnet-rename`): the SCaaS testnet's identifier is `scaas-testnet`.** Rename `private7622` → `scaas-testnet` everywhere it is a current identifier, replacing the owner's 2026-10-07 name: the Foundry profile `[profile.scaas-testnet]` (`FOUNDRY_PROFILE=scaas-testnet`; Foundry 1.8.5 accepts the hyphen), the directory `smartcontracts/evm/src/chains/scaas-testnet/`, the `chain-uids.json` key, the default profile of `verify-blockscout.sh`, the deploy scripts, CI and the node's end-to-end tests. In prose the chain is "the SCaaS testnet" (bare chain ids are avoided; "chain id 7622" is given once where a legend needs it). The future mainnet, chain id 22776, will be `scaas-mainnet`; nothing is created for it yet. History (`docs/history`, `docs/superpowers`, `docs/reviews`, `docs/research`, `legacy/`, `runs/`, `COMPLETED.md`, `HANDOFF.md`) keeps the old name. No hashed constant or test-vector preimage contained the old string, so no deployed digest changes. Status: **BUILT**.

### NET-EVM-03 — First target chain is the private PoA chain
- old: UD:§16, UD:§16:roadmap · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-03 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The first target chain is the private PoA chain; public chains follow, and CI builds the `scaas-testnet` profile.
**Why.** Owner decision: the private chain goes first because gas is not a constraint there (minimum gas price 0) and its Prague fork has EIP-2537 BLS12-381 from genesis, which confidential transfers need.
**Source.** [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 889; [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 929.

### NET-EVM-04 — Single-signer PoA must be named honestly
- old: UD:§16:single-signer · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-08-30 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A single-signer PoA chain is named honestly.
**Why.** A Clique chain with one signer is not a decentralised blockchain in any sense; it is a database with hashes and signatures, a single point of censorship and of failure, so partners settling on it must know who controls the signer.
**Source.** [research/_USER-DECISIONS.md](research/_USER-DECISIONS.md) line 917.

### NET-EVM-05 — CREATE2 deployer with fixed salts; chain_uid from the RPC; deploy gate checks chainUid()
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-05 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** Owner ruling A11: every SCaaS contract is deployed through a deterministic CREATE2 deployer with a fixed salt, so addresses follow from the init code (per-chain for contracts that take `chain_uid`, identical otherwise) instead of from the deployer's nonce; the deploy script reads `chain_uid` from the RPC and the gate checks every `chainUid()` and refuses a known genesis hash.
**Cost if wrong.** Unpredictable addresses across chains, or a contract deployed with another chain's `chain_uid`.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md](history/specs/2026-10-07-metatx-generic.md) §2 A11; §3 MG-4, MG-6; §6 step 2.
**Addendum (owner ruling 2026-10-30, fs3 Task 13 item 2(a): add the CREATE2 deployer `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` with its runtime code to the genesis alloc of the SCaaS testnet 7622 at this reset, backing the genesis up first, so `Deploy.s.sol` deploys RelayFeeRouter and the DEX): the CREATE2 deployer in the 7622 genesis alloc.** The SCaaS testnet 7622 genesis (`~dockers/mba-chain-nethermind/genesis.json`, backup `genesis.json.bak-pre-pqz6-20261031`) carries `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` = `{balance 0, nonce 1, code}` with the runtime code of the deterministic deployment proxy (github.com/Arachnid/deterministic-deployment-proxy; the code anvil puts there; `keccak256` `0x2fa86add…4989`). Its keyless pre-EIP-155 deploy transaction (fixed 100,000 gas) cannot pay Amsterdam's code-deposit state gas, so the alloc is the only way. The alloc changes the state root: genesis hash `0xf1f491abec46eb7c1784b7fc75a0174171b41831530e510c46b7178c02d63164` from the 2026-10-31 reset (`chain-uids.json`). `Deploy.s.sol` ran through it (31 transactions: UA registry, OpenFactory, RelayFeeRouter + executor, the NormalToken and SCaaSDex releases). Mainnet 22776: the same alloc is proposed; the owner decides at the 22776 launch. Status: **done** on 7622 (branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, fs3 Task 13 phase C); 22776 proposed.
Change (2026-11-07, owner; chain-neutral releases, CTR-TOK-29): the deterministic deployer is a requirement of every chain, the SCaaS mainnet's genesis alloc included; the factory (constructor `(registrar)`, `configureChain` once), its libraries, the body modules and the releases are chain-neutral and land at the same address everywhere, while contracts with a `chain_uid` constructor differ per chain; the release list `releases.json` pins every factory, library, module, release and the registrar by address and code hash, a later chain's deploy refuses a row that differs, and on a chain id listed more than once in `chain-uids.json` the registrar's run stops after `configureChain` until the siblings are configured. Status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-merge` (T71–T74; `test/v2/ChainNeutral.t.sol`, `ChainNeutralFactory.t.sol`; `DeployBase`).

Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3r; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3r`, UNAUDITED): the deploy order is the relay pair (under its constant salt, reused when already there), `SmartKeyAccountFactory` (its implementation is an argument of the next two), the UA registry, the router, `ComplianceRegistry(admin, router)`, `OpenFactory(pad(deployer))`, `configureChain` (the first admin's direct call, with the router's code hash), `setChainEntries`, the envs and the releases, then `transferAdmin` to an `msig` or PQ UA, accepted through the router. **Custody:** the first admin's key is in the factory's init code, so it stays the sole authority over the factory's address on every chain not yet configured; it is kept offline and used only for a new chain's `configureChain`, its first writes and its `transferAdmin`. Source: owner 2026-11-10; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md` §5.2, §6, §13.10; Fable review 2026-11-10 (P2-1, P2-2, P2-4).

### NET-EVM-06 — Every profile compiles for Amsterdam (Glamsterdam required on every chain)
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-21 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-06 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every Foundry profile (default, scaas-testnet, zether, gnosis, celo, bsc, polygon, base) uses `evm_version = "amsterdam"` (Foundry 1.8.5, `experimental = true`); every chain that runs these contracts requires Glamsterdam, and a public chain is deployed only after its fork. No contract reads `block.slotnum` (EIP-7843 is off on the SCaaS testnet: Clique has no slot).
**Why.** The SCaaS testnet runs Nethermind 2.2.0 with Amsterdam from block 1, and owner ruling 2026-10-21 makes Glamsterdam mandatory everywhere, so one set of gas bounds priced as the chain prices them is enough.
**Cost if wrong.** Gas bounds pinned for another schedule would pass in CI and fail on the chain.
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-21 (Task F185, "Đồng ý").
**Change (owner 2026-11-03, CTR-GOV-19).** The SCaaS testnet runs every Amsterdam EIP but EIP-7954, by removing `eip7954TransitionTimestamp` from its chainspec, because with EIP-7954 active the code limit is 65,536 B whatever `maxCodeSize` says (`pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-11-03-code-size-probe.txt`). `maxCodeSize` is `0x20000` (131,072 B); the init code limit is then 262,144 B, twice `maxCodeSize` (measured, governance plan T0b `dc14ebbe`). Old rule: Amsterdam from block 1 with every EIP of the fork. 22776 stays the owner's at launch; every other chain keeps the rule above. Status: executed 2026-11-04 (SCaaS testnet reset 1): `patch-chainspec.py --testnet-reset` wrote it (plan T16 `52ef7d22`); `pqz-core/nethermind/chain/RUNBOOK.md` "Code size 128 KiB on the SCaaS testnet: reset 1" holds the run; the SCaaS testnet's limit is 131,072 B since. Why: `WrappedPqzToken` (72,160 B) and the regulated kinds run only on a chain whose configuration its operator controls. Cost if wrong: one more key a customer chain has to change; every jump above 65,536 B widens. Source: owner 2026-11-03, two statements; [CTR-GOV-19](#ctr-gov-19--build-first-on-the-scaas-testnet-at-a-higher-code-size-ceiling-reduce-later).

**Addendum (review C5-1, 2026-10-27; controller proposal, owner may override).** A release needs a block gas limit of
`runtime × 1,530 + 2^24` (EIP-8037 state gas for the code deposit plus the EIP-7825 regular-gas cap): about 75.8 M for
`NORMAL`, about 110.9 M for `WRAPPED_PQZ` (table in [networks/evm.md](networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-06)), from
`size-baseline.json`. The deploy scripts read the chain's `block.gaslimit` and refuse a release deployment below the
kind's need. No code-size work (owner: not before Glamsterdam).
**Addendum 2 (metatx split, 2026-10-28; controller call, owner may override; commit: metatx-split T8 69fce983).** The split moved the runtimes: `NormalToken` 38,195 B (needs 75.2 M), `WrappedToken` 48,068 B (90.3 M), `NormalZetherToken` 48,313 B (90.7 M), `NormalPqzToken` 49,067 B (91.8 M), `WrappedZetherToken` 60,282 B (109.0 M), `WrappedPqzToken` 61,137 B (110.3 M); the table in networks/evm.md and the `DeployBase` comment follow `size-baseline.json` (its T8 comment entry; size gate 0 errors; the gate log `runs/2026-10-27-metatx-split-sizes.txt` holds only the verdict, the per-kind figures are in the baseline and `git show 69fce983`). Information for deployers: `MtxPipelineLib` is a linked library of every release (the release link closure is pinned, T6 `c213e24a`), and `RelayFeeRouter` with its executor is a separate `DeployBase` CREATE2 contract (CTR-MTX-27). The ceiling stays 64 KiB; no code-size work (owner).
**Addendum 3 (typed-signing, 2026-11-01; a measurement, no ruling).** The table in [networks/evm.md](networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-06) now carries forge's simulated Amsterdam gas (not receipts) from `runs/2026-11-01-typed-signing-deploy-gas.txt` next to the gate, and the registry. Gates: `NormalToken` 77.8 M, `WrappedPqzToken` 112.6 M. `UARegistry` simulates at 77.24 M, 81.1 M at × 1.05, so a plain stack asks about 81.1 M and the full stack about 114.1 M, and a 60 M chain no longer holds the smallest plain kind (it never gets past the registry). No registry gate was added: the owner has not ruled.

Under "Clients — signers":
Change (2026-11-02, typed-signing CD; controller correction of the text, no code change; status: documented; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands): **EIP-8037 inclusion and accounting.** A transaction is included only if its `tx.gas`, regular plus state, fits the block gas limit; the block's `gas_used = max(execution, state)` is accounting, not inclusion; the sender pays `max(total, floor)`. `accounts.md` "charged their sum" (registration gas table) is corrected to an upper bound, `pq-zero-knowledge.md` and the evm table follow. **`_requireReleaseGas` is not changed**: it reserves all of 2^24 as regular gas and so over-refuses (`UARegistryLib` 64.7 M against 54.7 M simulated, `UARegistry` 59.6 M against 46.5 M, `runs/2026-11-01-typed-signing-r2-deploy.txt`). Open for the owner: whether to tighten it. The evm.md table now lists the registry as two gated contracts (owner ruling 2026-11-01) and marks the simulated figures of the other kinds as measured at `daacd49a`, not re-measured.
Change (2026-11-10, the `ua*` / `mtx*` merge, [CTR-MTX-30](contracts/metatx.md#CTR-MTX-30), spec row R40, owner answer Q4 "as recommended"; status: the testnet gate BUILT (`script/DeployBase.sol`, `STATE_GAS_PER_BYTE = 1530`, `runtime x 1,530 + 2^24`), the public-chain gate SPECIFIED): the owner's formula stays the testnet gate; a public deploy is gated on the measured regular + state gas x 1.05 of the release transaction, with regular x 1.05 < 2^24.

### NET-EVM-07 — EIP-7702 is off on the SCaaS testnet and mainnet
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** EIP-7702 is off on the SCaaS testnet 7622 from its next reset (fs3 Task 13) and on the mainnet 22776 from its
launch. 7622: `"eip7702TransitionTimestamp": 0` is removed from `~dockers/mba-chain-nethermind/genesis.json` (backup
`genesis.json.bak-pre-no7702-20261030`); a reset must start from that chainspec, never from a scratchpad genesis copy
(17 stale copies still enable 7702). 22776: no chainspec exists yet; the launch chainspec must not enable 7702. Customer
chains keep 7702, so the contract rule (CTR-UA-24, rulings D1–D5) stays on every chain and the forge tests are its proof.
Owner ruling 2026-10-30 (after the 2026-10-29 EIP-7702 hot-wallet drain). Status: decided; chainspec edited 2026-10-30,
effective at the fs3 Task 13 reset; 22776 at launch.
**Why.** SCaaS's own chains need no 7702 (every SCaaS action is relayable and key-signed), and an account that cannot
delegate cannot be swept by a phished authorization.
**Cost if wrong.** Wallets that rely on 7702 batching or sponsorship do not work on 7622 / 22776; the SCaaS testnet can
no longer exercise 7702 end to end.
**Source.** [research/eip7702-node-check-2026-10-30.md](research/eip7702-node-check-2026-10-30.md) (throwaway node with the new chainspec: type-4 refused, `eth_estimateGas` -32603 "EIP-7702 is not enabled", `eth_sendRawTransaction` -32000 `InvalidTxType`; legacy and EIP-1559 transfers mined; the backup chainspec mined the same type-4 transaction); [research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md](research/eip7702-audit-2026-10-30.md) §1.

**Addendum (2026-10-31): verified on 7622.** The fs3 Task 13 reset started from `~dockers/mba-chain-nethermind/genesis.json` (`grep -c 7702` = 0 before and after `patch-chainspec.py`); on the live node a type-4 transaction with a fixed gas limit and a distinct raw type-4 transaction through `eth_sendRawTransaction` were both refused with `-32000 InvalidTxType: Transaction type in Custom is not supported`, and an EIP-1559 transfer mined. Log `pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-10-31-pqz6-live.txt`. Status: **done** for 7622 (branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, fs3 Task 13 phase C).

### NET-EVM-08 — The SCaaS testnet's node never signs for an RPC caller
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** One node (the Clique sealer; owner 2026-10-31: no second node) with three JSON-RPC endpoints: public `8545` / `8546` with `Eth`, `Net`, `Web3`, `Subscribe` and the limits `MaxBatchSize` 100, `MaxRequestBodySize` 4,194,304, `GasCap` 200,000,000, `Timeout` 20,000, `RequestQueueLimit` 500; the operator endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:8550` (`Eth`, `Net`, `Web3`, `TxPool`, `Debug`, `Trace`, `Parity`, `Clique`, `Admin`) bound to the node container's own loopback and not published, used from the host through a sidecar container that shares the node's network namespace (`docker run --rm --network container:mba_chain_node_nethermind curlimages/curl:8.21.0 …`; owner ruling 2026-10-31, review I1); the explorer endpoint `8547` (`Eth`, `Net`, `Web3`, `TxPool`) on the Docker network only (not the `scaas-node` gateway port). `Personal` is enabled nowhere. Step 1 of the owner's ruling (the sealer key used for block signing only, `UnlockAccounts` removed) does not work on Nethermind 2.2.0: the key's password is looked up through `UnlockAccounts` and start-up fails without it, and the other key file is not the sealer. So step 2 applies, as Nethermind's own calls filter instead of a reverse proxy: `JsonRpc.CallsFilterFilePath` with the one regex `^(?!eth_(sendtransaction|sign|signtransaction|signtypeddata.*)$).*$` refuses the four wallet methods (`-32601`) on every endpoint, over HTTP and WebSocket, inside batches and in any letter case; a proxy could not see WebSocket frames. Owner ruling 2026-10-31; status: **done** (branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, fs3 Task 13 phase C and its review fix; checks in RUNBOOK § 7622 node layout and access; probe 420 / 0 and the PQZ e2e 256 / 0 through the public RPC afterwards; after the loopback bind 8550 is refused from `mba-net`, the host and the LAN and answers through the sidecar).
**Why.** The unlocked sealer account answered `eth_sendTransaction` / `eth_sign` / `personal_*` for anyone who reached the RPC, and `admin` / `debug` / `parity` were public. The admin URL first bound `0.0.0.0:8550` with only the publish limited to `127.0.0.1`: the publish limit alone left every container on `mba-net` (the three Blockscout services, two of them reachable from the LAN) able to call `admin_*`, `clique_*` and `debug_*` on the sealer, e.g. `clique_propose` from the only signer adds a signer at once (review I1); the container-loopback bind closes that.
**Cost if wrong.** A wallet method left public lets any caller spend from, or sign as, the sealer; an endpoint that is too tight breaks the deploy scripts (`GasCap` must cover the largest estimate: the `WrappedPqzToken` release, 96.5 M gas).
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-31 (hardening brief, its single-node change and the step 1 / step 2 order); `pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-10-31-pqz6-live.txt` (H1–H5).
**Addendum (2026-10-31, owner ruling, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`): node split, NET-EVM-10.** The "one node, no second node" layout above is replaced: the public, Docker-only and admin endpoints are on the key-less `rpc` node (`eth_accounts` `[]`), and the sealer keeps the key with JSON-RPC only on its own container loopback (admin set, the same calls filter). The wallet-method filter and the limits are unchanged; admin calls use a sidecar per node (`--network container:mba_chain_sealer` or `container:mba_chain_rpc`).

### NET-EVM-09 — Blockscout on the SCaaS testnet, lean and capped
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Blockscout runs on 7622 (it was off for RAM / CPU) with caps: `explorer-db` (postgres:18) 1 GiB / 1 CPU, `explorer-backend` (`ghcr.io/blockscout/blockscout:9.0.2`) 2 GiB / 1.5 CPU, `explorer-frontend` (v2.3.5, pinned by digest `sha256:4b69f441…c90a`) 512 MiB / 0.5 CPU; UI on host port 8558 (owner 2026-10-31: not 3000), API on 4000; `restart: unless-stopped` like every service (NET-EVM-10 addendum, owner ruling 2026-10-31), started after the node; it reads only the Docker-network endpoint `8547`. Lean: internal transactions, block rewards, token-instance metadata, the cataloged-token updater, beacon blobs and market data off; blocks, receipts, logs, token transfers and balances, address pages, the API, pending transactions (`txpool_content`) and address coin balances on; `POOL_SIZE` 10, `POOL_SIZE_API` 5, indexer concurrency 2. Stop: `docker compose stop explorer-frontend explorer-backend explorer-db`. Owner rulings 2026-10-31 (on with caps; lean; pending transactions on; endpoint on the Docker network; UI on 8558). Status: **done** (branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, fs3 Task 13 phase C and its review fix): steady state backend 1–5 % CPU / 300 MiB, db ≈ 1 % / 105 MiB, frontend 0 % / 165 MiB.
**Why.** An explorer for the testnet's contracts and transactions, without the load that made the owner turn it off.
**Cost if wrong.** On this pruned node (no historical state) Blockscout's contract-code fetcher retries forever for contracts it sees more than about 64 blocks late (one core): Docker Hub's `blockscout/blockscout:latest` (7.0.2) also looped on block 0, so 9.0.2 from GHCR; after an outage spanning deploys, `chain/blockscout-code-backfill.py` fills the code from the latest state. Archive mode at the next reset would remove the issue.
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-31; RUNBOOK § Blockscout; `pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-10-31-pqz6-live.txt` (B1–B7).
**Change (2026-10-31, owner ruling, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, fs3 Task 13 phase C fix): the address coin balance fetcher is on.** With `INDEXER_DISABLE_ADDRESS_COIN_BALANCE_FETCHER=true`, Blockscout 9.0.2 does not start `CoinBalance.Realtime` but its realtime block fetcher still calls it, so every live import crashed after the insert (511 times in 3 h) and the home-page block list stopped updating; with it on: 0 crashes, the list follows the DB tip, address pages show balances. Measured cost: backend 1.7 % → 149 % median CPU (its 1.5-CPU cap) and 306 → 347–362 MiB, db unchanged (≈ 1 %, 119–123 MiB), node 1.5–3 % → ≈ 60 %: the catch-up fetcher retries forever the 1,734 balances at old blocks the pruned node cannot serve (`No state available`, ≈ 10,900 failed lookups per 2 min). Cost closed (owner ruling 2026-10-31, remedy 2): `chain/blockscout-code-backfill.py --prune-coin-balances` backed up and deleted the 1,734 unfetched rows more than 64 blocks behind the tip, then a backend restart: 0 `No state` errors over 5 min, backend 2.0 % median CPU / 301 MiB, node 1.9 %, home list on the tip, balances right; rerun after a Blockscout outage longer than the pruning window. Root fix: archive mode at the sealer / RPC node split (separate task). Status: **on, cost closed**.
**Addendum (2026-10-31, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`): Blockscout reads the archive `rpc` node (NET-EVM-10).** `ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_HTTP_URL` / `WS_URL` / `TRACE_URL` = `rpc:8547`. Re-checked: `eth_getBalance` / `eth_getCode` at blocks 0 and 1 answer; the 1,734 coin-balance rows deleted by the cleanup were put back from its backup CSV and all fetched in about 25 s with 0 `No state` errors (values equal to the node's); 0 created contracts without code. Neither `blockscout-code-backfill.py` mode is needed any more; they stay for a Blockscout on a pruned node. `FIRST_BLOCK` stays 1 (the index already starts there).
**Addendum (2026-10-31, owner ruling, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`): contract verification on, local only.** Service `sc-verifier` (`ghcr.io/blockscout/smart-contract-verifier` v1.11.1 pinned by digest `sha256:a7580f42…e063`, 512 MiB (768 MiB since 2026-10-31, addendum below) / 1 CPU, on `mba-net` only with no published port, Solidity only: Vyper, Sourcify and zkSync off; compilers from binaries.soliditylang.org, run natively in the container) with `MICROSERVICE_SC_VERIFIER_ENABLED` true, `MICROSERVICE_SC_VERIFIER_TYPE` `sc_verifier`, `MICROSERVICE_SC_VERIFIER_URL` `http://sc-verifier:8050/` on the backend (without the URL Blockscout 9.0.2 defaults to its hosted eth-bytecode-db; 7622 is private, so nothing but the solc download leaves the host). `smartcontracts/evm/script/verify-blockscout.sh` verifies every contract of the `Deploy.s.sol` broadcast, factory children included, after each reset or deploy. Status: **service and script in place, verification blocked**: v1.11.1 (the newest release) parses the standard JSON with `foundry-compilers-artifacts` 0.19, which has no `amsterdam` EVM version, so all 31 contracts fail with `Unknown evm version: amsterdam` (NET-EVM-06 compiles every contract for Amsterdam with solc 0.8.37 `experimental`); an `osaka` resubmission gives the same code but other metadata, so no match. The script's inputs reproduce the deployed code exactly with local solc. Measured: verifier idle 0.02 % CPU / 4.5 MiB; one large compile 100 % of its CPU cap, peak 364 MiB. **Update (2026-10-31, owner ruling option (a)):** the live stack uses a locally patched verifier image (built outside the repo, `~dockers/mba-chain-nethermind/sc-verifier/`: blockscout-rs v1.11.1 `9457af29` with the foundry-compilers 0.19.10 crates patched to accept `amsterdam` and pass `experimental` to solc; image `scaas/sc-verifier:v1.11.1-amsterdam1`, local only), temporary until upstream supports Amsterdam. Status: **verification on**: the 31 `Deploy.s.sol` contracts and the 95 contracts of the five PQZ e2e runs on this chain (`verify-blockscout.sh` reads the e2e run logs) verified, every one a full match, the 10 e2e token clones (EIP-1167, `OpenFactory.createToken`) linked by Blockscout to their implementations; latest 200 transactions: 43 calls shown as raw selectors before, 0 after; back to `ghcr.io/blockscout/smart-contract-verifier` once an upstream release passes that directory's `check-image.sh` (TODO).
**Addendum (2026-10-31, owner, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, Task 13 final): `sc-verifier` memory 768 MiB.** The patched verifier's 31-contract run hit the 512 MiB cap (cgroup `memory.peak` at the cap, page cache reclaimed, no OOM kill), so the cap is 768 MiB (stack config); later runs sit at the 768 MiB cap with no OOM kill. Owner: no further raise, verification is occasional. Status: **done** (live).
**Addendum (2026-10-31, owner, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, Task 13 final): `API_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED` true on the backend.** Blockscout's default per-IP API limit (500 `/api/v2` calls per 15 minutes) answered HTTP 429 to every caller, the UI included, during a verification run; on this private chain the limit is off. `verify-blockscout.sh` stays gentle anyway (one address call per check, curl retries a 429 up to six times with a fixed 15 s delay, a pause between contracts). Status: **done** (live; RUNBOOK § Contract verification).
**Addendum (2026-11-10, owner rulings via the controller, branch `ua-mtx-merge`, T66b Step 5b): every contract on the SCaaS testnet, by the chain-neutral step of NET-EVM-12.** The T66b Step 5 deploy had only its 7 linked libraries verified: the old run waited on `capped` slots held by other jobs, printed nothing until its end and never finished a pass. Now `sh script/onchain/verify.sh scaas-testnet` (Blockscout `http://127.0.0.1:4000/api` and RPC `http://127.0.0.1:8545` on loopback; the LAN address of the earlier notes is gone) compiles each source snapshot once under `capped`, then verifies outside it, one contract at a time in a 1 GiB scope. Result (rows `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-10-ua-mtx-merge-t66b-step5b/verify-scaas-testnet.txt`): of 345 contracts with code, before 74 verified / 5 linked clones / 265 unverified (34 of them CREATE3 proxies, then unclassified), after 255 verified (full match) / 8 linked clones / 35 CREATE3 proxies / 1 genesis predeploy, plus 90 SSTORE2 data contracts and 500 book or fork-broadcast addresses without code. Sources: `6df89135` (Step 5, PqChat, the tokens harness), `11349728` (the dex harness, `Dex.s.sol` changed after its run), `bf6f3d04` (the 2026-11-04 reset's PQZ e2e `GovernanceRouter`). Seen on the way: forge 1.8.5 exits 0 on Blockscout's `Fail - Unable to verify` (19 of the 67 contracts the last pass verified, large modules mostly, failed once and passed when submitted again), so the explorer's answer decides. **Open, for the owner (46 rows):** (1) 43 EIP-1167 clones with 95–175 bytes of appended data (the factory's `ChainEnv`, PqChat instances): Blockscout 9.0.2 answers `proxy_type` `unknown` with no implementation, while a 45-byte clone is linked (`eip1167`); every implementation is verified; options are the owner's (a patched Blockscout proxy detection, or accepting the clone's own code as its link as on Etherscan and Sourcify). (2) The 3 `OnchainFwd` harness contracts of the tokens group: `sc-verifier` answers `Fail - Unable to verify` on every attempt although their init code equals the snapshot's creation bytecode and their runtime differs only in the immutable; their standard JSON is 1,717,975 B against at most 1,255,036 B for every verified contract, so a request-size limit in the stack is the likely cause (not confirmed: the stack's containers were not touched). Status: **done** for the rest, the 46 rows open. **Closed (owner rulings 2026-11-10 via the controller):** (1) `vcheck.py` counts an EIP-1167 clone with appended data as linked, state `linked (clone, appended data)`, apart from Blockscout's own `linked clone`, when its first 45 bytes are exactly the EIP-1167 proxy naming an implementation and that implementation is fully verified (43 rows). (2) A partial match is accepted for a harness contract, state `verified (partial, harness)`: the code's metadata hash names a `script/` artifact of a source snapshot and the explorer's name matches. `forge verify-contract --flatten` was refused (the whole `Tokens.s.sol`, 1.65 MB, and the forwarder alone, 1,011 B); a standard JSON holding only the forwarder's source (1,784 B) verified the 3 `OnchainFwd`, partial match, which points to the request size for the 1.72 MB one. (3) For later deploys the forwarder is its own file without imports, `script/onchain/OnchainForwarder.sol`, renamed `OnchainFwd` → `OnchainForwarder` and `exec` (0xbe6002c2) → `forwardCall` (0x22bee494), behaviour unchanged, standard JSON 2,048 B, so a full match; the books and records of the deploy before the SCaaS testnet's reset 2 keep the old name. Read-only pass after: 0 unverified. Status: **done**, 0 open rows.

### NET-EVM-10 — The SCaaS testnet runs a sealer node and a public rpc node
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-10 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The single 7622 node is split into two nodes in the stack's one `docker-compose.yml`, both on `scaas/nethermind-pqz:2.2.0-pqz6`. `sealer` (container `mba_chain_sealer`, the single node's data dir kept): the Clique key (keystore + `PasswordFiles` + `UnlockAccounts` + `EnodeAccount`; Nethermind 2.2.0 signs with the node key), Mining on, pruned flat state, small caches (`Init.MemoryHint` 512 MB, `Pruning.CacheMb` 128, `FlatDb` block / trie cache 128 MiB, `mem_limit` 1g: the 768m set at the split reached 694 MiB total / 611 MiB anon under the PQZ e2e five minutes after a restart and was raised live with `docker update` to avoid an OOM kill halting the chain), JSON-RPC only on its container loopback `127.0.0.1:8550` (admin set, calls filter on), no published port, discovery off, static peer `rpc` only (`OnlyStaticPeers`), on the internal Docker network `chain-p2p` (`internal: true`, `com.docker.network.bridge.inhibit_ipv4`, members `sealer` and `rpc` only). `rpc` (container `mba_chain_rpc`, new data dir, full sync from `sealer`): no keystore, no unlocked account, Mining off, archive (`Pruning.Mode` `None` on the patricia backend, `FlatDb.Enabled` false: Nethermind 2.2.0's default flat state keeps no history), fixed P2P key (`KeyStore.EnodeKeyFile`), the public 8545 / 8546 (`Eth`, `Net`, `Web3`, `Subscribe`, the NET-EVM-08 limits and wallet-method filter), 8547 on `mba-net` only for Blockscout, admin 8550 on its container loopback, P2P 30303 tcp + udp published; static peer `sealer`, `MaxActivePeers` 25. The sealer sets `TxPool.AcceptTxWhenNotSynced` true: a sole signer has no peer ahead of it, so about 10–12 minutes after each session starts its sync mode turns `Disconnected` and Nethermind 2.2.0's `SyncedTxGossipPolicy` drops every transaction `rpc` gossips to it while blocks keep flowing (the first PQZ e2e after the split: 127 ok, 1 FAIL, a `mtxRollOver` with no receipt; log `…-node-split-1fail-sealer-not-synced.txt`); `TxPool.MaxTxSize` 2,097,152 (2 MiB) on both (owner ruling 2026-10-31: it matches `MaxRequestBodySize` 4 MiB, as `eth_sendRawTransaction` carries the transaction as hex, so about 2 MiB is the largest raw transaction the RPC accepts at all; a 2,097,263 B raw transaction gets HTTP 413 `-32005 Request body too large`; 2 MiB is harmless headroom, not a calldata enabler: on Amsterdam (EIP-8037 on from timestamp 1) Nethermind 2.2.0 caps a transaction's regular gas (intrinsic, the EIP-7976 calldata floor 15,000 + 64 per byte, execution) at 2^24 = 16,777,216, the gasLimit may go up to 2^32 − 1 within the block gas limit (200 M on the SCaaS testnet) and gas above 2^24 pays only state gas (so `mtxPrepareAcc` with gasUsed 23.15 M and the 96.5 M release deploy mine), hence at most 261,909 B of calldata per transaction, refused at pool admission above that: 240,000 B mined, 1.5 MiB refused with "Intrinsic gas … floor 100678296 exceeded cap of 16777216"; this restates CTR-PQZ-06 and CTR-PQZ-11, not a new rule; the largest PQZ e2e transaction is 107,268 B; the 544 KB PQZH M = 16 auditor-on proof is a bench shape only (no gas row, the Rust core refuses it), not a transaction anyone sends — corrected 2026-10-31, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, Task 13 final, after the first record gave it as the reason for 2 MiB). External nodes connect to `rpc` only. Owner ruling 2026-10-31 (two small nodes in the same compose file; `rpc` archive as remedy 3 for Blockscout's old-block lookups; the sealer never reachable from outside, external peers via `rpc`). Status: **done** (branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, fs3 Task 13 node split): block gaps 12 s at the switch and 9 s at the network recreation, otherwise every 5 s; probe 420 / 0 and the PQZ e2e 256 ok / 0 FAIL through the public RPC (after the sealer fix; the run before it: 127 ok, 1 FAIL); transfers through 8545 mine right after a restart and 15 min later with the sealer in sync mode `Disconnected`; `eth_accounts` `[]` on every `rpc` endpoint; the sealer unreachable from the host, the LAN and `mba-net`; RAM 5 min after the PQZ e2e: sealer 776 MiB median (cgroup anon 686–700 MiB, file 91 MiB) of 1 GiB, rpc 671 MiB median (anon 566–595 MiB, still rising slowly) of 1.5 GiB; the sealer's anon grew 617 → 700 MiB during the e2e and then stayed flat for 7 min (single node before: up to 1.13 GiB; a leak needs a longer series; the PQZ native-library harness test of 2026-10-31 found none: four runs against the live image's `libpqz_ffi.so`, anon flat or falling, < ≈ 50 B per honest verify, `pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-10-31-leak-harness.txt`). Further restarts: sealer 9 s and 11 s block gaps, rpc none.
**Why.** The key leaves the process that answers RPC (NET-EVM-08 still had the unlocked sealer key behind a calls filter); misbehaving peers and callers (a P2P flood, an `eth_call` that trips the PQZ node-fault exit, calls queueing on the PQZL verifier lock) reach only `rpc`, not block production (RUNBOOK rule W-H, now met on 7622); Blockscout reads old-block balances and code from the archive `rpc`, so the pruned-node workarounds (`blockscout-code-backfill.py` and `--prune-coin-balances`) are no longer needed (the 1,734 pruned rows were put back and fetched in about 25 s with 0 `No state` errors).
**Cost if wrong.** The two nodes are mutual static peers (the sealer lists `rpc` with `OnlyStaticPeers`, `rpc` lists the sealer), so either re-dials the other after a restart; if many external peers fill `rpc`'s `MaxActivePeers` (25), check that `rpc` keeps its static session to the sealer (not tested with a full peer table); remedy: a higher `MaxActivePeers` or the sealer as a trusted node on `rpc`. Two processes to run and start in order (sealer, rpc, Blockscout); while `rpc` is down the public RPC and Blockscout stop although blocks continue; while the sealer is down the chain stops as before; `rpc` archive grows with the chain (disk, not RAM). Without `inhibit_ipv4` the host itself reached the sealer's P2P port (seen during the switch, fixed).
**Source.** Owner 2026-10-31 (node split brief); `pqz-core/nethermind/runs/2026-10-31-pqz6-live.txt` § S; RUNBOOK § Node split. Mainnet 22776: the same topology is proposed and the owner decides at launch; an external signer for the sealer (Nethermind `Mining.Signer`, the ExternalSigner plugin) is still to check.
**Addendum (2026-10-31, owner ruling, branch `fs3-t13-rollout`, Task 13 final): restart policy `unless-stopped` on every service, the sealer included (option (b)).** Every service of the stack (`sealer`, `rpc`, `explorer-db`, `explorer-backend`, `explorer-frontend`, `sc-verifier`) runs `restart: unless-stopped`; set live with `docker update` and in the compose file (no container recreated). Why: a crashed Blockscout backend stayed down with no restart policy. Option (b) was chosen over option (a), `on-failure:3` for the sealer: one policy for every service, with the health checks reporting `RestartCount` so a crash loop is visible. Effect on the P6f D4 / D14 node fault: `PQZ-NODE-FAULT` still exits with code 120 and the block in progress is never sealed; Docker restarts the node, which re-processes it. A deterministic fault caused by a pooled transaction can loop on the sealer, because `rpc` gossips the transaction to it again after each restart; so the health check reports `RestartCount` (`chain/watch.sh` prints `restarts=` and a `WARN` line when it is not 0), and on a loop the operator stops the sealer and drops the transaction. After a host reboot Docker starts every service at once, so the documented start order (sealer, rpc, then Blockscout) is not enforced. Status: **done** (live; RUNBOOK § PQZ node and § Node split, `docs/node/ops.md` the PQZ node). This replaces the earlier "no restart policy, owner step" text of P6f, NET-EVM-09 and the RUNBOOK.

### NET-EVM-11 — Every deploy transaction carries an explicit gas limit within the block
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `deploy.sh evm` sends no transaction with forge's estimate: `Deploy.s.sol` is simulated on the RPC's fork with nothing sent, then `script/DeploySend.s.sol` sends that plan (forge's dry-run file, the linked libraries first) in order, each transaction with an explicit gas limit, `(regular + state) × 1.05` measured on the fork as `DeployBase._measuredGas` does, capped at the block gas limit read from the RPC. A transaction whose regular + state exceeds that block gas limit refuses the whole plan by name (`TxGasOverBlockLimit`) before the first is sent.
**Why.** Forge's estimate × 1.05 gave the `UARegistryCoreLib` transaction 61,800,392 of gas limit on the SCaaS testnet (T66b Step 5, commit `cd48e32b`) while it used 52,317,793 and its measured ask is 56.63 M: a chain with a 60 M block would refuse that transaction after the five before it had landed. On a 60 M anvil the old path stopped there (`intrinsic gas too high -- tx.gas_limit > env.block.gas_limit`, 5 transactions mined); with the rule the 104 transactions all land, the largest limit 56,629,029.
**Cost if wrong.** Two forge runs per deploy (the plan is simulated twice); a limit too tight for a client that prices a transaction above forge's Amsterdam EVM would fail on chain (anvil does not price EIP-8037, so its run proves the block fit, forge's own run of each call at its limit proves the need).
**Source.** Owner 2026-11-10 (T66b follow-up, fix 2); `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-10-ua-mtx-merge-t66b-followup-gas.txt`.

Change (owner 2026-11-10, group 3r; status: BUILT on branch `ua-mtx-3r`, UNAUDITED): the 60 M per-transaction bound stays as today. A release deploy carries no signature check (the factory admin approves the release by hash in a separate small transaction, CTR-GOV-23), so its gas is today's direct deploy plus the approval lookup, a few thousand gas; every release of the SCaaS testnet reset 2 fits the bound (the largest, `SCaaSDex`, 55,820,670 asked). Source: owner 2026-11-10; spec `superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-admin-not-owner.md` §5.6; `smartcontracts/evm/runs/2026-11-10-scaas-testnet-reset2/summary.txt`.

### NET-EVM-12 — Every contract a remote deploy leaves on a chain is source-verified on its explorer
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-12 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** After every remote EVM deploy (`deploy.sh evm`, `VERIFY_TARGET` naming the target) and after each group of a remote `matrix.sh` target, `smartcontracts/evm/script/onchain/verify.sh <target>` verifies every contract we deployed on that chain on the chain's explorer and then checks completeness: each address with code ends verified (full match), a linked EIP-1167 clone, SSTORE2 data or the 8-byte CREATE3 proxy, else a fail row and exit 1. The explorer comes from the environment, one config for every chain: `VERIFY_EXPLORER` `blockscout`, `etherscan` (the v2 API, the chain by `chainid`) or `sourcify`, `VERIFY_URL`, `VERIFY_RPC`, and `VERIFY_API_KEY_ENV`, the name of the env var holding the key (required for Etherscan; passed to forge in its environment only). A remote target without an explorer fails `VERIFY_NOT_CONFIGURED`; `VERIFY=none` skips the step only with a `VERIFY_REASON`, which the run prints; chain 31337 or `VERIFY_TARGET=local` is local and not verified. Names come from the metadata hash at the end of the runtime code against the artifacts of source snapshots (a commit's `git archive` plus the pinned `lib/`, compiled once under `scripts/capped` with the deploy's profile); every `forge verify-contract` runs outside `capped` in a 1 GiB scope, one at a time, bounded by `VERIFY_TIMEOUT`; a forge run that compiles aborts the step. Discovery: the deployment books, every broadcast of the chain, the getters that name a child, and on a chain of ours (`VERIFY_SCAN=1`, the SCaaS testnet's default) a block scan of the whole chain.
**Why.** The owner wants every deployed contract readable on its explorer. The SCaaS testnet's Step 5 deploy stayed unverified for hours because verification was a separate manual script tied to one broadcast and one explorer, and each `forge verify-contract` waited for a `capped` slot held by other jobs; a broadcast label can also be wrong (a fork broadcast writes the same chain id), so names come from the code.
**Cost if wrong.** A deploy on a chain whose explorer is not configured now ends with exit 1 after the contracts are on chain (the deployment JSON stays; set the explorer and rerun `verify.sh`, or `VERIFY=none` with a reason). A contract deployed from uncommitted or older sources needs that commit as a further snapshot (`verify.sh <target> HEAD <rev>`). The Etherscan and Sourcify paths are tested offline only (request shapes, answer parsing, no key on the command line); the first real run on a public chain is their first end-to-end test. On Etherscan and Sourcify a clone's link is its own code, as neither exposes a proxy link this check reads.
**Source.** Owner rulings 2026-11-10 (via the controller: verify every contract of the SCaaS testnet first, compile once under `capped`, verify outside it one at a time with bounded waits; then the chain-neutral step); `smartcontracts/evm/script/onchain/test_vcheck.py`.

### NET-EVM-13 — An EVM chain is named `<chain>-mainnet` / `<chain>-testnet`, and its deployment book by that name
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-11-10 · normative: networks/evm.md#NET-EVM-13 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** (1) Chain keys: every `chain-uids.json` row and `src/chains/` directory is `<chain>-mainnet` / `<chain>-testnet` (`ethereum-mainnet`, `ethereum-testnet` = Sepolia, a second testnet keeps its name `ethereum-hoodi`; `etc-*` (Mordor), `bsc-*`, `gnosis-*` (Chiado), `polygon-*` (Amoy), `base-*`, `celo-*`, `op-*`, `arbitrum-*`, `avalanche-*` (Fuji), `linea-*`, `hedera-*`; `scaas-testnet` stays, `scaas-mainnet` for 22776); the full name stays in `name`; every row has `"network": "mainnet" | "testnet"` (the `scaas-testnet` row's `"testnet": false` fixed). (2) Deployment books: `deployments/<key>.json`, the key resolved from `chain-uids.json` by (chainId, chain_uid); an unknown chain needs `DEPLOY_NAME`, else a named fail with no chain-id fallback; every book carries `key`, `name`, `chainId`, `chainUid`, `network` at the top and readers check `network` against the key suffix (a mismatch is a named fail); the books `7622.json`, `7622-t66b-releases.json`, `7622-pqz.json` … move to `scaas-testnet*.json`; `deployments/pre-reset2-20261110/` stays as a record; forge's `broadcast/<Script>/<chainid>/` stays. (3) Names (controller 2026-11-10): `<key>.json` is the chain's book, a companion `<key>-<what>.json` (`-t66b-releases`, `-zether-e2e`, `-pqz`); a Hedera chain's book is its `<key>.json` (`hedera-testnet.json`, no `hedera-` prefix): `DeployHedera.s.sol` is its only deploy (NET-HED-04) and `Deploy.s.sol` refuses chain ids 295–298; a book is written in the form of `json.dumps(…, indent=2)`, the header first, then the rest as forge wrote it.
**Why.** A chain id alone names neither the chain nor whether it is a test chain (ETH/ETC and Avalanche/Fuji share a genesis, NET-ALL-22); one naming rule on every chain; a book's file name and header say which chain and network it belongs to.
**Cost if wrong.** A reader still on `deployments/<chainid>.json` finds no book and fails by name; nothing is live with value, so no migration.
**Source.** Owner rulings 2026-11-10 (TODO 3q, "Ok": every chain the same). Status: (1) **done** on branch `ua-mtx-3q` (`c5b06283`); (2), (3) **done** on branch `ua-mtx-3q` (`8f8464c2`, (3) in the commit after it: `script/DeployBook.sol`, `script/deploybook.py`, every writer and reader; the git-ignored live books are renamed and given their header by hand at the merge, no reader falls back: `BOOK_OLD_NAME`).
