## 28. Networks — Hedera

### NET-HED-01 — Hedera HCS anchoring
- old: req:blockchain.md:hcs-anchoring · status: open · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-01 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** HCS anchoring is an open owner requirement.
**Why.** HCS gives an immutable, timestamped audit log for the hashes of important agent decisions; the consensus timestamp is the evidence.
**Open.** Owner decision pending; the default stated in the normative text applies.
**Source.** [history/blockchain.md](history/blockchain.md) line 235.

### NET-HED-02 — Hedera Schedule Service
- old: req:blockchain.md:hedera-schedule · status: open · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-02 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The Hedera Schedule Service is an open owner requirement.
**Why.** High-risk agent actions are created as scheduled transactions that execute only once reviewers have added enough signatures.
**Open.** Owner decision pending; the default stated in the normative text applies.
**Source.** [history/blockchain.md](history/blockchain.md) line 242.

### NET-HED-03 — ED25519 owners pay via mtxExecuteAsOwnerRaw
- old: CR-ADW-2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-03 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** An ED25519 owner pays from its `MandateWallet` only through `mtxExecuteAsOwnerRaw`.
**Why.** ERC-1271 runs under STATICCALL and the HIP-632 `isAuthorizedRaw` precompile halts there, so `isValidSignature` cannot cover an ED25519 owner; special-casing the token would add one more Hedera-only path to the signature pipeline for a rare case.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-addendum-wallets.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-payments-addendum-wallets.md) line 303.

### NET-HED-04 — Hedera = Solidity on HSCS + HIP-632
- old: R63 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Hedera is the EVM family on the Hedera Smart Contract Service: the same Solidity contracts behind a Hedera JSON-RPC relay, plus HIP-632 for ED25519 accounts; the payer-sponsored path is not used.
**Why.** The payer-sponsored path is a transaction from the subject's own Hedera account, which is exactly the subject lock NET-ALL-02 forbids; running the existing Solidity contracts on HSCS reuses all of them unchanged. The first wording of this ruling, "reuse SubjectAccount/pipeline on Hedera", was narrowed by the Hedera design: there is no `SmartKeyAccount` and no EVM pipeline on Hedera, because native Hedera accounts already rotate keys and the relayer runs `lane_runner`.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 536.

### NET-HED-05 — Hedera status code to outcome class table
- old: R6-7 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-05 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Each Hedera status code maps to one outcome class; a billed failure is never requeued without limit
**Why.** The adapter sent every known code except `CONTRACT_REVERT_EXECUTED` back to `queued`, including codes billed after consensus, with no attempt cap; a contract wallet whose `isValidSignature` burns almost no gas under estimation and the full cap at consensus then loops until `validUntil`.
**Cost if wrong.** Each loop the lane pays at least 80% of the estimated gas, again and again, for one payment that never lands.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 162.

### NET-HED-06 — v1 HTS wrapper fee check in initialize
- old: R6-8 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-06 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** An HTS underlying with any fixed, fractional or royalty fee breaks a wrapper — `MetaToken.wrap` measures what actually arrived (fine for receiver-side fees) but `unwrap` sends exactly `amount` (`MetaToken.sol:134-139`), so a fixed fee in the same token or a fractional fee with `netOfTransfers = true` is taken from the wrapper again (`balanceOf(this) < totalSupply`, the last redeemer is stuck), and a fixed fee in HBAR makes every `unwrap` revert (the wrapper holds no HBAR), locking the reserve. v2 refuses these; the built v1 `HederaMetaToken` only associates (the permissionless `associateUnderlying()` calling `0x167 associateToken(this, underlying)`), is still registered as `META v1` (`DeployHedera.s.sol:29-30`), and anyone may create it through the open factory (`OpenFactory.createMetaToken`, permissionless, `:91-96`; `deprecate` does not block creation — `_registered` checks only non-zero, `:167-170`). Fix (SPECIFIED): `MetaToken.initialize` calls an `internal virtual _checkUnderlying(u)` hook (empty by default); `HederaMetaToken` overrides it with `HederaHts.checkAndAssociate(u)` and reverts `UnderlyingInvalid` on any fee; `associateUnderlying()` is deleted (association inside `initialize` means a token that cannot associate is never born, and the auto-association slot is no longer a detour); a new implementation is deployed, registered as a new META version on the Hedera factory, and `deprecate(META, 1)` follows. Until then the wizard and the node's token registry refuse a v1 Hedera token whose underlying is an HTS token with custom fees. Forge tests (mock `0x167`): v1 on an underlying with fixed/fractional/royalty fees ⇒ creation reverts; no fee ⇒ associated once, wrap/unwrap conserve the reserve; `isToken` failure ⇒ `HtsQueryFailed`.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 201.

### NET-HED-07 — Wallets warn on HTS issuer keys
- old: R6-9 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Wizards and wallets read every key of the HTS issuer and warn before a wrapper is created.
**Why.** A wipe key can erase the wrapper's underlying balance and a freeze, KYC or pause key can lock every holder; these keys cannot be blocked on chain because real HTS tokens such as Hedera USDC carry them.
**Cost if wrong.** A wrapper loses its backing or locks its holders without anyone having been told.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 215.

### NET-HED-08 — Hedera runs lane_runner, one tx per lane
- old: R6-1 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Hedera runs `lane_runner` (one transaction in flight per lane), with no pipeline, replacement or gap-fill.
**Why.** Hedera has no mempool: a transaction with a future nonce is refused with `WRONG_NONCE`, so pipelining, replacement and gap-fill have nothing to work with.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 289.

### NET-HED-09 — HederaMetaToken HIP-632 for 64-byte signatures
- old: R6-2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `HederaMetaToken` verifies a 64-byte signature from an account without code through HIP-632 `isAuthorizedRaw`; a precompile revert means "not authorised"; everything else is `MetaToken`.
**Why.** A 64-byte signature is never ECDSA here (OpenZeppelin 5.2 `tryRecover` takes only 65 bytes) and the precompile itself classifies by length, so the branch is unambiguous; the precompile binds the key to the account from Hedera state, so a public key sent by the client never grants authority.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 291.

### NET-HED-10 — HashPack signMessage and KeyList are seams
- old: R6-4 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-10 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** HashPack `signMessage` and threshold/KeyList accounts are seams.
**Why.** HashPack `signMessage` (HIP-820) signs a prefixed message, which `isAuthorizedRaw` (exactly 32 bytes) cannot check; checking it through `isAuthorized` needs a protobuf `SignatureMap` built in Solidity and a test on a real network, so it is deferred.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 295.

### NET-HED-11 — Call HIP-632 system contract with CALL
- old: R6-6 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The HIP-632 system contract is called with `CALL`, never `STATICCALL`.
**Why.** The `isAuthorizedRaw` call does not allow a static frame, and the system contract halts inside one; on testnet the same call returned `ok = false` with no data under STATICCALL and a real answer under CALL.
**Cost if wrong.** Every ED25519 signature reads as not authorised.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 298.

### NET-HED-12 — HederaAdapter reports tx_fee and lane_balance
- old: R6-10 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-12 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** As built the adapter implements neither (both default to `None`, `adapter.rs:112-118`; `hedera.rs` implements only `op_consumed/build/sign/submit/tx_status/…`), so neither `gas_budget` nor `min_relayer_balance` ever sees a Hedera sample; only the zero-balance check in `build` (`hedera.rs:163-166`) stops a drain loop. Tests: a failed receipt still adds to `spent`; a balance below the floor stops the lane taking work.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 307.

### NET-HED-13 — Mesh sig_kind hedera_ed25519 verified locally
- old: R6-11 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-13 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** As built, `sig_kind` is only `eoa`/`erc1271` and `check_evm` returns `Ok` for every non-EOA intent (`mesh/digest.rs:193-195`), so garbage intents force every peer to simulate.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 308.

### NET-HED-14 — Hedera v2 wrappers: fail-closed HTS checks
- old: R144 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-06 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-14 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Hedera v2 wrappers check every underlying in `initialize`, fail-closed, through the HTS precompile `0x167`.
**Why.** An HTS underlying with any custom fee breaks a wrapper's reserve or makes `unwrap` revert (the hazard of NET-HED-06), and checking inside `initialize` means a token whose legs cannot be checked or associated is never born.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md](history/specs/2026-10-06-token-wrappers-v2.md) line 149.

### NET-HED-15 — Hedera ED25519 needs a raw signer
- old: CR-WSF-2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/hedera.md#NET-HED-15 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Hedera ED25519 subjects need a raw signer.
**Why.** The contracts accept raw ED25519 over the 32-byte EIP-712 digest only, and HashPack or WalletConnect `hedera_signMessage` adds the HIP-820 prefix, which `isAuthorizedRaw` cannot verify, so those wallets cannot sign meta-transactions for ED25519 accounts.
**Source.** [history/specs/round3-wallet-signing-formats.md](history/specs/round3-wallet-signing-formats.md) line 363.

### NET-HED-80 — Permissionless associateUnderlying
- old: R6-5 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: — · superseded-by: NET-HED-06, NET-HED-14

It said: Permissionless associateUnderlying; replaced by NET-HED-06, NET-HED-14.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-hedera.md) line 296.

## 29. Networks — Cosmos

### NET-COS-01 — IBC ICS-20/27 transfers
- old: req:blockchain.md:ibc · status: open · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-01 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** IBC token transfers (ICS-20) and interchain accounts (ICS-27) are an open owner requirement.
**Open.** Owner decision pending; the default stated in the normative text applies.
**Source.** [history/blockchain.md](history/blockchain.md) line 293.

### NET-COS-02 — Cosmos CW20 + ADR-036, no authz
- old: R66 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-02 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Cosmos = a CW20 token with a contract-level meta operation signed through ADR-036; `x/authz` is never used and `x/feegrant` is only a seam.
**Why.** An `x/authz` grantee would be the relayer, an ordinary account, which breaks the owner rule that only contracts are spenders; a contract grantee is unnecessary because the funds already sit in the contract.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 539.

### NET-COS-03 — Cosmos passkey bound to rpIdHash, origin and UV
- old: CR-R3-1(cosmos-binding) · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-03 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** As built the decoder checks only the UP flag (`ad[32] & 0x01`) and `type`/challenge by substring `contains` (`cosmos/metaop/src/lib.rs:130-148`; `metaop/src/lib.rs:131-144`; no low-s check before `secp256r1_verify`, `cosmos/metaop/src/lib.rs:147`), with no rpIdHash, origin, UV or low-s check, so any page that can obtain an assertion for the rpId (sibling subdomain, related origin, delegated iframe) signs any `MetaOp`. The low-s check closes signature malleability (the digest identity never depended on the signature).
**Cost if wrong.** Cosmos dev passkey accounts change.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 630.

### NET-COS-04 — Cosmos DEX has no Sweep
- old: CR-R3-10 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The Cosmos DEX has no `Sweep`
**Why.** The DEX never holds balances between transactions, as on EVM ("no owner, no sweep"), so an admin `Sweep` has nothing legitimate to move.
**Cost if wrong.** Tokens sent to the DEX directly are lost, as on EVM.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 708.

### NET-COS-05 — Cosmos DEX fill-or-kill, batch all-or-nothing
- old: R9-2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-05 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Cosmos DEX orders are fill-or-kill, and a multi-pair batch is atomic as a whole.
**Why.** Each leg is a fixed signed transfer, so a partial fill cannot be expressed on chain; several `MsgExecuteContract` messages in one Cosmos transaction revert together, so per-pair atomicity does not exist and the off-chain book sends single pairs when a failure must be isolated.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 117.

### NET-COS-06 — Post-simulation grief metered; DEX rereads nonces
- old: R9-3 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-06 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Subject-caused grief after simulation is metered and throttled, not excluded; the DEX re-reads both legs' nonces before settling.
**Why.** After simulation the subject can still move its own balance, and with an empty relayer field anyone can relay its op first, so the failure cannot be ruled out; before this ruling the breaker counted only mined fees and `Settle` was open.
**Cost if wrong.** Even metered, each new payer can cost the lane up to three failed transactions per 24 hours before it is throttled.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 233.

### NET-COS-07 — instantiate2 genesis salt; duplicate chain-id refused
- old: R9-4 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Cosmos contract addresses differ between chains, contracts are instantiated without an admin, and duplicate chain ids are refused.
**Why.** Chain ids are not globally unique (`testing`, `localwasm`, restarted testnets, forks that keep the id) and a classic wasmd address is a function of code id and instance id, so a `pay` signed on one chain ran on its twin; immutability without an admin follows CTR-GEN-02.
**Cost if wrong.** A signed payment replays on a twin chain.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 238.

### NET-COS-08 — contract and valid_until from signed payload
- old: R9-5 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `contract` and `valid_until` come from the signed payload
**Why.** The adapter took `contract` and `valid_until` from the unsigned job JSON, `op_consumed` asked the JSON's contract and the runner held the lane until that `valid_until` plus grace (NODE-LANE-16).
**Cost if wrong.** A job can hold a lane past any signed expiry, or be reported consumed against the wrong contract.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 243.

### NET-COS-09 — Cosmos passkey checks stored rpIdHash and origins
- old: R9-6 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-09 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The Cosmos passkey verifier checks the stored relying-party hashes and origins.
**Why.** The verifier checked only the UP flag, `type` and `challenge`, with no relying-party hash, origin or UV check, so an assertion made for another site was accepted.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 246.

### NET-COS-10 — Resubmit tx dropped from mempool
- old: R9-7 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-10 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A transaction dropped from the mempool is resent
**Why.** CometBFT can evict a transaction at recheck; status then reads `Unknown` while the send was `Ok`, and the runner did not resend, so the lane sat idle until `valid_until` plus grace. Resending the same bytes is idempotent (code 19 means already in the mempool).
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 249.

### NET-COS-11 — extra must be empty outside trade
- old: R9-8 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `extra` must be empty outside `trade`
**Why.** The token ignored `extra` on `pay` and `revoke`, so two payloads that differ only in `extra` authorised the same payment; with `extra` empty, the digest is the single key of one business operation.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 252.

### NET-COS-12 — Cosmos target: MetaCall/MetaTransfer JSON, Mtx messages
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/cosmos.md#NET-COS-12 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The family form of NET-ALL-26 to NET-ALL-29: the encoding of both kinds, the verifier, and the map from each built entry and struct to its `mtx` name; programs are immutable, so it ships as a new deployment.
**Cost if wrong.** Clients, node and contract drift on names and encodings per family.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-2, NM-3, NM-5.

### NET-COS-80 — Cosmos passkey v1 derived address
- old: R9-1 · status: superseded · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: — · superseded-by: NET-ALL-21

It said: Cosmos passkey v1 derived address; replaced by NET-ALL-21.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-cosmos.md) line 13.

### NET-COS-81 — Cosmos passkey v2 20-byte derived address
- old: CR-R3-1(cosmos-address) · status: superseded · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: — · superseded-by: NET-ALL-21

It said: Cosmos passkey v2 20-byte derived address; replaced by NET-ALL-21.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 630.

## 30. Networks — Soroban

### NET-SOR-01 — Soroban native auth as meta-tx; fee-bump
- old: R65 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-01 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** On Soroban the contract-level meta operation is the native Soroban authorization; a relayer lane is the transaction source, and fee-bump lets one lane pay for all.
**Why.** A Soroban authorization entry already is a contract-level verifier with a non-sequential nonce and a domain-separated preimage, so no second verifier is written and the subject's sequence never orders anything.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 538.

### NET-SOR-02 — Ledger expiry computed without RPC
- old: R8-1 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-02 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The ledger expiry is computed without RPC as a safe upper bound.
**Why.** The ERP makes no chain RPC (NODE-STO-03), and ledgers close no faster than one per second, so the anchor-based bound never expires before `valid_until`; overshooting only lengthens how long the host keeps the nonce.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 64.

### NET-SOR-03 — Soroban guardian recovery is a seam
- old: R8-2 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-03 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Soroban guardian recovery is a seam.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 96.

### NET-SOR-04 — __check_auth checks auth contexts per key
- old: R8-8 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-04 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `__check_auth` checks every auth context against the key's `(contract, function)` allowlist.
**Why.** Soroban host authorization is generic (any function that calls `require_auth`), so restriction, not dispatch, is the missing part once every gasless function is an `mtx_` entry (NET-ALL-27); the allowlist aligns with the universal account's key purposes (CTR-UA-10).
**Cost if wrong.** Any one passkey can add an attacker's key to the account.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 97.
Change (2026-10-08): no longer a seam — `__check_auth` checks every auth context against the key's `(contract, function)` allowlist (owner, via NET-ALL-27); Transitional (BUILT): contexts ignored. Source add: `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-2, §5.

### NET-SOR-05 — One signature settles once
- old: R8-3 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-05 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** One signature settles once.
**Why.** A Soroban auth entry consumes its nonce when used, so a partial fill needs the maker to re-sign the rest; `filled[order_hash]`, whose hash excludes the nonce, stops overfill across the re-signed copies.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 137.

### NET-SOR-06 — No multi-pair batch per Soroban tx
- old: R8-4 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-06 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** No multi-pair batch per Soroban transaction.
**Why.** A Soroban transaction is one host call, so a failure in one pair reverts the whole transaction and per-pair atomicity does not exist; the matcher sends one pair per transaction, in parallel across lanes.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 139.

### NET-SOR-07 — DEX jobs carry two auth entries
- old: R8-5 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-03 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-07 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A relayed DEX job carries two auth entries.
**Why.** `settle` needs both the maker's and the taker's `require_auth`, while a `signed_op` job carried only one signature.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 141.
Change (2026-11-02, branch `ua8-soroban` B9a review, after N2): a DEX `settle` is a `ua_metatx` job with named `args`, its native legs in `op.auth`; `signed_op`'s `extra.auth` stays and `extra.call` is gone.

### NET-SOR-08 — Token address is a per-family string
- old: R8-7 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-08 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** A Soroban token address is a per-family string.
**Why.** The token list was typed as an EVM address, which cannot hold the Soroban strkey (`C…`) contract address that `getEvents` filters on.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 182.

### NET-SOR-09 — pay_ref one-shot per (from, pay_ref)
- old: CR-R3-3(rule), R8-9 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-09 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** With a global key, a stranger's 0- or 1-unit `pay(attacker, receiver, …, victim_ref)` burns the victim's ref and blocks the victim's signed payment; booking already sums settlements per `entry_ref` and receiver, so a stranger's payment with someone else's ref is only money in (same direction as Cosmos, which never locks `pay_ref`, and the EVM `MetaToken`). SPECIFIED (as built the key is global, `token/src/lib.rs:203-209`, and `check_amount` accepts 0, `:113-117`). Tests: a third party `pay(self, x, 0, victim_ref)` ⇒ `NonPositiveAmount`; `pay(self, x, 1, victim_ref)` does not block the victim's `pay`; the same `from` paying the same `pay_ref` twice (two signatures) ⇒ `RefUsed`; `pay_under_mandate` cannot be burnt by a third party.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-blockchain-round3-design.md) line 658; [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 224.

### NET-SOR-10 — Soroban orders bind relayer, no open form
- old: R8-10, RS5-15(soroban) · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-10 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The host only matches `dex.settle(order)` (`dex/src/lib.rs:158-159`); the counter-order and `maker_fill` (`:153`) are the submitter's choice, so anyone who sees a pending `settle` (transactions flood to every peer before the ledger closes) re-submits both auth entries with `maker_fill = 1`: both nonces are consumed for a dust fill, the real `settle` fails (the relayer pays) and both makers must sign again. Binding the settler means only the DEX operator's lane can spend the auth entries; roles and `maker_fill` are chosen by the (trusted) operator. Binding `(order, fill)` into the signature is not possible: a resting order is signed before its fill is known. SPECIFIED (as built `Order` has no relayer, `:35-47`). Test: a third party re-submits both auth entries with `maker_fill = 1` ⇒ fails; the right relayer settles.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 230; [history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-dex-design.md) line 438.
Change (2026-10-31, branch `ua-soroban` T7): the `Order.relayer` rule is built with `maker` / `destination` as `Holder`; a relayer that is also a native maker needs two auth entries (NET-SOR-21).

### NET-SOR-11 — TTL extension and RestoreFootprint retry
- old: R8-11 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-11 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Entries in daily use extend their TTL, and an archived footprint is restored by the lane and retried.
**Why.** Only `save` and `set_payee` extended TTLs, so an account in daily use was archived about 60 days after its last key change and a payee 60 days after it was allowed; a `restorePreamble` from simulation killed the job.
**Cost if wrong.** Payments from an archived account or to an archived payee die as dead jobs.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 233.
Change (2026-10-31, branch `ua-soroban` T9): the node's restore half is **built** (a simulation that restores archived entries is accepted within `params.max_deposit_per_job`; NET-SOR-23); the UA entries and the mandate and DEX instances extend their TTL on use (NET-SOR-22).

### NET-SOR-12 — op_consumed reads host nonce key
- old: R8-12 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-12 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `op_consumed` reads the host nonce key
**Why.** An auth entry submitted by someone else, or by the subject itself, consumes the nonce; reading the host nonce key lets the job end as `consumed` instead of `dead` or `reverted`, so the ERP never asks the payer to re-sign an operation that already ran.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 236.

### NET-SOR-13 — Reject crossOrigin true and topOrigin
- old: R8-13 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-13 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The Soroban passkey verifier refuses `"crossOrigin":true` and any `topOrigin`
**Why.** The verifier checked only `type`, `challenge` and `origin`, so a relying-party page embedded in a cross-origin iframe (Permissions-Policy `publickey-credentials-get`) yields a valid assertion under an attacker's page.
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 238.

### NET-SOR-14 — Soroban adapter reports tx_fee and lane_balance
- old: R8-14 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-14 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The Soroban adapter reports `tx_fee` (`feeCharged` from the `resultXdr` of `getTransaction`, for both `SUCCESS` and `FAILED`) and `lane_balance` (native balance of the lane and of the `fee_bump_lane`)
**Why.** Both hooks were left at their `None` default, so the gas-budget and minimum-balance breakers were blind on Soroban, while a `FAILED` transaction still pays inclusion and resource fees that are not refunded (NODE-LANE-13).
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 240.
Change (2026-11-01, branch `ua8-soroban` B9a): **built**: `tx_fee`, `lane_balance`, landed failures counted, both limits required to start; see the B9a entries.
Change (2026-11-01, branch `ua8-soroban` B9a review, owner ruling I-1): `lane_balance` is the balance of the account that pays, under a fee bump the fee account alone, no longer the lane and the `fee_bump_lane`.

### NET-SOR-15 — Signed fields read from invocation
- old: R8-15 · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-07 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-15 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `build` takes `valid_until` (hence `TimeBounds.max_time` and the runner's expiry) and `contract` from the signed invocation
**Why.** `build` read `valid_until` from the unsigned job JSON, so a job could carry a later expiry than the one signed (NODE-LANE-16).
**Source.** [history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md](history/specs/2026-10-03-net-soroban.md) line 242.

### NET-SOR-16 — Soroban target: host authorizations of mtx_ functions
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-08 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-16 · superseded-by: —

**Why.** The family form of NET-ALL-26 to NET-ALL-29: the encoding of both kinds, the verifier, and the map from each built entry and struct to its `mtx` name; programs are immutable, so it ships as a new deployment.
**Cost if wrong.** Clients, node and contract drift on names and encodings per family.
**Source.** `history/specs/2026-10-08-nonevm-metacall-design.md` §3 NM-2, NM-3, NM-5.
Change (2026-10-31, branch `ua-soroban` T6, T6b): the mandate names (`mtx_set_mandate`, `mtx_set_payee`, `mtx_revoke`, `mtx_withdraw`, `mtx_mandate_pay`) are **built** in the UA-Soroban deployment; the token's `pay` and the DEX's `settle` / `cancel` keep their names (plan-F2, NET-SOR-21).

### NET-SOR-17 — Soroban UA registry: a stand-alone contract, portable register, immutable
- old: typed-signing:TS-D8, typed-signing:TS-D9 · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-17 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Records live in the `UaRegistry` contract (`contracts/ua-registry`), registered with the portable `register(kind, key_data, attrs, pop, pqz_pop, relayer)`; no admin, no upgrade; the ML-DSA kinds use only the CAP-0087 host functions; the registration event carries `pop_hash`; one error numbering per contract, appended and never renumbered (SOR-D16 below).
**Why.** Soroban cross-contract calls are synchronous, so tokens call the registry as EVM tokens do (CTR-UA-17); one place gives chain-wide `keyHash` uniqueness (CTR-UA-11) and the UA-8 records; there is no factory to invent. The registration form is the CTR-UA-07 digests so a record copies byte for byte (UA-8 P1). The events limit (16,384 B) forced the `pop_hash` ruling.
**Cost if wrong.** A rename of the registry crate; a registry bug or a new kind is a new registry generation and new token deployments (all chains test-only today).

Change (2026-10-31, controller call, owner may override; plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-typed-signing.md`, [TS-D8], [TS-D9]): **`register` hashes the typed portable records**, `typed(UARegistration{UAPortableRecord{ua, kind, 0, UAKemRecord{ua, 0, 0, 0}}, 0})` under the CTR-UA-07 domain, byte-identical to EVM `UAKinds`, because `main` must stay green when Part P lands. The **typed helpers and the DS / typehash constants live in `scaas-ua-common`, not `ua-registry/src/digest.rs`**, because the token, mandate, DEX and relay-fee tests register by them. An `evm-eoa` member of the portable `pop` signs the typed digest itself (S10 below); raw digests and the `personal_sign` path are in `ua-registry/legacy/typed-signing/`. No new entry point; `attrs` stay refused, the KEM key at version 0 included. Hand-over to `ua8-soroban`, which merges `main` after P + R land: B1 adds the `UAPqzKey` / `UAPqzKeyRecord` typehashes and the typed `kem_record_digest`, `pqz_key_digest`, `pqz_key_record_digest`; B2 / B3 pass the real hashes, store the `register` KEM key at version 0 and keep `set_kem_key` write-once (CTR-UA-32); the `kind_name` view (CTR-UA-35), explicit `contracttype` arguments (CTR-UA-36) and the Soroban packed-`Bytes` inventory of X0 are `ua8-soroban` items; `portable.json` conflicts are resolved by regenerating. Status: built in typed-signing P5; the hand-over items not built.

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S1 — Where the records live** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T3). Options: (a) entries in a `SmartKeyAccount` factory (accounts.md "Where the records live" row; no Soroban factory exists — `SmartKeyAccount` is deployed per account); (b) a stand-alone registry contract, the EVM `UARegistry` shape; (c) no registry, lazy open per token (NEAR / Algorand). Choice and why: **(b)** new crate `smartcontracts/soroban/contracts/ua-registry/`, contract `UaRegistry`. Soroban cross-contract calls are synchronous, so tokens call the registry as EVM tokens do (CTR-UA-17), unlike NEAR; one place for chain-wide `keyHash` uniqueness (CTR-UA-11) and for the UA-8 records; no factory to invent. This crate is the plan's "UA-Soroban registry crate"; its `ua8` module is Part B (plan: "the UA-Soroban name wins"). Cost if wrong: a rename; the accounts.md row is corrected by the build.
- **S2 — The registration form** (who: owner P1 / P2 (2026-10-25); split controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T2, T3). Options: (a) a chain-bound PoP first, the portable one in Part B; (b) the portable `register` from day one. Choice and why: **(b)** `register(kind, key_data, attrs, pop, pqz_pop, relayer)` on the CTR-UA-07 digests (UA-8 P1: "`register` accepts only this form (one rule)"). UA-Soroban accepts only empty `attrs` (error `Attrs`); Part B lifts that and adds the KEM / PQZ entries, `checked` and the relayer mode. UA-Soroban already defines the full `Registration` type, so Part B changes no layout. Cost if wrong: none found.
- **S4 — The ML-DSA verifier** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T2). Options: (a) CAP-0087 host functions; (b) pure Rust in the contract (third-party figure: ML-DSA-65 77.5 M instructions, 33–61 KB Wasm) until Protocol 30 is live. Choice and why: **(a) only.** The owner's "no waiting" (2026-10-29) puts all code on a local Protocol 30 network; mainnet votes Protocol 30 on 2026-11-23, before any use. One verifier module (`verify.rs` in `ua-registry`) serves `register`, `require_authorized` (UA-Soroban) and `set_kem_key` (Part B): the "shared ML-DSA verifier" of TODO step 4. P11's "pure Rust until then" is dropped. Cost if wrong: a Soroban network without Protocol 30 has no ML-DSA kinds (they are disabled there by the code, not by a flag).
- **S16 — Upgrade and admin** (who: CTR-UA-15 (owner); status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T3). Options: —. Choice and why: `UaRegistry`: no admin, no upgrade function (`update_current_contract_wasm` is never called), the relayer list a constructor argument (CTR-UA-15; UA8-D19). Tokens bind the registry at construction, immutable; `None` = the UA ledger is off (`UaLedgerOff`), as EVM's registry 0. Cost if wrong: a new kind or a bug fix is a new registry generation and new token deployments (all chains test-only today).

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D1 — Shared types** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T2). New lib crate `smartcontracts/soroban/contracts/ua-common/` (package `scaas-ua-common`, `crate-type = ["rlib"]`, no `#[contract]`): `Holder`, `Order`, `Checked`, `UaAttrs`, `Registration`, the `UaRegistryClient` (`#[contractclient]` trait), purpose tags, `op_digest`, `pay_lane`, `meta_pay_id`. A contract crate as a dependency would export its entry points into the dependent's Wasm; one type definition keeps the XDR identical in every contract.
- **SOR-D15 — `receivable`** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T3, T5). `false` for an unregistered id too; the token tells the two errors apart on the failure path only (`record_of(ua).is_none()` ⇒ `UaNotRegistered`, else `UaNotReceivable`).
- **SOR-D16 — Error codes** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T3 to T9). Registry: `KindDisabled = 1, KeyData = 2, IdInNativeSpace = 3, AlreadyRegistered = 4, KeyInUse = 5, MemberUnknown = 6, Attrs = 7, Pop = 8, NotRegistered = 9, Unauthorized = 10, NotVerifiable = 11, RelayerNotListed = 12` (Part B continues at 13: `PqzHolder, KemHolder, KemVersion, KemKeyLength, PqzPopHash`). Token (after the built 1–7): `UaLedgerOff = 8, UaNotRegistered = 9, UaNotReceivable = 10, UaPoolNotPayable = 11, BadNonce = 12`; T5 appends `BadOrder = 13` (`ua_trade`: maker not a UA, foreign `sell_token`, `dex` not a deployed contract, `UaPulled` over `sell_amount`) and a replayed `ua_cancel_nonce` digest (`UaCancelUsed`) is `BadNonce` (controller ruling 2026-10-30, owner may override); mandate adds `BadAuth` after its built codes, then `Expired = 10, BadNonce = 11, UaLedgerOff = 12` and (T6b, owner ruling 2026-10-30) `StaleEpoch = 13`; DEX appends `BadAuth = 9, UaLedgerOff = 10` and (T7 fix) `BadDestination = 11`; relay-fee appends `BadPayee` and (T9) `BadExecutor = 3`. A host crypto failure (ed25519 / P-256 / ML-DSA verify panics) is a host error, not `Pop` (finding F1).
- **SOR-D18 — Registry interface check** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T3). `smartcontracts/soroban/scripts/check-registry-interface.sh` compares `stellar contract info interface` of the built `ua-registry` Wasm with the exact function list of T3 (no admin, no upgrade, no setter); run by the `e2e-soroban-local` gate step.

**Rulings and changes (decided during the build):**
- **Plan-F1** (controller, owner may override; branch `ua-soroban` T2, plan review): host-verify failures (ed25519 / P-256 / ML-DSA verify panics, a P-256 point that is not on the curve) are host errors, not `Pop`; tests assert "refused", and an exact `Pop` only where the contract checks itself.
- **Owner A, 2026-10-30 (T0 hard gate)**: `UaRegistered` carries `pop_hash = keccak256(pop)` instead of `pop`; `pop` stays in contract state, readable by `registration_of`; same rule on every family including EVM (CTR-UA-33, merged to main as `msig-pophash`). Why: the full record of a 3-member ML-DSA-65 `msig` overran the events limit (17,228 B against 16,384 B). Cost if wrong: an indexer reads `pop` from state, not the log. Status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T0 fix pass 2, T3.
- The registry interface is checked by `check-registry-interface.sh` against the exact function list (SOR-D18); the S1 row's old plan of records as `UA(ua)` / `KEY(keyHash)` entries in a `SmartKeyAccount` factory (accounts.md, previous Soroban row) is replaced by the registry's `Ua(ua)` / `Key(key_hash)` entries; a UA is shown only as the URN `urn:scaas:ua:v1:<kind name>:<hex32>` (owner 2026-10-30: the kind **name** of `kinds.json`, never the code; lower-case hex; recorded on main in NET-ALL-21). A `urn:scaas:ua:` prefix in any case that is not the lower-case URN is a UA form, never a strkey: `clientkeys` `parseRecipient` refuses it as `UAIdFormat` and `assertNativeRecipient` as `UaNotNative` (final review B-m1, 2026-10-31; status: built).
- **ua8-soroban B2, explicit Soroban arguments** (controller call under the typed-signing hand-over TS-D9, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B2; supersedes the plan's "`register` signature unchanged" and its `attrs.kem_pk` / `kem_version` shapes). `UaAttrs` is EVM's `UAAttrs`: `{pqz_key, pqz_pop_hash, kem: KemKey{scheme, mlkem_ek, x25519}, kem_pk_hash}`; `register` takes no KEM version, its key is version 0, whole (`Kem(ua, 0)`) or hash-committed (`kem_pk_hash` ≠ 0, `kem` only its scheme, version 0 empty until B3's fill; `checked_of` then says `None` for it). `msig` has one typed form as EVM: `register_msig(structure: MsigStructure, attrs, pop: Vec<MemberSig>, pqz_pop, relayer)`, the CTR-UA-09 key data assembled in the contract, a `threshold`, `kind` or `weight` above `u16` or more than 16 members `KeyData` (no truncated id), the `pop` stored as `abi.encode(MemberSig[])` so `registration_of` returns EVM's bytes; `register(0x0120, …)` is `KeyData`. `require_authorized` takes `UaSig{key_data, signature, members}`: a single key only `signature`, an `msig` only `members`, `key_data` always empty on Soroban (the key is read from `Signer(ua)`, as EVM's stored kinds), any other field set `Unauthorized`; out-of-order slots, a slot-level `key_data` and a `sig` on a `G…` member are the caller's error, `Unauthorized` from `require_authorized`, `Pop` from `register`, as EVM `_msig` returning false (they were `Pop` everywhere; this amends the `Pop` in Owner B's `keyData` ruling for `require_authorized` only, the refusal itself stands). `set_kem_key` / `set_pqz_key` follow in B3. `register_webauthn(key: WebAuthnKey{x, y, rp_id_hash}, attrs, pop, pqz_pop, relayer)` is EVM `registerWebAuthn` (TS-D13): `x ‖ y ‖ rp_id_hash` assembled in the contract, the same id, digests and record as the packed `register(0x0100, …)`, which stays, as EVM. MuSig2 and FROST get no typed entry here: their kinds are `KindDisabled` on Soroban; whether B4's relayer-checked mode needs `register_musig2` / `register_frost` is B4's question.
- **ua8-soroban B2, tokens take `UaSig`** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B2). The `auth` of every Soroban entry (`ua_*`, `mtx_*`, DEX `settle` / `ua_cancel`, router `ua_relay`) is `UaSig`, an empty one for a native signer, with no `bytes auth` bridge. EVM's `UAKinds.uaSig` bridge until C2 needs a self-describing blob (`abi.encode(keyData, sig)`); Soroban's `auth` was the raw signature, so a bridge could not tell an `msig` without reading the record. Op digests exclude `auth` and are unchanged; `ua-ops.json` gains `authXdr` (the `UaSig` ScVal), `auth` stays the signature bytes.
- **ua8-soroban B2, the attribute check order** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B2). `check_attrs` is EVM `_attrs` in its order, over the brief's: PQZ holder, KEM holder, `pqz_pop_hash` rules, `pqz_pop` hash, PQZ key length (`KeyData`), KEM key. `pqzKeyHash` is `keccak256(PQZ_KEY_GROUP ‖ key)` (`portable.json`, the authority), not the plain `keccak256(pqz_key)` the plan wrote. `FNDSA512` is already a holder here so B4 only enables the kind.
- **ua8-soroban B2, `register` logs its attribute writes** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B2). U8S-D4 keeps `UaRegistered` without bytes, so nothing else would log a whole KEM key's hash: `register` also publishes `UaPqzKeySet`, `UaPqzPopStored` and `UaKemKeySet` (version 0), `sig_hash = keccak256("")`, before `UaRegistered`; about 1.5 KB for the largest row.
- **ua8-soroban B2, `kind_name`** (TS-D5, owner 2026-10-31; status: built, ua8-soroban B2). The view returns EVM's `UAKinds.name` table, enabled here or not; any other id panics `KindUnknown = 20`, continuing U8S-D5. `kem_record_digest` / `kem_pk_record_hash` of `(version 0, empty key)` is EVM's zero record `UAKemRecord{ua, 0, 0, 0}` (B1 review).
- **ua8-soroban B3, explicit `set_kem_key` / `set_pqz_key` and the KEM views** (controller call under the typed-signing hand-over TS-D9, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B3; supersedes the plan's `kem_pk: Bytes`, `sig: Bytes` and `(u64, Bytes, Bytes, Checked)`). `set_kem_key(ua, version, kem: KemKey, sig: UaSig, relayer)`, `set_pqz_key(ua, pqz_key, pqz_pop_hash, sig: UaSig, relayer)`, `kem_key_of(ua) -> Option<(u64, KemKey, Bytes, Checked)>`, `kem_key_at(ua, version) -> Option<(KemKey, Bytes, Checked)>`: EVM's shapes. `sig` is checked as EVM `_portableOk` (`key_data` never, a single key only `signature`, an `msig` only `members` under `check_msig`'s portable rule, U8S-D1) and stored as EVM `_portableBytes` (`signature`, or `abi.encode(MemberSig[])`); a minimal-rule failure is `Unauthorized`. `Kem(ua, version)` stays `(pk, sig, Checked)` with the assembled bytes (U8S-D3). `set_kem_key` is write-once for every version and takes version 0 only to fill a hash-committed `register`, with an empty `sig`, open to anyone (EVM rule, owner KEM rulings of 2026-10-31); a key given in whole at `register` is not refillable (`KemVersion`). `kem.scheme` is a `u32` here, so the field is checked and not the assembled first byte (0x101 is `KemScheme`).
- **ua8-soroban B3, `KemKeyHash = 21`** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B3; continues U8S-D5, which has no code for it). EVM `UAKemKeyHash`: `set_kem_key(ua, 0, …)` with a key that does not hash to `attrs.kem_pk_hash`. Soroban's enum had no error for it, and `KemKeyLength` or `Unauthorized` would name a different failure.
- **ua8-soroban B9, the B0 models move to `spike/legacy/ua8-b0`** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B9). `register_pqz_kem_model`, `store_pqz_pop_model`, `set_kem_key_model`, `set_pqz_key_model`, `keccak_model`, their six budget tests and their `measure.py` rows left the spike: `attrs.kemVersion` is gone from `portable.json` and the portable digests are typed, so keeping them would be a second copy of the registry, whose host figures (`e2e_ua8_network_fit`, `e2e_ua8_relayer_table`) replace them. The B0 run log stays. **If wrong:** the models come back from `legacy/` and are rebuilt on the typed digests.
- **ua8-soroban B3, `PqzK` carries `pqz_pop_hash`** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B3; amends U8S-D3's `PqzK(ua) → (key, sig, Checked)`). U8S-D3 keeps `attrs.pqz_key` out of `registration_of` for a `set_pqz_key` key by leaving `Ua(ua).attrs.pqz_pop_hash` 0, so that hash needs a place of its own, which `pqz_key_of` and `store_pqz_pop` read. It is `PqzK(ua) → (key, sig, Checked, pqz_pop_hash)`: one entry, one write, as B0 measured it, and `Ua(ua)` is not rewritten (at `msig` n = 16 it is 57,520 B of write budget). A second entry would be one more write for 32 B. `register` writes the same shape.
- **ua8-soroban B3, signature refusals are the caller's error** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B3; extends B2's slot-level rule). `verify::check`, `check_evm_eoa`, `ed25519`, `webauthn::check` and the ABI readers behind it take the caller's error for the checks the contract does itself (a wrong length, a wrong recovered address, a malformed assertion): `Pop` from `register`, `Unauthorized` from `set_kem_key`, `set_pqz_key` and `require_authorized`, as EVM. `portable.json`'s `kem-record-of-other-ua` (`UAUnauthorized`, a 666 B signature on an `mldsa65` UA) needs it. It changes `require_authorized`: a wrong-form signature, an empty one too, was `Pop`, now `Unauthorized` (the DEX test `dex_ua_maker_native_taker_settles` pinned the old code). A host verify failure stays a host error (plan finding F1), and `KeyData` for a key stays, unreachable for a stored key.
- **ua8-soroban B3, the `set_pqz_key` limit of an `msig`** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B3; closes B0's finding as the published Soroban maximum, not a STOP). Under U8S-D3 `PqzK` holds key and signature in one entry of at most 65,536 B, so `set_pqz_key` takes at most 13 signing ML-DSA-65 slots at n2048-kmax1024 / n2304-kmax4096 and 12 at n2560-kmax16384 / n2816-kmax65536. `ua8_set_pqz_key_msig_largest_fits` runs those; `ua8_set_pqz_key_msig_over_limit_*` show 13 at n2816-kmax65536 and 14 at n2048-kmax1024 refused by the SDK's entry-limit metering. The limit counts signing slots, not members: an `msig` of 16 members with a threshold those slots meet fits, and any size registers a PQZ key through `register` itself (the key in `PqzK`, the `pop` in `Ua(ua)`; B0: n = 16 fits). Over the limit the transaction fails and stores nothing, so no byte is lost. B0's alternative, a `PqzS(ua)` entry of its own lifting it to 16, is not built. The limit is permanent: there is no upgrade and the structure is the id, so an `msig` needing more slots that registered without a key can never add one on Soroban, and its EVM `setPqzKey` record cannot be copied here. The rule to publish is bytes, not a slot count: `key + 64 + n × 3,520` B for Chain kinds (ML-DSA-65 slots, 64,832 B at 12 slots with a 22,528 B key), plus the entry's own overhead, within 65,536 B. Amended by ua8-soroban B4: the 13 / 12 are the figures for ML-DSA-65 slots only. The rule is `key + 64 + Σ (192 + ⌈sig / 32⌉ × 32)` B over the signing slots, with `ua8_set_pqz_key_relayer_slots_*` asserting the stored size. A relayer-checked `slhdsa128s` slot is 7,856 B of signature, so 8,064 B in the entry: 6 slots at n2048-kmax1024 (64,832 B, 7 refused), 5 at n2304-kmax4096, n2560-kmax16384 and n2816-kmax65536 (62,912 B at n2816-kmax65536, 6 refused). The reviewer's "about 5 at n2816-kmax65536" holds exactly; only the smallest set takes a sixth. A `fndsa512` slot is 864 B, an `mldsa44` slot 2,624 B, an `ed25519` slot 256 B. The same bytes bound the other two stored signatures: `register`'s `pop` in `Ua(ua)` takes 7 `slhdsa128s` slots (`ua8_register_relayer_slots_*`; 8 are refused, the 64,576 B of `pop` leaving too little for the record around it, which B0's 16 ML-DSA-65 slots at 56,384 B do not reach), and `set_kem_key`'s `Kem(ua, v)` 7 by the formula, not run. So an `msig` needing 8 or more `slhdsa128s` signatures cannot register on Soroban at all, permanently, as the structure is the id; it stays usable on every chain that verifies it, and nothing is lost by the refusal. The real host's figures per set and kind, which B8 publishes, are in "the relayer's auth covers one word"; `set_kem_key` is now run, not only by the formula.
- **ua8-soroban B4, the relayer-checked mode** (U8S-D8, UA8-D18–D20, P11, spec §6; controller call within them, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B4). A part the chain cannot verify is stored only through `attest`: no `relayer` is `NotVerifiable`, a relayer outside the constructor's list is `RelayerNotListed`, then `relayer.require_auth()` over the whole call (since owner 2026-11-01 over one word, the digest of the call's arguments: "the relayer's auth covers one word"), and the part carries `Checked::Relayer(r)` in state and event. A part the chain verifies never reaches it, whatever `relayer` says: it is verified as before, stays open to anyone, and the relayer is not asked (no `require_auth`, an unlisted `relayer` ignored). The parts: the `pop` of a U8S-D8 kind; `set_kem_key` ≥ 1 and `set_pqz_key` of such a UA; an `msig` slot of a registered relayer-checked member or of an `evm-contract` member, on the three portable writes only. An `msig`'s `Checked` follows the slots given, one attestation for all of them (a second `require_auth` would need a second auth entry): a structure with a relayer-checked member whose `pop` is chain slots alone is `Chain`, which is what "a part the chain cannot verify" says and is narrower than spec §6's "an `msig` with such a member". A classical-dominant `msig` has no `pop`, so `Chain` and no relayer whatever its members (U8S-D2). What `register` carries (`Kem(ua, 0)`, `PqzK`) takes `pop_checked`, and so does the fill of a hash commit, which needs no relayer: the chain compares the hash, the `pop` signed it. A relayer-checked record: key data checked for length and layout only (the relayer checks canonical form with `scaas_ua::keydata`: 75 of `kinds.json`'s 130 `invalid[]` rows of these kinds store on chain, marked, 55 are `KeyData`), `keyHash` by its `kinds.json` group, in `KeyR` (the next entry), `signable = false`, no `Signer`, so never receivable and `require_authorized` is `Unauthorized`. An `msig`'s `signable` counts only `Signer` members and `G…`: a relayer-checked member weighs 0 (U8S-D8), and outside the portable writes its slot has no `Signer`, so `short`, and an `evm-contract` slot stays `NotVerifiable`. So a mixed `msig` whose `Signer` members alone reach the threshold is `signable` even when its `pop` is `Relayer`: its authority is those members' chain signatures, the attestation adds none (brief, over spec §6's "A `Relayer` record has `signable = false`", which reads as the single-key rule). The list has one writer, the constructor (`ua8_relayer_list_immutable` ties `check-registry-interface.sh` to the source). P11.6's remedy, delisting, means a new deployment on Soroban, the list being immutable.
- **ua8-soroban B4 review, a marked record blocks no `Chain` kind** (controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B4 review; amends U8S-D8's "`keyHash` uniqueness by its `kinds.json` group" and narrows P11.6). A shared `Key(kh)` let a listed relayer store a `bip340`, `musig2-secp256k1` or `frost-secp256k1` record over a victim's `x`, with no proof and any prefix byte: the real `secp256k1` key was then `KeyInUse` for good, with no UA and no `Signer`, and any `msig` naming it `MemberUnknown`. A relayer-checked record now keeps its key in its own `KeyR(kh)`. A `Chain` kind checks only `Key`; a relayer kind checks both, so it never stores over a key the chain proved and two relayer kinds still keep one key between them; `key_owner` returns `Key` before `KeyR`. So a marked record never blocks a `Chain` kind, in either order the real key registers or holds, and the marked record stays, marked, for clients to ignore. The rule is by class, so it covers every group a relayer kind shares with a `Chain` kind; today that is only `secp256k1`. Among relayer kinds P11.6 stands: a bad record takes its key there, on this chain only. `kinds.json` `keyHash` values are unchanged.

EVM's views `muSig2KeyOf` / `frostKeyOf` have no twin, as `msigOf` and `webAuthnKeyOf`.

Soroban's `check_msig` also admits a `stellar-account` (`G…`) member, by host auth, which has no off-chain form. The table lists what the chain verifies, not what it does not, so a kind the node does not know goes through `check_*` and is refused: a table behind the contract cannot skip a check. A part the chain verifies is not checked, because `check_*` refuses a valid `G…` member and the chain is that part's check. Neither the fill of a hash commit (`set_kem_key` version 0: the chain compares the hash, no `relayer`) nor `store_pqz_pop` attests anything. A marked part without a `relayer` is refused before simulation (it would be `NotVerifiable`). A `G…` member beside a marked slot stays refused (`UAKeyData`), the owner's question left open under B5. `set_kem_key` and `set_pqz_key` read the record with `record_of`, and the answer must hash to the job's `ua` (`ua_of`), since it decides whether anything is checked at all. `msig` members are read as `check_members` reads them, through `record_of` by simulation: a `Chain` kind counts only when `signable`, which is exactly when `Signer(id)` exists, a marked kind by its `Ua` record, natives not at all; so no second view is called. `scaas_ua::derive_ua` runs on the key data before any member is read, so the contract's 16 members bound one job's simulations (B6 review). A restore with no value, or a host refusal of `record_of`, is `Revert`: that is this job's state, and `relay_poll` is oldest first, so a requeued job would be claimed first every round and starve the chain's queue. Only an RPC failure is `Transport`, and it never reads as unregistered. The check runs with feature `pq`, without which every PQ signature is `Pop`.

While no read has answered nobody is listed, so a relayer-mode job fails closed; payments and Chain-part jobs keep running.

For `relayer = None` they are the real check and both fired on the real host: a `G…` slot of another account `the call needs another account's signature`, a `G…` slot of this lane `the lane's authority`. New: with PQZ key and KEM key at n2816-kmax65536 relayer-mode `register` takes 5 `slhdsa128s` slots (130,912 B), 6 are refused; a `fndsa512` with PQZ key, KEM key and proof at n2816-kmax65536 fits whole (124,224 B); the proof can always split off (`store_pqz_pop` has no relayer). The finding: `UaRegistered` carries `key_data`, so a large FROST key met the events limit: a `frost-bn254` key of 16 members registered up to threshold 13 and failed on chain from 14, the host saying `Error(Budget, ExceededLimit)`, `total events size exceeds network config maximum`, 16792, 16384. Such a key, valid on EVM, could never be copied here, there being no upgrade. The rule: `EVENT_KEY_DATA_MAX = 15,360`. `key_data` of length at most that is in the event, byte for byte, as EVM's `keyData`; a longer one leaves the event, which then has `key_data` empty. It is decided from `key_data.len()` alone, in `register_record`, the one path of `register`, `register_msig`, `register_webauthn`, `register_musig2` and `register_frost`. Stored data does not change: `ua` stays the topic and is the key's own, `record_of` and `registration_of` return the bytes. Derivation, from measured event sizes, return value included. `register_frost` emits one event, because a FROST key is no PQZ or KEM holder (`PqzHolder`, `KemHolder`), and that event is `key_data` plus 892 B, exactly, at every one of the 120 shapes measured (15,808 B around 14,916 B, 15,840 B around 14,948 B, 1,408 B around 516 B). So 16,384 − 892 = 15,492 B is the most that fits, rounded down to 15 KiB: at the constant the event is 16,252 B, 132 B under the limit. The overhead has no variable part, which is what lets a margin that size stand. No other entry comes near, and each has its worst case far under the limit with every event it emits: `register` 3,440 B (an `mldsa65` with PQZ key, proof and KEM key: `key_data` 1,952 B, four events), a relayer-checked `register` 2,564 B, `register_msig` 2,244 B (`key_data` at most 580 B), `register_musig2` 1,984 B (1,090 B), `register_webauthn` 96 B of `key_data`. The holders' `key_data` is bounded at 1,952 B, so attributes and a large key never meet. In practice FROST lengths are discrete: the largest key that stays in the event is 14 of 15, 14,948 B, 15,840 B of events, 544 B under the limit; on secp256k1 the largest key is 9,525 B and always stays. Exactly four shapes are emptied, all `frost-bn254`: 15 of 15 (15,908 B), 14 of 16 (15,940 B), 15 of 16 (16,964 B), 16 of 16 (17,988 B), each with an event of 892 B. A lower constant was refused: 14,336 B would also empty 13 of 16 and 14 of 15, which fit, against "only when it is too large". Threshold 1 exists on no chain (`t >= 2` on EVM `_frost`, in `scaas_ua::keydata` and here), so the shapes are thresholds 2 to 16 with `n` from the threshold to 16, 120 in all, and threshold 1 is `KeyData`. Readers: `scaas-node`'s `decode_event` takes `ua` and `kind` from the topics and reads nothing of the data, so an empty `key_data` is the same row; clientkeys and `scaas_ua` do not read the event; no event vector exists; nothing to regenerate. A reader that wants the key of a large record reads `record_of`. Cost if wrong: a log-only indexer cannot rebuild those four shapes from the log and needs one state read, which `pop` already needs on every family (CTR-UA-33.A).

Simulation refuses neither. Over the 65,536 B entry limit the transaction lands and fails, `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, the job `reverted`, nothing stored, the lane charged 0.039–0.065 XLM; B3's "the transaction fails and stores nothing" holds, at that price, on a job that is free to the client (P9). Over `tx_max_size_bytes` `sendTransaction` answers `ERROR` (`txSOROBAN_INVALID`), the transaction enters no ledger, and the node's `Rejected` path puts the job back to `queued` (seen on the real host, one step; the test double's job source does not offer it again). By the code it would then be rebuilt and refused again until its `valid_until`, at most 3,600 s, at the head of an oldest-first queue: the same starvation B6's review ruled out for an archived record. Fixed in the next entry. The entry limit stays open: simulation does not refuse the write, measured on a 14-slot `set_pqz_key` and on a 70,000 B `store_pqz_pop`, but it answers with what a check needs: `stateChanges[].after` is 70,128 B and `write_bytes` the same, so `build` could compare the largest `after` with the network's `contract_data_entry_size_bytes`, and no fee would be spent. Not built. An enforcing simulation, which every `Some(lane)` job gets, answers `stateChanges` too (B7b review, measured: 5 entries, all with `after`), so the check would cover relayer-mode jobs. One thing is not measured: the exact boundary (the largest entry that landed is 65,084 B, and the smallest refused 65,556 B, computed by the byte rule because it never landed).
- **ua8-soroban B7 review, a transaction over `tx_max_size_bytes` is refused at `build`** (controller ruling 2026-11-01, the class of B6's archived record: a per-job state never returns to `queued`; form: controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B7 review). `build`, the one exit of every Soroban job kind, compares the finished transaction with the network's limit before anything is signed: over it is `Revert`, so the job is `dead` on one claim, no fee, and the next job goes. The limit is read for each job through `getLedgerEntries` (the `ContractBandwidthV0` setting), since validators vote it and no job should go on an assumed value; that is one more RPC per job, next to a simulation. A read that fails uses the last good answer (B7 review, controller ruling, owner may override: a failed read must not stop payments while simulation works, the class of B6's first `relayers()` form), so only the first read of a process, with no answer yet, can be `Transport`, and a voted change is seen on the next good read, with no restart. What is counted was measured, not assumed: core counts the signed V1 envelope, and a fee bump's outer 128 B do not count. On the real host a V1 envelope of exactly 132,096 B lands and 132,100 B is `ERROR`; fee-bumped, 132,224 B sent (132,096 B counted) lands and 132,228 B is `ERROR`. So the node sizes the V1 envelope with a blank signature of ed25519's length, with no key used, on both paths. `e2e_ua8_tx_size_limit`, `oversized_job_does_not_hold_the_queue`, `transaction_of_exactly_the_limit_passes`, `oversized_ua_metatx_refused_at_build`, `unread_limit_is_transport`.
- **ua8-soroban B9a, a landed failure counts against the budget, on every family that reports a fee** (owner ruling 2026-11-01: the Soroban adapter gets a working spend stop before this branch merges; status: built, ua8-soroban B9a; builds the `fee` of NODE-LANE-13 on the generic runner, its `value_out` and `deposits` stay SPECIFIED; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands). `follow` now feeds `Breaker::spend` for `Reverted` as for `Mined`, so a lane burned by failing `call` jobs stops: the breaker opens at the budget and later jobs are never claimed, while a job in flight is still followed to its report. The change is on every family, because none double counts, read one by one: Solana (`meta.fee`), Aptos (`gas_used` × `gas_unit_price`) and NEAR (`tokens_burnt`) charge a failed transaction and answer what they charged; Algorand drops its `spent` entry at a `pool-error`, a group refused at the pool having paid nothing, so `tx_fee` answers `None`; Hedera, Sui, Cosmos and TON report no fee (the default `Ok(None)`); EVM never runs `follow` (`uses_adapter` is false) and `submit.rs` already meters every receipt, reverted ones too. Not every billed failure is `Reverted`, though: Solana's `classify_landed` (a compute-budget error, or a failure at instruction 0) and Aptos's `classify_committed` (out of gas) answer `Rejected` for a transaction that landed and paid, and `follow`'s `Rejected` arm reports `queued` with no `meter`, so those fees miss the budget and the counter; recorded, not changed here. Inside `follow` the `Reverted` arm runs again while `op_consumed` is unreadable, so the fee is metered once per transaction, and also on the path where the op was already consumed, since ours was billed all the same. A failed `tx_fee` read never holds the job's report; it is logged and counted per lane in the counter `scaas_fee_unread_total` (the budget adds no guess), `Ok(None)` is not a failed read. `recover_lane` still follows with no breaker: a restart resets the in-memory window anyway.
- **ua8-soroban B9a, what `tx_fee` and `lane_balance` answer on Soroban** (measured, `e2e_ua8_spend_stop`, Protocol 30 quickstart; status: built and proven, ua8-soroban B9a; builds NET-SOR-14). `tx_fee` is `feeCharged` of the `resultXdr` of `getTransaction`, for `SUCCESS` and `FAILED`; under a fee bump that outer result is the fee that left the fee account. Each figure equals the payer's balance drop on the real host: 956,837 stroops (`SUCCESS`), 377,361 (`FAILED`), 956,937 (fee bump `SUCCESS`), 377,461 (fee bump `FAILED`), with the sending lane down by 0 under the fee bump. A status other than these two, a missing `resultXdr`, bytes that do not decode or a negative fee is an `Err`, counted as above, never a zero. `lane_balance` is the balance of the account that pays (it was a sum of the two; see the owner's ruling below). An account that does not exist holds 0, which is an answer and opens the floor (the real RPC answers no entry for it, with its `latestLedger`); a failed read, or an answer with no `latestLedger`, is an `Err` and the last balance stands. Balances are raw, the base reserve not taken off, as on every family.
- **ua8-soroban B9a, a Soroban lane does not start without both spend limits** (controller call under the owner's ruling of 2026-11-01, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban B9a). `Config::validate` refuses a `soroban` chain whose `breaker.gas_budget_per_hour` or `breaker.min_relayer_balance` is unset or 0 when `modules.submit` is on; an indexer-only node has no lane to limit, and the rule holds for every Soroban chain, `ua_registry` set or not. Why refusing over a default: the amount is a money decision (ops names the finance owner for it), a default would be an XLM figure nobody chose, on a family that also serves Pi, and it would surface at run time as a lane stopped by a limit nobody set, while a refusal surfaces once, at deployment, naming both keys; a missing required parameter already ends this way (`params.network_passphrase`). All chains are test-only, so nothing migrates. `node.example.toml` sets 100 XLM an hour per lane and a 10 XLM floor on both Soroban chains. What that budget stops is large successes, about 10 of the largest an hour, 5 or 6 of them `call` jobs at their share. Failures alone never reach it: a lane lands at most 720 transactions an hour, so at the 0.07 XLM a failed job can cost that is 50.4 XLM, and 27 XLM at the measured 377,361 stroops; only the worst case reaches the `call` share of 50 XLM. An operator who wants failing jobs stopped inside the hour sets a lower budget. Amended by [NET-SOR-29](networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-29): 0.07 XLM was the failures measured, not a bound; the bound is the per-job cap.
- **ua8-soroban B9a, an entry over the limit is refused at `build`** (measured, `e2e_ua8_spend_stop`; status: built and proven, ua8-soroban B9a; closes the entry limit left open in "what a write over a limit does" and answers its unmeasured boundary). The host compares the whole `LedgerEntry`, which is what `stateChanges[].after` carries, with `contract_data_entry_size_bytes`, exactly: `after` of 65,520, 65,524, 65,528, 65,532 and 65,536 B landed `SUCCESS`, 65,540, 65,544, 65,548 and 65,552 B landed `FAILED`, every one of them on the real host. The earlier 65,084 B is the `LedgerEntryData` alone, 8 B less than its `after`. So `build` refuses when the largest `ContractData` `after` is over the network's limit: `Revert`, `dead` on one claim, nothing signed, no fee; 65,536 B still runs (`e2e_ua8_spend_stop`, through the node). The limit is read per job as `tx_max_size_bytes` is, a failed read keeping the last answer and a voted change seen on the next good read. What the check cannot read lets the job through, since it only saves a fee and the chain still refuses: no `stateChanges`, no `after`, an `after` that does not decode, or a limit never answered. Code entries are not compared, the limit being data's. This covers relayer-mode jobs, whose enforcing simulation answers `stateChanges` too.
- **ua8-soroban B9a review, `lane_balance` is the account that pays** (owner ruling 2026-11-01, I-1; status: built and proven, ua8-soroban B9a review; amends R8-14 and NET-SOR-14, which named the lane and the `fee_bump_lane`; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands). `lane_balance` reads `self.fee_bump.unwrap_or(lane)`: the lane's own account, or under a fee bump the fee account alone, every lane of the chain reporting that one balance. Why: under a fee bump only the fee account pays, so the sum built first kept an empty fee account behind a funded lane above the floor, and `sendTransaction` answered `ERROR`, `Rejected`, `queued`, `Step::Done` with no backoff, spinning at RPC speed and stalling the lane; the ceiling recorded with the sum said that case spends nothing, and that was true of the fee and wrong of the lane. `ops.md`'s runway alerts change with it: a lane's balance and its own burn would overstate the runway of a shared fee account, so a chain with `fee_bump_lane` has the alerts on the fee account over the burn of all its lanes. A JSON answer with no `result` used to sum to 0 and open the floor: `lane_balance` now requires `latestLedger`, else `Err`.
- **ua8-soroban B9a review, a job put back to the queue always backs off** (owner ruling 2026-11-01 with I-1: a tight loop must not exist; status: built, ua8-soroban B9a review; every family on the generic runner, EVM keeps its own runner). The spin of I-1 was not the fee account's: every `Rejected` ended in `Step::Done`, which skips the backoff, while the queue, oldest first, hands the same job straight back. So it remained for any other `sendTransaction` `ERROR` (`txSOROBAN_INVALID` from a resource limit the pre-checks do not compare, `txINSUFFICIENT_FEE`, `txBAD_SEQ`), on every family that answers `Rejected` (a CheckTx refusal on Cosmos, for one), and for the two puts-back before a send, `in flight on another path` and `SUBJECT_HELD`. `follow` now answers why it put the job back and `step_once` turns that, and those two, into `Step::Retry`: 1 s doubling to 60 s, reset by the next job that ends. Measured on the stub: 1 to 3 sends in 2.5 s, 550 without it. What stays: a job the network refuses for good under a code other than `txSOROBAN_INVALID` (next entry) holds the whole chain's queue, not one lane: the poll is per chain and every lane claims the oldest first, so all lanes retry it, each once per 60 s, and no job behind it runs until its `valid_until` (at most 3,600 s for a `call` job; other kinds carry the client's own). The attempt cap of NODE-LANE-14 is SPECIFIED and covers it.
- **ua8-soroban B9a review, `call` jobs stop at half the budget** (owner decision 2026-11-01, I-2; status: built, ua8-soroban B9a review; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands). Without it the budget gate has no notion of job kind: about 20 of the largest free `call` jobs open the breaker on 2 lanes in a minute and stop payments until the top of the hour. So `call` jobs stop at `breaker.call_budget_pct` of `gas_budget_per_hour`, default 50, 1 to 100 at config check, every other kind runs to 100 %, and the next window reopens both. The share compares the lane's whole spend in the window, payments included, the one counter the budget has. It is Soroban's: `step_once` asks `adapter.family()`, because Hedera runs the EVM job rules on the same runner and a `call` job there is not free in the same way, and EVM's own runner never asks, so both behave as before. A stopped `call` job is not claimed, so it stays `queued` and costs nothing. The queue is oldest first, so stopped `call` jobs at its head would hide a payment behind them from a read of 5: while `call` jobs are stopped the read is 50 jobs, the client's own clamp on `relay_poll`'s `limit`. That is a limit of the legacy pull path: a backlog over 50 `call` jobs hides a payment, across windows while the backlog lasts, because each new window runs those `call` jobs first and stops them again. The node's own queue claims by kind (NODE-JOB-21, next but one entry). The full budget gate moved from `lane_runner` into `step_once`, so `lane_step` honours it. A transition is logged; there is no metric for it yet, `NAMES` being the breakers that stop everything.
- **ua8-soroban B9a review, `txSOROBAN_INVALID` is terminal** (controller ruling 2026-11-02, under "a per-job state never returns to `queued`"; status: built, ua8-soroban B9a review; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands). A job refused for good holds the whole chain's queue, so `submit` decodes `errorResultXdr`: `txSOROBAN_INVALID`, plain or inside a fee bump's `txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED` (the real bytes of `e2e_ua8_tx_size_limit`), is the new `Refused`, and `follow` ends the job on its one claim, `dead`, or `consumed` if the op already ran, with `Step::Done`, so the next job runs. It is kept to that one code: `txBAD_SEQ`, `txINSUFFICIENT_FEE` and every other code stay `Rejected`, a rebuild being able to pass, and so do bytes that do not decode. An unreadable `op_consumed` goes back to `queued` with the backoff, as at `build`.
- **ua8-soroban B9a review, "a stopped kind never hides another" is the node's guarantee** (owner correction 2026-11-02: the node is open and any consumer can run it, so this is not a consumer's to give; status: SPECIFIED, NODE-JOB-21; the pull path's limit built and recorded). The node's own queue (`POST /v1/jobs`, the store, namespaces) claims by kind, so a stopped kind never hides another, with a per-namespace `call` quota. The built legacy pull path cannot give this: `relay_poll` hands the oldest jobs of a chain and the client clamps `limit` to 50, so a backlog over 50 `call` jobs can hide a payment across windows on that path. That is recorded as a limit of the path, not as a change asked of anyone who runs a client.
- **ua8-soroban B9a review, the smaller findings** (status: built, ua8-soroban B9a review). `scaas_fee_unread_total` gets the alert `ops.md` promised, `ScaasFeeUnread`, `increase(scaas_fee_unread_total[15m]) > 0`, P2. `meter` runs on the real host: `e2e_ua8_spend_stop` sends a mined job through `lane_step_metered` and compares the budget with the lane's balance drop, read through the new `Breaker::spent`. A tx not found after its status answered was `Ok(None)` on Solana, Aptos and NEAR, a silent zero that missed the counter: it is an `Err` now, and `Ok(None)` stays for a family with no fee to report and for Algorand's group refused at the pool. On Soroban an entry with no `xdr` in `lane_balance`'s answer is an `Err`, not 0.
- **ua8-soroban B7, B0's model against the real contract** (measured; status: closed, ua8-soroban B7; closes the carry "B0's model may not do the same"). B0's model did load the record: `set_kem_key` of an `msig` n = 16 is 57.4 M instructions in B0 and 58.1 M here, 58,312 B of writes in both, and the real `register_msig` n = 16 at n2816-kmax65536 is 63.7 M against 62.0 M, 118,764 B against 118,768 B, 89.9 % of both write bytes and transaction size. `register` and `set_kem_key` are within 6 % of B0 on CPU, `store_pqz_pop` 15–23 % above it (the real one reads `Ua(ua)` and `PqzK`), still under 2 % of the limit; write bytes agree to within 4 B. Peak memory, which B0 could not read, is 7.2 MB of 41.9 MB at its highest (`core_metrics`, `mem_byte`). The largest load a `set_pqz_key` can see is 54,124 B of `Ua(ua)`, not the n = 16 record (57,644 B as a ledger entry with attributes): U8S-D1's minimal rule means a 16-slot `pop` needs all 16 slots again, over the entry limit, so that `msig` has no `set_pqz_key` at all, and the largest that has one is 15 light slots at `register` and one heavy member later. A single-key `mldsa65` fits at every set, whole and split: no STOP.
- **ua8-soroban B7, the EVM side of a copy** (measured on anvil at `--hardfork amsterdam`, `script/Deploy.s.sol`; status: proven, ua8-soroban B7; for B8's text). An `mldsa65` record reaches an EVM chain without the ML-DSA precompile only after the two `cacheExpandedKey` transactions (9.6 M and 13.4 M gas), from anyone, on each chain; without them `register` is `UAPoP`. That selector is not in the guard's table, so a node `call` job cannot do it: the copier's own account does (the e2e's client). An `msig` of two ML-DSA-65 signers is refused by EVM's verify budget on such a chain, `UAKeyData(0x0120)` (2 × 5.95 M + the hold over 12 M): `msig-pq` exists only with the precompile, and the forge suite runs it on a mock. So a Soroban `msig` of that shape cannot be copied to an EVM chain without the precompile, and the e2e asserts the refusal. The copy runs `fndsa512` (relayer-checked here, KEM 3 then 1, `set_pqz_key`, `store_pqz_pop`), `mldsa65/n2816-kmax65536` (PQZ key, proof and KEM key at `register`, KEM 3, 1, 2) and `msig-pq-native` (an `evm-eoa` slot beside an `mldsa65` slot, then its `set_pqz_key` and proof); `msig-pq` with its minimal `pop` is in the unit round trip.
