A relayer-checked slot signing an `msig` now has a positive on a host: a fresh `fndsa512` slot beside an `mldsa65` slot, through `check_registration`, stored `Relayer`, and accepted by EVM's own verifiers. Every `Bytes` argument of every Soroban entry is classed as Appendix X classes EVM's. Bundles on `ua-registry` made explicit here: `set_kem_key.kem`, the two `sig`s, and `ua_of_msig(MsigStructure)`, `ua_of_webauthn(WebAuthnKey)` beside the packed `ua_of(kind, key_data)`, which stays for single keys and as EVM `uaOf`. The WebAuthn assertion in `pop` / `UaSig.signature` stays one `Bytes` (TS-D12 open question 3 default, as EVM). One bundle remains outside the registry, listed for the owner and unchanged: the token's `meta` on `pay_meta`, `ua_pay_meta`, `meta_pay_id` (EVM row 14, `PayMeta`, which EVM's Part C has not built).
- **ua8-soroban B8, the plan decisions of `ua8-soroban` in full** (controller calls unless marked, owner may override; the labels are the plan's `superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-ua8-soroban.md`, each given with its content and status; the state is "built, ua8-soroban <task>", no `main` merge yet; the `main` merge commit is added when it lands).
  - **U8S-D1, the `msig` minimal form: where it applies** (rule: owner 2026-10-31; scope: controller call; built, ua8-soroban M2 on EVM, M3 on Soroban). The owner's rule is "with `T` = the slots' total weight and `N` the threshold, require `T >= N` and, for every slot `i`, `T - weight(i) < N`; clientkeys / ua-rs build only minimal sets; regenerate the `msig` vector rows; one registry change with Part B's so the 4-set gas re-pin and the DEX KAT regeneration happen once". It applies to every **stored** `msig` signature, the three portable purposes (`pop` v2, `kem`, `pqz-key`), which are write-once and copied byte for byte: EVM `UARegistry._msig(…, portable = true)` (from `_sigOk`, by `register`, `setKemKey`, `setPqzKey`) and Soroban `check_msig(…, portable = true)`. A transaction authorisation (`requireAuthorized` / `require_authorized`) is not stored and keeps its rule (a slot after the threshold fails). Every slot counts its member's weight, native members included. Failure: `UAPoP` in `register`, `UAUnauthorized` in `setKemKey` / `setPqzKey` (EVM); `Pop` / `Unauthorized` (Soroban); no new error. One pass sums `T` and keeps the smallest slot weight `w_min`; accept iff `T >= N && T - w_min < N`. NEAR and Algorand: no code; a written requirement for each future UA round (U8S-D12).
  - **U8S-D2, a classical-dominant `msig` registers with an empty `pop`, as on EVM** (controller call, owner may override; built, ua8-soroban M3). EVM (CTR-UA-07): "a classical-dominant `msig` has no PoP of its own (its members proved theirs) and registers with an empty `pop`" (`!_pqEligible(d) ⇒ sig.length == 0`). Soroban first required a member-signed `pop` for every `msig`, so a classical `msig` copied from EVM was refused and one registered on Soroban was refused on EVM. `pq_eligible(d)` (members outside 0x0130 to 0x0133 weigh less than the threshold) is as on EVM; not eligible ⇒ `pop` must be empty (else `Pop`), `pop_checked = Chain`, `signable` by member weight. **Change (controller call, owner may override; B8):** "its members proved theirs" is false on Soroban for a member that is itself a relayer-checked UA, whose registration a listed relayer attested and the chain never verified; the `Chain` mark of that `msig` says only that its `pop` (empty) holds nothing unverified, and a client that relies on a member re-verifies it (`checked_of(member)`). Worded in NET-SOR-18 and CTR-UA-07.
  - **U8S-D3, the entry layout** (spec §4, C12; built, ua8-soroban B2, B3; amended by B3's `PqzK` tuple). `Ua(ua) → Registration` with `attrs.pqz_key` and `attrs.kem_pk` empty (`pqz_pop_hash` and `kem_version` kept); `PqzK(ua) → (key, sig, Checked, pqz_pop_hash)` (B3 added the hash, one entry, one write); `PqzP(ua) → Bytes`; `Kem(ua, version) → (pk, sig, Checked)`; `KemMax(ua) → u64`; `KeyR(kh)` (B4 review). `registration_of` returns exactly what EVM `registrationOf` returns for the same history. Every entry extends its TTL on write and read.

The 16,384 B events limit cannot carry a 22,528 B PQZ key or a 16-member `msig` signature. `UaRegistered` keeps its shape (`pop` as `pop_hash`, `attrs` as stored); `UaPqzKeySet { ua, pqz_key_hash, pqz_pop_hash, sig_hash, checked }`, `UaPqzPopStored { ua, pqz_pop_hash }`, `UaKemKeySet { ua, version, kem_pk_hash, sig_hash, checked }` carry hashes. B7c: `UaRegistered` also carries `key_data` unless it is over 15,360 B (owner 2026-11-01). Readers take the bytes from the views; a log-only indexer needs one `record_of` read for the four emptied `frost-bn254` shapes.
  - **U8S-D5, error codes** (built, ua8-soroban B2 to B4). Continue SOR-D16: `PqzHolder = 13, KemHolder = 14, KemVersion = 15, KemKeyLength = 16, PqzPopHash = 17, KemScheme = 18, PqzKeySet = 19`, then `KindUnknown = 20` (B2, `kind_name`) and `KemKeyHash = 21` (B3). `Attrs = 7` stays, unused after B2. The `portable.json` `negatives[].expect` map: `UAPoP → Pop` (or a host error for host-verified parts, plan finding F1), `UAPqzPopHash → PqzPopHash`, `UAKeyData → KeyData`, `UAPqzHolder → PqzHolder`, `UAKemHolder → KemHolder`, `UAKemVersion → KemVersion`, `UAKemKeyLength → KemKeyLength`, `UAKemScheme → KemScheme`, `UAPqzKeySet → PqzKeySet`, `UAKemKeyHash → KemKeyHash`, `UAUnauthorized → Unauthorized` (an unregistered id: `NotRegistered`); a relayer kind's wrong-signature rows are `NotVerifiable` without a relayer (B4).
  - **U8S-D6, PQZ attributes on Soroban** (UA-6 U3 holders; built, ua8-soroban B2, B3). Holders: `mldsa44`, `mldsa65`, `fndsa512`, a PQ-eligible `msig`, else `PqzHolder`. The key's length is one of the four set lengths in `portable.json` `sets` (16,384 / 18,432 / 20,480 / 22,528 B), else `KeyData`. `pqz_pop_hash` ≠ 0 and ≠ `keccak256("")` with a key, 0 without (`PqzPopHash`); a given `pqz_pop` must hash to it. `proven = false` and `pqz_pop_checked = None` always; no `Key` entry for a PQZ key. `set_pqz_key` is write-once (`PqzKeySet`): no verifier, so nothing is replaced. `store_pqz_pop` is open to anyone, hash-checked, a no-op when stored.
  - **U8S-D7, KEM records on Soroban** (CTR-UA-32; built, ua8-soroban B3). Holders as U8S-D6 (`slhdsa128s` not, `KemHolder`); versions ≥ 1, each `(ua, version)` once including the `register` one (`KemVersion`); first byte scheme 1 (`KemScheme`), exactly 1,601 B (`KemKeyLength`); the signature in the `pop` format over `ua_message(kind, PURPOSE_KEM, kem_record_digest)`; no owner check, no revocation; `kem_key_of` follows `KemMax`. B8: a listed relayer can pin `kem_key_of` through a high version, so clients read `kem_key_at` with a version they verified.
  - **U8S-D8, the relayer-checked kind set** (spec S3, §6; UA8-D20; built, ua8-soroban B4; amended four times). `Chain`: the seven enabled kinds. `Relayer(id)`: `bip340`, `schnorr-bn254`, `schnorr-bls12381`, `bls12381-minsig`, `bls-bn254-minsig`, the group kinds 0x0110 to 0x0113, `fndsa512`, `slhdsa128s` and `zether-bls12381` 0x0141 (classical Zether, until its own round); any other kind `KindDisabled`. Key data checked on chain for length and layout only; `signable = false`, never receivable, never a signer. An `msig` slot is `Relayer` when its member is a registered relayer-checked UA (weight 0 for `signable`) or an `evm-contract` member. Amendments, each in its entry: (1) the relayer's auth is `require_auth_for_args` over `attest_digest`, not `require_auth()` over the call (owner decision 2026-11-01, B7b); (2) a relayer-checked record keeps its key in `KeyR`, so it blocks no `Chain` kind (B4 review); (3) a mixed `msig` keeps `signable` by its `Signer` members (B4; spec §6, S9 reworded in B8); (4) twelve `TAG`s of these kinds entered production `digest.rs`, `fndsa512`'s message helper stays test-only (B4).
  - **U8S-D9, the gen-1 kind gate** (owner 2026-10-31, option (a); Soroban half controller call; built, ua8-soroban G1; no code on Soroban). `DeployBase._checkGen1Kinds(reg, bls, isHedera)` runs at the end of `_deployUARegistry`: when the probe passes EIP-2537 the gen-1 registry must enable `schnorr-bls12381`, `bls12381-minsig` and, except on Hedera, `zether-bls12381`, else the deploy reverts; no `UARegistry` change; normative: accounts.md §1.9. Soroban has no generations: "a Soroban registry meant to stay (mainnet) is deployed from a build carrying every kind built for Soroban at that time" (so after `zether-soroban`).
  - **U8S-D10, the relay-fee minimum is research only** (owner ruling 2026-10-28, final review item 7; owner 2026-10-31: "owner decides there; if it changes contracts it lands before the freeze, if it is node config it goes with P6i"; status: no build, R1 research note written, owner decision pending). The flat `params.relay_fee.min_amount` stays until before mainnet, to be re-decided then between a per-token minimum and gas-proportional pricing (`research/relay-fee-minimum.md`).
  - **U8S-D11, order and T14** (controller call, owner may override; plan). Everything but B10 runs before 2026-11-03; T14 runs on its own (work order item 1); after it lands on `main`, `main` is merged into `ua8-soroban`, the Soroban gate steps re-run at the new commit, then B10 (the Stellar testnet run). Status: B10 not run.
  - **U8S-D12, NEAR and Algorand** (owner 2026-10-31 via the controller; status: written requirement, no code). Neither has a UA registry (base family contracts only). The minimal form is in NET-ALL-84 row 10 (the shared answer, every family) and goes into the NEAR UA round and, as a separate line, the Algorand UA round. The post-round freeze covers EVM and Soroban.
  - **UA8-D18, the relayer argument** (built, ua8-soroban B2 to B4, amended by B7b). `register`, `set_kem_key` (and the other registry writes) take `relayer: Option<Address>`, consulted only for a part the chain cannot verify, which then needs `relayer` in the list and its authorisation (now `require_auth_for_args` over `attest_digest`, the lane being the transaction source); parts the chain verifies are verified on chain, `checked = Chain`, open to anyone (P11.2).
  - **UA8-D19, the relayer list** (built, ua8-soroban B4). The constructor's `relayers`, the node's lane addresses at deploy, immutable, no admin. "The operator delists such a relayer" (P11.6) means a new registry and new tokens, the records of the old one staying readable; the mitigation to tell operators is to list a lane whose signing key can be rotated (controller ruling, owner may override; wording in B8).
  - **UA8-D20, who checks what on Soroban** (amended by U8S-D8 and spec §6; built, ua8-soroban B4). `Chain` for the classical kinds the base verifies and for `mldsa44` / `mldsa65` (CAP-0087, empty context); `Relayer(id)` for `fndsa512`, `slhdsa128s` and any kind Soroban does not verify; an `msig` part is `Chain` when every signature of its signing set is chain-verifiable, else `Relayer(id)`; the PQZ proof always `None`. A mixed `msig` with a `Relayer` `pop` keeps `signable` by its `Signer` members (B8 rewording of spec §6 "a `Relayer` record has `signable = false`" and S9 "`pop` checked by the chain").
  - **UA8-D21, PQZ bytes on Soroban** (amended by C12: no hash-only fallback, a key or proof that cannot be stored is a STOP for the owner; built, ua8-soroban B2, B3). Stored in full, the key in `PqzK`, the proof in `PqzP`. B0 (run log `smartcontracts/soroban/runs/2026-10-31-ua8-soroban-b0-spike.txt`) recorded the case: full in one `register` at every set, `store_pqz_pop` for a proof stored later; no STOP. The one limit that exceeds an entry, `set_pqz_key` of a large `msig`, is published as a maximum in bytes (B3, B7b; NET-SOR-27), not a STOP.
  - **UA8-D22, TTL** (S11; built, ua8-soroban B2 to B4). `extend_ttl(30 days, 60 days)` on each write and in-transaction read; an archived entry is restored by its next access; no node TTL job.
  - **UA8-D23, node `call` jobs on Soroban** (amended by the owner's explicit-parameter rule of 2026-10-31; built, ua8-soroban B6, B7b, B9a). Named JSON fields per function, the node builds the XDR; target the configured registry only; function one of the registry's eight writes; `relayer` must be the lane and listed; the node adds one `SourceAccount` entry only when a relayer is named. Fields in `node/job-api.md`.
  - **UA8-D24, the off-chain verifier** (amended by C14: per-kind gating, not a STOP; built, ua8-soroban B5). `scaas-ua` feature `pq` with exact-pinned crates (`ml-dsa =0.1.1`, `slh-dsa =0.2.0-rc.5`, `pqcrypto-falcon =0.4.1`), accepted only if every `pq_kat.json` / `pq_external.json` / `pq_signatures.json` row agrees; the node and the clients re-check with it; `clientkeys` re-checks with its own verifiers. `slh-dsa` is a release candidate: re-pin to a stable release before the mainnet freeze.
- **ua8-soroban B8, published limits are bytes per entry and final** (measured, B7b's `e2e_ua8_relayer_table` and `e2e_ua8_network_fit`; controller call on the form, owner may override; status: published in NET-SOR-27, ua8-soroban B8). The limits are the rule `PqzK = key + 64 + Σ slots`, `Kem(ua, v) = 1,601 + 64 + Σ slots`, `Ua(ua)` with `pop = 64 + Σ slots`, slot `192 + ⌈sig / 32⌉ × 32` B, each within 65,536 B: `register` + PQZ + KEM 7 `slhdsa128s` slots at every set (8 refused), `set_pqz_key` 6 / 5 / 5 / 5 `slhdsa128s` slots at `n2048-kmax1024` / `n2304-kmax4096` / `n2560-kmax16384` / `n2816-kmax65536`, `set_kem_key` 7, `fndsa512` up to 16 members everywhere, `set_pqz_key` 13 / 12 ML-DSA-65 slots for the `Chain` kinds. The registry has no upgrade and the structure is the id, so each limit is final for a deployment: an `msig` that needs more is never registered, or never gets that record, on Soroban, and the refusal stores nothing. The figures hold on the quickstart's `--limits testnet` and are re-read at B10.
- **ua8-soroban B8, spec texts reworded where the build differs** (controller call, owner may override; status: worded, ua8-soroban B8). Each is a marked Change in the text, not a silent edit: (1) UA-Soroban spec §6 "a `Relayer` record has `signable = false`" and S9 "`pop` checked by the chain": a mixed `msig` with a `Relayer` `pop` keeps `signable` by its `Signer` members (B4 ruling; if wrong, refuse in `check_msig`, one branch). (2) UA-8 spec P11.6, "the operator delists such a relayer": on Soroban a new registry and new tokens; a bad relayer can pin `kem_key_of` through a high version, so clients use `kem_key_at`; `KeyR` keeps marked records from blocking a `Chain` kind; `key_owner` can return a marked-only record, so readers check `checked_of` (CTR-UA-34 rule 6). (3) U8S-D2 "its members proved theirs": false for a relayer-checked member (above). (4) The UA-Soroban spec's relayer rule, `relayer.require_auth()`, is `require_auth_for_args((attest_digest,))` (owner 2026-11-01; the plan's U8S-D8 text said `require_auth`, superseded by B7b's entry).
- **ua8-soroban B8, `register` and WebAuthn: the comment and the note** (controller call; status: comment corrected, note left, ua8-soroban B8). EVM `register` takes the packed key data of `webauthn-p256`, MuSig2 and FROST and refuses only `msig` (`UARegistry.register`), as the typed `registerWebAuthn` / `registerMuSig2` / `registerFrost` do for the same bytes; so the comment in `scaas-node/src/abi.rs` ("`register` refuses those kinds") is corrected. `portable.json`'s `note` says "register(0x0100, ...) is refused": it is generator text (`clients/clientkeys/scripts/ua-portable-vectors.mjs`), the file is never edited by hand and was not regenerated here; the generator's sentence needs the same correction at its next change.
- **ua8-soroban B8, questions left open for the owner** (stated as open, not decided). (1) An `msig` whose `pop` has a `G…` member's slot beside a relayer-checked slot is refused off chain (`UAKeyData`, B5) and through `call` jobs (B6); widening it needs a new `validate_key_data` mode and a partial-attestation rule. (2) `call` jobs are free to the client (P9) and `max_deposit_per_job` caps only restores, so the lane's cost is limited by the spend breaker alone; whether they should stay free is the owner's. (3) The relay-fee minimum (U8S-D10). Not decided by this round.
- **ua8-soroban B8, the row "5 `slhdsa128s` slots + PQZ + KEM without the proof"** (what was measured; status: recorded, ua8-soroban B8). The row belonged to the first `network_fit` data block, deleted with it in B7b's review round (B7c restored `e2e_ua8_tx_size_limit` and kept the other rows out, `e2e_ua8_relayer_table` covering them except this one). It was measured once, in B7, before the attestation change: 130,912 B of transaction at `n2816-kmax65536`, 6 slots refused. After the change it is not measured as a row; the asserted edge is 7 slots, so 5 sits under it. No other figure is claimed.
- **ua8-soroban N2, every Soroban `ua_metatx` function takes named fields, and the node builds the XDR** (owner's explicit-parameter rule of 2026-10-31 over SOR-D14's hex `op.args`; TS-D21; form: controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban N2). `op = {contract, function, args, auth?, valid_until?}`, `args` every argument by the contract's name, `auth` included, any other field refused at every level. One table, `UA_FNS`, gives each function its arguments in order and their types; B6's parser reads them, so a `call` job and a `ua_metatx` job refuse alike. The digest, the XDR, `valid_until` and every policy check read one built `InvokeContractArgs`, and `ua_metatx_digest_matches_ua_ops_vectors` builds each of the 84 job rows of `ua-ops.json` from the row's names and types and compares args and digest. Forms: `i128`, `u128`, `u256`, `i256` decimal strings, as every amount the node reports; `u64`, `i64`, `Timepoint`, `Duration` a number or a decimal string, because a JavaScript client cannot write a `salt` past 2^53 as a number; `Holder` `{"Addr": …}` or `{"Ua": …}`, the contract's variants, as the CLI writes them. A relayed call's `args` have no declared types, so each is `{type, value}`, with `Vec<Val>`, `Void` and `Map` (a list of `{key, val}`, any key type, sorted by the node), so a relayed call and a signed invocation reach what a contract can take; a decimal form is digits only, so a `0x…` is no `u256`. `Error` and the host's ledger-key values have no form (N2 review item 3; the first form closed the list to the types the repo's contracts took, which the owner's rule against dropping an API for lack of callers refuses). Cost if wrong: one decoder.
- **ua8-soroban N2, `HEX_ARGS_REFUSED` on every Soroban job kind** (owner's rule; name: controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban N2). `op.args` as a string, `op.extra.call` at all, or a string where a job has named fields, is refused by that name; the job goes `dead` on its one claim and nothing is sent.
- **ua8-soroban N2, `extra.call` is gone from `signed_op`, and the native relay fee is built from the signed root** (owner's rule, TS-D21 said "the named target call object"; form: controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban N2; run on a real host, `e2e_soroban_native_relay_fee`). The payer's signed root already holds the eight arguments of `relay`, so the node builds `relay(payer, …, relayer)` from it, `payer` the signer and `relayer` this lane: no field to name, and no second copy of the call to differ from the signed one. The checks that compared the two copies (payer argument, relayer argument, root against call) have nothing left to compare. A multi-party DEX `settle` is a `ua_metatx` job with its native legs in `op.auth` (`e2e_soroban_dex_both_native`); `extra.auth` stays for co-signers of the signed call. Cost if wrong: a `signed_op` that needs a call other than the signed root has no form.
- **ua8-soroban N2 review, `signed_op`'s `payload` is named JSON** (owner ruling 2026-11-02; form: controller call, owner may override; status: built and run on a local Protocol 30 host, ua8-soroban N2 review). `payload` bundled a nonce, an expiry and an invocation tree, so it falls under the explicit-parameter rule: `{nonce, expiry, invocation}`, `invocation` `{contract, function, args: [{type, value}], sub_invocations}`, in `signed_op`, `op.auth[]` and `extra.auth[]` alike, one function (`auth_entry`), and either list as a string is `HEX_ARGS_REFUSED` too (`auth_entries`; the first form dropped an `extra.auth` string without a word). The node rebuilds the entry on its own network id and the host checks the signature over what it rebuilt; `named_payload_rebuilds_the_signed_bytes` gives the cross vector's `HashIdPreimage` from the names. Hex `payload` is `HEX_ARGS_REFUSED`; `clientkeys` builds the same fields (`authPreimage`, `authDigest`, `signedAuth`). What stays hex is one crypto object: an account's signature bytes, and a `C…` subject's `signature`, the `ScVal` XDR its own `__check_auth` reads. The node's old check of a payload's network id has no field left to read: a signature for another network fails at the host, at simulation (`e2e_soroban_native_relay_fee` shows a signature over other bytes dead with nothing sent). A non-UTF-8 symbol or string has no JSON form, and a `CreateContract…` authorization has no form: nothing the node relays signs one. Cost if wrong: a client sends fields instead of bytes.
- **ua8-soroban N2 review, a `signed_op` is no open host call** (owner ruling 2026-11-02, refined the same day, next entry; name and `params.mandates`: controller call, owner may override; status: built, ua8-soroban N2 review). It runs only on a token, a mandate, the DEX or the router the chain's `params` name; the chain had no list of mandates, so `params.mandates` (`C…`) is new, and a `ua_metatx` job still serves any mandate. It never runs on the registry, even one listed as something else, so a registry write has one door, the `call` job, with its checks. Anything else is `CALL_TARGET_REFUSED`, `dead` on its one claim, nothing sent. A `G…` `msig` member whose signature the registry needs must submit that write itself: the `signed_op` route for it is closed on purpose, and a `call` job carries no other signer. That B7 note (a `signed_op` reaching the registry) is closed by this rule, not by the removal of `extra.call`, which left a subject-signed root at the registry open. A relayed call (`relay`, `ua_relay`) still names any target: the executor runs it as itself, with no authority of the lane's. A plain `signed_op` counted in the `call` share and stopped at `call_budget_pct`, being as free to the client as a `call` job; as first built that included a native plain `pay`, which the next entry takes out. Amended by [NET-SOR-29](networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-29): a `ua_metatx` serves a mandate of a listed Wasm.
- **ua8-soroban N2 review 2, a plain `signed_op` that pays a token runs to the whole budget** (owner ruling 2026-11-02, refining the entry above; hook and name of the error: controller call, owner may override; status: built and tested, ua8-soroban N2 review 2). A plain `signed_op` whose root is a token payment, `invocation.function` in {`pay`, `pay_meta`, `transfer`} on a contract of `policy.tokens`, is outside the `call` share; every other plain `signed_op` stays in it. `ChainAdapter::in_call_share` is the hook, by kind by default; Soroban's reads the job with `token_payment`, which parses the whole named `op` with the function that builds it (`host_call`), so a job that does not parse, or carries `salt` / `meta` with no `op.kind`, stays in the share (fail closed). The client cannot mislabel one: the host call is exactly the root. `job_tx` re-checks at build (`runs_as_read`): a job read as a token payment that builds any other call is `CALL_TARGET_REFUSED`, nothing sent. The two read one value, so nothing reaches that refusal today; it holds the rule if a later change lets them part, and an injected difference shows it fires. A `pay` on an unlisted contract, the mandate or the DEX, and a `call` job, stay in the share. Cost if wrong: free native payments can spend the whole hour's budget, up to the breaker.
- **ua8-soroban N2 review 2, one rule for a job's bytes** (review finding; controller call, owner may override; status: built and tested, ua8-soroban N2 review 2). `credential_signature` and `op_bytes` (`ref`, `salt`, `meta`, `pay_ref`) took hex with or without `0x`; every other leaf takes `0x…` (`hex_of`). Now all do, and `unhex` left the adapter. A consumer sends `signature` as `0x…` (`clientkeys` `signedAuth` does); a bare one is refused, `dead`, nothing sent. Cost if wrong: one prefix.
- **ua8-soroban N2 review, XDR a job puts in is bounded by depth** (pre-existing, review finding; status: built, ua8-soroban N2 review). `Limits::len` leaves the depth at `u32::MAX`, about 2,700 levels in 64 KiB of hex, and a stack overflow aborts the whole node, every chain with it. `XDR_DEPTH` is 64, as `recorded_auth` already had: a `C…` subject's `signature` decodes under it (8,192 B), and `job_tx` reads every built call and entry back under it, so the named path has the same bound (`serde_json` stops a job's JSON at 128 levels before any of this). `sign` and `submit` decode the node's own bytes at twice that, the transaction's levels around what `job_tx` bounded. XDR the RPC answers (events, ledger entries, transaction data) is not job input and keeps its limits: a contract may store deeper values than 64 levels. Cost if wrong: a real value nested past 15 `Vec`s is refused (`deep_xdr_is_refused_not_a_stack_overflow` pins 15 and 16).
- **ua8-soroban N2 review, a `ua_metatx` job's deadline after a restart is the built call's** (review finding; status: built, ua8-soroban N2 review). `recover_lane` read `op.valid_until`, which a `ua_metatx` need not carry, so it got 0 and the first `Unknown` reported `dead` while the transaction might still land. `job_valid_until` reads the deadline from the built call, the rule NET-SOR-15 states; `follow` saturates the grace on it, so a job signing `u64::MAX` is no overflow to `dead` (or a panic in a debug build).

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`; T0 hard-gate ruling in the ledger
Change (2026-11-08, plan T66a, [CTR-UA-32](contracts/accounts.md#CTR-UA-32)): **an `msig` holds no KEM key**, so the published limits lose their KEM rows: `register` + PQZ (no KEM key) keeps 7 `slhdsa128s` slots at every set (8 refused); `set_kem_key` of an `msig` is refused `KemHolder` (the "`set_kem_key` 7" limit goes). Measured on the local Protocol 30 host (`smartcontracts/soroban/runs/2026-11-08-ua-mtx-merge-t66a-fix-e2e-ua8.txt`): `register_msig` 7 `slhdsa128s` + PQZ 74,916 / 76,964 / 79,012 / 81,060 B of transaction at the four sets (with the proof 103,216 / 107,456 / 111,660 / 116,648), 16 `fndsa512` + PQZ 33,276 … 39,420 B (with the proof 61,576 … 75,008); the largest `msig`, 16 ML-DSA-65 members at `n2816-kmax65536` with a PQZ key, 64.05 M instructions, 117,260 B written. Status: BUILT (T66a, Soroban `65afdcff`); NET-SOR-27 carries the table.

### NET-SOR-18 — Soroban kinds and msig members: seven kinds, host-checked Soroban natives, canonical WebAuthn
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-18 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Seven kinds are enabled (`webauthn-p256`, `p256`, `ed25519`, `secp256k1`, `msig`, `mldsa44`, `mldsa65`); `msig` members are those kinds plus `stellar-account` 0x0011 (`soroban-contract` 0x0012 is `MemberUnknown`: owner ruling 2026-10-31, after the final review), a registered member signs with an empty `keyData` and the registry reads only that member's `(kind, key_data)` from `Signer(ua)`; the WebAuthn signature blob is accepted in its canonical encoding only.
**Why.** Classical first (owner 2026-10-29), then PQ where a host function exists; Soroban natives make the host the verifier, so no second verifier is written. Empty member key data keeps the `MemberSig[]` small enough for the events and entry limits (T0). A lenient WebAuthn decode would let a front-runner register the same id with different `pop` bytes, against the CTR-UA-07 identical-record rule.
**Cost if wrong.** A UA of a disabled kind cannot use Soroban until a later generation; an EVM `msig` that needs its EOA members for its threshold is discovery-only here; a Soroban-native member makes a network-local record; a `C…` contract account cannot be an `msig` member (owner ruling 2026-10-31).

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S3 — Kinds of generation 1 on Soroban** (who: controller call within the owner's list; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T2, T2b, T3). Options: classical first (owner 2026-10-29), then PQ where a host function exists; pure-Rust BIP-340 / FROST / MuSig2, the BLS12-381 kinds (CAP-59 host functions exist), `fndsa512` / `slhdsa128s` pure. Choice and why: **enabled:** `webauthn-p256` 0x0100, `p256` 0x0101, `ed25519` 0x0102, `secp256k1` 0x0108, `msig` 0x0120, `mldsa44` 0x0130, `mldsa65` 0x0131 (§3). Every other derived kind is disabled (`KindDisabled`), stays valid elsewhere (UA-8 P3), and reaches Soroban only through Part B's relayer-checked mode, never as a signer. A later generation may add BLS12-381 or pure-Rust kinds after a budget spike (CTR-UA-05: a new generation). Cost if wrong: a UA of a disabled kind cannot use Soroban until that generation.
- **S10 — `msig` members on Soroban** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T3; owner confirmed 2026-10-30). Options: the EVM MEMBER set; plus Soroban natives; plus EVM natives. Choice and why: **MEMBER = the enabled single-key kinds of S3, plus `stellar-account` 0x0011** (verified by the host: `member.require_auth_for_args((ua, purpose, digest))`, Soroban's form of the EIP-712 `UAAuth`). Change note, owner ruling 2026-10-31, after the final review: 0x0012 dropped from MEMBER (invoker auth); status: built 2026-10-31, branch `ua-soroban` final fix wave. As built at T3 MEMBER also held `soroban-contract` 0x0012, and the final review (A-I1) showed it unsafe: Soroban counts a contract's authority as given for any `require_auth` in a contract it calls directly, and the token, the mandate and the DEX call `registry.require_authorized` directly, so a `C…` member that is one of them met its own empty slot for free. The repro: a 1-of-2 `msig` of an ed25519 UA and the token's `C…`, registered by the ed25519 member's `pop` alone, was drained by anyone through `ua_transfer` with no auth entries; the same held for a mandate owner or delegate `msig` listing the mandate (anyone acts as owner, including `mtx_withdraw`) and for the DEX (anyone runs `ua_cancel`). Of the three fixes offered ((a) a documented rule plus a `clientkeys` refusal of SCaaS contracts as members, (b) drop 0x0012 from MEMBER, (c) check `C…` members through a one-hop helper contract) the owner chose (b): a `G…` account is never an invoker, so 0x0011 stays; `register` refuses an `msig` with a 0x0012 member as `MemberUnknown` (the layout still parses it, so it is not `KeyData`), `clientkeys` `soroban.encodeMsig` refuses one when building, and a `C…` stays a native subject and holder (§8) but is no member; SmartKeyAccount members are lost (a later generation may add (c)). Tests: `msig_member_equal_to_token_refused` (the reviewer's repro, now refused at `register`), `msig_soroban_contract_member_refused`. An `msig` with a 0x0011 member is a **Soroban-network-local record** (no other registry verifies those members, as EVM's 0x0003 is Hedera-only). **`evm-eoa` 0x0001 members** are verified for the portable purposes only (`pop` v2, `kem`: ECDSA over the EIP-191 `personal_sign` of `memberDigest`, by `secp256k1_recover`, exactly CTR-UA-07; change note, owner decision 4 of 2026-10-31: ECDSA over the record's typed digest instead, no `personal_sign`, `register`'s `pop` built in typed-signing P5, `kem` with `ua8-soroban`), and have **zero signing weight** for every other purpose (no Soroban signing form); `evm-contract` 0x0002 members are never chain-verified here (Part B: the part is `Relayer`). Cost if wrong: an EVM `msig` that needs its EOA members to reach its threshold is discovery-only on Soroban (S9).

**Rulings and changes (decided during the build):**
- **Owner B, 2026-10-30 (T0 hard gate)**: a registered member's `MemberSig` carries an empty `keyData` (CTR-UA-33 B); a non-empty one is refused (`Pop`). Status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T0 fix pass 2, T3; the Soroban member check reads only `Signer(ua)` (384 B against the 16,768 B record, same CPU and memory).
- **WebAuthn canonical** (owner 2026-10-30, every registry; branch `ua-soroban` T2b): `webauthn::check` re-encodes the decoded blob and refuses unless byte-equal (`Pop`); the shared WebAuthn negatives (21 rows) are all refused. EVM has the same rule (CTR-UA-33 C, branch `webauthn-clients`).
- ML-DSA is exercised only under `metatx` / `member` (no `trade` / `cancel` vectors, no Rust ML-DSA signer): the purpose enters only `ua_msg`, so the verifier path is the same (T3 review, accepted); `IdInNativeSpace` is unreachable through `register` for a derived kind, the check function is tested against `kinds.json`; an `evm-eoa` slot in `require_authorized` is `NotVerifiable` (zero weight, fails closed as on EVM); a malformed `MemberSig[]` is `Pop` (spec §3).

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`

### NET-SOR-19 — Soroban receivability: only a UA that can spend here
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-19 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** `receivable(ua)` is true only for a registered, enabled-kind UA with a chain-checked `pop` and, for `msig`, Soroban-signable weight at least the threshold (`Registration.signable`, fixed at `register`); false for an unregistered id; a part the chain cannot verify is `NotVerifiable` whatever `relayer` says.
**Why.** CTR-UA-23: a registrable but unusable account can receive and never spend; UA-8 P11.5. The token tells `UaNotRegistered` from `UaNotReceivable` on the failure path only, so the hot path reads one flag.
**Cost if wrong.** A few `msig` forms register for discovery only; Part B's relayer-checked mode adds the `Relayer` parts without a caller change (C13).

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S9 — Which UAs may receive** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T3, T5). Options: any registered UA / only a UA that can spend on Soroban. Choice and why: **only a UA that can spend here**: registered, kind enabled, `pop` checked by the chain, and for `msig` the weight of members Soroban can verify for signing ≥ threshold (`Registration.signable`, computed at `register`). Else `UaNotReceivable`. CTR-UA-23: a registrable but unusable account can receive and never spend; UA-8 P11.5. Cost if wrong: a few `msig` forms register for discovery only.

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D6 — UA-Soroban and unverifiable parts** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T3). In UA-Soroban a signature part the chain cannot verify (an `evm-contract` member's slot, any `MemberSig` of a kind outside MEMBER) is `NotVerifiable`, whatever `relayer` says; `relayer` is accepted and ignored for chain-verified parts (UA8-D18). Part B's B4 adds the relayer-checked mode on top, with no caller change (C13).

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`

### NET-SOR-20 — Soroban UA ledger in the token: ua_* entries, persistent lanes, the token as pool
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-20 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Tokens keep `UaBalance(ua)` and `ua_*` entries beside the native ones; replay is `UaNonce(ua, lane)` in persistent storage; a relayer-bound entry takes `relayer: Option<Address>`; the UA pool is the token's own address; `ua_trade` is bounded by a running `UaPulled(digest)` and a contract-only `dex`; a cancel digest runs once.
**Why.** A per-UA custom account would be a contract per user per chain and give a derived UA a native address (against CTR-UA-02, NET-ALL-21); a `Holder` in the built entries would change `pay` / `pay_meta` and their cross vectors. Temporary nonces are deleted on expiry and would reopen spent ones (NET-ALL-01, CTR-MTX-04).
**Cost if wrong.** More entry points in the token; one extra persistent entry per order (`UaPulled`) and per cancel digest (`UaCancelUsed`) in rent.

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S6 — The UA ledger in Soroban tokens** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T5; owner confirmed 2026-10-30). Options: (a) a per-UA custom account (`C…` contract at a salt = the UA, whose `__check_auth` asks the registry): every existing entry works unchanged; (b) a `Holder` enum in the existing entries (NEAR shape); (c) a `UaBalance(ua)` ledger with separate `ua_*` entries beside the native ones (EVM CTR-UA-18 / -26 shape). Choice and why: **(c).** (a) is a contract per user per chain and gives a derived UA a native address, against CTR-UA-02 and NET-ALL-21; (b) changes the built `pay` / `pay_meta` and their cross vectors. The UA pool is the token's own address (§5.1). Cost if wrong: more entry points in the token.
- **S7 — UA replay protection** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T5). Options: (a) host-style random nonces in temporary storage; (b) lanes `UaNonce(ua, lane) → u64` in persistent storage, EVM `_uaNonce[ua][batch]`. Choice and why: **(b)**; `ua_pay` uses `lane = payLane(pay_ref)`, `nonce = 0` (CTR-MTX-26). Temporary entries are deleted on expiry, so (a) would re-open spent nonces (NET-ALL-01, CTR-MTX-04). Cost if wrong: none found.
- **S8 — Relayer binding of UA entries** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T5, T8; amended by the executor ruling (NET-SOR-21)). Options: unbound (native Soroban today, NET-SOR-01) / `relayer: Option<Address>`. Choice and why: **`relayer: Option<Address>`**; `Some(r)` ⇒ `r.require_auth()`: a lane satisfies it by an explicit `SourceAccount` auth entry rooted at the call (as `relay-fee` today), the relay-fee router as the direct invoker of its own fee call (it never calls a target as itself: §5.4 Executor, controller ruling 2026-10-31). Needed for CTR-MTX-27's router marker. Cost if wrong: none found.

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D7 — `ua_ref_used`** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T4, T5). Derived, no own entry: `ua_ref_used(ua, pay_ref) = ua_nonce(ua, pay_lane(pay_ref)) > 0` (`ua_pay` is nonce 0 of its pay lane, S7).
- **SOR-D8 — Constructors** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T5 to T8; router amended by the executor ruling). Token `__constructor(admin, decimals, name, symbol, registry: Option<Address>)`; mandate `__constructor(owner: Holder, registry: Option<Address>)`; DEX `__constructor(admin, fee_recipient, registry: Option<Address>)` (its `ua_cancel` verifies a UA); the router stores the executor id (`__constructor(executor)`; change note, controller ruling 2026-10-31 after the T8 review: it was stateless before, but the target now runs through `contracts/relay-executor`, which stores the router id, so a router cannot call a target as itself; spec §5.4); its `ua_relay` reaches the registry through `token.ua_pay`.

**Rulings and changes (decided during the build):**
- **T5 review I1, ruling (controller, owner may override; branch `ua-soroban` T5 fix pass 1):** `ua_trade` without a bound let a `dex` that is a `G…` account drain a UA. Fix: contract-only `dex` (`executable() == Some(Wasm)` before `require_auth`), `amount ≤ sell_amount`, and the persistent running total `UaPulled(order digest) + amount ≤ sell_amount` (EVM `pulled[h]` parity, one rule on every family); `BadOrder = 13` for a maker that is not a UA, a foreign `sell_token`, a non-contract `dex` or an over-pull. Cost: one entry per order.
- **Additions not in the first spec (controller, owner may override; T5):** `UaCancelUsed(digest)` makes a replayed `ua_cancel_nonce` a `BadNonce` (EVM `cancelUsed`), checked before the signature; `pay_to_ua` emits the native `MetaTransactionExecuted { from, digest }` as `pay` does.
- **T5 minor m2, not added (controller):** no pool check on `pay_to_ua`'s `from`; native `pay` has none, so the UA path mirrors it. Cost if wrong: a pool-held balance could be paid to a UA, as to a native address today.
- Open test gaps (T5 re-review, deferred to the final review): no test with an existing account or a SAC as `dex`; none pins the cancel check order.

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`

### NET-SOR-21 — Soroban mandate, DEX and relay-fee router for UA holders; executor; mandate epoch
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-21 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The mandate, the DEX and the router accept `Holder` owners, delegates, makers, destinations and payers; the mandate keeps an epoch per token (CTR-ACC-07); every DEX leg is pull-then-pay; the relay-fee router runs a target only through `contracts/relay-executor` and is therefore not stateless.
**Why.** One entry per operation for a native and a UA holder keeps the names of NET-SOR-16. The epoch makes an unused delegate signature die with the owner's revoke and re-set (one rule on every family, owner 2026-10-30). Soroban treats a contract's authority as given for a direct call, so a router that called a target itself let a relayer submit a victim's router-bound `ua_pay` as the target; the executor (EVM `RelayFeeRouter` parity) closes it.
**Cost if wrong.** One more contract and one more deploy step (the executor); a middle hop and an extra token call per DEX leg; a first deployment with the new `Order` type.

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D9 — Mandate names** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T6, T6b). The mandate takes the NET-SOR-16 names in this deployment (spec §5.2): `mtx_set_mandate`, `mtx_set_payee`, `mtx_revoke`, `mtx_withdraw`, `mtx_mandate_pay` — one entry each for a native and a UA holder. Owner entries end in `(lane, nonce, valid_until, relayer, auth)`; a native holder authorises by host auth (`auth` must be empty, `BadAuth`), its lane is not consumed; expiry and `relayer` are checked for both. The token's `pay` and the DEX's `settle` / `cancel` keep their names (their NET-SOR-16 renames stay SPECIFIED, outside UA-Soroban). Change note (owner ruling 2026-10-30, T6b): the mandate epoch of CTR-ACC-07 — `epoch(token)` +1 on every `mtx_set_mandate` and every revoke; the delegate's `mtx_revoke(token, by, epoch, …)` and `mtx_mandate_pay(token, payee, amount, pay_ref, epoch, …)` sign it and are refused `StaleEpoch` unless current; the owner's `epoch` argument is not checked.
- **SOR-D10 — DEX `ua_cancel` purpose** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T7). Purpose `trade` over `op_digest(dex, "ua_cancel", (order,))`, verified by the DEX through the registry (the spec names the entry, not its purpose; the function name in the digest separates it from the order signature).
- **SOR-D11 — `RelayFeePaid`** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T8, T9). `payer` **and** `payee` become `Holder` (a bound payee of `ua_relay` may be a UA; one event shape for `relay` and `ua_relay`).

**Rulings and changes (decided during the build):**
- **Plan-F2** (controller, owner may override): only the mandate takes the `mtx_*` names in this deployment; the token's `pay` and the DEX's `settle` / `cancel` keep theirs (their NET-SOR-16 renames stay SPECIFIED). **Plan-F3**: DEX `ua_cancel` signs purpose `trade` over `digest("ua_cancel", (order,))` (SOR-D10). **Plan-F4**: `RelayFeePaid` payer and payee are both `Holder` (SOR-D11). Branch `ua-soroban` T6 to T8.
- **Mandate epoch (owner ruling 2026-10-30, branch `ua-soroban` T6b):** CTR-ACC-07 now covers Soroban (mandates.md no longer says "EVM only"): `epoch(token) -> u64`, +1 on every `mtx_set_mandate` and every revoke; the delegate's `mtx_revoke(token, by, epoch, …)` and `mtx_mandate_pay(token, payee, amount, pay_ref, epoch, …)` sign it (the UA `op_digest`, a native delegate's `require_auth_for_args`) and are `StaleEpoch = 13` unless current; **the owner may pass any epoch to `mtx_revoke`**, unchecked (EVM parity: the owner's revoke has no epoch; the lane nonce stops replay). Cost if wrong: none found. NEAR, Algorand, Cosmos and Solana get the epoch in their own family rounds (TODO).
- **Mandate error codes beyond the first plan (T6 review m4, controller):** `Expired = 10`, `BadNonce = 11`, `UaLedgerOff = 12`, `StaleEpoch = 13`; `pay_ref` is checked before the signature; no `UaMetaTransactionExecuted` from the mandate; `mtx_set_payee` does not check receivable (EVM parity); the mandate's instance TTL is extended on every path and it has a `registry()` view (T6 m1, m2, branch T7).
- **DEX built behaviour (T7 review, controller):** every leg is pull-then-pay, native legs too (spec §5.3, EVM `settleOne`); a destination equal to the DEX is `BadDestination = 11` before any pull (fix I1); errors `BadAuth = 9`, `UaLedgerOff = 10`; the fee is rounded down (floor; EVM rounds up); no `SelfTrade` check (the DEX does not refuse `maker == taker`); the `Cancelled` event topic is a `Holder`; a relayer that is also a native maker needs two auth entries (its `SourceAccount` entry for `order.relayer` and its order entry); a DEX built without a registry settles native legs but cannot `ua_cancel` (`UaLedgerOff`); the DEX instance TTL is extended in `settle`, `cancel`, `ua_cancel`. The node refuses any `settle` whose destinations are the router or the executor. The signature in soroban.md was `settle(maker, taker, maker_fill)` and is now `settle(maker, taker, maker_fill, maker_auth, taker_auth)`; the mandate entry was `pay_under_mandate(token, payee, amount, pay_ref, valid_until)` (`delegate.require_auth()` then `token.pay`) and is `mtx_mandate_pay` with the epoch, the relayer and `auth`.
- **Relay-fee executor (controller ruling 2026-10-31 after the T8 review, owner may override; branch `ua-soroban` T8 fix pass 1, T9):** the T8 review found a critical flaw (repro passed in a scratch copy): the router invoked the target as the router, so a victim's signed `ua_pay` with `relayer = router` was usable as the target of an attacker's `relay` / `ua_relay` (victim fee paid, ref burned, no call; open-mode fee stuck on the router then drained by `token.transfer(router, attacker)`), breaking CTR-MTX-13 and CTR-MTX-27 for the native `relay` too. Fix: `executor.exec(target, func, args)` on `contracts/relay-executor`, callable only by the router (`router.require_auth()`), the router calls the token only for its own fee and the open-mode forward; constructors name each other (`RelayExecutor(router)`, `RelayFee(executor)`), the router's constructor checks `executor.router() == self` (`BadExecutor = 3`), a router or executor payee is `BadPayee` (unreachable when the router or executor is itself the relayer: `require_auth` fails first), `deploy.sh soroban <net> relay_fee` derives the router id by salt, then deploys executor and router. Cost if wrong: one more contract and deploy step. Docs changed: spec §5.4 and S8, plan SOR-D8 ("stateless" removed), the metatx-split spec's Soroban row, soroban.md. The separate branch `soroban-router-fix` ports the executor to main with its own docs; at the merge the ua-soroban side of these texts is kept.

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`; T8 review

### NET-SOR-22 — Soroban storage, TTL, who pays, warm at deploy
- old: — · status: current · owner: no · date: 2026-10-31 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-22 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** Every UA record, balance, lane, pay ref and cancel digest is a persistent entry (one per key; `Signer(ua)` is the fifth entry of a record); instance storage holds only constructor constants; TTL `extend_ttl(30 days, 60 days)` on each write and in-transaction read; no node TTL job; the lane pays fees, rent and restores; `deploy.sh` warms every deployed contract to 60 days.
**Why.** Temporary entries are deleted for good (NET-ALL-01); an archived persistent entry is restored by the next transaction that lists it (Protocol 23), never read as absent; users and UAs hold no XLM (owner precedent 2026-10-28 for NEAR and Algorand). A first call to a fresh contract paid the 60-day rent (`set_market` 83.8 M stroops, `mtx_set_mandate` 88.0 M, a first relayed `ua_relay` 51.5 M against 0.7 M warm), which would charge the lane.
**Cost if wrong.** Rent for large entries; relayer cost on registration spam (CTR-UA-25: node sponsorship limits); the deployer pays about tens of M stroops per contract once for the warm step.

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S11 — Storage class and TTL** (who: controller call (UA8-D22); status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T3, T5, T7, T10). Options: instance / persistent / temporary. Choice and why: **persistent, one entry per key**, for every record, balance, lane, pay ref and (Part B) KEM / PQZ entry; instance storage only for constructor constants; temporary only for SEP-41 allowances (a UA never holds one). TTL `extend_ttl(30 days, 60 days)` on each write and each in-transaction read (UA8-D22); **no node TTL job**; an archived entry is restored on its next use (§7). Cost if wrong: rent for large entries (§7).
- **S12 — Who pays fees, rent and restores** (who: owner precedent 2026-10-28 (NEAR / Algorand: "the relayer pays storage"), applied here; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T9, T10). Options: the user / the relayer. Choice and why: **the relayer** (lane); users and UAs hold no XLM. Reimbursement: the relay-fee router (`ua_relay`, §5.4) or the node's sponsorship policy; registry writes have no fee form (UA-8 P9). Cost if wrong: relayer cost on spam (CTR-UA-25: node sponsorship limits).

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D19 — `Signer(ua)` entry (T3 review)** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T3). A fifth persistent entry per record, `Signer(ua) → (kind, key_data)`, written once at `register`; the member checks of an `msig` read it and never the record with its `pop`. It duplicates the key data (rent) and is the only layout that keeps `pop` in `Ua(ua)` with key-only member reads (384 B read against 16,768 B, identical CPU 3,279,036 and memory 87,048).
- **SOR-D20 — Warm at deploy (T10 ruling)** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T10). `deploy.sh` extends the instance and the code of every deployed contract (token, mandate, DEX, registry, executor, router) to 60 days (1,036,800 ledgers), paid by the deployer, so no relayed job pays a first-call rent (a first relayed `ua_relay` 51.5 M stroops cold, 0.44 M warm).

**Rulings and changes (decided during the build):**
- **Signer(ua) (T3 review, accepted by the controller):** a fifth persistent entry per record, spec §4 and SOR-D19; the duplicated key data costs rent and is write-once.
- **Warm at deploy (controller ruling 2026-10-31 after the T10 review, owner may override; branch `ua-soroban` T10 fix pass 1):** `deploy.sh` extends instance and code of token, mandate, DEX, registry, executor and router to 1,036,800 ledgers (60 days); the step fails non-zero on error. Measured after warming (local run, stroops): first `ua_relay` 51,527,609 -> 437,890; `set_market` 83.8 M -> 181 k; `mtx_set_mandate` 88.0 M -> 502 k; all relayed jobs at most about 1.1 M.
- A per-job resource-fee cap for Soroban jobs (operator policy, so a relayed first call cannot charge a lane without bound) is a TODO item on main, not repeated here.

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`; T10 run log `smartcontracts/soroban/runs/2026-10-31-ua-soroban-e2e-local.txt`

### NET-SOR-23 — Soroban node: ua_metatx jobs, lane authority never lent, executor refusal
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-23 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The node relays UA operations as `ua_metatx` jobs (registry writes will be `call` jobs, Part B), attaches only the subject's signed entries and one `SourceAccount` entry for a bound lane, fails any other recorded `SourceAccount` entry, refuses a router or executor as a payee or destination, accepts auto-restore within `params.max_deposit_per_job`, and reports `Holder` fields as plain strings.
**Why.** An account signs with its own key and a lane's authority is never lent (owner rulings D1 to D5, 2026-10-30; NET-ALL-83). A recording-mode simulation returns every auth entry the call asked for, including `SourceAccount` ones, so the adapter must filter. The `ua_metatx` name is the EVM job kind.
**Cost if wrong.** A payment to the executor is stranded or executor-drainable; a lent lane authority spends the lane's funds.
Change (2026-11-02, branch `ua8-soroban` B9a review, after N2): `args` is every argument by the contract's name, no longer a hex XDR `ScVec`; SOR-D14's form below is replaced (N2, `job-api.md`).

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S14 — Code authority** (who: owner; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T9). Options: —. Choice and why: **an account signs with its own key; no delegated code authority** (owner rulings D1–D5, 2026-10-30; NET-ALL-83 lists Soroban as having no analogue). Applied in §8: `G…` accounts only add key / hash / pre-auth-tx signers; a `C…` account is a contract account (the EVM 0x0002 analogue), its own authority, never a key account's delegate; a UA is a key, never code; the node never lends a lane's authority. Cost if wrong: —.
- **S15 — Node job kinds** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T9). Options: new names / the EVM names. Choice and why: **`ua_metatx`** for the UA-ledger, mandate and DEX UA entries (the EVM job kind, `scaas-node/src/submit.rs`), **`call`** for the registry writes (UA8-D23). Cost if wrong: —.

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D14 — Soroban `ua_metatx` job** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T9). `{kind: "ua_metatx", op: {contract, function, args: "<hex XDR ScVec>", auth?: [{payload, from, signature}], valid_until?}}` (`args` replaced by named fields, ua8-soroban N2, below in NET-SOR-17's rulings; `op.valid_until` is optional and never read: the node takes the expiry from the signed arguments, NET-SOR-15; final review B-m5, 2026-10-31); allow-list by function and contract class (below, T9); chain param `params.max_deposit_per_job` (stroops; absent = 0 = no restore accepted).
- **SOR-D21 — Node rows and `StaleEpoch` (T9 rulings)** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T9). `Holder` event fields are plain strings (`G…`, `C…`, `0x` + 64 hex); a delegate job refused `StaleEpoch` returns the signed and the current epoch, the client re-signs (the node holds no delegate key).

**Rulings and changes (decided during the build):**
- **Holder event rows as plain strings (controller ruling 2026-10-30 after the T9 review, owner may override):** `G…`, `C…` or `0x` + 64 hex, like the NEAR and Algorand rows; the Holder tag decides the form and the three cannot collide; `join_pay_events` compares strings; the URN is display-only, built by the client with the kind. The EVM row form differs (UA pool sentinel with `from_ua` / `to_ua`); aligning them would need an owner ruling. Cost if wrong: a later event-format change for Soroban rows.
- **StaleEpoch (T6b, T9):** the node holds no delegate key, so it cannot re-sign; a delegate job refused `StaleEpoch` re-reads `epoch(token)` and returns the signed and the current epoch in the failure reason, the client re-signs (EVM parity).
- **Executor refusal (T8 review m2, T9 fix pass 1):** `pays_router` refuses the router and the executor as the payee of `mtx_mandate_pay`, `mtx_withdraw`'s `to`, `mtx_set_payee` (when allowing), the delegate of `mtx_set_mandate` (final review B-I1, 2026-10-31: an executor delegate is anyone's, `relay` runs `mtx_mandate_pay` as it), both `settle` destinations and native signed-op mandate calls, as well as `pay` / `pay_meta` / relay-fee recipients; `op_consumed` uses the contract allow-list and requires the `ua_relay` fee token to be registered; an op with any `op.kind` on a `ua_metatx` job is refused (controller ruling, T9 fix pass 1: a `ua_metatx` job's kind is `job.kind`; an `op.kind` on its op is a misrouted job and is refused, so the rule "an unknown kind is refused" holds); a `settle` job is refused unless both orders' relayer is this lane; the router's `deploy.sh` forwards its extra arguments to `stellar contract id wasm`.
- **Lane-authority host refusal (T10 review):** the Protocol 30 host refuses the smuggled `SourceAccount` entry at simulation with `Error(Auth, InvalidAction)` before the node guard runs; the e2e asserts that outcome (`simulation:` and `Error(Auth,`); the guard is the second line and is unit-tested. The lane's entry is root-only, so a lane that is a `G…` `msig` member never lends that membership: the registry's nested `lane.require_auth_for_args((ua, purpose, digest))` has no node in the entry, and a recorded lane entry carrying a `registry.require_authorized` sub-invocation fails the job (final review A-I1 note, 2026-10-31; test `ua_metatx_lane_entry_root_only_no_member_auth`).
- **Open items:** NODE-JOB-08 `lane_hint` (a lane-bound UA, and native `relay_fee`, job claimed by another lane goes dead on a two-lane chain) is a TODO item on main; the deposit cap applies to the resource fee after the 15 % margin.

**Source.** the UA-Soroban spec `superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ua-soroban-design.md` and plan `superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ua-soroban.md`; branch `ua-soroban`; T9 review

### NET-SOR-24 — Soroban UA round: pins, test order, task order, measured limits
- old: — · status: current · owner: yes · date: 2026-10-30 · normative: networks/soroban.md#NET-SOR-24 · superseded-by: —

**Rule.** The workspace pins `soroban-sdk =30.0.0-rc.1` (30.0.0 before the testnet run), `stellar-cli` 30.0.0 and the quickstart image by digest; tests run unit, then local quickstart at Protocol 30, then the Stellar testnet only after 2026-11-03; `ua-soroban` merges before `ua8-soroban`; the measured limits and figures of T0 and the local run are published in soroban.md section 10.
**Why.** The owner's "no waiting" (2026-10-29) puts all code on a local Protocol 30 network; the first SDK release with `Crypto::ml_dsa_*_verify` is the 30.0.0 release candidate; mainnet votes Protocol 30 on 2026-11-23.
**Cost if wrong.** An RC API change before 30.0.0 means one rebuild; a figure that exceeds a limit is a hard gate for the owner.

**Spec rows recorded here** (UA-Soroban spec §0):
- **S5 — SDK and network pins** (who: controller call; status: built, branch `ua-soroban` T1 (SDK 30.0.0 swap owed before the testnet run)). Options: soroban-sdk 26.1.1 (today) / 29.0.1 (latest stable) / 30.0.0-rc.1 (2026-10-21, the first release with `Crypto::ml_dsa_{44,65,87}_verify`) / a git revision. Choice and why: **`soroban-sdk = "=30.0.0-rc.1"`** for the whole Soroban workspace (every crate rebuilds and re-tests); swapped to 30.0.0 when released, **before** the testnet e2e (this closes C16b). `stellar/quickstart` pinned by digest, run `--local --protocol-version 30 --limits testnet`. Cost if wrong: an RC API change before 30.0.0 means one more rebuild.
- **S17 — Test order** (who: owner 2026-10-29 ("no waiting"); status: followed, T0 to T10 done; the testnet run is owed). Options: —. Choice and why: unit tests (SDK testutils at protocol 30) → local quickstart at Protocol 30 → Stellar testnet e2e **only after 2026-11-03** and only when the RPC reports protocol 30. Cost if wrong: —.
- **S18 — Order inside the round** (who: plan (controller), unchanged; status: followed; `ua-soroban` awaits the owner's go, `ua8-soroban` after it). Options: one branch for UA-Soroban and Part B / two. Choice and why: **two, as the UA-8 plan says:** branch `ua-soroban` from `main` (after the token-family rename merges); on the owner's go it merges, then Part B branches `ua8-soroban`. The testnet e2e of both runs once, as the round's last step. Cost if wrong: none found.

**Plan decisions recorded here:**
- **SOR-D2 — Task order vs spec §10** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: followed). Spec T0–T12 map to plan T0, T1, T2, T3, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, T4 (clientkeys before the token: the token, mandate, DEX and router tests reproduce `ua-ops.json`), T11, T12, T14; new: T10 local e2e, T13 review. Spec C16b's "UA-Soroban T12" (the testnet task) is this plan's **T14**.
- **SOR-D3 — The spike crate** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T0). `smartcontracts/soroban/spike/` is its own cargo workspace (package `scaas-ua-spike`, pinned `=30.0.0-rc.1`), outside `contracts/*`, so T0 runs before T1 touches the workspace. Kept, never deployed; Part B's B0 extends it for the full PQZ + KEM registration (C11); Part Z's Z0 extends it with the real verifier.
- **SOR-D4 — Quickstart** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T0, T10). One script `smartcontracts/soroban/scripts/quickstart.sh up|down|wait` holds the pinned image digest and the command `docker run -d --rm --memory 3g --name scaas-stellar -p 127.0.0.1:31980:8000 <image@digest> --local --protocol-version 30 --limits testnet --enable core,rpc,horizon`; `up` exits 3 when a `scaas-stellar` container already runs; `wait` polls `getNetwork` until `protocolVersion == 30` (else fails). `smartcontracts/scripts/devnet.sh soroban` dispatches to it.
- **SOR-D5 — stellar-cli** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T0). Pinned at T0 (`scripts/capped cargo install --locked stellar-cli --version =<v>`; the installed 22.2.0 predates Protocol 30): the first release whose `stellar-xdr` supports Protocol 30, version recorded in the run log and `quickstart.sh`.
- **SOR-D12 — `ua-ops.json`** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T4). Generated by clientkeys (`scripts/soroban-ua-ops-vectors.mjs`, the deterministic signers of `scripts/ua-signers.mjs`), network passphrase `Standalone Network ; February 2017`, fixed contract ids; `--check` mode; the contract tests (registered at those ids with that network id), the adapter and clientkeys reproduce it.
- **SOR-D13 — e2e signing** (controller proposal, owner may override; status: built, T4, T10). The e2e signs through `node clients/clientkeys/scripts/soroban-sign.mjs` (the vector signers, already the reference); no Rust ML-DSA / WebAuthn signing crate is added.

T0 review I2 (`msig_model` with n distinct members' keyData and sig) and I3 (`ua_pay_model` split into token and registry contracts with the receiver read) were fixed toward the spec, controller ruling, cost if wrong: an extra spike round only. After the fix: register 4.36 M instructions, events 2,628 B (16.0 %); `msig` of three 11.64 M, events 788 B; `ua_pay` 6.04 M; every `msig` size 1 to 16 fits (the spec cap `count ≤ 16` binds, 64 KiB entry at 87.8 % for n = 16).
